chapters.title: Chapter 162
paragraphs: There are moments when a place bursting with noise suddenly falls silent.
This was one of them.
Creeeeak.
The inn went quiet as its old door swung open.

The four leaders had been raising a toast to their plan to turn Shanxi Province upside down. Now, their gazes—and those of the more than two hundred mounted bandits and nomads around them—all turned toward the entrance.
Step. Step. Step.
What the...?
Black Sand’s eyes narrowed as the uninvited guest slowly approached.
What’s with this old man?
The intruder was an old man. Quite literally, an extremely old man.
Black Sand had never seen anyone as ancient as the figure shuffling toward them.
He’s practically a corpse.
He tottered as though he might collapse at any moment. His wrinkled skin looked frozen stiff, and each breath that escaped his lips was faint and shallow.
Temur, Chinggen, and the Human Butcher watched him for a moment before exchanging a few words.
“That’s the oldest person I’ve ever seen. He’s even older than our tribe’s shaman.”
“But what’s an old man doing here? And why does he look like that?”
“He must have run into some mounted bandits.”
The old man did indeed look utterly wretched. His clothes hung in tatters, as though he had suffered some terrible misfortune, exposing a body that was little more than skin and bones.
“What an unlucky old man. He barely survives, only to end up in a mounted-bandit den.”
The Human Butcher clicked his tongue.
“I don’t even feel like killing someone that old. Get rid of him.”
“Yes, sir.”
His subordinate was about to step forward when—
“Wait.”
Black Sand raised a hand to stop him. His brow furrowed as he stared at the old man.
Something’s strange.
Mounted bandits had built this inn. Its owner, cook, and servers were all either mounted bandits or former ones.
As the only neutral ground in Northern Gaoyuan, it sometimes hosted gatherings and reconciliations like the one taking place today.
But he came crawling into a place like this on his own? An old man like that?
Anyone who set foot in Northern Gaoyuan knew about this inn.
They also knew that any ordinary civilian who entered it was as good as dead.
“What is it?”
“Shh. Wait a moment. Something about this doesn’t feel right.”
Black Sand’s reaction made the others notice the oddity as well.
“Come to think of it, how did he get here?”
“He looks like an outsider...”
“He couldn’t have come from outside. There’s no way an old man like that could have made it here in one piece.”
Hundreds of mounted-bandit groups and nomadic tribes were scattered throughout Northern Gaoyuan. No one without extraordinary nerve would even consider crossing the plateau alone.
The four men, including Black Sand, fell into thought.
Could he be...?
It would be possible if he were a martial artist.
A martial artist? That old man?
He bothers me. I should kill him.
To the Human Butcher, murder was hardly different from breathing. He reached for his scabbard without hesitation, but Black Sand shot him a glare.
A thread of Sound Transmission pierced the Human Butcher’s ear.
—I told you to wait. It won’t be too late to act after we watch him a little longer. Haven’t you ever heard that in the Murim, you should beware of women, children, and old men?
—You worry too much. Over that sickly old man?
—Don’t act rashly. You never know what might happen in the Murim.
The old man looked as though a single poke would kill him.
Still, the Human Butcher could not simply ignore Black Sand’s warning.
With an irritated sigh, he took his hand off his scabbard.
—Good choice.
By then, the mysterious old man had tottered all the way up to the four men.
A strange tension hung in the air. The old man looked around through hazy eyes, then opened his mouth.
“W-Water...”
At the sound of his parched voice begging for water, everyone shook their heads as if to say, Of course.
Everyone except Black Sand. Careful and calculating by nature, he refused to lower his guard until the very end.
“The elder seems thirsty. Bring him some cool water.”
“Yes, sir.”
A mounted bandit handed the old man a cup, and he gulped down the water as though his life depended on it. He drank so frantically that it seemed he might collapse.
Only after downing five or six cups in succession did he finally raise his head.
“Whew.”
“Feeling better now?”
A broad smile spread across the old man’s wrinkled face.
“Yes!”
“Thank you, mister!”
Mister?
Startled, Black Sand shot to his feet and seized the old man’s wrist.
There was no resistance. No strength whatsoever. His gaunt bones felt as though they might snap under the slightest pressure.
“Elder?”
“Yes? Why?”
The old man smiled and spoke like a child. Black Sand stared at him, and his expression twisted.
“Damn it. He’s senile.”
All the tension drained out of him. He had definitely sensed something strange, but apparently it had all been in his head.
With such an important undertaking ahead of him, his nerves were bound to be on edge.
As Black Sand shook his head, the Human Butcher laughed at him.
“You said anything could happen in the Murim, and you were right. An old man suffering from the infirmities of old age! Ha-ha-ha!”
“Shut your mouth.”
Black Sand answered curtly and started to release the old man’s wrist.
That was when—
“Where the hell is this?”
His voice was sharp and clear, completely different from before. His eyes had suddenly regained their focus. He looked around, then heaved a deep sigh.
“Damn it. Once you get old, you ought to die.”
It seemed he had finally returned to his senses. Laughter trickled from all around the inn at his grumbling.
Black Sand had relaxed completely as well. He let out a quiet laugh and asked,
“Elder, have you come to your senses?”
The old man answered.
“Who told a little bastard like you he could use hao-style speech with me? Are you from the Lower District Sect or something?”
“And why are you holding my wrist? You trying to get fresh with me?”
“H-Hey, you.”
“Are you letting go or not? I’ll count to three. One, two, three.”
Whoosh.
Before he knew what he was doing, Black Sand had released the old man’s wrist. The sudden turn of events had left him completely bewildered.
What the hell is this old man?
The stream of coarse curses and rapid-fire words had made his body move on its own.
The man was clearly nothing more than a deranged old fool who did not know a single martial art, yet Black Sand felt as though he had been bewitched.
“Ha-ha-ha-ha! He got you good!”
The Human Butcher burst into raucous laughter. He had already resented Black Sand acting as their leader despite being a step below him in martial arts.
Seeing Black Sand humiliated by a senile old man was deeply satisfying.
“That old man has quite a mouth on him. He gave me a good laugh, so I suppose I’ll let him live.”
But the satisfied smile on the Human Butcher’s face did not last long.
A single sentence from the old man wiped it away.
“You worthless bastard... Don’t you have a mother and father?”
The inn plunged into icy silence.
Who were Black Sand and the Human Butcher?
They were major figures who dominated the Northern Gaoyuan. Their forces were formidable, but each of them was also a Peak master capable of crushing an average mounted-bandit group with ease.
They commanded respect and fear in equal measure, yet the old man had carved them apart with a few words.
“One’s a sodomite from the Lower District Sect. One grew up without parents and has only half a tongue. And as for the other two...”
The old man glanced at Temur and Chinggen, both of whom wore their hair in queues, then sighed.
“You’re still young, but your foreheads are already bare. How pitiful.”
No one had the energy left to be surprised. Amid the atmosphere of shock and horror, the old man clicked his tongue. Then he noticed the food spread out before the four men, and his eyes widened.
“Well, damn. You’ve laid out one hell of a feast. I was hungry, too. Perfect.”
No one had time to stop him.
The old man grabbed a well-roasted duck by one leg and ripped into it.
“Would you look at how tender that meat is? Melts right on the tongue.”
Crunch, crunch.
After devouring both legs in the blink of an eye, he abruptly held out a chunk of meat to the Human Butcher, who was trembling with rage and shock.
“You’re still young. Why are you shaking like that? Don’t go wasting away from weakness—eat this. I don’t like dry breast meat. No, I can’t eat it. My teeth are bad.”
Crack.
Everyone in the inn heard the same sound.
It was the sound of the last thread of the Human Butcher’s reason snapping—and the death knell of a man.
“You goddamn old bastard!”

The next moment, the Human Butcher, beside himself with rage, shot upward like lightning. At the same time, crimson Sword Energy poured from the horse-chopping sword in his hand and swept across everything in front of him.
“What the hell!”
“Move!”
Kaboom!
Temur and Chinggen had barely thrown themselves aside when a thunderous explosion shook the inn.
Hundreds—thousands—of wooden fragments flew in every direction as a cloud of dust billowed through the air.
“Die! Die! Die!”

The sight sent chills down the onlookers’ spines. Judging by the madness pouring from the Human Butcher, the old man could not possibly have survived. There would not be so much as a scrap of flesh left.
“How dare a senile old man—! Aaaaargh!”
Boom! Boom! Boom!
A relentless storm of Sword Energy continued to pour forth. The Human Butcher finally withdrew his horse-chopping sword after the time it takes to drink a cup of tea.
“Huff... huff...”
Breathing heavily, he swung his weapon through the air. The resulting pressure scattered the dust cloud, revealing ruins that had been half reduced to powder.
Just as everyone had expected, the old man was nowhere to be seen.
“He was the bravest man I’ve ever seen.”
“Farewell, elder.”
“Why did he have to provoke the Human Butcher...?”
“As expected of those Han Chinese. They’re unbelievably savage.”
The more than two hundred mounted bandits and nomads were whispering among themselves when—
Crunch, crunch. Gulp. Guh-hup!
At first, they were simply dumbfounded.
What kind of clueless bastard would be eating and drinking at a time like this?
But it took only an instant for their disbelief to turn to shock.
“T-The old man! The old man’s alive!”
“What? Where?”
“Behind us! It came from behind us!”
Someone shouted.
Then a sharp, clear voice followed, making everyone doubt their own ears.
“Young people these days have no manners. Is my name ‘old man’? Am I your friend?”
“W-Whoa!”
“That does it. I’ll teach you bastards some manners today.”
Thud-thud-thud! Whoosh!
The mounted bandits and nomads filling the inn went flying one after another.
Every one of them was hurled aside with mangled limbs and smashed faces. The sight made the leaders break out in cold sweats.
W-What is this?
How did he get over there?
I didn’t even see him move.
A master.
A master capable of deceiving the eyes of Peak masters like them.
Black Sand, Temur, and Chinggen went rigid. Only one man charged toward the old man.
“You goddamn old bastard!”
The Human Butcher had already lost all reason. Nothing could hold him back now.
The old man saw him barreling forward and frowned.
“You’re...”
“That’s right! It’s me! This time, I’ll kill you for sure!”
“So you’re the one without parents.”
“Graaaargh!”
Whoooosh!
Mount Tai Presses Down on the Crown.
The horse-chopping blade, its crimson Sword Energy blazing, was about to split the crown of the old man’s head. The old man swung something.
Slice! Thud!
Time seemed to stop.
Not a single breath could be heard. Everyone stared in disbelief.
The horse-chopping sword had been cut in half.
And in the old man’s hand was something tiny.
“T-That’s...”

“...A chicken bone?”
“No part of a chicken goes to waste. The meat tastes good, the bones make a fine broth when you simmer them long enough, and sometimes they’re even handy for wielding Sword Energy.”
Sword Energy wielded through a chicken bone.
The Human Butcher had never seen or heard of anything so bizarre.
He understood instinctively.
A master. A Supreme Peak master. Someone I could never hope to fight.

“Hm?”
“Please spare me. Please...”

“Don’t be afraid.”
I’m safe. I’m alive! I escaped death!

That was when—
Thump.

That was the end.
The world turned upside down along with his faint question. Blood poured from the seven orifices of his fallen body and soaked the floor.
He said he’d spare me. Why?

“Don’t be afraid. I’ll send you off without pain.”
The old man had told the truth.

The Human Butcher.

“Well, then...”
The old man addressed the people who had frozen in place.
“Where is this place?”

sentences.text: There are moments when a place bursting with noise suddenly falls silent.
This was one of them.
Creeeeak.
The inn went quiet as its old door swung open.
The four leaders had been raising a toast to their plan to turn Shanxi Province upside down.
Now, their gazes—and those of the more than two hundred mounted bandits and nomads around them—all turned toward the entrance.
Step.
Step.
Step.
What the...?
Black Sand’s eyes narrowed as the uninvited guest slowly approached.
What’s with this old man?
The intruder was an old man.
Quite literally, an extremely old man.
Black Sand had never seen anyone as ancient as the figure shuffling toward them.
He’s practically a corpse.
He tottered as though he might collapse at any moment.
His wrinkled skin looked frozen stiff, and each breath that escaped his lips was faint and shallow.
Temur, Chinggen, and the Human Butcher watched him for a moment before exchanging a few words.
“That’s the oldest person I’ve ever seen.
He’s even older than our tribe’s shaman.”
“But what’s an old man doing here?
And why does he look like that?”
“He must have run into some mounted bandits.”
The old man did indeed look utterly wretched.
His clothes hung in tatters, as though he had suffered some terrible misfortune, exposing a body that was little more than skin and bones.
“What an unlucky old man.
He barely survives, only to end up in a mounted-bandit den.”
The Human Butcher clicked his tongue.
“I don’t even feel like killing someone that old.
Get rid of him.”
“Yes, sir.”
His subordinate was about to step forward when—
“Wait.”
Black Sand raised a hand to stop him.
His brow furrowed as he stared at the old man.
Something’s strange.
Mounted bandits had built this inn.
Its owner, cook, and servers were all either mounted bandits or former ones.
As the only neutral ground in Northern Gaoyuan, it sometimes hosted gatherings and reconciliations like the one taking place today.
But he came crawling into a place like this on his own?
An old man like that?
Anyone who set foot in Northern Gaoyuan knew about this inn.
They also knew that any ordinary civilian who entered it was as good as dead.
“What is it?”
“Shh.
Wait a moment.
Something about this doesn’t feel right.”
Black Sand’s reaction made the others notice the oddity as well.
“Come to think of it, how did he get here?”
“He looks like an outsider...”
“He couldn’t have come from outside.
There’s no way an old man like that could have made it here in one piece.”
Hundreds of mounted-bandit groups and nomadic tribes were scattered throughout Northern Gaoyuan.
No one without extraordinary nerve would even consider crossing the plateau alone.
The four men, including Black Sand, fell into thought.
Could he be...?
It would be possible if he were a martial artist.
A martial artist?
That old man?
He bothers me.
I should kill him.
To the Human Butcher, murder was hardly different from breathing.
He reached for his scabbard without hesitation, but Black Sand shot him a glare.
A thread of Sound Transmission pierced the Human Butcher’s ear.
—I told you to wait.
It won’t be too late to act after we watch him a little longer.
Haven’t you ever heard that in the Murim, you should beware of women, children, and old men?
—You worry too much.
Over that sickly old man?
—Don’t act rashly.
You never know what might happen in the Murim.
The old man looked as though a single poke would kill him.
Still, the Human Butcher could not simply ignore Black Sand’s warning.
With an irritated sigh, he took his hand off his scabbard.
—Good choice.
By then, the mysterious old man had tottered all the way up to the four men.
A strange tension hung in the air.
The old man looked around through hazy eyes, then opened his mouth.
“W-Water...”
At the sound of his parched voice begging for water, everyone shook their heads as if to say, Of course.
Everyone except Black Sand.
Careful and calculating by nature, he refused to lower his guard until the very end.
“The elder seems thirsty.
Bring him some cool water.”
“Yes, sir.”
A mounted bandit handed the old man a cup, and he gulped down the water as though his life depended on it.
He drank so frantically that it seemed he might collapse.
Only after downing five or six cups in succession did he finally raise his head.
“Whew.”
“Feeling better now?”
A broad smile spread across the old man’s wrinkled face.
“Yes!”
“Thank you, mister!”
Mister?
Startled, Black Sand shot to his feet and seized the old man’s wrist.
There was no resistance.
No strength whatsoever.
His gaunt bones felt as though they might snap under the slightest pressure.
“Elder?”
“Yes?
Why?”
The old man smiled and spoke like a child.
Black Sand stared at him, and his expression twisted.
“Damn it.
He’s senile.”
All the tension drained out of him.
He had definitely sensed something strange, but apparently it had all been in his head.
With such an important undertaking ahead of him, his nerves were bound to be on edge.
As Black Sand shook his head, the Human Butcher laughed at him.
“You said anything could happen in the Murim, and you were right.
An old man suffering from the infirmities of old age!
Ha-ha-ha!”
“Shut your mouth.”
Black Sand answered curtly and started to release the old man’s wrist.
That was when—
“Where the hell is this?”
His voice was sharp and clear, completely different from before.
His eyes had suddenly regained their focus.
He looked around, then heaved a deep sigh.
“Damn it.
Once you get old, you ought to die.”
It seemed he had finally returned to his senses.
Laughter trickled from all around the inn at his grumbling.
Black Sand had relaxed completely as well.
He let out a quiet laugh and asked,
“Elder, have you come to your senses?”
The old man answered.
“Who told a little bastard like you he could use hao-style speech with me?
Are you from the Lower District Sect or something?”
“And why are you holding my wrist?
You trying to get fresh with me?”
“H-Hey, you.”
“Are you letting go or not?
I’ll count to three.
One, two, three.”
Whoosh.
Before he knew what he was doing, Black Sand had released the old man’s wrist.
The sudden turn of events had left him completely bewildered.
What the hell is this old man?
The stream of coarse curses and rapid-fire words had made his body move on its own.
The man was clearly nothing more than a deranged old fool who did not know a single martial art, yet Black Sand felt as though he had been bewitched.
“Ha-ha-ha-ha!
He got you good!”
The Human Butcher burst into raucous laughter.
He had already resented Black Sand acting as their leader despite being a step below him in martial arts.
Seeing Black Sand humiliated by a senile old man was deeply satisfying.
“That old man has quite a mouth on him.
He gave me a good laugh, so I suppose I’ll let him live.”
But the satisfied smile on the Human Butcher’s face did not last long.
A single sentence from the old man wiped it away.
“You worthless bastard...
Don’t you have a mother and father?”
The inn plunged into icy silence.
Who were Black Sand and the Human Butcher?
They were major figures who dominated the Northern Gaoyuan.
Their forces were formidable, but each of them was also a Peak master capable of crushing an average mounted-bandit group with ease.
They commanded respect and fear in equal measure, yet the old man had carved them apart with a few words.
“One’s a sodomite from the Lower District Sect.
One grew up without parents and has only half a tongue.
And as for the other two...”
The old man glanced at Temur and Chinggen, both of whom wore their hair in queues, then sighed.
“You’re still young, but your foreheads are already bare.
How pitiful.”
No one had the energy left to be surprised.
Amid the atmosphere of shock and horror, the old man clicked his tongue.
Then he noticed the food spread out before the four men, and his eyes widened.
“Well, damn.
You’ve laid out one hell of a feast.
I was hungry, too.
Perfect.”
No one had time to stop him.
The old man grabbed a well-roasted duck by one leg and ripped into it.
“Would you look at how tender that meat is?
Melts right on the tongue.”
Crunch, crunch.
After devouring both legs in the blink of an eye, he abruptly held out a chunk of meat to the Human Butcher, who was trembling with rage and shock.
“You’re still young.
Why are you shaking like that?
Don’t go wasting away from weakness—eat this.
I don’t like dry breast meat.
No, I can’t eat it.
My teeth are bad.”
Crack.
Everyone in the inn heard the same sound.
It was the sound of the last thread of the Human Butcher’s reason snapping—and the death knell of a man.
“You goddamn old bastard!”
The next moment, the Human Butcher, beside himself with rage, shot upward like lightning.
At the same time, crimson Sword Energy poured from the horse-chopping sword in his hand and swept across everything in front of him.
“What the hell!”
“Move!”
Kaboom!
Temur and Chinggen had barely thrown themselves aside when a thunderous explosion shook the inn.
Hundreds—thousands—of wooden fragments flew in every direction as a cloud of dust billowed through the air.
“Die!
Die!
Die!”
The sight sent chills down the onlookers’ spines.
Judging by the madness pouring from the Human Butcher, the old man could not possibly have survived.
There would not be so much as a scrap of flesh left.
“How dare a senile old man—!
Aaaaargh!”
Boom!
Boom!
Boom!
A relentless storm of Sword Energy continued to pour forth.
The Human Butcher finally withdrew his horse-chopping sword after the time it takes to drink a cup of tea.
“Huff... huff...”
Breathing heavily, he swung his weapon through the air.
The resulting pressure scattered the dust cloud, revealing ruins that had been half reduced to powder.

“He was the bravest man I’ve ever seen.”
“Farewell, elder.”
“Why did he have to provoke the Human Butcher...?”
“As expected of those Han Chinese.
They’re unbelievably savage.”
The more than two hundred mounted bandits and nomads were whispering among themselves when—
Crunch, crunch.
Gulp.
Guh-hup!
At first, they were simply dumbfounded.
What kind of clueless bastard would be eating and drinking at a time like this?
But it took only an instant for their disbelief to turn to shock.

The old man’s alive!”
“What?
Where?”
“Behind us!
It came from behind us!”
Someone shouted.

“Young people these days have no manners.

Am I your friend?”
“W-Whoa!”
“That does it.
I’ll teach you bastards some manners today.”
Thud-thud-thud!
Whoosh!
The mounted bandits and nomads filling the inn went flying one after another.
Every one of them was hurled aside with mangled limbs and smashed faces.
The sight made the leaders break out in cold sweats.

chapters.title: Chapter 163
paragraphs: “What? The Northern Gaoyuan? And there are only three days left until New Year’s Day?”
“Yes.”
“Well, now.”
The old man fell silent. Before him, the three leaders and more than two hundred of their men knelt respectfully, hanging on his every word.
“Is that really true?”
“W-We’re certain.”
“How could we possibly dare lie to your face?”
“...I see.”
The old man’s expression darkened at their desperate excuses.
He knew what they were saying was true. He had only wanted to deny it, if only a little—the fact that he was growing old.
So I was out of it for seven days and nights. Seven days and nights... It’s getting longer.
It was because of the infirmities of old age.

He had first noticed the strange symptoms more than twenty years ago. While cultivating, he had felt his essence, qi, and spirit falling out of alignment and realized that time had finally caught up with him.
He was already nearing a hundred. He did not fear death, but he had no desire to be remembered as a senile old man.
Even after all that effort...
He had reached his limit. The curse of time could not be held back even by two jiazi of internal energy or the Force of a Supreme Peak master.
He had managed to stave off the infirmities of old age for twenty years. He should be satisfied with that alone. The old man forced himself to cast aside his bitterness.
“Pour me a drink.”
“Um, the wine has gone cold, so we’re preparing a fresh batch.”
At Black Sand’s cautious reply, the old man clicked his tongue.
“How long will that take? Never mind. Bring me the cold wine.”
“Yes.”
Who would dare argue with him? At a glance from Black Sand, two burly mounted bandits hauled over a wine jar, grunting with effort.
The enormous jar, tall enough to reach a man’s chest, sloshed with half-cooled mare’s-milk wine.
“Tsk, tsk. Young men these days are so weak. Don’t you feed your men?”
“H-How could we not?”
“Then why are they struggling so much? Good grief. I can’t stand watching this.”
The old man sprang to his feet and snatched the jar away. Weighing several hundred geun at the very least, it rose effortlessly in one hand.
It was almost impossible to believe such strength could come from a body reduced to little more than skin and bones. Black Sand wanted to gouge out his own eyes.
I must have been insane. I thought a monster like that was nothing more than a senile old man.
At least he had watched his words. The Human Butcher had swung his sword around while calling the man an old geezer, and look how horribly he had died.
Black Sand had no desire to meet the same end, bleeding from all seven orifices.
“Elder! I’ll do it!”
“Don’t call me elder. Sit down and stop talking nonsense.”
“No, no. Mare’s-milk wine tastes best when it’s piping hot. I’ll heat it myself...”
“Piping hot, you say?”
Black Sand fell speechless.
The next moment, tremendous heat burst from the wine jar.
It came from the old man’s hand gripping the jar.
White flames that made them feel suffocated and sent goose bumps crawling over their skin at the mere sight instantly heated the jar and warmed the mare’s-milk wine.
“T-That’s...”
“S-Samadhi True Fire?”
Temur, Chinggen, and the more than two hundred underlings were stunned by the sight before them.
The three leaders were particularly shocked.
What the hell?
He’s using Samadhi True Fire on a wine jar that size?
That’s an unbelievable amount of internal energy. Who is this old man?
Samadhi True Fire was a flame produced by burning internal energy. Any Peak master with sufficiently profound internal energy could use it without much difficulty.
However, the flames were weak compared to the enormous amount of internal energy they consumed, making them hopelessly inefficient in actual combat.
“Bring me a bowl. A big one.”
But this old man was different.
The heat they had felt, though momentary, had been tremendous. If he wished, he seemed capable not only of harming people but of melting steel.
His martial arts and internal energy have already reached a transcendent realm.
It isn’t only the Samadhi True Fire. His internal energy itself is overwhelmingly powerful Scorching Yang Qi.
Keep your mouth shut. One wrong word and... you’re dead.
The three men swallowed hard and hurried about like waiters attending an honored guest.
“Allow me to pour you a drink.”
“Bring meat! Meat!”
“Just tear off the legs!”

Black Sand, the Squad Leader of the Black Sand Band—known across the steppe as a harbinger of death—poured the mare’s-milk wine. The two tribal chieftains, descendants of the Great Khan and commanders of hundreds of mounted warriors, circled the table, tearing off only the tender leg meat and presenting it to the old man.
It was a sight even gold could not buy.
“Mm. This is why rude bastards need a good beating. They only learn manners after someone teaches them a lesson.”
“You’re absolutely right, elder.”
The old man, who had been washing down carefully stripped meat with mare’s-milk wine, paused.
“Elder?”
“Y-Yes. Did I make some kind of mistake?”
“You’re making me sound old. Like some old man who could drop dead at any moment.”
Yes. You really do look like you’re about to drop dead.
Black Sand barely swallowed the words before they escaped. His opponent was a peerless master whose realm he could not even begin to fathom. He had to stay on the old man’s good side somehow.
“Then, big brother...”
“Do I look like a pushover?”
“I-I’m sorry!”
Bam!

Without another word, Black Sand slammed his forehead against the floor. He wanted to die. The man hated “elder” because it made him sound old, but apparently “big brother” made him sound like a pushover. What the hell was Black Sand supposed to call him?
The old man gave the prostrated Black Sand a light kick.
“Get up.”
“Yes, sir!”
“You two with the scraped foreheads as well.”
Whoosh!
Temur and Chinggen, who had been diligently stripping meat from the bones, rushed over at the speed of light and knelt.
Only after taking a long drink of mare’s-milk wine did the old man finally speak.
“So, what kind of bastards are you?”
Mounted bandits. And nomads who were little different from mounted bandits.
They had no idea what would happen if they told the truth to an old man who was clearly a senior master of the orthodox faction.
Just as the three desperately exchanged glances—
Smack! Smack! Smack!
“Ghk!”
“Gasp!”
“Argh!”
The old man struck each of them on the head with a knuckle at a speed too fast to see, then glared.
“You goddamn bastards. An adult asks you a question, and all you do is roll your eyes at each other?”
“I-I’m sorry, elder.”
“I told you not to call me elder. Are you performing some ritual to pray for my death? Huh?”
Smack!
Black Sand answered and got hit again for his trouble. He felt tears welling up. He was over fifty, and all his subordinates were watching him...
“Oldest one first. Answer me.”
Black Sand gazed at the old man with watery eyes and opened his mouth.
“I, that is... I roam the steppe with like-minded brothers, with our horses as companions...”
“So you’re a worthless mounted bandit. You loot, murder, and set fires every chance you get.”
The old man regarded Black Sand with utter contempt before turning away. Temur and Chinggen flinched and lowered their heads.
“You two call yourselves nomads, but you’re no different. Am I wrong?”
“N-No, sir.”
“You are absolutely right.”

“The only way you’re better than mounted bandits is that, although you loot and kill, at least you aren’t arsonists setting fire to everything in sight. Bastards who burn down other people’s homes deserve to be beaten to death!”
Wasn’t murder normally considered the gravest crime?
The three men tilted their heads at this strange distinction, only to be struck by another hail of blows.
Smack! Smack! Smack!
“Anyway, I have a general idea what sort of holes you crawled out of. What I want to know is how much influence you have around here.”
“Ow... What do you mean by influence?”
“Exactly what I said. Do you have any clout?”
Rubbing the tops of their heads, the three men answered carefully.
“If we join forces, there aren’t many who could stand against us.”
“Most of our people are spread across separate branch families, but if all our relatives gathered, we could easily make up dozens of tribes and still have people left over.”
“We share every piece of news from across the steppe.”
The old man’s eyes flashed at Chinggen’s final answer.
“Oh? That’s useful.”
Quick to read the situation, Chinggen realized the old man wanted information and immediately answered.
“If you need information, we’ll tell you anything you wish to know.”
“I’m looking for someone. I don’t know exactly where he is, but... he probably isn’t too far away. Can you find him?”
“Yes. If you could describe his appearance or any distinguishing features, it would be even easier.”
“Wait here.”
The old man pulled a crumpled sheet of xuan paper from his robes. A fairly skilled artist appeared to have drawn it, and the face of the person he sought was clearly depicted.
“Will this do?”
Chinggen nodded without hesitation.
“Of course. With a portrait sketch as well, we should be able to start asking around immediately.”
If they sent messengers in all directions and dispatched messenger eagles, they could learn the answer within fifteen days at the longest.
The steppe was vast, but no one could escape the eyes of the nomads.
Besides, every scrap of news about outsiders reaches my ears.
But Chinggen’s confidence faltered at the old man’s next words.
“He’s a Peak master. He primarily uses a sword and palm techniques.”
“...Did you say he’s a Peak master?”
“Why? Doesn’t that make things easier? He’ll stand out wherever he goes, so you should find him quickly.”
Chinggen struggled to speak.
“I-I’m sorry, but if he’s a master of that level, my brothers would have noticed him long ago.”
“Hmm. What do you two think?”
“I oversee a fairly wide territory myself, but I’ve never heard of such a master appearing.”
“If Chinggen cannot find him, then neither can I.”
After receiving similar answers from Black Sand and Temur, who had been sitting quietly with their shoulders hunched, the old man furrowed his brow.
“Damn that bastard. Making an old man go through all this trouble.”
The three men’s ears perked up at the bitterness in his mutter.
What circumstances could have driven an unidentified Supreme Peak master to search for someone personally? Especially while suffering from the infirmities of old age.
His son? Or his Disciple?
Judging by his attitude, the man had to be a blood relative or Disciple...
Black Sand felt his heart pounding. An old man standing at the end of his life was searching for someone while struggling to hold on to a mind that came and went.
Someone he had to meet before he died. A final lingering regret he had to resolve, even if it meant going to such lengths.
Could this be...?
Black Sand’s thoughts raced. Perhaps he could turn the greatest crisis of his life into an opportunity.
His lips parted slightly, and Sound Transmission slipped out.
—Chinggen.
Despite the sudden Sound Transmission, Chinggen showed no reaction. As expected, he was a shrewd one.
—Are you listening? Answer me.
—Accept the old man’s offer. Quickly!

—Impossible. I can’t find the person he wants. If we succeed, we may earn a tremendous favor, but if we raise his hopes for nothing and fail, all we’ll earn is his resentment. I have no intention of taking that risk. Nor do I want to become any more entangled with that old man.
—Find him.
—What?
—If you find him, you can obtain the old man’s martial arts. Martial arts powerful enough to look down upon the entire world!
At that moment, Black Sand was utterly convinced. Whether the person was the old man’s Disciple or his son, they had to find him. If they did...
We could steal not just one city, but the entire world!
He intended to blackmail a Supreme Peak master. Chinggen’s lips trembled slightly as he grasped Black Sand’s meaning.
—Are you insane? Greed has blinded you!
—No, it’s entirely possible. You’re too frightened of that old man to think clearly.
—Don’t be ridiculous. Do you think he’ll fall for a threat like that? He’ll tear us apart before that happens!

—He’s already an old man whose mind comes and goes because of his infirmities. First, we scour the surrounding area and find the bastard. Then we drag things out until the old man loses his mind again.
Even Black Sand thought it was a perfect plan. When the old man’s mind was not clear, he was no different from a child.
They would wait for that moment, then subdue him. Through persuasion and threats, they would steal every bit of that powerful martial arts knowledge.
—What are you hesitating for? Accept already!
That was when an answer came.
“Yes, hurry up and accept. What are you waiting for?”
Black Sand froze.
The old man was staring at him with reddish, glowing eyes. Flames no one could possibly resist streamed from his dark, sunken pupils.
“Are you finished?”
“E-Elder.”
“You aren’t particularly bright, are you? You’ve already made me say the same thing three times.”
Thud.
At that same instant, the old man’s palm pierced Black Sand’s abdomen. Scorching Yang Qi at its utmost burned his organs and seared his blood vessels.
“Didn’t I tell you not to call me elder?”
Thump.
Black Sand collapsed as a charred lump. Chinggen closed his eyes as a voice drier than desert sand bored into his ears.
“I’ll be back in about a month.”
When Chinggen opened his eyes again, the old man was nowhere to be seen.
The old man clicked his tongue.
“Nothing has changed. Absolutely nothing has changed.”
The world he had returned to after so long was still the same. Evil men, righteous men, and those who belonged to neither side were all mixed together.
No matter who lived or died, someone always filled the empty space they left behind. The same was true of those mounted bandits. They had simply been unlucky.
“Speaking of which, the Northern Gaoyuan...”
“I certainly came a long way,” the old man muttered as he looked around.
The horizon stretched to the ends of the world. Here, where green grasslands and parched earth existed side by side, there was only one place for him to go.
I’ll leave this area to that nomad bastard and search Shanxi Province myself.
The old man began to walk. With every step, the landscape flashed past and the grasses bowed low.
His stride was leisurely, yet he moved as swiftly as a loosed arrow.
The arrow was bound for Datong, on the border between Shanxi and the Gaoyuan.

sentences.text: “What?
The Northern Gaoyuan?
And there are only three days left until New Year’s Day?”
“Yes.”
“Well, now.”
The old man fell silent.
Before him, the three leaders and more than two hundred of their men knelt respectfully, hanging on his every word.
“Is that really true?”
“W-We’re certain.”
“How could we possibly dare lie to your face?”
“...I see.”
The old man’s expression darkened at their desperate excuses.
He knew what they were saying was true.
He had only wanted to deny it, if only a little—the fact that he was growing old.
So I was out of it for seven days and nights.
Seven days and nights...
It’s getting longer.
It was because of the infirmities of old age.
He had first noticed the strange symptoms more than twenty years ago.
While cultivating, he had felt his essence, qi, and spirit falling out of alignment and realized that time had finally caught up with him.
He was already nearing a hundred.
He did not fear death, but he had no desire to be remembered as a senile old man.
Even after all that effort...
He had reached his limit.
The curse of time could not be held back even by two jiazi of internal energy or the Force of a Supreme Peak master.
He had managed to stave off the infirmities of old age for twenty years.
He should be satisfied with that alone.
The old man forced himself to cast aside his bitterness.
“Pour me a drink.”
“Um, the wine has gone cold, so we’re preparing a fresh batch.”
At Black Sand’s cautious reply, the old man clicked his tongue.
“How long will that take?
Never mind.
Bring me the cold wine.”
“Yes.”
Who would dare argue with him?
At a glance from Black Sand, two burly mounted bandits hauled over a wine jar, grunting with effort.
The enormous jar, tall enough to reach a man’s chest, sloshed with half-cooled mare’s-milk wine.
“Tsk, tsk.
Young men these days are so weak.
Don’t you feed your men?”
“H-How could we not?”
“Then why are they struggling so much?
Good grief.
I can’t stand watching this.”
The old man sprang to his feet and snatched the jar away.
Weighing several hundred geun at the very least, it rose effortlessly in one hand.
It was almost impossible to believe such strength could come from a body reduced to little more than skin and bones.
Black Sand wanted to gouge out his own eyes.
I must have been insane.
I thought a monster like that was nothing more than a senile old man.
At least he had watched his words.
The Human Butcher had swung his sword around while calling the man an old geezer, and look how horribly he had died.
Black Sand had no desire to meet the same end, bleeding from all seven orifices.
“Elder!
I’ll do it!”
“Don’t call me elder.
Sit down and stop talking nonsense.”
“No, no.
Mare’s-milk wine tastes best when it’s piping hot.
I’ll heat it myself...”
“Piping hot, you say?”
Black Sand fell speechless.
The next moment, tremendous heat burst from the wine jar.
It came from the old man’s hand gripping the jar.
White flames that made them feel suffocated and sent goose bumps crawling over their skin at the mere sight instantly heated the jar and warmed the mare’s-milk wine.
“T-That’s...”
“S-Samadhi True Fire?”
Temur, Chinggen, and the more than two hundred underlings were stunned by the sight before them.
The three leaders were particularly shocked.
What the hell?
He’s using Samadhi True Fire on a wine jar that size?
That’s an unbelievable amount of internal energy.
Who is this old man?
Samadhi True Fire was a flame produced by burning internal energy.
Any Peak master with sufficiently profound internal energy could use it without much difficulty.
However, the flames were weak compared to the enormous amount of internal energy they consumed, making them hopelessly inefficient in actual combat.
“Bring me a bowl.
A big one.”
But this old man was different.
The heat they had felt, though momentary, had been tremendous.
If he wished, he seemed capable not only of harming people but of melting steel.
His martial arts and internal energy have already reached a transcendent realm.
It isn’t only the Samadhi True Fire.
His internal energy itself is overwhelmingly powerful Scorching Yang Qi.
Keep your mouth shut.
One wrong word and... you’re dead.
The three men swallowed hard and hurried about like waiters attending an honored guest.
“Allow me to pour you a drink.”
“Bring meat!
Meat!”
“Just tear off the legs!”
Black Sand, the Squad Leader of the Black Sand Band—known across the steppe as a harbinger of death—poured the mare’s-milk wine.
The two tribal chieftains, descendants of the Great Khan and commanders of hundreds of mounted warriors, circled the table, tearing off only the tender leg meat and presenting it to the old man.
It was a sight even gold could not buy.
“Mm.
This is why rude bastards need a good beating.
They only learn manners after someone teaches them a lesson.”
“You’re absolutely right, elder.”
The old man, who had been washing down carefully stripped meat with mare’s-milk wine, paused.
“Elder?”
“Y-Yes.
Did I make some kind of mistake?”
“You’re making me sound old.
Like some old man who could drop dead at any moment.”
Yes.
You really do look like you’re about to drop dead.
Black Sand barely swallowed the words before they escaped.
His opponent was a peerless master whose realm he could not even begin to fathom.
He had to stay on the old man’s good side somehow.
“Then, big brother...”
“Do I look like a pushover?”
“I-I’m sorry!”
Bam!
Without another word, Black Sand slammed his forehead against the floor.
He wanted to die.
The man hated “elder” because it made him sound old, but apparently “big brother” made him sound like a pushover.
What the hell was Black Sand supposed to call him?
The old man gave the prostrated Black Sand a light kick.
“Get up.”
“Yes, sir!”
“You two with the scraped foreheads as well.”
Whoosh!
Temur and Chinggen, who had been diligently stripping meat from the bones, rushed over at the speed of light and knelt.
Only after taking a long drink of mare’s-milk wine did the old man finally speak.
“So, what kind of bastards are you?”
Mounted bandits.
And nomads who were little different from mounted bandits.
They had no idea what would happen if they told the truth to an old man who was clearly a senior master of the orthodox faction.
Just as the three desperately exchanged glances—
Smack!
Smack!
Smack!
“Ghk!”
“Gasp!”
“Argh!”
The old man struck each of them on the head with a knuckle at a speed too fast to see, then glared.
“You goddamn bastards.
An adult asks you a question, and all you do is roll your eyes at each other?”
“I-I’m sorry, elder.”
“I told you not to call me elder.
Are you performing some ritual to pray for my death?
Huh?”
Smack!
Black Sand answered and got hit again for his trouble.
He felt tears welling up.
He was over fifty, and all his subordinates were watching him...
“Oldest one first.
Answer me.”
Black Sand gazed at the old man with watery eyes and opened his mouth.
“I, that is...
I roam the steppe with like-minded brothers, with our horses as companions...”
“So you’re a worthless mounted bandit.
You loot, murder, and set fires every chance you get.”
The old man regarded Black Sand with utter contempt before turning away.
Temur and Chinggen flinched and lowered their heads.
“You two call yourselves nomads, but you’re no different.
Am I wrong?”
“N-No, sir.”
“You are absolutely right.”
“The only way you’re better than mounted bandits is that, although you loot and kill, at least you aren’t arsonists setting fire to everything in sight.
Bastards who burn down other people’s homes deserve to be beaten to death!”
Wasn’t murder normally considered the gravest crime?
The three men tilted their heads at this strange distinction, only to be struck by another hail of blows.
Smack!
Smack!
Smack!
“Anyway, I have a general idea what sort of holes you crawled out of.
What I want to know is how much influence you have around here.”
What do you mean by influence?”
“Exactly what I said.
Do you have any clout?”
Rubbing the tops of their heads, the three men answered carefully.
“If we join forces, there aren’t many who could stand against us.”
“Most of our people are spread across separate branch families, but if all our relatives gathered, we could easily make up dozens of tribes and still have people left over.”
“We share every piece of news from across the steppe.”
The old man’s eyes flashed at Chinggen’s final answer.
“Oh?
That’s useful.”
Quick to read the situation, Chinggen realized the old man wanted information and immediately answered.
“If you need information, we’ll tell you anything you wish to know.”
“I’m looking for someone.
I don’t know exactly where he is, but... he probably isn’t too far away.
Can you find him?”
“Yes.
If you could describe his appearance or any distinguishing features, it would be even easier.”
“Wait here.”
The old man pulled a crumpled sheet of xuan paper from his robes.
A fairly skilled artist appeared to have drawn it, and the face of the person he sought was clearly depicted.
“Will this do?”
Chinggen nodded without hesitation.
“Of course.
With a portrait sketch as well, we should be able to start asking around immediately.”
If they sent messengers in all directions and dispatched messenger eagles, they could learn the answer within fifteen days at the longest.
The steppe was vast, but no one could escape the eyes of the nomads.
Besides, every scrap of news about outsiders reaches my ears.
But Chinggen’s confidence faltered at the old man’s next words.
“He’s a Peak master.
He primarily uses a sword and palm techniques.”
“...Did you say he’s a Peak master?”
“Why?
Doesn’t that make things easier?
He’ll stand out wherever he goes, so you should find him quickly.”
Chinggen struggled to speak.
“I-I’m sorry, but if he’s a master of that level, my brothers would have noticed him long ago.”
“Hmm.
What do you two think?”
“I oversee a fairly wide territory myself, but I’ve never heard of such a master appearing.”
“If Chinggen cannot find him, then neither can I.”
After receiving similar answers from Black Sand and Temur, who had been sitting quietly with their shoulders hunched, the old man furrowed his brow.
“Damn that bastard.
Making an old man go through all this trouble.”
The three men’s ears perked up at the bitterness in his mutter.
What circumstances could have driven an unidentified Supreme Peak master to search for someone personally?
Especially while suffering from the infirmities of old age.
His son?
Or his Disciple?
Judging by his attitude, the man had to be a blood relative or Disciple...
Black Sand felt his heart pounding.
An old man standing at the end of his life was searching for someone while struggling to hold on to a mind that came and went.
Someone he had to meet before he died.
A final lingering regret he had to resolve, even if it meant going to such lengths.
Could this be...?
Black Sand’s thoughts raced.
Perhaps he could turn the greatest crisis of his life into an opportunity.
His lips parted slightly, and Sound Transmission slipped out.
—Chinggen.
Despite the sudden Sound Transmission, Chinggen showed no reaction.
As expected, he was a shrewd one.
—Are you listening?
Answer me.
—Accept the old man’s offer.
Quickly!
—Impossible.
I can’t find the person he wants.
If we succeed, we may earn a tremendous favor, but if we raise his hopes for nothing and fail, all we’ll earn is his resentment.
I have no intention of taking that risk.
Nor do I want to become any more entangled with that old man.
—Find him.
—What?
—If you find him, you can obtain the old man’s martial arts.
Martial arts powerful enough to look down upon the entire world!
At that moment, Black Sand was utterly convinced.
Whether the person was the old man’s Disciple or his son, they had to find him.
If they did...
We could steal not just one city, but the entire world!
He intended to blackmail a Supreme Peak master.
Chinggen’s lips trembled slightly as he grasped Black Sand’s meaning.
—Are you insane?
Greed has blinded you!

You’re too frightened of that old man to think clearly.

paragraphs: System Status Window Lv. 71 Jin Taekyung Class: Peak Master Fame: 2,400 (+250) Titles: 5 (Title effects active) - Returnee (All stats +10) - Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi (All stats +15, Fame +200) - Scion of a Prestigious Family (All stats +5, Fame +50) - Gambler (Combat-related stats +10% in one-on-one combat) - Intermediate Trainee (Training speed +20%) Strength: 255 (+30) Stamina: 207 (+30) Agility: 250 (+30) Intelligence: 40 (+30) Charm: 40 (+30) Internal Energy: 45 years Toughness: 200 (+30) Remaining Points: 70 - Distribute your remaining points.
I checked my Status Window more than ten times a day, but it still made me grin every time.
Who knew the four characters meaning “Peak Master” could make me this happy?
The System calls me a master. A Peak Master.
Only a few hours ago, the Class field had read First Rate Martial Artist. But now I was a Peak Master. Not just a martial artist, but a master.
I had become a genuine master, recognized even by the System.
And I’m already Level 71.
The rewards had been incredible.
Seven level-ups, a one-stage increase in both the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique and Qi Sense, and...
I even got something money couldn’t buy.
Open Inventory.
As soon as I entered the command in my mind, a familiar System notification chimed and a translucent holographic window appeared.
My Inventory was packed with all kinds of junk I had collected in the Murim, but my gaze went straight to one item.
Summon Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
Whoosh.
A heavy sphere suddenly popped into existence in midair. It was about the size of a bowling ball, its unpolished surface rough and jagged, with lumps jutting out in every direction.
At first glance, it looked like nothing more than a useless lump of metal or rock. But anyone who looked a little closer would recognize its true value.
Inspect Item.
Ding.

System Item Window Unprocessed Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron Type: Material Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: Master Artisan Description: Ten-thousand-year-old cold iron is harder, sharper, and rarer than any other mineral in existence. Only a craftsman who has reached the level of Master Artisan will be able to work with this precious material.
“Now, this is the real deal.”

Personally, I was happier about obtaining the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron than I was about leveling up. I was a Hunter and a martial artist. Everyone in this line of work dreamed of owning great equipment.
I had simply never had the means to make that dream a reality.
I had no money in the real world, and in the Murim, I didn’t have a decent spear.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan’s roots lay in sword techniques, not spear techniques.

Supply followed demand. Most of the family’s members, from its lowest-ranking martial artists to its leadership, were swordsmen. Naturally, both the family’s martial arts and the weapons in its armory favored swords by a wide margin.
If Jin Wikyung hadn’t looked out for me, I might have ended up fighting with a cheap wooden or bamboo spear.
How many times had my guts twisted whenever I swung an iron spear while leaving the [Unnamed Sword], made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, at my side?
But that humiliation is over now.
I had obtained the finest mineral in the world. Now I could have a weapon of my own made from it.
Of course, there was one prerequisite.
The Quest I had just received was related to that.
Inspect Quest.
Ding.

System Quest Find the Master Artisan Forging Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron requires tremendous experience and skill. Only an exceptionally skilled artisan will be able to draw out the full power of this precious material. Grade: Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Commission a Master Artisan to make a weapon (Incomplete) Reward: ??? Failure: ???
I smiled contentedly and closed the Quest Window.
Of course. I can’t entrust something as valuable as Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron to just anyone.
Even without the Quest, I would have looked into it myself.
Just as a famed sword only revealed its true brilliance in the hands of a master, the same was true of a precious material like Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
Although the Quest was graded Peak, the mission itself didn’t seem particularly difficult.
Finding someone shouldn’t take long.
Surely there had to be at least one Master Artisan in this enormous land.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan had branches throughout Shanxi. If I asked Jin Wikyung to send out word, we would soon know where to find one.
And if that doesn’t work, I can ask the Lower District Sect.
I even had a powerful connection in Wolhwa. With eyes and ears planted throughout Shanxi Province, finding someone like that would be a piece of cake for her.
Whatever it takes, I’m completing this Quest before I leave.
A month in the Murim was only three hours in the modern world.
I still had plenty of time.
“Hehehe. A spear made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. A spear made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron...”
Just as I was grinning from ear to ear—
Bang!
The door blew apart with a deafening crash. Someone rushed in like lightning, charging toward me with both arms spread wide.
“Youngest!”
Yep. I knew it would be you.
I let out a deep sigh and asked Jin Wikyung, “What’s going on?”
“What do you mean, what’s going on? I heard the wonderful news that you broke through the wall and rushed here at once!”
“...How did you hear about that?”
It had only happened an hour or two ago, but the speed of the information network was no joke. Had this guy attached a Familiar to me or something?

As I stared at him in bewilderment, I spotted Hyuk Mujin standing in front of the blown-open doorway with a proud smile. He rubbed beneath his nose and said, “Shouldn’t such wonderful news be delivered first by one’s closest aide?”
Not a Familiar. A Hyuk-miliar.
That bastard had definitely used my name to score points with Jin Wikyung.
“Waaah! Our youngest broke through the wall! He reached the Peak realm!”
Sure enough, Hyuk Mujin quickly cut in.
“Lesser Family Head, I stood guard over him!”
“Thank you. Truly, thank you. Your contribution was enormous!”

“Not at all. As your right arm, I merely did what I was supposed to do. I had not a shred of selfish intent. However, I noticed that the position of Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion is still vacant...”
“It’s yours without question! No, you’ll be the next Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan!”
“W-Whaaat? Is that really true?”
Of course it wasn’t, you dumbass.
Did it make any sense to appoint someone Family Head just because he had stood guard? Besides, all that bastard had actually done was snore.
But the two men, blinded by joy and power, were already out of their minds.
“Hyuk Mujin. You said your name was Hyuk Mujin, right?”
“Yes, Lesser Family Head!”
“Our Mujin can do whatever he wants! Become Family Head! Smash the Nine Sects and One Gang! Smash the world!”
“Smash!”
“...What are you smashing, you lunatics?”
The future of the Jin Family of Taiyuan looked bleak.
Once the commotion died down, Jin Wikyung finally managed to calm himself and looked at me with moist eyes.
“Your brother is proud of you.”
“I’m proud of you too, Captain. But if I hadn’t stood guard over you...”
“Mujin, let’s keep quiet unless you want your pot cracked. And by ‘pot,’ I mean your head.”
“Yes, sir.”
Hyuk Mujin, now sporting a lump on his forehead, answered at once. As expected, he only listened after getting hit.
“Your useless older brother couldn’t even look after you properly, and yet you grew up so well all on your own. Sniff.”
Look at this human weapon getting all sentimental.
Whenever Jin Wikyung acted like this, I was grateful that this world had no social media. If it did, a post tagging every member of the Jin Family of Taiyuan would have gone up on Outstagram.
Complete with a teary-eyed selfie and hashtags.

\#JinFamilyofTaiyuan #UselessOlderBrother #OurYoungestIsAPeakMaster #KeepYourChinUpToday └ Wolhwa: Oh my! Young Master Jin? Congratulations! └ Cheongpung: Wow, I’ve never clicked Like before! └ Wipeng: Don’t lie. └ Hyuk Mujin: I stood guard over him. └ Jin Mukyung: Is this what you call a country? └ Zhu Bao: An autograph, please.
Imagining the reactions from countless Shanxi Province celebrities made my vision swim.
I hurriedly pushed the horrifying thought from my mind and tried to soothe Jin Wikyung.
“Please stop crying. How old are you?”
“Sniff. How did my immature youngest brother grow into such a fine man?”
Jin Wikyung gazed at me with a mixture of emotion and pride, then wiped the corners of his eyes with his sleeve.
“No, this won’t do. I need to go right now and...”
“You’re not planning to write ‘Jin Taekyung has become a Peak Master’ on a gigantic banner like last time, are you?”
“Gasp.”
I knew it. Judging by everything Jin Wikyung had done until now, there was no way he would let this opportunity pass. I had to make myself perfectly clear.
“Don’t do anything like that. It’s cringe.”
“Cringe? What does that mean?”
“It means embarrassing.”
Jin Wikyung looked shocked.
“Are you saying you’re embarrassed by me? By your own brother?”
“No, that’s not what I...”
This was driving me insane.
Before I could answer, Hyuk Mujin, who had been sitting quietly with his shoulders hunched, suddenly cut in with a baffled look.
“Huh? Captain, you usually like getting attention.”
“When have I ever?”
“You don’t? If I remember correctly, you seemed to love it. When we returned from the Mount Heng Sword Sect, you stood at the very front and waved like crazy.”
“...Ahem.”
If he had made that up, I would have punched him. But it was true, so I had nothing to say.
I quietly avoided Hyuk Mujin’s gaze and replied, “That was different. I had my reasons.”
“What reasons?”
“There were reasons. You don’t need to know.”
“Wow, there he goes again.”
I ignored Hyuk Mujin’s muttering and turned back to Jin Wikyung.
“Anyway, we’re not doing anything like that. The attention I’m getting now is more than enough.”
“Hmm. If that’s truly what you want...”
Jin Wikyung couldn’t hide his disappointment, but I was so firm that he reluctantly nodded. That let me breathe a sigh of relief.
What’s the point of advertising that I became a Peak Master? I’ll only attract a whole swarm of flies.
There had been a time when I would have risked my life for Fame, but not anymore.
If anything, Fame now felt ominous.
Why does it feel like the higher my Fame gets, the stronger the people it attracts become?
My life’s motto was to live a quiet, long life. Of course, living large and long would be even better, but people who tried that rarely had peaceful lives.
Constantly fighting battles where my life hung in the balance had also left me exhausted in both body and mind.
I need to make at least the bare minimum of preparations.
I planned to make one hell of a spear from the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron and hone my martial arts. To do that, I absolutely needed Jin Wikyung’s help.
“Could you do me one favor?”
Jin Wikyung was not the sort of person to refuse. He nodded confidently.
“Say the word.”
“I need information.”
“Information? About what, exactly?”
“Two things. First, the whereabouts of a Master Artisan skilled enough to work with Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. Second, news about the Fire King.”
“The first is understandable, but the Fire King... Surely you aren’t thinking of learning that?”
That referred to the Flame Divine Palm.
I had never told Jin Wikyung directly, but he already knew everything.

It made sense. The Flame Divine Palm was the Fire King’s signature martial art, and touching it carelessly was no different from holding a bomb that could put the entire family at risk. I had already assumed Jin Mukyung would have reported it to Jin Wikyung, the Lesser Family Head, long ago.
“Taekyung.”
Hearing the concern in his voice, I waved a hand.
“I’m not planning to learn it right away. I just want to confirm whether the Fire King is alive or dead before I decide.”
“Hmm.”
After a brief silence, Jin Wikyung spoke.
“Will you promise me one thing? Before you do that, you’ll consult with me first.”
“Yes.”
“Then that’s settled.”
Jin Wikyung nodded decisively and rose from his seat.
“Information about the Fire King may take some time, but I can tell you about the first matter right now.”
Already? That was the Jin Family of Taiyuan for you. They seemed to have a handle on almost everything.
The progress was much faster than I had expected. My butt practically itched with impatience to go find the man immediately.
“He must be nearby?”
“Yes. He has been living in seclusion, hidden from everyone. Even our family only learned of his existence recently.”
“And his skill?”

sentences.text: System Status Window Lv.

71 Jin Taekyung Class: Peak Master Fame: 2,400 (+250) Titles: 5 (Title effects active) - Returnee (All stats +10) - Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi (All stats +15, Fame +200) - Scion of a Prestigious Family (All stats +5, Fame +50) - Gambler (Combat-related stats +10% in one-on-one combat) - Intermediate Trainee (Training speed +20%) Strength: 255 (+30) Stamina: 207 (+30) Agility: 250 (+30) Intelligence: 40 (+30) Charm: 40 (+30) Internal Energy: 45 years Toughness: 200 (+30) Remaining Points: 70 - Distribute your remaining points.
I checked my Status Window more than ten times a day, but it still made me grin every time.
Who knew the four characters meaning “Peak Master” could make me this happy?
The System calls me a master.
A Peak Master.
Only a few hours ago, the Class field had read First Rate Martial Artist.
But now I was a Peak Master.
Not just a martial artist, but a master.
I had become a genuine master, recognized even by the System.
And I’m already Level 71.
The rewards had been incredible.
Seven level-ups, a one-stage increase in both the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique and Qi Sense, and...
I even got something money couldn’t buy.
Open Inventory.
As soon as I entered the command in my mind, a familiar System notification chimed and a translucent holographic window appeared.
My Inventory was packed with all kinds of junk I had collected in the Murim, but my gaze went straight to one item.
Summon Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
Whoosh.
A heavy sphere suddenly popped into existence in midair.
It was about the size of a bowling ball, its unpolished surface rough and jagged, with lumps jutting out in every direction.
At first glance, it looked like nothing more than a useless lump of metal or rock.
But anyone who looked a little closer would recognize its true value.
Inspect Item.
Ding.

System Item Window Unprocessed Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron Type: Material Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: Master Artisan Description: Ten-thousand-year-old cold iron is harder, sharper, and rarer than any other mineral in existence.
Only a craftsman who has reached the level of Master Artisan will be able to work with this precious material.
“Now, this is the real deal.”
Personally, I was happier about obtaining the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron than I was about leveling up.
I was a Hunter and a martial artist.
Everyone in this line of work dreamed of owning great equipment.
I had simply never had the means to make that dream a reality.
I had no money in the real world, and in the Murim, I didn’t have a decent spear.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan’s roots lay in sword techniques, not spear techniques.
Supply followed demand.
Most of the family’s members, from its lowest-ranking martial artists to its leadership, were swordsmen.
Naturally, both the family’s martial arts and the weapons in its armory favored swords by a wide margin.
If Jin Wikyung hadn’t looked out for me, I might have ended up fighting with a cheap wooden or bamboo spear.
How many times had my guts twisted whenever I swung an iron spear while leaving the [Unnamed Sword], made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, at my side?
But that humiliation is over now.
I had obtained the finest mineral in the world.
Now I could have a weapon of my own made from it.
Of course, there was one prerequisite.
The Quest I had just received was related to that.
Inspect Quest.
Ding.
System Quest Find the Master Artisan Forging Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron requires tremendous experience and skill.
Only an exceptionally skilled artisan will be able to draw out the full power of this precious material.
Grade: Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Commission a Master Artisan to make a weapon (Incomplete) Reward: ???
Failure: ???
I smiled contentedly and closed the Quest Window.
Of course.
I can’t entrust something as valuable as Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron to just anyone.
Even without the Quest, I would have looked into it myself.
Just as a famed sword only revealed its true brilliance in the hands of a master, the same was true of a precious material like Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
Although the Quest was graded Peak, the mission itself didn’t seem particularly difficult.
Finding someone shouldn’t take long.
Surely there had to be at least one Master Artisan in this enormous land.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan had branches throughout Shanxi.
If I asked Jin Wikyung to send out word, we would soon know where to find one.
And if that doesn’t work, I can ask the Lower District Sect.
I even had a powerful connection in Wolhwa.
With eyes and ears planted throughout Shanxi Province, finding someone like that would be a piece of cake for her.
Whatever it takes, I’m completing this Quest before I leave.
A month in the Murim was only three hours in the modern world.
I still had plenty of time.
“Hehehe.
A spear made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
A spear made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron...”
Just as I was grinning from ear to ear—
Bang!
The door blew apart with a deafening crash.
Someone rushed in like lightning, charging toward me with both arms spread wide.
“Youngest!”
Yep.
I knew it would be you.
I let out a deep sigh and asked Jin Wikyung, “What’s going on?”
“What do you mean, what’s going on?
I heard the wonderful news that you broke through the wall and rushed here at once!”
“...How did you hear about that?”
It had only happened an hour or two ago, but the speed of the information network was no joke.
Had this guy attached a Familiar to me or something?
As I stared at him in bewilderment, I spotted Hyuk Mujin standing in front of the blown-open doorway with a proud smile.
He rubbed beneath his nose and said, “Shouldn’t such wonderful news be delivered first by one’s closest aide?”
Not a Familiar.
A Hyuk-miliar.
That bastard had definitely used my name to score points with Jin Wikyung.
“Waaah!
Our youngest broke through the wall!
He reached the Peak realm!”
Sure enough, Hyuk Mujin quickly cut in.
“Lesser Family Head, I stood guard over him!”
“Thank you.
Truly, thank you.
Your contribution was enormous!”
“Not at all.
As your right arm, I merely did what I was supposed to do.
I had not a shred of selfish intent.
However, I noticed that the position of Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion is still vacant...”
“It’s yours without question!
No, you’ll be the next Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan!”
“W-Whaaat?
Is that really true?”
Of course it wasn’t, you dumbass.
Did it make any sense to appoint someone Family Head just because he had stood guard?
Besides, all that bastard had actually done was snore.
But the two men, blinded by joy and power, were already out of their minds.
“Hyuk Mujin.
You said your name was Hyuk Mujin, right?”
“Yes, Lesser Family Head!”
“Our Mujin can do whatever he wants!
Become Family Head!
Smash the Nine Sects and One Gang!
Smash the world!”
“Smash!”
“...What are you smashing, you lunatics?”
The future of the Jin Family of Taiyuan looked bleak.
Once the commotion died down, Jin Wikyung finally managed to calm himself and looked at me with moist eyes.
“Your brother is proud of you.”
“I’m proud of you too, Captain.
But if I hadn’t stood guard over you...”
“Mujin, let’s keep quiet unless you want your pot cracked.
And by ‘pot,’ I mean your head.”
“Yes, sir.”
Hyuk Mujin, now sporting a lump on his forehead, answered at once.
As expected, he only listened after getting hit.
“Your useless older brother couldn’t even look after you properly, and yet you grew up so well all on your own.
Sniff.”
Look at this human weapon getting all sentimental.
Whenever Jin Wikyung acted like this, I was grateful that this world had no social media.
If it did, a post tagging every member of the Jin Family of Taiyuan would have gone up on Outstagram.
Complete with a teary-eyed selfie and hashtags.
\#JinFamilyofTaiyuan #UselessOlderBrother #OurYoungestIsAPeakMaster #KeepYourChinUpToday └ Wolhwa: Oh my!
Young Master Jin?

Congratulations! └ Cheongpung: Wow, I’ve never clicked Like before! └ Wipeng: Don’t lie. └ Hyuk Mujin: I stood guard over him. └ Jin Mukyung: Is this what you call a country? └ Zhu Bao: An autograph, please.
Imagining the reactions from countless Shanxi Province celebrities made my vision swim.
I hurriedly pushed the horrifying thought from my mind and tried to soothe Jin Wikyung.
“Please stop crying.
How old are you?”
“Sniff.
How did my immature youngest brother grow into such a fine man?”
Jin Wikyung gazed at me with a mixture of emotion and pride, then wiped the corners of his eyes with his sleeve.
“No, this won’t do.
I need to go right now and...”
“You’re not planning to write ‘Jin Taekyung has become a Peak Master’ on a gigantic banner like last time, are you?”
“Gasp.”
I knew it.
Judging by everything Jin Wikyung had done until now, there was no way he would let this opportunity pass.
I had to make myself perfectly clear.
“Don’t do anything like that.
It’s cringe.”
“Cringe?
What does that mean?”
“It means embarrassing.”
Jin Wikyung looked shocked.
“Are you saying you’re embarrassed by me?
By your own brother?”
“No, that’s not what I...”
This was driving me insane.
Before I could answer, Hyuk Mujin, who had been sitting quietly with his shoulders hunched, suddenly cut in with a baffled look.
“Huh?
Captain, you usually like getting attention.”
“When have I ever?”
“You don’t?
If I remember correctly, you seemed to love it.
When we returned from the Mount Heng Sword Sect, you stood at the very front and waved like crazy.”
“...Ahem.”
If he had made that up, I would have punched him.
But it was true, so I had nothing to say.
I quietly avoided Hyuk Mujin’s gaze and replied, “That was different.
I had my reasons.”
“What reasons?”
“There were reasons.
You don’t need to know.”
“Wow, there he goes again.”
I ignored Hyuk Mujin’s muttering and turned back to Jin Wikyung.
“Anyway, we’re not doing anything like that.
The attention I’m getting now is more than enough.”
“Hmm.
If that’s truly what you want...”
Jin Wikyung couldn’t hide his disappointment, but I was so firm that he reluctantly nodded.
That let me breathe a sigh of relief.
What’s the point of advertising that I became a Peak Master?
I’ll only attract a whole swarm of flies.
There had been a time when I would have risked my life for Fame, but not anymore.
If anything, Fame now felt ominous.
Why does it feel like the higher my Fame gets, the stronger the people it attracts become?
My life’s motto was to live a quiet, long life.

Constantly fighting battles where my life hung in the balance had also left me exhausted in both body and mind.
I need to make at least the bare minimum of preparations.

Already?
