paragraphs: Knock, knock, knock.
The information I had asked Jin Wikyung for arrived sooner than expected.
What surprised me was the identity of the messenger.
“Huh? What brings you here?”
“My lord said he had a letter that needed delivering, so I came.”
“You came personally?”
The man who had come to deliver Jin Wikyung’s letter was none other than Wipeng.
He stared silently at me for a while before tossing out a single remark.
“So it was true. You really crossed the wall.”
From a low hill, one could not see what lay atop a high peak. But someone standing on that peak could see everything below.
The same was true of Wipeng now.
An accomplished Peak master himself, he recognized the change in me at a glance. He regarded me with a mixture of awe and disbelief.
“How is such a thing possible?”
What was I supposed to say to that?
Most people believed the ridiculous rumors about me without question, but Wipeng was different.
Along with the brothers of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, he was one of the very few people who knew the truth.
It really is absurd.
A Third Rate thug had become a Peak master in only two or three months.
Even the most open-minded person would find that impossible to comprehend. Perhaps that was precisely why people believed the rumors.
Because those actually sound more plausible.
When I hesitated, unable to answer, Wipeng waved a hand. He was probably mindful of Hyuk Mujin listening beside us as well.
“We should save that discussion for another time.”
Still looking troubled, Wipeng pulled a letter from inside his robes. It contained the information I had asked Jin Wikyung to find.
As I accepted and unfolded it, Wipeng began to explain.
“His name is Jang Taebo. Until a little over ten years ago, he belonged to the Ironcraft Guild.”
“The Ironcraft Guild?”
“It is a guild based in Hubei. Most of its members are skilled craftsmen rather than martial artists.”
In other words, it was a blacksmiths’ guild.
I asked the most important question.
“How skilled is he?”
“He was the Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild.”
“Oh.”
That brief answer told me everything I needed to know.
If he had risen to become Guild Leader in the Ironcraft Guild, which was packed with skilled craftsmen, then he was practically a Master Artisan already.
I carefully read through the information about Jang Taebo.
“He lives fairly close by, too?”
“In a village near Jeongyang. Do you remember? The place where we received Prince Shangshan’s invitation...”
“Oh, there.”
Had it been about fifteen days ago? That was where I had marched with the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s elites like a victorious general.
Hyuk Mujin, who had been listening quietly beside us, spoke up.
“If we don’t slacken the reins, we should arrive around sunset.”
“Right?”
“Yes.”
“So what are you still doing here?”
“...What?”
“Go get ready to leave. Set aside two strong horses and pack some food for the road.”
“Wait, what... Am I a servant?”
“There’s no high or low in honest work. Are you looking down on servants now? Should I call every servant in the Jin Family of Taiyuan and give you a lecture?”
“Oh, fine! I get it, so stop already!”
Unable to endure my nagging any longer, Hyuk Mujin grumbled his way out of the room. Wipeng clicked his tongue.
“Your subordinate’s attitude is terribly insolent.”
Well, from where I was standing, he wasn’t exactly one to talk.
The way you constantly hounded people to work whenever you had the chance was enough to make even a mother-in-law slap someone across the face with a bundle of kimchi.
Look at this hypocrite.
Oblivious to my thoughts, Wipeng continued.
“In any case, you must return by noon tomorrow at the latest. You have not forgotten that New Year’s Day is in two days, have you?”
“Ah, right.”
The entire Jin Family of Taiyuan was already in an uproar over it. I had nearly grown used to the sight of servants and maids rushing around in a frenzy.
That was only natural. This was a grand banquet that would last at least three days, not some event that would end in a single day.
It is a pretty big deal.
It was an occasion to reaffirm the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s position as the ruler of Shanxi Province.
With so many guests arriving, everyone in the family was working day and night to ensure that nothing went wrong.
Everyone except me, of course.
“Do you really think I’ll be late? It’s only half a day away at most.”
Wipeng’s eyes narrowed.
“This is an important occasion, so I trust you will conduct yourself appropriately.”
“Your eyes say you don’t trust me at all.”
“That is a misunderstanding. A misunderstanding.”
“I’m just going to ask him for one favor and come straight back, so don’t worry.”
“Given the Third Young Master’s track record, I cannot help but worry.”
Trouble did seem to follow me wherever I went, so he wasn’t entirely wrong.
But I was a full-fledged Peak master now. I was far too grown-up to be treated like a little kid playing by the water.
“Even if I look like this—”
“I trust you were not about to say, ‘I’m a Peak master now, so stop treating me like a child by the water.’”
Was he a ghost or something? I hurriedly swallowed the rest of my words.
“Of course not.”

“In Murim, no one knows what awaits them even a single step ahead. And be respectful toward Jang Taebo—Guild Leader Jang. The Ironcraft Guild has close ties with the Nine Sects and One Gang, and its current Guild Leader is Jang Taebo’s Disciple. It would be unwise to offend him.”
“My hobby is filial piety, and my specialty is respecting the elderly.”
“I can still vividly recall the Third Young Master hurling every imaginable obscenity at the Head Elder.”
“Hey, that was different!”
“Of course. I was merely pointing it out. Why are you getting so angry? Do you think I’m a pushover now that you’re a Peak master?”
Look at those eyes. He looked ready to challenge me to a duel.
Of course, if we actually fought, I would still be the one getting beaten. I casually changed the subject.
“But aren’t you busy? You must have a lot of work piled up.”
Wipeng frowned.
“I do need to return as soon as possible. There has been suspicious activity near Datong.”
“Datong... the northern Gaoyuan?”
“I hear the mounted bandits are prowling around again.”
“How long has it even been since the Red Wind Band was crushed?”
“Precisely.”
Rubbing his dry eyes, Wipeng rose from his seat.
“Then I will be going. I suppose we will see each other again at noon tomorrow.”
Wipeng placed pointed emphasis on noon tomorrow right to the end. He was about to leave when he suddenly stopped.
“And there is something I have been meaning to ask...”
“Yes?”
Looking utterly bewildered, Wipeng pointed at the badly mangled door.
“What happened to this? It can’t have been more than a few days since it was completed.”
“Who do you think did it?”
The same person you, I, and everyone else would suspect, of course.
Wipeng appeared to realize who the culprit was. He let out a long sigh and left the room. Judging by the murderous set of his shoulders, he was clearly going to lay into Jin Wikyung.
“Well, I should get going too.”
I was on my way to have my own custom weapon made. My steps felt light enough to fly.
“Are you ready?”
In front of the stables, Hyuk Mujin was inspecting the saddles. He answered curtly.
“Not yet.”
“Still?”
“Yes.”
What was taking him so long?
When I approached, I saw the horse’s flanks were covered in bundles. One sniff told me they were all filled with food. They were still warm, as though they had only recently been cooked.
“What’s all this?”
“What do you think? Food.”
“You think I’m asking because I don’t know that? Huh? Why did you pack so much? Some jerky and water would’ve been enough.”
Hyuk Mujin gave me a wounded look.
“I didn’t pack it.”
“If you didn’t, who did?”
“Who do you think?”
Hyuk Mujin pointed behind me. A young man came racing toward us, weighed down by bundle after bundle.
The moment Cheongpung spotted me, his face lit up.
“Oh! Hello, Benefactor!”
“Ah... hello.”
Sure, hello. But why are you here?
I turned a demanding look on Hyuk Mujin, and he began to explain.
“I ran into him on the way to the stables. He said he wanted to come along. What was I supposed to do?”
Cheongpung shouted enthusiastically.
“Benefactor! Take me with you! I want to go on a trip too!”
“This isn’t a trip.”
“Oh, really? I heard we were leaving today and coming back tomorrow...”
Did going somewhere today and returning tomorrow automatically make it a trip?
When I explained that I was going to meet a blacksmith in Jeongyang, Cheongpung’s eyes lit up.
“Wow! A blacksmith!”
Hyuk Mujin and I spoke at the same time.
“You’ve never seen a blacksmith before, have you?”
“This must be your first time seeing a blacksmith.”
“Yes, that’s right! How did you know?”
It was more surprising that he didn’t know.
Anyone who had spent even a single day with Cheongpung would understand exactly how I felt.
“Anyway, please take me with you.”
“Well, I don’t mind if you come along, but...”
“Wow!”
“Let people finish speaking, you idiot.”
Ugh, this was exhausting. Was this what extrovert energy felt like?
Already feeling tired, I leaped onto my saddle. I also made sure to remove the securely tied food bundles ahead of time.
One dropped to the ground with a thud, and Cheongpung screamed.
“Ah! That’s five-spice pork!”
“Why did you pack five-spice pork? I told you we’d be back soon!”
“No! My five-spice pork!”
“...Fuck.”
It wasn’t even mine.
Cheongpung insisted on gathering every last bundle, then grinned.
“Now let’s go!”
I really do want to go. Just without you.
Clicking my tongue inwardly, I took hold of the reins and set off.
Then I had to listen to him chewing behind me until the sun went down.
Winter days were short.
As the sun vanished beyond the plateau’s horizon, a dry voice slipped between the huge man’s lips.
“It is time.”
No sooner had he finished speaking than hundreds of silhouettes stirred in the darkness.
Draped in the hides of all manner of beasts, they mounted their horses, armed with curved sabers, sandalwood bows, and lances.
Within moments, a cavalry force of some four hundred riders had formed before the huge man. His parched voice rang out once more.
“Our task is simple.”
His eyes gleamed dangerously. The veins bulging along his forearms and the breath steaming from his lips made him look like a wild beast.
“To kill and trample.”
Low laughter rose here and there.
Their leader had given them permission to run wild. The roughly four hundred mounted bandits of the Heavenly Wind Band trembled with excitement.
The sight brought a satisfied smile to the huge man’s face.
At last, I can do this properly.
The plan devised by his sworn elder brother, Black Sand, was brilliant.
Of course, what he liked most was that he only had to slaughter and plunder the enemies before him without thinking.
His role was the most important—and the simplest.
My blood is boiling.
These men were nothing like the ragtag forces of the Red Wind Band and the other dregs they had scraped together from far and wide.
They had eaten from the same pot and fought side by side for over a decade. They were seasoned elites, veterans of a hundred battles.
Heh heh. Just wait. Jin Family of Taiyuan or not, I’ll trample every last one of you.
A thunderous roar erupted from the Heavenly Wind Band Leader’s mouth.
“Go! Kill and plunder them all! Slaughter and burn everything in sight!”
“Waaaaah!”
“Let’s go!”
The roughly four hundred mounted bandits, wild with excitement, had just turned their horses south when—
“You goddamn sons of bitches. What the hell do you think you’re burning?”
A diminutive figure emerged with a sharp, ringing voice.
The unidentified old man’s hand shone a blinding white.

Most people believed the ridiculous rumors about me without question, but Wipeng was different.
Along with the brothers of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, he was one of the very few people who knew the truth.
It really is absurd.
A Third Rate thug had become a Peak master in only two or three months.
Even the most open-minded person would find that impossible to comprehend.
Perhaps that was precisely why people believed the rumors.
Because those actually sound more plausible.
When I hesitated, unable to answer, Wipeng waved a hand.
He was probably mindful of Hyuk Mujin listening beside us as well.
“We should save that discussion for another time.”
Still looking troubled, Wipeng pulled a letter from inside his robes.
It contained the information I had asked Jin Wikyung to find.
As I accepted and unfolded it, Wipeng began to explain.
“His name is Jang Taebo.
Until a little over ten years ago, he belonged to the Ironcraft Guild.”
“The Ironcraft Guild?”
“It is a guild based in Hubei.
Most of its members are skilled craftsmen rather than martial artists.”
In other words, it was a blacksmiths’ guild.
I asked the most important question.
“How skilled is he?”
“He was the Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild.”
“Oh.”
That brief answer told me everything I needed to know.
If he had risen to become Guild Leader in the Ironcraft Guild, which was packed with skilled craftsmen, then he was practically a Master Artisan already.
I carefully read through the information about Jang Taebo.
“He lives fairly close by, too?”
“In a village near Jeongyang.
Do you remember?
The place where we received Prince Shangshan’s invitation...”
“Oh, there.”
Had it been about fifteen days ago?
That was where I had marched with the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s elites like a victorious general.
Hyuk Mujin, who had been listening quietly beside us, spoke up.
“If we don’t slacken the reins, we should arrive around sunset.”
“Right?”
“Yes.”
“So what are you still doing here?”
“...What?”
“Go get ready to leave.
Set aside two strong horses and pack some food for the road.”
“Wait, what...
Am I a servant?”
“There’s no high or low in honest work.
Are you looking down on servants now?
Should I call every servant in the Jin Family of Taiyuan and give you a lecture?”
“Oh, fine!
I get it, so stop already!”
Unable to endure my nagging any longer, Hyuk Mujin grumbled his way out of the room.
Wipeng clicked his tongue.
“Your subordinate’s attitude is terribly insolent.”
Well, from where I was standing, he wasn’t exactly one to talk.
The way you constantly hounded people to work whenever you had the chance was enough to make even a mother-in-law slap someone across the face with a bundle of kimchi.
Look at this hypocrite.
Oblivious to my thoughts, Wipeng continued.
“In any case, you must return by noon tomorrow at the latest.
You have not forgotten that New Year’s Day is in two days, have you?”
“Ah, right.”
The entire Jin Family of Taiyuan was already in an uproar over it.
I had nearly grown used to the sight of servants and maids rushing around in a frenzy.
That was only natural.
This was a grand banquet that would last at least three days, not some event that would end in a single day.
It is a pretty big deal.
It was an occasion to reaffirm the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s position as the ruler of Shanxi Province.
With so many guests arriving, everyone in the family was working day and night to ensure that nothing went wrong.
Everyone except me, of course.
“Do you really think I’ll be late?
It’s only half a day away at most.”
Wipeng’s eyes narrowed.
“This is an important occasion, so I trust you will conduct yourself appropriately.”
“Your eyes say you don’t trust me at all.”
“That is a misunderstanding.
A misunderstanding.”
“I’m just going to ask him for one favor and come straight back, so don’t worry.”
“Given the Third Young Master’s track record, I cannot help but worry.”
Trouble did seem to follow me wherever I went, so he wasn’t entirely wrong.
But I was a full-fledged Peak master now.
I was far too grown-up to be treated like a little kid playing by the water.
“Even if I look like this—”
“I trust you were not about to say, ‘I’m a Peak master now, so stop treating me like a child by the water.’”
Was he a ghost or something?
I hurriedly swallowed the rest of my words.
“Of course not.”
“In Murim, no one knows what awaits them even a single step ahead.
And be respectful toward Jang Taebo—Guild Leader Jang.
The Ironcraft Guild has close ties with the Nine Sects and One Gang, and its current Guild Leader is Jang Taebo’s Disciple.
It would be unwise to offend him.”
“My hobby is filial piety, and my specialty is respecting the elderly.”
“I can still vividly recall the Third Young Master hurling every imaginable obscenity at the Head Elder.”
“Hey, that was different!”
“Of course.
I was merely pointing it out.
Why are you getting so angry?
Do you think I’m a pushover now that you’re a Peak master?”
Look at those eyes.
He looked ready to challenge me to a duel.
Of course, if we actually fought, I would still be the one getting beaten.
I casually changed the subject.
“But aren’t you busy?
You must have a lot of work piled up.”
Wipeng frowned.
“I do need to return as soon as possible.
There has been suspicious activity near Datong.”
“Datong... the northern Gaoyuan?”
“I hear the mounted bandits are prowling around again.”
“How long has it even been since the Red Wind Band was crushed?”
“Precisely.”
Rubbing his dry eyes, Wipeng rose from his seat.
“Then I will be going.
I suppose we will see each other again at noon tomorrow.”
Wipeng placed pointed emphasis on noon tomorrow right to the end.
He was about to leave when he suddenly stopped.
“And there is something I have been meaning to ask...”
“Yes?”
Looking utterly bewildered, Wipeng pointed at the badly mangled door.
“What happened to this?
It can’t have been more than a few days since it was completed.”
“Who do you think did it?”
The same person you, I, and everyone else would suspect, of course.
Wipeng appeared to realize who the culprit was.
He let out a long sigh and left the room.
Judging by the murderous set of his shoulders, he was clearly going to lay into Jin Wikyung.
“Well, I should get going too.”
I was on my way to have my own custom weapon made.
My steps felt light enough to fly.
“Are you ready?”
In front of the stables, Hyuk Mujin was inspecting the saddles.
He answered curtly.
“Not yet.”
“Still?”
“Yes.”
What was taking him so long?
When I approached, I saw the horse’s flanks were covered in bundles.
One sniff told me they were all filled with food.
They were still warm, as though they had only recently been cooked.
“What’s all this?”
“What do you think?
Food.”
“You think I’m asking because I don’t know that?
Huh?
Why did you pack so much?
Some jerky and water would’ve been enough.”
Hyuk Mujin gave me a wounded look.
“I didn’t pack it.”
“If you didn’t, who did?”
“Who do you think?”
Hyuk Mujin pointed behind me.
A young man came racing toward us, weighed down by bundle after bundle.
The moment Cheongpung spotted me, his face lit up.
“Oh!
Hello, Benefactor!”
“Ah... hello.”
Sure, hello.
But why are you here?
I turned a demanding look on Hyuk Mujin, and he began to explain.
“I ran into him on the way to the stables.
He said he wanted to come along.
What was I supposed to do?”
Cheongpung shouted enthusiastically.
“Benefactor!
Take me with you!
I want to go on a trip too!”
“This isn’t a trip.”
“Oh, really?
I heard we were leaving today and coming back tomorrow...”
Did going somewhere today and returning tomorrow automatically make it a trip?
When I explained that I was going to meet a blacksmith in Jeongyang, Cheongpung’s eyes lit up.
“Wow!
A blacksmith!”
Hyuk Mujin and I spoke at the same time.
“You’ve never seen a blacksmith before, have you?”
“This must be your first time seeing a blacksmith.”
“Yes, that’s right!
How did you know?”
It was more surprising that he didn’t know.
Anyone who had spent even a single day with Cheongpung would understand exactly how I felt.
“Anyway, please take me with you.”
“Well, I don’t mind if you come along, but...”
“Wow!”
“Let people finish speaking, you idiot.”
Ugh, this was exhausting.
Was this what extrovert energy felt like?
Already feeling tired, I leaped onto my saddle.
I also made sure to remove the securely tied food bundles ahead of time.
One dropped to the ground with a thud, and Cheongpung screamed.
“Ah!
That’s five-spice pork!”
“Why did you pack five-spice pork?
I told you we’d be back soon!”
“No!
My five-spice pork!”
“...Fuck.”
It wasn’t even mine.
Cheongpung insisted on gathering every last bundle, then grinned.
“Now let’s go!”
I really do want to go.
Just without you.
Clicking my tongue inwardly, I took hold of the reins and set off.
Then I had to listen to him chewing behind me until the sun went down.
Winter days were short.
As the sun vanished beyond the plateau’s horizon, a dry voice slipped between the huge man’s lips.
“It is time.”
No sooner had he finished speaking than hundreds of silhouettes stirred in the darkness.
Draped in the hides of all manner of beasts, they mounted their horses, armed with curved sabers, sandalwood bows, and lances.
Within moments, a cavalry force of some four hundred riders had formed before the huge man.
His parched voice rang out once more.
“Our task is simple.”
His eyes gleamed dangerously.
The veins bulging along his forearms and the breath steaming from his lips made him look like a wild beast.
“To kill and trample.”
Low laughter rose here and there.
Their leader had given them permission to run wild.
The roughly four hundred mounted bandits of the Heavenly Wind Band trembled with excitement.
The sight brought a satisfied smile to the huge man’s face.
At last, I can do this properly.
The plan devised by his sworn elder brother, Black Sand, was brilliant.
Of course, what he liked most was that he only had to slaughter and plunder the enemies before him without thinking.
His role was the most important—and the simplest.
My blood is boiling.
These men were nothing like the ragtag forces of the Red Wind Band and the other dregs they had scraped together from far and wide.
They had eaten from the same pot and fought side by side for over a decade.
They were seasoned elites, veterans of a hundred battles.
Heh heh.
Just wait.
Jin Family of Taiyuan or not, I’ll trample every last one of you.
A thunderous roar erupted from the Heavenly Wind Band Leader’s mouth.
“Go!
Kill and plunder them all!
Slaughter and burn everything in sight!”
“Waaaaah!”
“Let’s go!”
The roughly four hundred mounted bandits, wild with excitement, had just turned their horses south when—
“You goddamn sons of bitches.
What the hell do you think you’re burning?”
A diminutive figure emerged with a sharp, ringing voice.
The unidentified old man’s hand shone a blinding white.

chapters.title: Chapter 166
paragraphs: Old Man Jang’s daily routine was simple: eat, sleep, and shit.
Every now and then, he visited a pleasure house or an inn for a drink, or sat in on a gambling game and played dominoes, but he spent most of his time at home.
By now, the villagers had grown accustomed to him. They would sometimes ask,
“Don’t you get lonely?”
But Old Man Jang’s answer was always firm.
“Don’t talk nonsense.”
People whispered that the solitary old man only said that out of pride, but he meant every word.
Life couldn’t be more comfortable.
He slept when he was tired, ate when he was hungry, and shit when he needed to.
Some might mock him for living like a beast, but Old Man Jang had more than earned the right.
No—he felt even that was insufficient.
After the life I’ve lived.
He had spent an entire jiazi before vats of boiling molten iron.
Once he started something, he had to see it through to the end. He had forgotten people and love alike. The anvil and hammer had been his friends and lovers.
I lived like a man possessed.
Then one day, he came to his senses and found that his hair had turned white and his vision had grown dim.
He had become one of the finest smiths under heaven and the Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild, but that was all.
No matter how many times he brought down his hammer, he could not fill the emptiness in his heart.
In the end, he decided to retire. And so Jang Taebo, the Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild, became Old Man Jang.
“Grandpa!”
“Uh, hm?”
Old Man Jang jerked out of his reverie. He had been squatting in the yard, staring blankly into space.
A little boy from the neighboring house was looking at him with enormous eyes.
“What are you thinking about?”
“I was thinking that if you used polite speech, I might give you a piece of candy.”
“What are you thinking about, Grandpa?”
“...What a sly little brat. Here.”
“Tank you!”
Old Man Jang watched the boy busily suck on the candy.

He had known the child since he was a newborn. At first, the boy had been a nuisance, constantly clinging to him and calling him Grandpa. Then, at some point, Old Man Jang had found himself carrying snacks around for him.
Well, this isn’t so bad either.
For a blunt and prickly old man like him, the boy was his only real conversation partner.
Looking at the child sometimes made him wonder what it might have been like to have a family of his own.
“Would you like another one?”
“Yeah, yeah!”
“Ahem. Polite speech.”
“Yes!”
“Eat them slowly so you don’t ruin your teeth. Understand?”
“Yeah!”
“...That polite speech didn’t last long.”
After licking two pieces of candy clean in the blink of an eye, the boy suddenly spoke.
“Oh, right. Grandpa.”
“What is it?”
“What’s your name?”
“You should ask an elder’s name more respectfully... No, never mind. Why do you suddenly want to know?”
“Hmm, I was just curious.”
“Hmm.”
“I asked Mom and Dad too, but they said they didn’t know your name. Nobody knows.”
Though he had settled here more than ten years ago, Old Man Jang had never revealed his name to anyone.
He had been worried that flies might start buzzing around him. No—mere flies would have been a blessing.

Skilled smiths were needed everywhere, especially by Murim sects whose members would stake their lives on their weapons. If his identity became known, his remaining years would be anything but peaceful.
“Grandpa, aren’t you going to tell me?”
Old Man Jang looked into the boy’s large, innocent eyes.
Well, it should be safe to tell him a little.
He was too young to understand what any of it meant. Besides, a few more pieces of candy would distract him, and he would soon forget.
Old Man Jang only had to conceal enough to keep his identity hidden.
“I’ll tell you one character of my name. It’s Bo.”
“Your family name is Jang, so... are you Jang Bo?”
“No. I said my name ends in Bo.”
“What’s the other character?”
“Curious, are you?”
“Yeah!”
“Fine. Use polite speech properly for the next month, and I’ll think about telling you.”
“Wow, that’s mean.”
Old Man Jang let out a quiet laugh as the boy puffed out his cheeks.
“Hng. Can’t you just tell me? I need to know so I can eat something tasty.”
“Whew. I guess it can’t be helped.”
What was that supposed to mean?
As Old Man Jang wondered, the boy heaved a sigh like an old man and sprang to his feet.
“Where are you going?”
“I’ll come back later!”
“Don’t bother. The sun’s already down, you brat. Go home and sleep!”
“I don’t want to!”
For someone with such short legs, the boy had boundless energy. He quickly disappeared in the opposite direction from his house.
“That boy never listens.”
Muttering under his breath, Old Man Jang hauled his stiff body upright.
Until about ten years ago, he had still been able to manage well enough. But once he began losing muscle, his joints started aching all over.
“Good grief. I’d better warm up the room.”
He fed firewood into the firebox and lit the brazier.
After puttering around for a while, he stepped outside to use the privy before bed.
That was when—
“Grandpa!”
The boy’s innocent cry rang out.
But Old Man Jang did not hear it.
His seasoned gaze was fixed on the three large men standing behind the child.
Martial artists?
The sun had already set, leaving their faces hidden in darkness, but he could clearly make out the sword sheaths protruding from their waists.
He had made countless such objects himself.
Without taking his eyes off the men, Old Man Jang beckoned to the boy.
“Hanga, come here.”
“Yeah!”
Now that he looked, the boy was clutching a large bundle to his chest. It radiated warmth and gave off an appetizing smell.
Having roughly grasped the situation, Old Man Jang glared at the figures in the darkness.
“Who are you?”
A spark snapped in the darkness, then flared to life. The fire starter in someone’s hand illuminated the three men’s faces.
They were all young men around twenty. One stepped forward.
“My goodness. Good evening.”
He had a handsome face and a sly smile.
Old Man Jang studied the vaguely familiar face before speaking.
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
He had seen that face from a distance about half a month ago.
The young man, Jin Taekyung, broke into a wide grin.
“Oh, you know the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. That’s me. Hahaha.”
“An old man named Jang?”
“Yes. I was told he definitely lived in this village.”
“Well, there are so many of them. There must be twenty old men with the family name Jang.”
“He’s around eighty...”
“They all suffered when they were young, so they’ve all aged about the same. Mr. Jang next door is fifty, but he looks a hundred and fifty.”
“Anyway, they’re all like that.”
“Um, he lives alone, and his name is...”
“Who bothers remembering everyone’s name? Once they get old, they’re all just Old Man Jang. Plenty of people live alone too. War, drought, epidemics... Whew.”
Damn it. We had arrived before sunset, only to run into trouble immediately.
I had wondered why such a tiny village had so many old men named Jang. It turned out to be a clan village. Half the people we passed on the road had the family name Jang.
“Do you know where he lives?”
As Hyuk Mujin grew frustrated, I waved the letter containing the information in front of him.
“No. It only says he lives here. I guess they thought we’d find him quickly since it’s a small village.”
Cheongpung pulled some meat from his bundle and began tearing into it.
“Chomp, chomp, chomp.”
“Then how are we supposed to find him? Jang is already a common family name.”
“We’ll have to find out for ourselves. There are only a few hundred people here, and he’s an old man, so we should locate him quickly.”
“Chomp, chomp, chomp.”
That bastard Cheongpung had done nothing but eat this whole time.
Then again, maybe that could work in my favor. I was just about to give up and ask him for a piece of meat when—
“Oh, the grandpa who lives three houses down from us is a Jang too.”
The speaker was a little boy whose head barely reached my waist. With his enormous eyes, he was pretty cute.
I ruffled his shaggy hair.
“Really?”
“Yeah. He’s Grandpa Jang.”
“Really?”

I played along, though I wasn’t expecting much. The woman selling vegetables at the roadside stall was a Jang, and so was the butcher over there. In a clan village crawling with Jangs, what were the odds?
The boy sniffed and continued.
“Grandpa is always alone. He doesn’t have a family, so I go play with him.”
“Oh, you little rascal. That’s kind of you—wait. He doesn’t have a family?”
“Yeah! I asked Mom, and she said he’d been alone ever since he first came here.”
“Since he first came here? He isn’t originally from this village?”
The boy nodded vigorously.
“My dad told me Grandpa came from somewhere else. Since he came from outside, he doesn’t have any friends or family.”
“I see.”
Hyuk Mujin and I exchanged glances. This sounded promising, but it was hardly conclusive.
“Little one, do you know his name?”
“Do you know anything else about him?”
“I don’t know his name. He’s just Grandpa Jang.”
It seemed that was all the boy knew. Hyuk Mujin asked with an eerily kind smile,
“Little one, could you tell us where he lives?”
“Waaay over there. At the edge of the village.”
As expected of the continent. This damn village was absurdly large for its population.
Hyuk Mujin roughly gauged the distance before turning to me.
“It’ll take about fifteen minutes.”
Even on horseback, it would take that long. I shook my head.
“What if he isn’t the one? Let’s search nearby first and work our way over there.”
“Yes, that’s probably better. Aside from the fact that he came from elsewhere, there’s nothing that really marks him as the man we’re looking for.”
Cheongpung nodded.
“Chomp. Chomp. Chomp.”
While I wondered whether I should simply hurl away that food bundle, the boy boldly held out both his little hands toward Cheongpung.
“Hmm?”
“Grandpa Jang said there’s no such thing as a favor without a price.”
The kid already understood how the world worked.
He had given us information, so now he wanted a bite in return. That Grandpa Jang or whatever his name was sure had taught a fine lesson to a child of five or six.
“Wow, my grandfather said something similar. Here.”
“Wow! Thank you!”
Look at them, united under the banner of grandfathers.
Cheongpung casually handed him a large leg of meat. He had been periodically warming the food with the Zaha Divine Technique, which was based on Scorching Yang Qi, so the meat was still hot.
He’s using the Zaha Divine Technique to heat meat?
The boy happily tore into the meat, then looked at us with naked longing in his eyes.
“By the way, I need to go home anyway. And on the way back, I’m going to visit Grandpa Jang three houses down.”
“Oh, really?”
I immediately understood what he meant. When you were desperate, you would borrow even a cat’s paw. Why not a child’s?
“Then could you ask Grandpa Jang his name? Meet us back here in half a shichen.”
“Hmm. I think I’ll be even hungrier by then.”
“See those food bundles? I’ll give you a whole one.”
“Really?”
The boy’s eyes lit up, but then he hesitated.
“Why are you looking for Grandpa Jang?”
“It’s nothing serious. We just have a favor to ask him.”
“You’re not bad people, are you?”
Introducing myself as the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi from the Jin Family of Taiyuan would only draw a crowd. I gave him my most innocent smile.
“Of course not.”
“Ugh. Why are you smiling like such a bad person?”
Should I just smack him on the head and send him away?
Hyuk Mujin stepped in on my behalf.
“I’ll give you two bundles.”
“So you were good people after all. I’ll be back!”
The child was already becoming a monster born of capitalism.
Hyuk Mujin shrugged.
“Where should we start looking?”
“Search everything from the nearest entrance onward.”
“That’ll take half a shichen.”
Hyuk Mujin was wrong. It took us more than half a shichen to search half the village.
Then the boy returned with an extremely valuable clue.
If his name starts with Jang and ends with Bo...
The former Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild, Jang Taebo.
That had to be him.
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
“Oh, you know the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. That’s me. Hahaha.”
The fact that he knew who I was was a good sign. It felt strange to say this about myself, but wasn’t the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi practically Shanxi Province’s idol?
If this world had internet access, I would already have a fan club.
“I’m sorry to visit so late at night. The thing is, I have a favor to ask...”
“There’s no need.”
“Pardon?”
Jang Taebo was over eighty, but he still had a sturdy build. He fixed me with a cantankerous stare.
“I won’t accept the commission anyway.”
“Still, you should at least hear what it is...”
“No!”
Well, that was decisive.

“Good grief.
I’d better warm up the room.”
He fed firewood into the firebox and lit the brazier.
After puttering around for a while, he stepped outside to use the privy before bed.
That was when—
“Grandpa!”
The boy’s innocent cry rang out.
But Old Man Jang did not hear it.
His seasoned gaze was fixed on the three large men standing behind the child.
Martial artists?
The sun had already set, leaving their faces hidden in darkness, but he could clearly make out the sword sheaths protruding from their waists.
He had made countless such objects himself.
Without taking his eyes off the men, Old Man Jang beckoned to the boy.
“Hanga, come here.”
“Yeah!”
Now that he looked, the boy was clutching a large bundle to his chest.
It radiated warmth and gave off an appetizing smell.
Having roughly grasped the situation, Old Man Jang glared at the figures in the darkness.
“Who are you?”
A spark snapped in the darkness, then flared to life.
The fire starter in someone’s hand illuminated the three men’s faces.
They were all young men around twenty.
One stepped forward.
“My goodness.
Good evening.”
He had a handsome face and a sly smile.
Old Man Jang studied the vaguely familiar face before speaking.
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
He had seen that face from a distance about half a month ago.
The young man, Jin Taekyung, broke into a wide grin.
“Oh, you know the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
That’s me.
Hahaha.”
“An old man named Jang?”
“Yes.
I was told he definitely lived in this village.”
“Well, there are so many of them.
There must be twenty old men with the family name Jang.”
“He’s around eighty...”
“They all suffered when they were young, so they’ve all aged about the same.
Mr.
Jang next door is fifty, but he looks a hundred and fifty.”
“Anyway, they’re all like that.”
“Um, he lives alone, and his name is...”
“Who bothers remembering everyone’s name?
Once they get old, they’re all just Old Man Jang.
Plenty of people live alone too.
War, drought, epidemics...
Whew.”
Damn it.
We had arrived before sunset, only to run into trouble immediately.
I had wondered why such a tiny village had so many old men named Jang.
It turned out to be a clan village.
Half the people we passed on the road had the family name Jang.
“Do you know where he lives?”
As Hyuk Mujin grew frustrated, I waved the letter containing the information in front of him.
“No.
It only says he lives here.
I guess they thought we’d find him quickly since it’s a small village.”
Cheongpung pulled some meat from his bundle and began tearing into it.
“Chomp, chomp, chomp.”
“Then how are we supposed to find him?
Jang is already a common family name.”
“We’ll have to find out for ourselves.
There are only a few hundred people here, and he’s an old man, so we should locate him quickly.”
“Chomp, chomp, chomp.”
That bastard Cheongpung had done nothing but eat this whole time.
Then again, maybe that could work in my favor.
I was just about to give up and ask him for a piece of meat when—
“Oh, the grandpa who lives three houses down from us is a Jang too.”
The speaker was a little boy whose head barely reached my waist.
With his enormous eyes, he was pretty cute.
I ruffled his shaggy hair.
“Really?”
“Yeah.
He’s Grandpa Jang.”
“Really?”
I played along, though I wasn’t expecting much.
The woman selling vegetables at the roadside stall was a Jang, and so was the butcher over there.
In a clan village crawling with Jangs, what were the odds?
The boy sniffed and continued.
“Grandpa is always alone.
He doesn’t have a family, so I go play with him.”
“Oh, you little rascal.
That’s kind of you—wait.
He doesn’t have a family?”
“Yeah!
I asked Mom, and she said he’d been alone ever since he first came here.”
“Since he first came here?
He isn’t originally from this village?”
The boy nodded vigorously.
“My dad told me Grandpa came from somewhere else.
Since he came from outside, he doesn’t have any friends or family.”
“I see.”
Hyuk Mujin and I exchanged glances.
This sounded promising, but it was hardly conclusive.
“Little one, do you know his name?”
“Do you know anything else about him?”
“I don’t know his name.
He’s just Grandpa Jang.”
It seemed that was all the boy knew.
Hyuk Mujin asked with an eerily kind smile,
“Little one, could you tell us where he lives?”
“Waaay over there.
At the edge of the village.”
As expected of the continent.
This damn village was absurdly large for its population.
Hyuk Mujin roughly gauged the distance before turning to me.
“It’ll take about fifteen minutes.”
Even on horseback, it would take that long.
I shook my head.
“What if he isn’t the one?
Let’s search nearby first and work our way over there.”
“Yes, that’s probably better.
Aside from the fact that he came from elsewhere, there’s nothing that really marks him as the man we’re looking for.”
Cheongpung nodded.
“Chomp.
Chomp.
Chomp.”
While I wondered whether I should simply hurl away that food bundle, the boy boldly held out both his little hands toward Cheongpung.
“Hmm?”
“Grandpa Jang said there’s no such thing as a favor without a price.”
The kid already understood how the world worked.
He had given us information, so now he wanted a bite in return.
That Grandpa Jang or whatever his name was sure had taught a fine lesson to a child of five or six.
“Wow, my grandfather said something similar.
Here.”
“Wow!
Thank you!”
Look at them, united under the banner of grandfathers.
Cheongpung casually handed him a large leg of meat.
He had been periodically warming the food with the Zaha Divine Technique, which was based on Scorching Yang Qi, so the meat was still hot.
He’s using the Zaha Divine Technique to heat meat?
The boy happily tore into the meat, then looked at us with naked longing in his eyes.
“By the way, I need to go home anyway.
And on the way back, I’m going to visit Grandpa Jang three houses down.”
“Oh, really?”
I immediately understood what he meant.
When you were desperate, you would borrow even a cat’s paw.
Why not a child’s?
“Then could you ask Grandpa Jang his name?
Meet us back here in half a shichen.”
“Hmm.
I think I’ll be even hungrier by then.”
“See those food bundles?
I’ll give you a whole one.”
“Really?”
The boy’s eyes lit up, but then he hesitated.
“Why are you looking for Grandpa Jang?”
“It’s nothing serious.
We just have a favor to ask him.”
“You’re not bad people, are you?”
Introducing myself as the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi from the Jin Family of Taiyuan would only draw a crowd.
I gave him my most innocent smile.
“Of course not.”
“Ugh.
Why are you smiling like such a bad person?”
Should I just smack him on the head and send him away?
Hyuk Mujin stepped in on my behalf.
“I’ll give you two bundles.”
“So you were good people after all.
I’ll be back!”
The child was already becoming a monster born of capitalism.
Hyuk Mujin shrugged.
“Where should we start looking?”
“Search everything from the nearest entrance onward.”
“That’ll take half a shichen.”
Hyuk Mujin was wrong.
It took us more than half a shichen to search half the village.
Then the boy returned with an extremely valuable clue.
If his name starts with Jang and ends with Bo...
The former Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild, Jang Taebo.
That had to be him.
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
“Oh, you know the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
That’s me.
Hahaha.”
The fact that he knew who I was was a good sign.
It felt strange to say this about myself, but wasn’t the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi practically Shanxi Province’s idol?
If this world had internet access, I would already have a fan club.
“I’m sorry to visit so late at night.
The thing is, I have a favor to ask...”
“There’s no need.”
“Pardon?”
Jang Taebo was over eighty, but he still had a sturdy build.
He fixed me with a cantankerous stare.
“I won’t accept the commission anyway.”
“Still, you should at least hear what it is...”
“No!”
Well, that was decisive.

chapters.title: Chapter 167
paragraphs: “No!”
What a set of lungs.
The shout rang out so loudly that it belied the speaker’s eighty years, and Cheongpung gulped down whatever was in his mouth.
“Benefactor, he really doesn’t want to do it, does he?”
I heard him, you idiot.
I’d heard he was pretty cantankerous, but I hadn’t expected this.
Still, if a few shouts were enough to make me back down, I never would have come this far in the first place. I calmly tried again.
“Elder, please calm down and hear me out—”
“What is there to hear? You want me to make you a weapon, don’t you?”
“Uh, well, yes.”
“You barge in on an old man who retired ten years ago, in the middle of the night no less, and ask him to make you something meant for killing people?”
Jang Taebo glared and shouted,
“Get out of my sight this instant!”
“Waaah!”
At the sound of yet another shout, the little boy in Jang Taebo’s arms burst into tears.
Holding the fire starter, Hyuk Mujin muttered quietly enough that only I could hear him.
“What a temper on that old man...”
I agreed, though it was also true that I’d been in too much of a hurry.
Judging by the way things were going, he wouldn’t accept my commission even if I died and came back to life.
This is a problem.
I had to be back by tomorrow for the New Year’s Day banquet.
As I hesitated, villagers alarmed by the commotion began poking their heads out of their doors one by one.
“What’s all this racket?”
“That was Old Man Jang’s voice, wasn’t it? I heard Hanga crying next door, too.”
“Elder, is something wrong over there?”
There was nothing to gain from having our identities exposed here. No—in fact, they were the ones who stood to lose.
Jang Taebo frowned.
“It’s nothing. Seems some young men got dead drunk and came to the wrong house.”
“Tsk, tsk. Young people these days are all like that. If you need any help...”
“Your concern is enough.”
At his firm reply, the open doors closed one by one, and the murmuring voices abruptly fell silent.
When the surroundings grew quiet, Jang Taebo fixed us with his bulging eyes.
“Go home. And don’t come back.”
His tone was gentler than before, and his voice had dropped, but icicles still seemed to fall from every word.
There was nothing to be done. I turned away and bowed toward Jang Taebo’s back as he soothed the whimpering child.
“I’ll come see you again tomorrow.”
“You’re hard of hearing, aren’t you? Didn’t you hear what I just said?”
“...Then we’ll be going.”
I was about to leave when another thought occurred to me, something that might move him even a little.
“I truly need the help of a Master Artisan. That’s why I came to find you, elder.”
But Jang Taebo answered without even looking back.
“Go west for one shichen and you’ll find a large village with a smithy. The owner there is fairly skilled.”
“Is he skilled enough to forge Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”
Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron—a mysterious mineral imbued with supernatural properties, the hardest and sharpest material in the world, capable of withstanding even Sword Energy.
It was so valuable and rare that even highly skilled blacksmiths could go their entire lives without ever laying eyes on it.
If anything could pique his interest, it would be Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
But Jang Taebo’s reaction fell far short of my expectations.
“Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron? Then go to the Ironcraft Guild. Leave it with that Guild Leader fellow, and he should do a passable job. He learned a thing or two by watching me work.”
The indifference in his voice told me everything.
To him now, even a legendary metal like Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron was no different from copper.
“It’s late.”
It was an unmistakable dismissal. I had no choice but to turn away. Hyuk Mujin and Cheongpung followed me.
“What are you going to do?”
“What do you mean? I’ll keep pestering him until tomorrow.”
“Chomp, chomp, chomp.”
“He’s not just stubborn... By the way, where did you get the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”
“That’s a long story.”
“Chomp, chomp, chomp.”
Cheongpung cautiously studied the looks Hyuk Mujin and I were giving him, then held out a bundle.
“Would either of you like some? There’s still plenty left.”
We shouted in unison.
“We’re not eating it!”
We spent the night at a half-collapsed inn. As the only inn in the small village, it was old and shabby in every possible way, but it did have one advantage.
The innkeeper was a local who had lived in the Jang clan village for forty years.
He had been wary of the three of us, dressed as martial artists, but the moment I pressed a silver nyang into his hand, his grin stretched from ear to ear.
“Old Man Jang?”
“Yes. The man who lives over the hill.”
The innkeeper immediately nodded.
“Ah, of course I know him. He comes to our inn from time to time.”
“Does he?”
“Yes. Sometimes he drinks by himself, and sometimes he joins a gambling game.”
“He likes gambling?”
“Not exactly. I think he only does it to pass the time. Usually, he barely leaves his house once every seven days.”
“He’s a homebody.”
“Pardon?”
“Nothing. I was talking to myself. Is he any good at gambling?”
The innkeeper thought for a moment before answering.
“He’s about average. If anything, he tends to lose a little each time. But considering he keeps coming despite not working for a living, I suppose he must have made a fortune in his youth.”
That made sense. Geeks never spared any expense when it came to their obsessions.
Every martial artist was a weapon geek in one way or another, and Jang Taebo was one of the best custom weapon makers in the world.
He had clearly earned more money than most.
So luring him with money is out?
I’d suspected as much after last night, but the man really was difficult.
A deal only worked when you could satisfy something the other party wanted, and Jang Taebo seemed quite content with his current life.
“Is there anything else? Does he ever make things, for example?”
“Make things?”
“You know, like kitchen knives or pickaxes.”
A repetitive life eventually became a habit. That had to be especially true of someone like Jang Taebo, who had spent his entire life working with fire and iron.
If I were in his position, I’d be too restless to sit still.
But the innkeeper gave me a strange look.
“Old Man Jang? He hates moving so much that he pays the Escort Bureau extra to deliver his winter firewood. I’ve never heard of him making anything.”
Escort Bureau rocket delivery, huh?
A homebody with a severe case of laziness. There wasn’t a single opening to exploit.
Hyuk Mujin and Cheongpung, who had been listening while they ate breakfast, suddenly joined in.
“He’s completely impenetrable.”
“Chomp, chomp. Wow, I’ve never seen anyone like that before.”
“...I’ve never seen anyone like you before, either.”
One of the inn’s flaws was that the food was absolutely terrible.
The state of the owner’s hands alone raised serious questions about the place’s hygiene, but Cheongpung swept up the remaining food as though none of that mattered.
“Is it good?”
“Yes! When I lived with Grandpa, all I ate was grass and fasting pills every day.”
“Ah, fasting pills.”
That, I could understand. I’d rather make pancakes out of Jinho hyung’s vomit than eat those.
“Captain, why do you look like that?”
“Munch, munch. Benefactor, is something wrong?”
“...No. My stomach just feels a little queasy.”
On second thought, even that was going too far.
I rose from my seat after watching Cheongpung clean out the last plate.
“All right, let’s go.”
“Already? It’s only between seven and nine in the morning.”
“Can I have just one more dumpling?”
The innkeeper quickly cut in.
“Old Man Jang is getting on in years, so he doesn’t sleep late in the morning. And I’ll pack the dumplings for you right now.”
“There. Happy?”
I handed the innkeeper another silver nyang. He stood in front of the inn and waved until we disappeared from view.
“Elder, did you sleep well?”
Jang Taebo was standing in the courtyard. When he saw us, he frowned. More precisely, he frowned when he saw me.
“I believe I told you not to come back.”
“Could I really just leave after coming all this way?”
I gave him an easygoing smile.
Back when I was a lowest-level Hunter, people had hurled obscenities right to my face. This was nothing.
“It felt wrong to come empty-handed, so I brought you a small gift.”
“Hmm?”
“The innkeeper was quite talkative. Apparently, an acquaintance of his dug up a thirty-year-old He Shou Wu not long ago.”
He Shou Wu was still used as a medicinal herb in the modern world.
Century-old and millennium-old He Shou Wu appeared all the time in martial arts novels, but here, even finding a thirty-year-old specimen was said to be as difficult as plucking a star from the sky.
In other words, it was hard to find in this area even if you had money.
“A thirty-year-old He Shou Wu... So?”
“I was worried you might be feeling weak lately. It made me think of you, so I brought it along.”
Jinho hyung was always saying that the body started breaking down once a person passed thirty.
Your eyes got dry, your stomach started burning, and the day after you lent someone a USB, you could barely stand on your own legs.
If that was what happened to Jinho hyung in the prime of his life, how much worse must it be for the elderly? A thirty-year-old He Shou Wu was perfect for looking after one’s health.
“Hmm. Why don’t you eat it?”
“Oh, goodness, me? No, no. I brought it for you, elder.”
The bait had caught his interest.
Feeling a tug on the line, I held out the He Shou Wu.
Properly consumed, it could provide about a year’s worth of internal energy, but I didn’t begrudge it in the slightest.
“Please, eat it. They say it’s best to chew it raw, roots and all.”
“Hmm. Should I?”
Yes, hurry up and eat it, then spit out a Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron spear.
At my bright smile, Jang Taebo popped the He Shou Wu into his mouth and began chewing noisily. The atmosphere was completely different from last night.
Oh, this is looking good.
If I coaxed him gently while the atmosphere was this pleasant, then submitted my commission...!
But the next moment, I heard the sound of my hopeful future being abruptly cut off.
“Ptooey!”
Hyuk Mujin, Cheongpung, and I stared at the half-chewed He Shou Wu lying on the ground.
He spat it out? A thirty-year-old He Shou Wu? Why?
When we stared at him in confusion, Jang Taebo asked as though nothing had happened.
“Why are you looking at me like that? Is something wrong?”
“...Why did you spit it out?”
“It’s bitter.”
“Pardon?”
“I said it’s bitter.”
His unabashed answer left me speechless.
What kind of bullshit was that?
“Of course it’s bitter. It’s good for you.”
“Tsk, tsk. You’ve never eaten He Shou Wu before, have you?”
I had eaten Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng once, but I hadn’t been in my own body at the time, so I couldn’t say.
When I found myself agreeing, Jang Taebo rummaged through his robes and tossed something at me.
“What is this?”
I caught it and found myself holding a wooden box about the size of a pencil case. Jang Taebo gave me a scornful smile.
“Open it.”
For a man who only gambled occasionally, he sounded exactly like a cardsharp.
I opened the wooden box with an inexplicable sense of tension.
“A fake! ...Wait, no, it’s He Shou Wu?”
He Shou Wu?
And not just any He Shou Wu.
Its body and roots were thicker than those of the He Shou Wu I’d given Jang Taebo moments ago.
A fragrant scent struck my nose.
Item check.
Ding.

System Item Window Fifty-Year-Old He Shou Wu Type: Spirit Herb Grade: First Rate Restriction: None Description: He Shou Wu that grew in nature for fifty years and has finally begun to hold spiritual energy. If absorbed by a martial artist who has learned a cultivation technique, it can provide up to about two years of internal energy.
Even a thirty-year-old specimen was supposed to be difficult to obtain. Where on earth had he gotten one that was fifty years old?
I was too dumbfounded to speak. Jang Taebo gave me a triumphant smile.
“It comes through the Nine-Room Escort Bureau once every four months. The head of the bureau owes me a favor. He knows how to keep his mouth shut, too.”
“...I see.”
So it was a regular delivery from the Nine-Room Escort Bureau. No wonder the old man looked healthier than most young men.
“Enough with these transparent tricks. I’m a man who no longer needs anything.”
“You certainly seem that way.”
He had money saved up and had achieved professional success.
He even had a full head of hair.
The only thing he lacked was a family—but if I offered to introduce him to a pretty old lady, he’d probably try to kill me.
“What would it take for you to accept my commission?”
Jang Taebo dug his pinky into his ear.
“Bring me the Herb of Eternal Youth, and I’ll think about it.”
“Pardon?”
“You didn’t hear me? The Herb of Eternal Youth. The spirit herb said to grant eternal youth and immortality.”
Ding.
System Quest In Search of the Herb of Eternal Youth has been created. Would you like to accept the Quest? Y / N
This time, I shouted,
“No!”

I’d rather make pancakes out of Jinho hyung’s vomit than eat those.
“Captain, why do you look like that?”
“Munch, munch.
Benefactor, is something wrong?”
My stomach just feels a little queasy.”
On second thought, even that was going too far.
I rose from my seat after watching Cheongpung clean out the last plate.
“All right, let’s go.”
“Already?
It’s only between seven and nine in the morning.”
“Can I have just one more dumpling?”
The innkeeper quickly cut in.
“Old Man Jang is getting on in years, so he doesn’t sleep late in the morning.
And I’ll pack the dumplings for you right now.”
“There.
Happy?”
I handed the innkeeper another silver nyang.
He stood in front of the inn and waved until we disappeared from view.
“Elder, did you sleep well?”
Jang Taebo was standing in the courtyard.
When he saw us, he frowned.
More precisely, he frowned when he saw me.
“I believe I told you not to come back.”
“Could I really just leave after coming all this way?”
I gave him an easygoing smile.
Back when I was a lowest-level Hunter, people had hurled obscenities right to my face.
This was nothing.
“It felt wrong to come empty-handed, so I brought you a small gift.”
“Hmm?”
“The innkeeper was quite talkative.
Apparently, an acquaintance of his dug up a thirty-year-old He Shou Wu not long ago.”
He Shou Wu was still used as a medicinal herb in the modern world.
Century-old and millennium-old He Shou Wu appeared all the time in martial arts novels, but here, even finding a thirty-year-old specimen was said to be as difficult as plucking a star from the sky.
In other words, it was hard to find in this area even if you had money.
“A thirty-year-old He Shou Wu...
So?”
“I was worried you might be feeling weak lately.
It made me think of you, so I brought it along.”
Jinho hyung was always saying that the body started breaking down once a person passed thirty.
Your eyes got dry, your stomach started burning, and the day after you lent someone a USB, you could barely stand on your own legs.
If that was what happened to Jinho hyung in the prime of his life, how much worse must it be for the elderly?
A thirty-year-old He Shou Wu was perfect for looking after one’s health.
“Hmm.
Why don’t you eat it?”
“Oh, goodness, me?
No, no.
I brought it for you, elder.”
The bait had caught his interest.
Feeling a tug on the line, I held out the He Shou Wu.
Properly consumed, it could provide about a year’s worth of internal energy, but I didn’t begrudge it in the slightest.
“Please, eat it.
They say it’s best to chew it raw, roots and all.”
“Hmm.
Should I?”
Yes, hurry up and eat it, then spit out a Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron spear.
At my bright smile, Jang Taebo popped the He Shou Wu into his mouth and began chewing noisily.
The atmosphere was completely different from last night.
Oh, this is looking good.
If I coaxed him gently while the atmosphere was this pleasant, then submitted my commission...!
But the next moment, I heard the sound of my hopeful future being abruptly cut off.
“Ptooey!”
Hyuk Mujin, Cheongpung, and I stared at the half-chewed He Shou Wu lying on the ground.
He spat it out?
A thirty-year-old He Shou Wu?
Why?
When we stared at him in confusion, Jang Taebo asked as though nothing had happened.
“Why are you looking at me like that?
Is something wrong?”
“...Why did you spit it out?”
“It’s bitter.”
“Pardon?”
“I said it’s bitter.”
His unabashed answer left me speechless.
What kind of bullshit was that?
“Of course it’s bitter.
It’s good for you.”
“Tsk, tsk.
You’ve never eaten He Shou Wu before, have you?”
I had eaten Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng once, but I hadn’t been in my own body at the time, so I couldn’t say.
When I found myself agreeing, Jang Taebo rummaged through his robes and tossed something at me.
“What is this?”
I caught it and found myself holding a wooden box about the size of a pencil case.
Jang Taebo gave me a scornful smile.
“Open it.”
For a man who only gambled occasionally, he sounded exactly like a cardsharp.
I opened the wooden box with an inexplicable sense of tension.
“A fake! ...Wait, no, it’s He Shou Wu?”
He Shou Wu?
And not just any He Shou Wu.
Its body and roots were thicker than those of the He Shou Wu I’d given Jang Taebo moments ago.
A fragrant scent struck my nose.
Item check.
Ding.

System Item Window Fifty-Year-Old He Shou Wu Type: Spirit Herb Grade: First Rate Restriction: None Description: He Shou Wu that grew in nature for fifty years and has finally begun to hold spiritual energy.
If absorbed by a martial artist who has learned a cultivation technique, it can provide up to about two years of internal energy.
Even a thirty-year-old specimen was supposed to be difficult to obtain.
Where on earth had he gotten one that was fifty years old?
I was too dumbfounded to speak.
Jang Taebo gave me a triumphant smile.
“It comes through the Nine-Room Escort Bureau once every four months.
The head of the bureau owes me a favor.
He knows how to keep his mouth shut, too.”
“...I see.”
So it was a regular delivery from the Nine-Room Escort Bureau.
No wonder the old man looked healthier than most young men.
“Enough with these transparent tricks.
I’m a man who no longer needs anything.”
“You certainly seem that way.”
He had money saved up and had achieved professional success.
He even had a full head of hair.
The only thing he lacked was a family—but if I offered to introduce him to a pretty old lady, he’d probably try to kill me.
“What would it take for you to accept my commission?”
Jang Taebo dug his pinky into his ear.
“Bring me the Herb of Eternal Youth, and I’ll think about it.”
“Pardon?”
“You didn’t hear me?
The Herb of Eternal Youth.
The spirit herb said to grant eternal youth and immortality.”
Ding.
System Quest In Search of the Herb of Eternal Youth has been created.
Would you like to accept the Quest?
Y / N
This time, I shouted,
“No!”

paragraphs: Quest

System In Search of the Herb of Eternal Youth This spirit herb exists only in legend. Rulers who dreamed of immortality and eternal youth poured vast amounts of wealth and manpower into searching for the Herb of Eternal Youth, but no one has ever found it. However, if you have about a thousand years left to live, it might not be a bad idea to give it a try. Grade: ??? Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Acquire the Herb of Eternal Youth (Incomplete) Reward: ??? Failure: ???
“No!”
Beep.
System You rejected the Quest.
Just look at this damn quest. Even its Grade was nothing but question marks.
What? “If you have about a thousand years left to live, it might not be a bad idea to give it a try”?
What kind of bullshit was that?
At my incredulous stare, Jang Taebo stroked his beard.
“What? Can’t you do it?”
“...How exactly am I supposed to do that?”
“Then forget it. Give me back the He Shou Wu.”
Jang Taebo snatched the He Shou Wu from my hand and began chewing it with a crisp crunch.
“Oh, it’s sweet. Just what you’d expect from a fifty-year-old specimen.”
“Hm? Are you all still standing there? Did you need something?”
“No, elder.”
“Why?”
“Does asking someone to bring you the Herb of Eternal Youth sound remotely reasonable?”
“It’s been a long time since I met someone who cared about common sense in the Murim. There’s Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, so why wouldn’t there be an Herb of Eternal Youth?”
That sounded surprisingly plausible.
I almost let myself be persuaded, but quickly came to my senses. Somehow, I had to convince this old man who seemed impervious even to a needle.
“If there’s anything else you need, I’ll get it for you. Anything you want. Just not something like the Herb of Eternal Youth.”
“Really?”
“Of course. If necessary, I’ll mobilize the full strength of my family.”
“Hm. I’ve heard plenty about how formidable the Jin Family of Taiyuan has become these days.”
Jang Taebo nodded and opened his mouth.
“Then I’m thirsty. Bring me a bottle of gongcheong seokyu.”
“Pardon?”
Gongcheong seokyu? The stuff said to grant a jiazi of internal energy with a single drop?
I barely stopped myself from letting loose a stream of profanity. Jang Taebo continued with a sly grin.

“You said you wanted to make a weapon out of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, didn’t you? Then you’ll need a fine scabbard, too. I hear there’s a dragon at the end of the world. Pull out one of its claws and bring it back. And while you’re at it, bring me a dragon pearl.”
Ding.
System Quest Get Gongcheong Seokyu, a Dragon’s Claw, and a Dragon Pearl has been created. Would you like to accept the Quest? Y / N
...As if.
Feeling my insides boil, I closed the Quest window. Hyuk Mujin covered his mouth and whispered,
“I think the old man’s senile.”
“I can hear you. You wet-behind-the-ears brat certainly have a lot to say.”
Just as Jang Taebo began waving a fist the size of a pot lid, Cheongpung thrust his hand into the air and shouted,
“I’ll go find them! Let me do it!”
“What?”
“The Herb of Eternal Youth! Gongcheong seokyu! A dragon!”
At last, the neighborhood’s resident lunatic had stepped forward.
His eyes sparkled like morning stars, and his every gesture burned with enthusiasm. Faced with Cheongpung’s intensity, Jang Taebo flinched and took a step back.
“Who are you?”
Cheongpung answered energetically,
“I’m my grandpa’s grandson!”
“Who’s your grandfather?”
“My grandpa!”
“...What a lunatic.”
Welcome. First time dealing with Cheongpung?
As Jang Taebo shook his head from side to side, I casually added,
“Do you happen to know Great Hero Mae Jonghak?”
“Though I’m not a martial artist, I’ve spent my entire life with one foot in the Murim. Do you think I wouldn’t know the Sword Saint, whom even butchers have heard of?”
“That friend is the disciple personally raised and taught by the Sword Saint.”
“What? Is that true?”
“Why would I lie? Especially while staking the name of someone as distinguished as the Sword Saint?”
“Hah. So he’s the Sword Saint’s successor...”
Had that worked? No matter where you went in the world, connections were king: school ties, hometown ties, and blood ties.
In the Murim, the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak’s very existence inspired respect and awe.
Jang Taebo stared at Cheongpung in evident surprise, then opened his mouth.
“So what do you want me to do about it?”
“I have nothing to do with Huashan. Well, I did make a sword at the request of the current Sect Leader of Huashan, Heavenly Sword True Person, about thirty years ago. But that’s all.”
His firm voice continued.
“I’m eighty years old. I’m still in good health, and I’ve accumulated plenty of wealth. As a man who has worked iron all his life, I can proudly say that I rank among the top three in the world.”
“That’s why I’m asking you.”
“That’s why I’m refusing you. I’ve finished all the work I care to do. I’ve made swords until I’m sick of them.”
“I use a spear.”
“Oh, did you?”
“Yes.”
“A spear would take even more work. I’d rather make a sword.”
“Elder!”
I grabbed Jang Taebo’s hand and gave him an earnest look.
“Couldn’t you think of it as something to pass the time and help me just this once?”
“When did I say I wouldn’t?”
“You just said you wouldn’t.”
Jang Taebo harshly shook off my hand.
“I said I’d help you. If you bring me the Herb of Eternal Youth.”
“Oh, please.”

“Bring me the gongcheong seokyu and dragon pearl while you’re at it. I hear that when fighting a dragon, you should avoid its tail, circle around behind it, and choke its neck. I’m telling you so you don’t get hurt.”
“...A dragon isn’t a person. How am I supposed to kill it by choking it?”
“Then burst its balls.”
“What if it’s female?”
“See you in the next life.”
I had finally met a formidable opponent.
His way of screwing with people had been honed over decades. My fists trembled, and the back of my head throbbed.
“Are you really going to be like this?”
“That is precisely how I’m going to be.”
“I didn’t want to go this far...”
“Go on. Spit it out.”
“Should I spread the word that the former Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild lives here?”
I was only saying it. Obviously, I had no intention of actually doing it.
But Jang Taebo merely grinned at my threat to make his life difficult.
“Then I suppose I have no choice. I’ll have to return to the Ironcraft Guild before all sorts of gnats start swarming around.”
“Huh?”
This wasn’t how it was supposed to go. As I was thinking that, Jang Taebo asked,
“If I return to the Ironcraft Guild, what do you think I’ll do?”
“...How would I know?”

“I’ll devote the rest of my life to making ten weapons. Then I’ll distribute those weapons, each made with all my heart and soul, to the leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang, while having in-depth conversations with them about the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Your name will come up quite a lot, especially.”
“W-What are you planning to tell them?”

“I’ll leave that to your imagination. Oh, and you do know that martial artists will stake their lives on their weapons regardless of how advanced their martial arts are, don’t you? I’m sure they’ll be happy to grant a small request of mine.”
It might be a small request to the leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang, but it would be anything but small to me or the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
If he bad-mouthed us with even a few words in front of them, a hit to our reputation would be the least of it. We might even face real pressure from them.
“Well, I suppose I should start preparing to leave. Let’s see, what should I pack...?”
As he turned to go into his room and pack, I grabbed his wrist. Jang Taebo asked innocently,
“What is it?”
I lowered my head helplessly.
“Please stop. I admit defeat.”
“Is that all?”
“I’m sorry for acting cocky.”
“And?”
“I won’t tell anyone that you’re living here.”
“Given that you came looking for me like this, it can’t be something only you know, can it?”
“I’ll explain everything properly to my eldest brother, too.”
“You’re sure?”
“Of course.”
“Hm. You’re not completely ill-mannered, then.”
Having gotten every answer he wanted, Jang Taebo smiled with satisfaction.
I had defeated enemies stronger than me time and again, but I couldn’t break the will of an old man enjoying a quiet retirement.
So where am I supposed to have the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron forged?
I’d finally thought I was about to have my first cherished weapon...
I was staring dejectedly at the half-chewed, discarded He Shou Wu when Jang Taebo spoke.
“You said you were making a spear?”
“Pardon?”
“Are you deaf? Why do you keep asking me to repeat myself?”
I hurriedly raised my head and saw Jang Taebo’s gruff face. He continued,
“Well, if you ask me to make it myself, I’ll obviously refuse. But I can at least give you an introduction.”
“You mean the Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild, your disciple...”
“Do you think the Guild Leader has that much time on his hands? He’s busy, too. Even someone like you would have to wait several years at the very least.”
“Several years?”

“What, did you think a weapon could be completed overnight? He’s not as good as me, but he’s skilled enough that his orders are bound to be backed up. Even picking and choosing which ones to accept, it still takes that long.”
Even so, several years?
The prospect of such an unexpectedly long project left me short of breath.
“T-Then what do I do?”

“What do you mean, what do you do? I’ll write you a letter of introduction. Take it with you. You’ll be going there with a recommendation from his master, so he’ll probably finish it a little sooner. That fellow makes one hell of a spear.”
“Ooh. Ooooh.”
“The village was in an uproar because of those mounted bandits, and I heard you were the one who dealt with them. I’ll do this for you as a special favor. Do you have paper, a brush, and ink?”
Hyuk Mujin, suddenly singled out, answered with a bewildered expression,
“No.”
“Right. One look at you, and I can tell you don’t carry such things. Then what about you...?”
“Chomp, chomp, chomp.”
He’s eating those now?
Jang Taebo sighed at the sight of Cheongpung stuffing the dumplings we had bought at the inn into his mouth until his cheeks looked ready to burst.
“...Are the dumplings good?”
“Chomp, chomp. Yes.”
“Mae Jonghak took in a strange one in his later years. Fine, wait here a moment.”
“Old people should just die. Young people these days have no manners.”
Muttering loudly enough for us to hear, Jang Taebo went inside and returned with paper, a brush, and ink.
“First, the weapon is a spear... Do you have a particular shape or weight in mind?”
“Ah, yes.”
“Tell me.”
I described in detail the weight and shape that had become thoroughly familiar to me over seven years of wielding a spear.
Each time, Jang Taebo either nodded silently or added advice on how to make a spear better suited to me.
He really is an expert.
Sixty years in the trade had not gone to waste.

He gave my body a quick once-over, then rattled off one correction after another. He gauged the size of my hands and the length of my arms and legs with uncanny accuracy, then adjusted the thickness and shape of the spear shaft little by little.
“All right, this is the last thing. Where are you planning to put the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron? In the spearhead, presumably?”
“Why are you making that face? You said you had Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. You’re not planning to leave it out, are you?”
“No, I’m going to use it...”
“Do you not have much? By my estimate, ten nyang should be enough to produce something worthy of being called a renowned spear. You could pass it down as a family heirloom without shame.”
How much was ten nyang? I still wasn’t used to the unit of weight, so I had no idea.
As I hesitated, Jang Taebo barked,
“Ah! How much of it are you going to put in?”
“That’s... Just a moment.”
Seeing was believing. It would be faster to show him directly.
Pretending to rummage through my travel bag, I took the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron from my Inventory and casually held it out.
“It’s about this much.”
“Elder?”
Jang Taebo didn’t answer. He stared intently at the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, which was larger than an adult’s head, for a long time before asking in an intensely hoarse voice,
“This... This is all Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”
“Yes. This isn’t your first time seeing it, is it?”
“I-I can’t believe this.”

His wrinkled hands trembled faintly. Jang Taebo stroked the cold, blue-tinged Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron as though he had been reunited with a child after sixty years. A sharp light flashed in his eyes.
“Entrust it to me.”
The old man who had found everything a nuisance was nowhere to be seen. His voice brimmed with passion and vitality.
“I’ll make you the greatest divine weapon in the world.”
Ding.

“Well, if you ask me to make it myself, I’ll obviously refuse.
But I can at least give you an introduction.”
“You mean the Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild, your disciple...”
“Do you think the Guild Leader has that much time on his hands?
He’s busy, too.
Even someone like you would have to wait several years at the very least.”
“Several years?”
“What, did you think a weapon could be completed overnight?
He’s not as good as me, but he’s skilled enough that his orders are bound to be backed up.
Even picking and choosing which ones to accept, it still takes that long.”
Even so, several years?
The prospect of such an unexpectedly long project left me short of breath.
“T-Then what do I do?”
“What do you mean, what do you do?
I’ll write you a letter of introduction.
Take it with you.
You’ll be going there with a recommendation from his master, so he’ll probably finish it a little sooner.
That fellow makes one hell of a spear.”
“Ooh.
Ooooh.”
“The village was in an uproar because of those mounted bandits, and I heard you were the one who dealt with them.
I’ll do this for you as a special favor.
Do you have paper, a brush, and ink?”
Hyuk Mujin, suddenly singled out, answered with a bewildered expression,
“No.”
“Right.
One look at you, and I can tell you don’t carry such things.
Then what about you...?”
“Chomp, chomp, chomp.”
He’s eating those now?
Jang Taebo sighed at the sight of Cheongpung stuffing the dumplings we had bought at the inn into his mouth until his cheeks looked ready to burst.
“...Are the dumplings good?”
“Chomp, chomp.
Yes.”
“Mae Jonghak took in a strange one in his later years.
Fine, wait here a moment.”
“Old people should just die.
Young people these days have no manners.”
Muttering loudly enough for us to hear, Jang Taebo went inside and returned with paper, a brush, and ink.
“First, the weapon is a spear...
Do you have a particular shape or weight in mind?”
“Ah, yes.”
“Tell me.”
I described in detail the weight and shape that had become thoroughly familiar to me over seven years of wielding a spear.
Each time, Jang Taebo either nodded silently or added advice on how to make a spear better suited to me.
He really is an expert.
Sixty years in the trade had not gone to waste.
He gave my body a quick once-over, then rattled off one correction after another.
He gauged the size of my hands and the length of my arms and legs with uncanny accuracy, then adjusted the thickness and shape of the spear shaft little by little.
“All right, this is the last thing.
Where are you planning to put the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?
In the spearhead, presumably?”
“Why are you making that face?
You said you had Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
You’re not planning to leave it out, are you?”
“No, I’m going to use it...”
“Do you not have much?
By my estimate, ten nyang should be enough to produce something worthy of being called a renowned spear.
You could pass it down as a family heirloom without shame.”
How much was ten nyang?
I still wasn’t used to the unit of weight, so I had no idea.
As I hesitated, Jang Taebo barked,
“Ah!
How much of it are you going to put in?”
“That’s...
Just a moment.”
Seeing was believing.
It would be faster to show him directly.
Pretending to rummage through my travel bag, I took the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron from my Inventory and casually held it out.
“It’s about this much.”
“Elder?”
Jang Taebo didn’t answer.
He stared intently at the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, which was larger than an adult’s head, for a long time before asking in an intensely hoarse voice,
“This...
This is all Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”
“Yes.
This isn’t your first time seeing it, is it?”
“I-I can’t believe this.”
His wrinkled hands trembled faintly.
Jang Taebo stroked the cold, blue-tinged Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron as though he had been reunited with a child after sixty years.
A sharp light flashed in his eyes.
“Entrust it to me.”
The old man who had found everything a nuisance was nowhere to be seen.
His voice brimmed with passion and vitality.
“I’ll make you the greatest divine weapon in the world.”
Ding.
