paragraphs: In the dim light before dawn, a group of people made their way through the thick fog.
At their head, two middle-aged men spoke in low voices.
“Are you sure the information is reliable?”
“More than ninety percent.”
“Ninety percent?”
“I can’t be certain until we confirm it ourselves.”
“Then the other ten percent...”
“They may have leaked the information deliberately.”
“Which would make this a trap.”
“That’s why we’re taking every possible precaution, isn’t it?”
The two middle-aged men swallowed hard. So did everyone following them.
Each man gripped his weapon tightly, his eyes brimming with anxiety and tension.
“Damn it. We really stepped in shit.”
“Same here. I had a bad feeling from the moment they put me in charge of the Datong Branch.”

The two middle-aged men exchanged sympathetic looks. They were the Branch Leaders of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Lower District Sect’s respective Datong Branches, both established barely a month ago.
“I was bragging to my wife about my promotion just the other day. At this rate, I’m going to make her a widow.”
“Stop whining. I told you, we’re more than ninety percent certain.”
“And if we land in the other ten percent?”
“We die surrounded by more than four hundred mounted bandits.”
“Look at your face. Enough with the ill-omened talk. Watch where you’re going—we should be there soon.”
After the Lower District Sect Branch Leader finished speaking, silence descended.
They continued forward, slow but steady, muffling even their footsteps. The dense fog blanketing the area concealed both their figures and the sounds they made.
How long had they been walking?
By the time everyone was drenched in sweat and moisture—
“Stop!”
The low, restrained shout came from the Datong Branch Leader of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Gripping the hilt of his sword hard enough to crush it, he asked the Lower District Sect Branch Leader,
“Did you hear that?”
“What...? Ah!”
The Lower District Sect Branch Leader’s face stiffened.
A sound from beyond the fog had reached his ears.
That’s...
Horses snorting. And not just one or two.
The two men raised clenched fists. At once, dozens of sword blades smeared black with ash emerged from their sheaths.
Beyond the dense fog, which limited their vision to less than a zhang, it felt as though hundreds of mounted bandits armed with bows and lances might come charging out at any moment.
Gulp.
Just as someone’s throat bobbed loudly, a sudden gust swept across the grassland and brushed away the fog.
The sight it revealed made everyone’s eyes fly open.
“Gasp!”
“W-What in the world...?”
Beneath the grassland’s blue sky lay a field of red. The earth had been scorched black, and the stench of blood and death hung heavy in the air.
The Lower District Sect Branch Leader groaned involuntarily.
“So the information was true.”
Dozens of bewildered gazes swept the area. Hundreds of men and horses lay sprawled across the ground, every trace of life already gone.
Severed limbs lay scattered like weeds, and eyes frozen wide with terror and shock stared blankly into space.
The few horses that remained alive let out hungry snorts as they trampled a flag covered in hastily scrawled red characters.
HEAVENLY WIND
There was no mistake. It was the flag of the Heavenly Wind Band.

The annihilation of the Heavenly Wind Band, which had once made a name for itself throughout the northern Gaoyuan through its brutality. The ninety-percent guess had finally become a hundred-percent certainty.

For nearly half a month, the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Lower District Sect had been closely monitoring the Heavenly Wind Band’s movements. They should have felt the relief of having a rotten tooth pulled, yet the longer the two Branch Leaders surveyed the scene, the darker their faces became.
“T-This...”
“That’s right. One person did all this.”
The scattered corpses told the story themselves.
A single person had killed them all.
“What a terrifying master. I can’t even begin to fathom his strength.”
The Jin Family Branch Leader, the strongest martial artist among them, continued in a trembling voice.
“Every one of them was killed in a single strike. Judging by their burned-out organs, the killer must have cultivated Scorching Yang Qi to its utmost limit.”
“W-What about his martial arts? Can you tell what he used?”
“Not at all. He didn’t use any distinctive martial art. This was... nothing but overwhelming power crushing everything in its path.”
One person had slaughtered four hundred mounted bandits as easily as crushing ants.
The bodies strewn in every direction showed that they had tried to flee. Their horribly contorted faces showed the terror they had felt.
Not a single person had escaped the hands of this unidentified master and his fearsome martial arts.
“C-Could something like this really be possible?”
“It must be. We’re seeing it with our own eyes.”
He was right. The scene before them was both evidence and witness.
The two men fell silent, unable to find anything more to say.
“Over here! There’s a survivor!”
A survivor?

Their eyes snapped open at the sudden shout. The two Branch Leaders immediately displayed their movement techniques and ran like the wind. As they arrived, they muttered like men groaning in disbelief.
“A survivor?”
“He’s still breathing. Not for much longer, though.”
As the man had said, the sole survivor was already little better than a corpse.
His left arm had been ripped off as though devoured by a beast, and a sickening smell of charred flesh rose from the gaping hole in his side.
The Lower District Sect Branch Leader stared intently at the man’s relatively intact face.
“This is the Heavenly Wind Band Leader.”
“...Are you sure?”
“Certain.”
The Heavenly Wind Band Leader had begun making a name for himself ten years ago, and his face was widely known.
Though only recently appointed head of the Lower District Sect’s Datong Branch, the Branch Leader had memorized the features of every major figure in the region.
Lately, he had seen the Heavenly Wind Band Leader’s face more often than those of his own children.
“He was one of the five strongest men in the Gaoyuan—no, one of the top three... To think he would end up like this.”
The chieftains of the mounted-bandit forces ruling the Gaoyuan were all accomplished martial artists, but the Heavenly Wind Band Leader had stood out even among them.
He was dull-witted, but his innate talent for combat alone had made him one of the pillars of the Gaoyuan—a Peak master.
Now, however, he was nothing more than a defeated man on the verge of death.
“I suppose being a Peak master earned him two attacks. One tore off his arm, and the other put a fist through his side.”
A Peak master defeated in only two exchanges?
It was so absurd that he could no longer even feel shocked.
Everyone stood speechless when—
“Khrrk. Khrrrk.”
A wet rattle came from the Heavenly Wind Band Leader’s throat as his body twitched.
He laboriously opened his eyes, and a hoarse voice leaked between his lips.
“Save... save me.”
“You’re the Heavenly Wind Band Leader. Is that right?”
“Y-Yes. That’s me.”
The Jin Family Branch Leader sent internal energy toward his wrist. The man’s eyes became a little clearer. Just a little.
“Don’t worry. You can survive.”
It was a lie.
They would gladly have saved him if they could, but it was already too late. There was a mountain of questions they needed answered before he breathed his last.
“Who did this?”
Before the words had fully left his mouth, the Heavenly Wind Band Leader jerked like a bird struck by an arrow. His remaining hand shot up and seized the Branch Leader’s collar.
His grip held a strength impossible for a dying man. The stench of death poured from his open mouth.
“An old man. It was an old man. He’s a demon who rose from a pit of fire.”
“Let go!”
“They’re all dead. I’m dead too. I’m already dead. The demon killed me.”
“Y-You!”
The horrified Branch Leader hurriedly tried to pull away, but the strength slowly drained from the Heavenly Wind Band Leader’s grip.
The lifeless body slowly tipped over and collapsed. His wide-open eyes glared at the blue sky.
“Hah... Hah... Is he dead?”
The Lower District Sect Branch Leader nodded and sighed.
“He had completely lost his mind.”
“No wonder. It’s a miracle he was alive at all. He survived in that condition for nearly two days.”
“At least we learned something.”
“What do we know besides the fact that he was old?”

“He was an old master in the Supreme Peak realm who primarily used Scorching Yang Qi. Judging by the fact that he didn’t leave a single person alive, he’s merciless as well. If he came this way past Datong, he’d attract attention in no time.”
After a moment’s hesitation, the Lower District Sect Branch Leader added,
“...One way or another.”
Whether he was merely an old master who showed no mercy or a great fiend beyond anything they could imagine, they had no way of knowing.
There was only one thing they could do to prepare for the worst.
“We need to send word to our family.”
“I’ll do the same.”
The two men exchanged dark looks, each thinking much the same thing.
Who—or what—was the old man the Heavenly Wind Band Leader spoke of? And...
Where is he now?
The woodcutter met the old man halfway up an unnamed mountain.
The moment he saw the old man strolling leisurely along the rugged mountain path, only one thought crossed his mind.
Is he a mountain spirit?
In all his life, he had never seen anyone so old. Looking at the woodcutter awkwardly prostrating himself, the old man asked,
“What is it?”
“My name is Jang-pal.”
“I’ve come to pay my respects, Mountain Spirit.”
After a brief silence, the old man spoke.
“What kind of lunacy is this...? Are you trying to make a perfectly healthy living man ascend to immortality?”
“Y-You’re not a mountain spirit?”
Jang-pal the woodcutter looked the old man up and down.
Now that he thought about it, more than a few things seemed strange. An immortal should radiate a sacred aura at first glance and speak with dignified elegance...
“Have you ever seen an immortal dressed like this? My robes gape so badly that the cold wind blows straight through them.”
That eccentric way of speaking, those loose clothes torn in places...
The only thing about him that resembled an immortal was his extraordinary age.
“I’m sorry. I’m completely uneducated.”
Jang-pal gave an embarrassed smile, and the old man waved him away.
“If you understand, then be on your way.”
“Yes.”
Jang-pal bowed politely and continued walking.
“...You there.”
“Yes?”
The old man scowled.
“Why do you keep following me?”
“Oh, this is the road to my village.”
“What’s down this road?”
“Jang Family Village. It’s a small place. I live there myself.”
“Jang Family Village? From the name, I take it everyone there belongs to the same clan.”
“That’s right.”
The old man clicked his tongue.
“Why are there so many clan villages around here? Half a shichen ago, I passed one called Hong Family Village or something.”
“Hong Family Village?”
“Why? You know it?”
“Yes. Of course I do. But...”
Jang-pal tilted his head.
“Hong Family Village should be at least three hundred li from here. Are you perhaps confusing it with somewhere else?”
“Do I look like an idiot who can’t remember what happened half a shichen ago?”
Three hundred li was far enough that even Jang-pal, who had sturdy legs, would need two full days to cover it.
But three hundred li in half a shichen?
Jang-pal, a simple country bumpkin, clicked his tongue inwardly in pity.
The poor old man’s senile.
His appearance certainly fit. His body was painfully thin, and his hair hung wild and unkempt.
What had brought an old man like him to a mountain climbed only by woodcutters like Jang-pal?
Ah, could it be...?
He suddenly recalled stories of unfilial sons abandoning their elderly parents in the mountains to leave themselves one less mouth to feed. Perhaps this old man had suffered the same fate.
Jang-pal gazed at him with guileless sympathy, then took something from inside his clothes and held it out respectfully.
“Elder, please have this.”
“Hmm? What is it?”
Jang-pal scratched the back of his head.
“I brought it along just in case... but I’m full.”
It was a rice ball his wife had prepared early that morning. He was hungry after working so hard, but surely the old man before him must be even hungrier.
“It isn’t much, but please eat it.”
“It certainly doesn’t look like much.”
“I’m joking.”
The old man glanced between Jang-pal and the crude rice ball.
“My stomach happened to be empty. This will do nicely.”
He devoured the palm-sized rice ball in the blink of an eye. Jang-pal then offered him the wooden carrying frame on his back.
“Please climb on. If you sit atop the bundle of firewood, the ride should be bearable.”
“Hmm? You want me to ride on that?”
“Yes. The mountain path is rough, and you’re heading down anyway, aren’t you?”
“I am, but...”
Jang-pal smiled guilelessly.
“You remind me of my father, who passed away long ago.”
A complicated expression crossed the old man’s face. He clicked his tongue, then climbed onto the carrying frame.
He was so light that Jang-pal could lift him with one hand.
“Are you comfortable?”
“These sticks are poking my backside to death.”
“Should I walk a little more slowly?”
“Slowly? You should be running as if you’re flying. Oh, and about that late father of yours...”
“Yes?”
“What sort of man was he? If I reminded you of him, he must have been exceptionally handsome and strapping.”
Jang-pal suddenly became much less talkative.
Ahead of him, Jang Family Village began to come into view.

“I brought it along just in case... but I’m full.”
It was a rice ball his wife had prepared early that morning.
He was hungry after working so hard, but surely the old man before him must be even hungrier.
“It isn’t much, but please eat it.”
“It certainly doesn’t look like much.”
“I’m joking.”
The old man glanced between Jang-pal and the crude rice ball.
“My stomach happened to be empty.
This will do nicely.”
He devoured the palm-sized rice ball in the blink of an eye.
Jang-pal then offered him the wooden carrying frame on his back.
“Please climb on.
If you sit atop the bundle of firewood, the ride should be bearable.”
“Hmm?
You want me to ride on that?”
“Yes.
The mountain path is rough, and you’re heading down anyway, aren’t you?”
“I am, but...”
Jang-pal smiled guilelessly.
“You remind me of my father, who passed away long ago.”
A complicated expression crossed the old man’s face.
He clicked his tongue, then climbed onto the carrying frame.
He was so light that Jang-pal could lift him with one hand.
“Are you comfortable?”
“These sticks are poking my backside to death.”
“Should I walk a little more slowly?”
“Slowly?
You should be running as if you’re flying.
Oh, and about that late father of yours...”
“Yes?”
“What sort of man was he?
If I reminded you of him, he must have been exceptionally handsome and strapping.”
Jang-pal suddenly became much less talkative.
Ahead of him, Jang Family Village began to come into view.

chapters.title: Chapter 170
paragraphs: Old and small.
That was the old man’s first impression of Jang Family Village.
Seated atop the gently swaying wooden carrying frame, he gazed at the sparse scattering of houses and added in a voice too quiet for anyone to hear,
“...And peaceful.”
It seemed the years had passed after all. Even an insignificant view like this made his body relax and a corner of his heart itch.
Just like that day, more than twenty years ago.
It was the same when I took that child in.
The image of a child he had met long ago suddenly flashed before his eyes.
Normally, he would have tossed the child a few iron coins or simply ignored them and walked on. But that day had been different.
Perhaps it was because he had only just realized that he was suffering from the infirmities of old age.
He had stared at the owner of that desperately outstretched hand and, before he knew it, spoken a single sentence.
“Will you come with me?”
“Elder, we’re here.”
The woodcutter’s voice brought the old man back to his senses.
They had stopped in front of a small house. Something tiny burst out from behind a loosely woven fence made of bundles of branches.
“Dad!”
“Oh, my daughter!”
The little girl, no more than six or seven years old, came pattering over and flung herself against her father’s leg.
The old man hopped lightly down from the carrying frame and watched them.
“Is she your child?”
“Ah, yes. She is. Hanga, say hello. This gentleman is...”
Come to think of it, Jang-pal did not even know the old man’s name.
As he trailed off, the old man waved a hand.
“No need to exchange names. It’s nothing.”
Just then, Hanga, who had been gazing up at the old man with sparkling eyes, toddled over and slapped his bony thigh.
“Grandpa!”
“Hm?”
“What’s your name, Grandpa?”
“I don’t know. I’ve forgotten it too.”
The old man had only said it to spare himself the bother, but Jang-pal took it differently.
He’s not sound of mind enough to remember even his own name.
As a simple mountain villager, Jang-pal found the old man terribly pitiable.
He could not leave someone who had apparently been abandoned by his children to wander around in clothes scarcely better than rags.
“Elder, why don’t you at least stay for a meal? We’ll have something ready in no time.”
“No need. What you gave me earlier was enough.”
“Even so...”
“There’s someone I must find. I’ve already been delayed for quite some time, so I ask for your understanding.”
After speaking, the old man paused.
Understanding?
The word that had slipped from his mouth felt foreign.
He had lived his entire life without restraint. Everyone had feared and revered him. Even the most renowned masters of Murim had tucked their tails between their legs in his presence.
And yet such words came easily before this country bumpkin he had known for less than half a shichen.
I’m old. I really have grown old.
As the old man stood there in bewilderment, someone tugged at his sleeve.
He looked down and saw plump, baby-soft cheeks twitching.
“Who are you looking for? Hanga is good at finding people.”
“...Is that so?”
“Uh-huh! Yesterday, I found Grandpa Jang from three houses over.”
“Well done.”
“When I found him, he gave me something tasty. I ate until my belly almost burst.”
After that baffling remark, she planted a hand on her waist. Her expression was almost solemn.
“And people need to eat so they’ll have strength. At your age, Grandpa, you can even chew up iron.”
“H-Hanga!”
“Ha ha ha!”
The old man laughed heartily for the first time in a long while. When was the last time he had laughed like this? It must have been more than ten years ago.
Once his laughter subsided, he patted Hanga’s round head.
“Yes, you’re right. This old man can chew up iron.”
“Uh-huh. I’m always right.”
Beaming with pride, Hanga caught hold of his sleeve and led him into the house. The old man let himself be dragged along.
Even the strongest man under heaven could not have made him budge, but today was an exception. More importantly...
This isn’t half bad.
He rather liked the situation. For once, he almost felt like an ordinary old man.
When they entered the room, Jang-pal’s wife soon brought out a meal.
“I’m afraid the side dishes aren’t much.”
As she had said, the food was simple: a few kinds of namul and mixed-grain rice. Even the meat soup they had served for his sake was pale and bland.
But everything had been prepared with care. They were clearly not well-off, yet they treated the shabby old man seated at their table as a guest rather than an unwelcome intruder.
Well, now.
The old man finished the meal with a strange feeling in his heart. Hanga asked him with sparkling eyes,
“Grandpa, was it good?”
“Yes. It was the best meal I’ve had in quite some time.”
“Right? My mom is the best cook in our whole village.”
“...Is that so?”
“Uh-huh!”
I wouldn’t go that far.
The old man swallowed the words and nodded.
He had not enjoyed the meal for its taste, but for the care with which it had been prepared.
Oblivious, Hanga continued chattering away.
“Grandpa Jang from three houses over sometimes comes to eat at our house too. Yesterday I ate at his house, though. Hee hee.”
Jang-pal watched his daughter fondly.
“Hanga, did you go to the elder’s house again?”
“Uh-huh. Grandpa gave me something tasty yesterday. So did the other older brothers.”
“How many times have I told you not to bother the elder? But what do you mean, older brothers?”
Jang Family Village was a small place. The few young men there had either left for other regions or joined Murim sects with dreams of making their fortunes in the martial world.
Those who remained had families of their own, so there was hardly anyone Hanga would call an older brother.
“Were they strangers?”
“Uh-huh. They were tall and handsome, and they gave me this much food. So I found Grandpa for them.”
“You found him? Were they looking for the elder?”
“I don’t know. They were just looking for Grandpa. They were cool older brothers with sticks hanging from their waists.”
“Sticks at their waists... Swords?”
Martial artists. They had to be.
Jang-pal and his wife exchanged grave looks.
To ordinary civilians like them, martial artists were objects of fear.
Only a few months had passed since the war between the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect. How terrified had they been then?
Now, unidentified martial artists had appeared right next door—and their only daughter had become involved with them.
Jang-pal asked anxiously,
“What happened after that?”
“When I took them to Grandpa, he shouted.”
“D-Did you hear who those older brothers were?”
“I did, but I forgot!”
Her answer was bright and innocent, but dark clouds gathered over her parents’ hearts. Jang-pal hurriedly rose to his feet.
“I need to go. The elder may have come to harm.”
“Hanga’s father!”
“You stay here with Hanga. I’ll only sneak over and take a look, so don’t worry.”
Despite his words, he picked up the axe propped against one corner of the room. His horrified wife was about to stop him when—
“Sit down.”
“Pardon?”
“Are your ears clogged? I said sit down.”
The old man, who had been sitting quietly, rose to his feet. His bony knees cracked loudly.
“I’ve had a hearty meal. I might as well go for a stroll. Consider it payment for the food.”
Jang-pal stared blankly at him, then gave a hollow laugh.
“Elder, that’s no place for you.”
“You have it backward. It’s no place for you.”
“Please stay here. I’ll be back soon.”
“Will you be able to come back?”
The old man gazed at Jang-pal with an unreadable expression.
The moment Jang-pal met those deep, still, unfathomable eyes, his breath caught.
“If they’re even a little—just the slightest bit—unsavory, you won’t be coming back. Do you intend to leave your daughter without a father?”
The old man’s eyes flashed like a streak of light, then faded.
As if nothing had happened, he patted his lower back and held out a hand to Jang-pal.
“Give it here.”
That was all.
Yet Jang-pal handed him the axe as if under a spell.
“You’ve maintained it well. Best use this only for chopping wood.”
The old man calmly studied the sharpened blade, then grinned at Hanga. The child had sensed the change in the air, and her large eyes were already glistening.
“Why the long face?”
“I think Hanga did something wrong. Hanga was wrong.”
“Yes. This time, you were.”
Just as a miserable wail was about to burst from her, the old man continued in a voice as soft and warm as a quilt.
“So take special care not to let this happen again. Listen to your parents. Do you understand?”
“Uh-huh... But, Grandpa.”
“Go on.”
“Will you come back?”
The old man could not suppress the quiet laugh that escaped him.
“Of course. I’m old enough to chew iron. What couldn’t I do?”
At that moment, Jang-pal snapped out of his daze.
What had he been thinking, handing an axe to an old man suffering from the infirmities of age? He must have been completely bewitched.
He had to put a stop to this at once.
“Elder, please give me back the axe. This—this is ridiculous...”
Jang-pal’s words died in his throat. His mouth fell open at the unbelievable sight unfolding before him.
Crunch. Crunch.
The axe blade was breaking apart.
Each time the old man’s yellow teeth moved—teeth that looked incapable of chewing even a soft chicken bone—the blade Jang-pal carefully sharpened every day snapped off piece by piece.
“W-What is this?”
“Your daughter has a fine eye for people. She was exactly right.”
A conversation from earlier flashed through Jang-pal’s horrified mind.
“Why are there so many clan villages around here? Less than half a shichen ago, there was something called Hong Family Village or whatever.”
“Hong Family Village? Hong Family Village should be at least three hundred li from here. Are you perhaps confusing it with somewhere else?”
“Do I look like some idiot who can’t even remember something that happened less than half a shichen ago?”
Only then did Jang-pal realize that none of the old man’s words had been lies.
He was not an ordinary old man. Someone who could walk three hundred li in half a shichen and chew iron could not possibly be ordinary.
Only one kind of person could perform such extraordinary feats.
“A martial artist...”
The old man asked Jang-pal, whose legs were trembling,
“So, where are they?”
A voice brimming with joy slipped between Jang Taebo’s lips.
“I’ll make you the greatest divine weapon in the world.”
Ding.
System The Quest mission has been completed. Quest Find the Master Artisan has been successfully completed. A linked Quest has been created.
Shit. If I’d known this would happen, I would’ve shown him sooner.
Hyuk Mujin looked dumbfounded too. No, on closer inspection, he looked horrified.
“Is all of that Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”
I scratched my chin. What did I know? The System said it was Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, so I simply took its word for it.
“Yeah, probably.”
“You can’t just say ‘probably’!”
“Tell me about it.”
To be honest, I was flustered too.
When Jang Taebo had shown no reaction after hearing that I possessed Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, I had assumed that people in the upper circles treated Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron as basic gear.
But as it turned out...
Is it like a drink made with ten percent apple flavoring?
They called it the greatest mineral under heaven, and if people only shaved off tiny pieces to attach to a blade, it must be incredibly rare.
While everyone else used weapons containing five or ten percent Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, I could have one made from a hundred percent.
That was an enormous advantage.
My gear alone would give me a head start.
“With this—with this, I can create the masterpiece of my lifetime.”
Jang Taebo trembled all over, overcome with emotion.
It was hard to believe he was the same old man who had acted indifferent and played hard to get only moments ago. Not that I was complaining, now that everything had worked out.
“Where in the world did you obtain such an enormous amount of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”
“That’s a secret.”
“D-Did you perhaps discover a mine containing vast deposits of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”
Jang Taebo’s eyes flared like high beams. He had claimed he no longer needed anything, but now...
“Tell me!”
I coldly shook my head. I did not even know where the mine was, and I could not tell him the truth anyway.
“No.”
“Please! I’m begging you!”
“W-Wait, what are you doing?”
Now he was clinging to my trouser leg. The spirit of an artisan who had devoted decades to a single path blazed in his eyes.
“Please!”
“Oh, for crying out loud!”
Just as I hurriedly pried Jang Taebo’s hands away—
“Is this the house of Grandpa Jang, who lives three houses over...? Damn it. It’s rubbing off on me already. Anyway, is this Old Man Jang’s house?”
A sharp voice pierced my eardrums.

chapters.title: Chapter 171
paragraphs: The sharp, ringing voice belonged to a squat old man.
He was shorter than most elementary schoolchildren these days and dressed in grimy clothes. But more than anything else...
He’s incredibly old.
I hadn’t lived all that long, but in all my years, I had never seen anyone so ancient.
Just as I was thinking that, my eyes met the old man’s.
“Hey!”
“Yes?”
“When an elder asks you a question, you’re supposed to answer. Is this Old Man Jang’s house?”
Is that the vibe that comes with experience?
The old man looked as though he could drop dead at any moment, yet his eyes were more than lively—they practically blazed. Feeling strangely intimidated, I answered.
“It is.”
Jang Taebo, who had been clutching my trouser leg, awkwardly rose to his feet.
I wondered if the old man might be one of his friends from the senior center, but the wary look on Jang Taebo’s face suggested otherwise.
“Who are you?”
“Just a traveler passing through. Are you Old Man Jang?”
“That’s right.”
“I see. I stopped by just in case.”
The old man glanced around, then added,
“Though I suppose there wasn’t any need.”
“Then I’ll be going. Once you’re finished here, stop by the house where that kid lives. The child’s worried about you.”
With that, the old man turned around.
What the hell was that old man’s deal?
As everyone stood there bewildered by his incomprehensible words and actions, Cheongpung poked me in the side.
“Munch, munch. Benefactor. Don’t you think there’s something strange about him?”
“...You look stranger to me. And swallow what’s in your mouth before you talk.”
How long is this guy going to keep chewing those dumplings? Does he have some magic jar that keeps producing more?
At my scolding, Cheongpung gulped down what was in his mouth and muttered,
“No, but there’s something strange about him.”
“Like what?”
“I don’t know. It’s just a feeling.”
“What kind of answer is th—”
Wait.
It was just a feeling?
I froze. Cheongpung might have been an eccentric, but he was also the disciple who had inherited everything from the Sword Saint and a Peak master far above me in skill.
Could he have sensed something about that old man that I couldn’t?
He looks like an ordinary old man...
There was nothing to lose by checking. In Murim, where anything could happen, it was best to tap even a stone bridge before crossing it.
Activate Qi Sense.
Ding!
System You have used the Skill Qi Sense. - You can detect targets up to Level 90 within a range of 70 jang. - Internal energy is consumed in proportion to range.
Whoosh.
A blue line visible only to me shot outward.
It passed through Cheongpung, Hyuk Mujin, and Jang Taebo, who were closest to me, before finally reaching the back of the old man as he slowly walked away.
A translucent holographic window sprang up above his snow-white hair.
System Lv. 3 Jeok Cheongang
Jeok Cheongang? Now that’s a name fit for a final boss.
But despite his impressive name, his Level was pitifully low. The old man was unquestionably an ordinary civilian who had never learned martial arts.
“Looks like you were just barking up the wrong tree...”
My voice trailed off.
The old man’s leisurely steps had stopped.
His squat body slowly turned around. Though he was more than ten jang away, the strange light in his eyes made my skin prickle.
What?
My body went rigid. My heart pounded, and my fingertips twitched.
If the old man’s lips had not opened at that moment, I might have summoned a weapon from my Inventory right then and there.
“Well, now...”
The corners of the old man’s wrinkled mouth twitched as he stared at me. His low voice bored into my ears.
“What an interesting fellow.”
The old man, Jeok Cheongang, encountered a rather interesting situation the moment he reached his destination.
Oh-ho. Well, look at these brats.
The Supreme Peak realm was an inhuman domain where one could be called a Martial God without exaggeration. He recognized the young men’s martial prowess at a glance.
One was nothing special, but the other two...
Frankly, they impressed him.
At that age, they’ve already broken through the wall.
The one noisily chewing dumplings in front of an elder, in particular, had already reached full maturity in the Peak realm.
Would only the Elders of the Nine Sects and One Gang whom I crossed paths with briefly in the past be able to compare?
As for the other one, the tall, broad fellow...
L-Look at the insolent way that bastard’s staring. Maybe I should gouge his eyes out.
The young man had a face like he had seen a walking corpse. Even so, it was obvious that he possessed martial arts far beyond what his age suggested.
No one his age could stand against him.
The rear waves of the Yangtze pushed the waves before them.
That was what they said. Jeok Cheongang suddenly realized that the new wave was quite large and fierce.
Large enough to swallow the entire Yangtze.
I suspected as much when they started making a fuss about Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron and all that... but they’re even more interesting than I expected.
Jeok Cheongang could detect presences from dozens of jang away. He had been listening to their conversation from the moment he left Jang’s house.
He also knew that the matter Jang had been worried about had not happened.
Far from being coerced, Old Man Jang appeared to be the one clinging to them.

Given their accomplishments and the fact that they’d even brought Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, could they be from the Nine Sects and One Gang? Well, either way, they clearly belong to a prestigious orthodox faction.
That was the extent of Jeok Cheongang’s interest.
He had no reason to form a connection with those young men and no desire to reveal his identity.
He had done enough to repay the meal he had been given, so he intended to leave immediately.
“Then I’ll be going. Once you’re finished here, stop by the house where that kid lives. The child’s worried about you.”
Jeok Cheongang tossed out those final words and turned away.
He had already wasted a considerable amount of time. He intended to reach Taiyuan before the day was out and pay a visit to the Lower District Sect.
Of course, he had no intention of letting anyone discover his identity.
If I wrap a mask around my face and threaten them a little, they should spill everything.
But Jeok Cheongang’s train of thought went no further.
The next moment, something unknown shot toward him from behind.
Whoosh.
He could neither see nor hear it.
He had only sensed it. A cold, unfamiliar presence pierced toward Jeok Cheongang’s back.
An ambush?
No. He sensed none of the sticky, unpleasant killing intent that accompanied one.
Instead, it felt as natural as a breeze blowing from afar, which only made it more alien.
The unknown energy vanished the moment it touched Jeok Cheongang’s back.
What in the world...?
He had lived for nearly a hundred years, yet this was the first time he had ever experienced anything like it.
Still bewildered, he turned around and immediately identified the culprit.
“Looks like you were just barking up the wrong tree...”
The young man’s mouth snapped shut the instant their eyes met. His gaze wavered, and his fingertips twitched.
As Jeok Cheongang stared at the culprit, the corners of his mouth slowly rose.
“Well, now...”
He stroked his chin, intrigued.
“What an interesting fellow.”
At the same time, his foot pushed off the ground.
In the next instant, the distance of more than ten jang between them vanished. Jeok Cheongang whispered into Jin Taekyung’s ear.
Inventory summon.
Just six syllables.
All I had to do was picture the spear and shout the words in my mind. But...
“What are you?”
The breath tickling the back of my neck made every hair on my body stand on end.
When did he—?
No, before that...
How?
He was definitely, definitely Level 3.
It was impossible to believe.
Jeok Cheongang looked as though he could drop dead at any moment, yet he was faster than anyone I had ever seen.
So fast that I did not even dare consider resisting him.
“Hey. When an elder asks you a question, you’re supposed to answer.”
“Y-Yes?”
“You call that an answer?”
A thin, wrinkled finger repeatedly poked me in the solar plexus. There was no force or internal energy behind it, yet it felt as though someone were stabbing me with a sword.
“I’m asking what you are.”
I swallowed hard. My mouth felt as dry as if someone had poured a handful of sand into it.
“I’m Jin Taekyung.”
“Not that crap. Which sect are you a disciple of?”
“Taiyuan—the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan? Are you one of those demonic, heterodox sorts?”
I nearly nodded without thinking.
The old man’s eyes had flashed when he mentioned demonic, heterodox arts. If I said yes even by mistake, he looked ready to cut my life short on the spot.
“I’m with an orthodox faction.”
“Are you? Then why are you stammering?”
“I’m telling the truth.”
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan... I feel like I’ve heard of it. Or perhaps I haven’t.”
Jeok Cheongang sank deep into thought, then suddenly gave me a peculiar look.
“The more I look at you, the stranger you seem. That thing just now—it was you, wasn’t it?”
That thing just now?
His words were vague, but I immediately understood.
This old man definitely sensed Qi Sense.
How is that possible?
I had vaguely suspected as much when he reacted right away, but the realization still made my vision go dark.
Good God. A monster who can sense Qi Sense.
“Why aren’t you answering?”
I bit down hard on my lower lip.
“No.”
“How do you know what I’m talking about?”
“Hey. It was you, wasn’t it?”
“No. Anyway, it wasn’t me.”
“Oh, I like that. You’ve got some backbone. Very manly.”
Jeok Cheongang laughed heartily, then continued,
“Should I break a few bones and ask again?”
“It was me! Yes, it was me!”
“Good. Fine. Then what did you do to me?”
I hesitated.
My opponent was an old man whose instincts were every bit as sharp as his age suggested. If I lied and got caught, I would not be leaving with my body intact.
I needed to stick as closely to the truth as possible while phrasing it in a way he would find agreeable.
“You seemed like an extraordinary person, so I just...”
“A little?”
“I checked whether you had learned martial arts.”
“How?”
“Yes?”
“I asked how you did it.”
“I sent a little of my qi toward you and read yours. Something like that.”
“Ha. Is that so?”
Jeok Cheongang laughed as though amused, then clenched his fist.
“If you keep lying, I’ll break your legs. Answer me again.”
I hurriedly waved my hands.
“W-Wait. Why are you suddenly acting like this?”

“You’ve completely misjudged this old man. Do I look like some fool who can’t distinguish something like that? What I felt just now... was different. Different enough to make me think it was the dark arts.”
“What dark arts? I’m telling you, it’s real!”
This is driving me insane.
Qi Sense was certainly a cheat Skill, closer to a System function than martial arts.
Because of that, someone like Jeok Cheongang, who appeared to be a Supreme Peak master, might have sensed something alien that he had never encountered before.
The problem is, how the hell am I supposed to explain that?
“You bastard! Can’t you tell me the truth?”
Fuck this. I’m done.
I decided to lay everything out honestly.
“The truth is, I use something called the System. It’s a bit of a cheat, so it might have felt strange to you. I’m sorry.”
Jeok Cheongang remained silent for a moment.
Then he opened his mouth.
“What kind of bullshit is that?”
“...I told you exactly what happened. I figured you wouldn’t understand.”
“Have you said all you have to say?”
“There’s plenty I haven’t said. I’ve been through a lot.”
“You’ve led a turbulent life.”
“You have no idea.”
“Don’t worry. After today, your life won’t have any more twists and turns.”
“Are you planning to make it all downhill from here?”
“Why bother saying it? How about we warm you up a little before we begin?”
It happened in an instant—too fast for me, Cheongpung, Hyuk Mujin, or Jang Taebo to react.
Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh and poked me in the chest with one finger.
And then...
Fwoosh!
An overwhelming wave of heat swept through my body.

chapters.title: Chapter 172
paragraphs: Jeok Cheongang wore a smug grin.
Heh heh. Have a taste of the heat, you little punk.
His fingertip carried Scorching Yang Qi refined to its pinnacle.
Though he was using only three-tenths of his internal energy, it was still far more than a fledgling who looked barely twenty could withstand.
This ought to snap him back to his senses.
Jeok Cheongang had no particular taste for tormenting youngsters, but this one needed to be taught a lesson.
The boy had been spouting incomprehensible nonsense about some “shisudaem” or whatever for a while now, and Jeok Cheongang was sick of listening to it.
I’ve controlled my strength, so if things go well, he might even avoid an internal injury.
If things went well.
Jeok Cheongang silently added that caveat as he reached out.
Tap.
The instant his bony, wrinkled finger touched the young man’s broad chest, Extreme Yang Qi surged forward like a tidal wave. Jin Taekyung sucked in a startled breath.
“Hk!”
“How is it? Feels like you’re burning up inside, doesn’t it?”
Jeok Cheongang could not help laughing when he saw the boy’s face turn bright red. The saying that a beating was the best medicine truly was an eternal truth.
“Now, stop talking nonsense and tell me the truth—”
Whooosh! Shhk!
Jeok Cheongang could not finish his sentence. Two swords flashed in like lightning, slicing through his waist and arm.
“Did it work? It worked! Cheongpung, you did it!”
Unlike Hyuk Mujin, who was celebrating with a bewildered expression, Cheongpung merely scratched the back of his head.
Before his eyes, Jeok Cheongang’s figure scattered like mist instead of spraying blood.
“Uh... Returning to Simplicity and Shifting Form and Position... I think we picked the wrong fight.”
Jeok Cheongang was already perched on a fence some distance away, laughing heartily.
“You’ve got a decent pair of eyes.”
“I grew up seeing things like that.”
“You grew up seeing them?”
Jeok Cheongang was genuinely surprised when he realized what those words implied.

Returning to Simplicity and Shifting Form and Position were both realms accessible only to Supreme Peak masters. That meant Cheongpung had grown up around a master who stood at the same level as Jeok Cheongang.
“Who is your Master?”
“My grandfather.”
“What an obtuse brat. How would this old man know who your grandfather is?”
“My grandfather always said that any man who hides behind another man’s name ought to have his balls cut off.”
“Ha ha ha! Splendid words!”
After bursting into laughter, Jeok Cheongang studied Cheongpung for a long moment.
“Can you bear the consequences of daring to point your sword at this old man?”
Cheongpung smacked his lips, looking troubled.
“But I didn’t use Sword Energy. Couldn’t you let it slide?”
“Would it have made a difference if you had?”
“Hmm. I don’t think so.”
Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh. He did not know whose disciple the boy was, but he was certainly an interesting one.
“Then why did you interfere?”
Cheongpung pointed at Jin Taekyung, who stood frozen like a stone statue.
Hot steam rose in wisps from his entire body, which had been heated to a reddish hue.
“I owe him a little. How could I stand by while you bullied my Benefactor, Grandpa?”
“You must owe him quite a lot if you’re willing to risk your life.”
Cheongpung’s eyes widened.
“Are you going to kill me?”
Of course, Jeok Cheongang had no intention of killing anyone here. But he deliberately hardened his expression and lowered his voice.
“Of course.”
“Uh-oh. That won’t do. There are still so many things I haven’t tried.”
“This is the Murim. Should this old man take circumstances like that into account?”
Cheongpung thought it over before answering.
“I suppose not.”
Hyuk Mujin, who had been listening to their conversation with mounting anxiety, exploded.
“You can’t just accept that, you idiot!”
“Why not?”
“Because that old man—no, that gentleman—is going to kill us!”
“He isn’t wrong. Hmm, and besides...”
Cheongpung calmly added,
“We won’t know whether we live or die until we fight.”
“...Damn it. Fine, let’s do it. If we just sit here, Captain will beat us to death later anyway, so whatever.”
Jeok Cheongang rested his chin on one hand and gazed at the two young men.
They truly were interesting.
One was willing to stake his life because he owed someone a debt. The other grumbled even as he stepped into a fight whose outcome was obvious.
They possessed something that some called reckless bravado and others called chivalry.
People like this always die young.
That had been true forty years ago, and it would probably be true now.
That was why Jeok Cheongang had grown somewhat fond of the youngsters. At the very least, they possessed the courage to risk their lives for someone else.
Just as they were doing now.
“Then shall I teach you a thing or two?”
Jeok Cheongang slowly rose.
At the same moment, an aura as vast as a mountain erupted from his short frame and pressed down on everything around him.
Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin gripped their sword hilts, while Jang Taebo sank to the ground, his face deathly pale.
“You sit this one out.”
Jeok Cheongang flicked a finger.
Jang Taebo’s body floated over the fence as though an invisible hand had seized him and lifted him away.
Cheongpung muttered at the sight.
“Seizing an Object Through Empty Space...”
With a single gesture, the old man had lifted Jang Taebo, who was larger than most full-grown men.
It was proof that the old man possessed internal energy no weaker than Cheongpung’s grandfather.
Hyuk Mujin stared blankly and muttered,
“Shit. I’ve only ever seen that in novels.”
They were on entirely different levels.
At this moment, everything surrounding Jeok Cheongang was both his weapon and his shield. The corner of his wrinkled mouth rose slightly.
“Come.”
That was the signal.
Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin charged with all their strength.
The two knew each other’s martial arts intimately after countless duels. Their swords meshed perfectly as they launched a coordinated attack.
Whooosh!
Shhk-shhk!
Just as the two blades were about to pierce Jeok Cheongang’s flank and neck, he extended both hands.
His hands, now engulfed in white flame, closed around the blades.
“Do you think this will be enough?”
Grrrk.
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes widened.
His beloved sword, forged from the exceptionally hard Baekryeon Jeonggang, was bending. A moment later, it turned into molten metal and began dripping away.
“What the hell?”
He had poured everything into that strike, yet he had failed to leave so much as a scratch.
As he stared blankly at the blade, already half melted, Jeok Cheongang’s voice reached his ears.
“Your courage was admirable. Now get some rest.”
The next moment, Hyuk Mujin’s vision turned white. A palm struck him in the chest, and he crumpled helplessly to his knees.
“Mujin!”
“Don’t worry. He should have suffered only a minor internal injury. More importantly...”
Jeok Cheongang glanced at the blade caught in his other hand.
It had neither bent nor melted. Instead, it was wrapped in faint purple Sword Energy.
Jeok Cheongang dredged up a memory from long ago.
“Zaha Divine Technique. Are you a disciple of Huashan?”
Cheongpung answered with a punch.
The Crouching Tiger Fist, a fierce and powerful fist technique said to subdue tigers, slammed into Jeok Cheongang’s chest.
Thud!
Jeok Cheongang’s white eyebrows curved like a crescent moon.
“Well, look at you.”
The blow should have been more than enough to shatter a man’s chest, yet that was the extent of his reaction.
Cheongpung felt as though he were facing his grandfather, the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.
He’s strong. Overwhelmingly strong.
But he could not give up.
Cheongpung exhaled slowly and stamped his foot. The energy of the Zaha Divine Technique rippling through his body flared even more fiercely.
“Good. Show me everything you’ve got.”
Jeok Cheongang grinned and loosened his grip on the blade.
Freed from its restraint, the sword unleashed the ultimate moves of the Plum Blossom Sword Technique.
Shiiiiing!
The sword tip moved fluidly, drawing plum blossoms through the air.
One became two. Two became five. Five became nine...
At last, twenty-four fully formed plum blossoms transformed into streaks of light and poured down toward Jeok Cheongang.
Even Jeok Cheongang could not help but marvel.
Huashan has produced an incredible talent.
And that brought one person to mind.
A figure who was practically synonymous with Huashan.
No—a figure revered by every swordsman under heaven.
“Mae Jonghak. What is your relationship with that friend of mine?”
The twenty-four plum blossoms wavered dangerously at the word friend.
The next moment, the Sword Energy narrowly missed Jeok Cheongang and devastated the surrounding area.
Kaboom!
Cheongpung swallowed a mouthful of the billowing dust and coughed.
“Cough, cough. You know my grandfather? Cough!”
Jeok Cheongang laughed with evident delight.
“I’ve met him. A very long time ago.”
It had been more than forty years earlier.

The Demonic Cult’s Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples had devoured half the world. As the tide of war turned against the orthodox faction, the orthodox Murim sought out even the reclusive eccentrics hidden deep within remote mountains and valleys.
That was when the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak visited Mount Jiuhua.
“Help us.”
Those were his opening words.
Jeok Cheongang was surprised to receive a visit from a master who could rival him, but his answer had already been decided.
“No.”
“Even with the world in danger?”
“Let’s speak plainly. It’s your orthodox Murim that’s in danger, not the world.”
Even if the ruler of the Murim changed, the world itself would remain the same. There were villains among the orthodox factions and good people within the Demonic Cult.
And Jeok Cheongang intended to remain on Mount Jiuhua forever.
Mae Jonghak sank into thought for a long while before suddenly smacking his forehead.
“Oh, now that I think about it, you’re right.”
“...Didn’t you come here to persuade me?”
“That’s that, and this is this, isn’t it?”
“What kind of... If you’re going to keep spouting nonsense, go home.”
“Then let’s settle this according to the laws of the Murim.”
“Might Makes Right?”
“If I lose, I’ll leave without complaint. Not only that, I’ll never speak of your existence to anyone. However...”
“If you win, I have to help the orthodox Murim.”
“Exactly. What do you say?”
“Draw your sword.”
They fought for seven days and seven nights.

It was a battle between Huashan, which had stood as a great tree of the Murim for centuries, and the Fire Gate Clan, whose martial arts had been passed down to one successor per generation and never transmitted to outsiders.
It was a bloody struggle between two Martial Gods.
And it ended in a draw, with neither victor nor loser.
“What a pity. With martial arts like yours, why are you holed up in a mountain backwater like this?”
“Mind your own business. It’s my affair. What does it have to do with you?”
“Oh. Now that I think about it, you’re right.”
“...Just listening to you is exhausting. What are you going to do now?”
“Honestly, I’d love to keep going, but... they crossed Gansu and Sichuan fifteen days ago. It’s a shame, but let’s leave it here this time.”
That had been fortunate for Jeok Cheongang.
If their battle had continued for even a few more days, he would have been the one to lose.
Mae Jonghak was ten years younger than him, yet he was already an astonishingly powerful master.
Without his own formidable internal energy, Jeok Cheongang would never have lasted so long.
“They may reach Anhui soon. Take care of yourself.”
“No problem. All I have to do is guard Mount Jiuhua.”
“Oh. That’s true.”
“...Please stop talking and leave.”
The Sword Saint Mae Jonghak left just like that, and the Demonic Cult’s army surged forward like a wave and swept into Anhui.
Fifteen days later, the Demonic Cultists passing through Mount Jiuhua made a grave mistake.
“Set it on fire!”
Mount Jiuhua burned, and Jeok Cheongang emerged into the world.
Not one of the thousand Demonic Cultists survived.
And people began calling him by another name.
“Then my grandfather...?”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, merely smiled faintly instead of answering.

chapters.title: Chapter 173
paragraphs: “Then...?”
At Cheongpung’s astonished expression, the Fire King Jeok Cheongang gave him a faint smile.
“Have you heard of me?”
“My grandfather mentioned you sometimes.”
“Oh-ho. So that friend of mine hasn’t forgotten me. What did he say?”
“He said your martial arts were strong, but your personality was... well, pretty terrible.”
The truth was, Jeok Cheongang had never been particularly sociable. No, “not sociable” did not begin to cover it. He was downright awful.
He had suffered all manner of hardships as a child, leaving him with a deep-rooted distrust of people. After that, he had grown up under an eccentric Master.
So perhaps it was only natural.
“I heard you got into fights nearly every day during the Great Faction War. Apparently, you hit practically every young prodigy from the Nine Sects and One Gang at least once...”
“Ahem. Who says I hit all of them? And I was young back then. When you’re young and full of energy...”
“I heard you were sixty at the time.”
“Cough, cough!”
Unable to defend himself, Jeok Cheongang merely cleared his throat. Then Cheongpung added one more thing.
“But he said you were a good person once someone got to know you, so if I ever met you, I should treat you the way I treat him.”
The corner of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth twitched.
“Hmm. Mae Jonghak really does know me well.”
Jeok Cheongang had fought in the Great Faction War for a little over a year.

It was rare for two Supreme Peak masters to fight on the same battlefield, and he had met Mae Jonghak only about ten times. Even so, they had unquestionably been close enough to call each other kindred spirits.
He did a fine job raising his grandson.
Wait a moment. Had Mae Jonghak ever married?
Jeok Cheongang quietly examined Cheongpung’s face.
There was not a single feature that resembled the Mae Jonghak he remembered.
He doesn’t look like a biological grandson...
Well, it did not matter.
Whether they shared blood or not, the boy was clearly his successor.
Judging by his behavior and the way he spoke, it would not be an exaggeration to say that they shared a soul rather than blood.
With a pleased smile, Jeok Cheongang spoke to Cheongpung.
“I gained a dependable grandson today. Come, give this old grandfather a formal bow.”
“What?”
Cheongpung tilted his head and asked again.
“Why?”
“...What do you mean, why?”
Caught off guard, Jeok Cheongang began to stammer.
“Didn’t Mae Jonghak tell you to treat me the way you treat him?”
“Yes.”
“You little punk, if a grandson meets his grandfather, he should give him a formal bow.”
“My grandfather doesn’t care about things like that. He said only hidebound old men obsess over empty formalities.”
Jeok Cheongang trembled, having suddenly become a hidebound old man.
“What was this called again? I learned it recently.”
Cheongpung thought hard for a moment, then slapped his forehead.
“Oh, right. A boomer!”
“A boo... what?”
“A boomer. They say ‘boomer-brain’ means something similar.”
What? A boomer? Boomer-brain? Neither the sound nor the feel of the words was particularly pleasant.
Jeok Cheongang did not know exactly what they meant, but he understood the context well enough.
Have I been hiding in the mountains for too long?
The new waves of the Yangtze were stronger than he had imagined. Even so, he could not beat up the only grandson of his one kindred spirit...
Jeok Cheongang felt his head begin to ache and opened his mouth.
“Is that something young people are saying these days?”
“I don’t know. I only heard it for the first time recently.”
“From whom?”
“My Benefactor.”
Jeok Cheongang followed the direction Cheongpung was pointing and turned his head.
His eyes met those of a young man squinting at him.
“Hey, come here.”
Did he see me? It felt like our eyes met for a moment...
No, he didn’t. Absolutely not. I closed my eyes right away. How could he have seen me?
I trembled with my eyes shut, as if I were struggling with all my might to treat an internal injury.
Just in case, I even added a groan.
“Uuugh!”
“Hey, I said come here.”
Stay calm.
He was just making a wild guess. If I fell for it immediately, I would be Third Rate.
At times like this, a Peak master had to clench his ass and keep acting his heart out.
“Uuugh!”
“Don’t force it. I’ve seen plenty of people shit themselves doing that.”
He had a point. I relaxed slightly at Jeok Cheongang’s helpful advice.
“Huuugh!”
“Good grief, what a brat. This is the last time I’m asking. Are you coming, or should this old man come to you?”
The last time.
I could not fall for a phrase like that.
I had to hold out until the very last last.
“This old man will go, then. You’re dead today.”
“...I’ll come.”
With tears in my eyes, I opened them.
Jeok Cheongang was glaring at me, his eyes blazing like fire.
He truly looked worthy of the title Fire King.
Fuck. The Fire King.
What are you doing here, hyung...?
No matter how many times I thought it over, the situation was utterly unbelievable.
But reality did not change. That short, squat old man was the Fire King, a Supreme Peak master counted among the twenty strongest under heaven.
I had a feeling from the start.
I might have been the first person here to realize his true identity.
The moment Jeok Cheongang’s internal energy surged into me, the System had delivered a telling message.
Ding.
System Your Scorching Yang Qi is responding intensely. - It is assimilating the internal energy that has entered your body. - Your internal energy has risen slightly.

It had happened in the blink of an eye. At first, I thought I was about to be roasted alive. But soon my stomach grew warm, as if I had just eaten a bowl of gukbap, and my internal energy even increased.
What the hell is this?
At first, I was bewildered, but I figured something good was something good. The more I thought about it, though, the less I could afford to be so relaxed.
Wait. My Scorching Yang Qi came from eating the Blazing Flame Divine Pill.
Just because it was the same kind of Scorching Yang Qi, why would that make me immune to harm? I had even absorbed his internal energy.
After a brief but intense deliberation, I eventually reached a conclusion.
It was because they were of the same kind, both born from the same root.
That meant the old man belonged to the Fire Gate Clan, which passed its legacy down to a single successor in each generation. As far as I knew, the current Sect Leader was probably...
The Fire King... No way. Why would a man who had been off the radar for nearly forty years come here?
That was what I thought at the time.
They say the first of the five psychological stages cancer patients go through is denial. I was no different.
The only difference was that I reached the final stage—acceptance—in less than five minutes.
He was close friends with the Sword Saint, lived on Mount Jiuhua during the Great Faction War, and wiped out all the Demonic Cultists after they set fire to the mountain...
Fuck. He really is the Fire King.
The more I listened to Jeok Cheongang and Cheongpung’s conversation, the more certain his identity became.
He had not explicitly declared that he was the Fire King, but anyone who had not figured it out by this point would have to be an idiot.
Once I finally reached the acceptance stage, a chill ran down my spine.
I’m fucked.
I pictured Jopil, dead with half his body blown away by my One Annihilation. I also thought of the Nameless Sword and the Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual sitting in my Inventory.
I had already gulped down the Blazing Flame Divine Pill, and it was safely stored in my dantian.
God, my stomach hurts.
Whether Jopil was that old man’s disciple or not, I had a problem either way.
My thoughts in chaos, I trudged forward like an ox being led to slaughter. Jeok Cheongang raised a finger.
“I’ll count to three. One.”
Whoosh!
I charged forward with every ounce of strength I possessed. The Fire King looked at me as though I were the craziest bastard he had ever seen and opened his mouth.
“Hey.”
“Yes!”
“You startled me! I’m not deaf, so speak softly!”
Smack!
A crisp impact left the back of my head throbbing. It was the first time I had ever been hit like that in the Murim.
Of course, I had no intention of protesting. My opponent was an irritable Supreme Peak master.
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his eyes as I kept my mouth shut.
“Well, look at you. You’re much quieter than before.”
“No, I’m not.”
“Don’t lie to this old man. You’d have better luck deceiving a ghost. Even the way you opened your eyes was different.”
Cheongpung approached with a worried expression.
“Benefactor, are you all right?”
My body is fine. My soul is dying.
I answered in a half-dead voice.
“Yes. More or less...”
“More or less?”
Without so much as a turn signal, Jeok Cheongang stuck his head in and looked me up and down.
“Hmm. Now that I think about it, why are you so fine? You should have been unable to move and forced to circulate your energy for at least half an hour.”
Why am I fine? Because I absorbed the Blazing Flame Divine Pill.
But I could not say that. Under his suspicious gaze, my mouth went dry.
“You’re a strange one, the more I look at you. Which sect are you from?”
“I’m from the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan... I’m sure I’ve heard of it somewhere.”
Jeok Cheongang furrowed his brow for a moment, then exclaimed, “Ah!”
“Was it the Blade of Flowers? That’s right. That fellow Jin Baekyang was from the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
Blade of Flowers Jin Baekyang.
He was the Head Elder.
I never expected that name to come up here.
Under Jeok Cheongang’s demanding gaze, I licked my lips.
“That’s right.”
“I ran into him a few times in my travels. He was a decent fellow. He had a somewhat gloomy side, but everyone was like that back then. He was also unfailingly courteous.”
All that remained to a person were their memories, especially for an old man like Jeok Cheongang, who did not have many years left to live.
But why did that memory have to be of the Head Elder?
Apparently, he remembered him quite fondly.
Then again, until recently, no one would have expected the Head Elder to do what he had done.
During the Great Faction War, his martial arts had been formidable enough to make him a leading candidate for Family Head, and he had been widely respected.
“Judging by your attainment, you carry the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s blood. What is your relationship with the Blade of Flowers?”
“He’s my great-uncle.”
In reality, we had been locked in a relationship of killing or being killed. But I was not technically lying.
At the mention of shared blood, Jeok Cheongang’s eyes softened.
“Oh-ho. Is that so?”
“Yes, sir.”
“How old are you?”
“Twenty this year. I’ve just come of age.”
“You seem to have learned Scorching Yang Qi. Did the Blade of Flowers teach you?”
He had given me some instruction about two months ago at Eight Spring Gorge.
He had been so enthusiastic about it that Sword Energy had nearly split my head open.
“Your achievements are remarkable for your age. You’re far more advanced than the Blade of Flowers was in his day.”
Jeok Cheongang was even offering me compliments now.
The atmosphere had become warm and friendly overall.
Then he opened his mouth again.
“So, is he doing well?”
Well, he’s doing fine in his grave, I suppose.
“His martial arts must have improved considerably by now. Should I stop by and see him while I’m here?”
“About that...”
You can visit, but you won’t be seeing his face.
The Head Elder’s grave was in one corner of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s cemetery—in other words, the family cemetery.
The family elders had vehemently opposed it, but Jin Wikyung had pushed it through. He had felt guilty about the mistake made by his grandfather, the former Family Head.
“I suppose I should have a drink with him. It’s been a long time since we last met. Surely he won’t treat me coldly.”
I imagined Jeok Cheongang pouring liquor beside the Head Elder’s grave.
Damn it. I can’t keep this up.
I took a deep breath and opened my mouth.
“Um, there’s something I need to tell you.”
“What is it? Go ahead.”
“He passed away.”
“...What?”
“Just a couple of months ago, unfortunately.”
Jeok Cheongang was silent for a moment before muttering, “Already? He was still going strong.”
Going strong? He was over eighty.
Of course, he had possessed powerful internal energy. If he had stayed out of trouble, he might have lived another twenty years.
“What happened?”
“He fell in battle.”
“He fell in battle?”
A trace of anger appeared in Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.
“Was it the Demonic Cult bastards?”
“No. The circumstances were complicated and sensitive, so it’s difficult to explain.”
“Do you know who killed him?”
“Did you avenge him? From the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s perspective, he was the kind of bastard they could grind up and eat, bones and all, and still not be satisfied.”
Listening to him made me feel as if my bones were turning to jelly.
I lowered my head silently with a sorrowful expression. Sensing the subdued atmosphere, Jeok Cheongang stopped speaking.
Good. Perfect. Hyuk Mujin being unconscious was a stroke of genius.
If he had been awake, he would have been shooting me sidelong glances and practically shouting, This is the culprit. He killed him.
All right. As soon as I get out of here, I’m getting the hell away. Maybe I should just use Logout altogether.
Then, in the next moment, I realized something.
“Huh? Blade of Flowers Jin Baekyang—isn’t he the person you killed, Benefactor? Right?”
I had forgotten about that bastard.

sentences.text: “Then...?”
At Cheongpung’s astonished expression, the Fire King Jeok Cheongang gave him a faint smile.
“Have you heard of me?”
“My grandfather mentioned you sometimes.”
“Oh-ho.
So that friend of mine hasn’t forgotten me.
What did he say?”
“He said your martial arts were strong, but your personality was... well, pretty terrible.”
The truth was, Jeok Cheongang had never been particularly sociable.
No, “not sociable” did not begin to cover it.
He was downright awful.
He had suffered all manner of hardships as a child, leaving him with a deep-rooted distrust of people.
After that, he had grown up under an eccentric Master.
So perhaps it was only natural.
“I heard you got into fights nearly every day during the Great Faction War.
Apparently, you hit practically every young prodigy from the Nine Sects and One Gang at least once...”
“Ahem.
Who says I hit all of them?
And I was young back then.
When you’re young and full of energy...”
“I heard you were sixty at the time.”
“Cough, cough!”
Unable to defend himself, Jeok Cheongang merely cleared his throat.
Then Cheongpung added one more thing.
“But he said you were a good person once someone got to know you, so if I ever met you, I should treat you the way I treat him.”
The corner of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth twitched.
“Hmm.
Mae Jonghak really does know me well.”
Jeok Cheongang had fought in the Great Faction War for a little over a year.
It was rare for two Supreme Peak masters to fight on the same battlefield, and he had met Mae Jonghak only about ten times.
Even so, they had unquestionably been close enough to call each other kindred spirits.
He did a fine job raising his grandson.
Wait a moment.
Had Mae Jonghak ever married?
Jeok Cheongang quietly examined Cheongpung’s face.
There was not a single feature that resembled the Mae Jonghak he remembered.
He doesn’t look like a biological grandson...
Well, it did not matter.
Whether they shared blood or not, the boy was clearly his successor.
Judging by his behavior and the way he spoke, it would not be an exaggeration to say that they shared a soul rather than blood.
With a pleased smile, Jeok Cheongang spoke to Cheongpung.
“I gained a dependable grandson today.
Come, give this old grandfather a formal bow.”
“What?”
Cheongpung tilted his head and asked again.
“Why?”
“...What do you mean, why?”
Caught off guard, Jeok Cheongang began to stammer.
“Didn’t Mae Jonghak tell you to treat me the way you treat him?”
“Yes.”
“You little punk, if a grandson meets his grandfather, he should give him a formal bow.”
“My grandfather doesn’t care about things like that.
He said only hidebound old men obsess over empty formalities.”
Jeok Cheongang trembled, having suddenly become a hidebound old man.
“What was this called again?
I learned it recently.”
Cheongpung thought hard for a moment, then slapped his forehead.
“Oh, right.
A boomer!”
“A boo... what?”
“A boomer.
They say ‘boomer-brain’ means something similar.”
What?
A boomer?
Boomer-brain?
Neither the sound nor the feel of the words was particularly pleasant.
Jeok Cheongang did not know exactly what they meant, but he understood the context well enough.
Have I been hiding in the mountains for too long?
The new waves of the Yangtze were stronger than he had imagined.
Even so, he could not beat up the only grandson of his one kindred spirit...
Jeok Cheongang felt his head begin to ache and opened his mouth.
“Is that something young people are saying these days?”
“I don’t know.
I only heard it for the first time recently.”
“From whom?”
“My Benefactor.”
Jeok Cheongang followed the direction Cheongpung was pointing and turned his head.
His eyes met those of a young man squinting at him.
“Hey, come here.”
Did he see me?
It felt like our eyes met for a moment...
No, he didn’t.
Absolutely not.
I closed my eyes right away.
How could he have seen me?
I trembled with my eyes shut, as if I were struggling with all my might to treat an internal injury.
Just in case, I even added a groan.
“Uuugh!”
“Hey, I said come here.”
Stay calm.
He was just making a wild guess.
If I fell for it immediately, I would be Third Rate.
At times like this, a Peak master had to clench his ass and keep acting his heart out.
“Uuugh!”
“Don’t force it.
I’ve seen plenty of people shit themselves doing that.”
He had a point.
I relaxed slightly at Jeok Cheongang’s helpful advice.
“Huuugh!”
“Good grief, what a brat.
This is the last time I’m asking.
Are you coming, or should this old man come to you?”
The last time.
I could not fall for a phrase like that.
I had to hold out until the very last last.
“This old man will go, then.
You’re dead today.”
“...I’ll come.”
With tears in my eyes, I opened them.
Jeok Cheongang was glaring at me, his eyes blazing like fire.
He truly looked worthy of the title Fire King.
Fuck.
The Fire King.
What are you doing here, hyung...?
No matter how many times I thought it over, the situation was utterly unbelievable.
But reality did not change.
That short, squat old man was the Fire King, a Supreme Peak master counted among the twenty strongest under heaven.
I had a feeling from the start.
I might have been the first person here to realize his true identity.
The moment Jeok Cheongang’s internal energy surged into me, the System had delivered a telling message.
Ding.
System Your Scorching Yang Qi is responding intensely. - It is assimilating the internal energy that has entered your body. - Your internal energy has risen slightly.
It had happened in the blink of an eye.
At first, I thought I was about to be roasted alive.
But soon my stomach grew warm, as if I had just eaten a bowl of gukbap, and my internal energy even increased.
What the hell is this?
At first, I was bewildered, but I figured something good was something good.
The more I thought about it, though, the less I could afford to be so relaxed.
Wait.
My Scorching Yang Qi came from eating the Blazing Flame Divine Pill.
Just because it was the same kind of Scorching Yang Qi, why would that make me immune to harm?
I had even absorbed his internal energy.
After a brief but intense deliberation, I eventually reached a conclusion.
It was because they were of the same kind, both born from the same root.
That meant the old man belonged to the Fire Gate Clan, which passed its legacy down to a single successor in each generation.
As far as I knew, the current Sect Leader was probably...
The Fire King...
No way.
Why would a man who had been off the radar for nearly forty years come here?
That was what I thought at the time.
They say the first of the five psychological stages cancer patients go through is denial.
I was no different.
The only difference was that I reached the final stage—acceptance—in less than five minutes.
He was close friends with the Sword Saint, lived on Mount Jiuhua during the Great Faction War, and wiped out all the Demonic Cultists after they set fire to the mountain...
Fuck.
He really is the Fire King.
The more I listened to Jeok Cheongang and Cheongpung’s conversation, the more certain his identity became.
He had not explicitly declared that he was the Fire King, but anyone who had not figured it out by this point would have to be an idiot.
Once I finally reached the acceptance stage, a chill ran down my spine.
I’m fucked.
I pictured Jopil, dead with half his body blown away by my One Annihilation.
I also thought of the Nameless Sword and the Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual sitting in my Inventory.
I had already gulped down the Blazing Flame Divine Pill, and it was safely stored in my dantian.
God, my stomach hurts.
Whether Jopil was that old man’s disciple or not, I had a problem either way.
My thoughts in chaos, I trudged forward like an ox being led to slaughter.
Jeok Cheongang raised a finger.
“I’ll count to three.
One.”
Whoosh!
I charged forward with every ounce of strength I possessed.
The Fire King looked at me as though I were the craziest bastard he had ever seen and opened his mouth.
“Hey.”
“Yes!”
“You startled me!
I’m not deaf, so speak softly!”
Smack!
A crisp impact left the back of my head throbbing.
It was the first time I had ever been hit like that in the Murim.
Of course, I had no intention of protesting.
My opponent was an irritable Supreme Peak master.
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his eyes as I kept my mouth shut.
“Well, look at you.
You’re much quieter than before.”
“No, I’m not.”
“Don’t lie to this old man.
You’d have better luck deceiving a ghost.
Even the way you opened your eyes was different.”
Cheongpung approached with a worried expression.
“Benefactor, are you all right?”
My body is fine.
My soul is dying.
I answered in a half-dead voice.
“Yes.
More or less...”
“More or less?”
Without so much as a turn signal, Jeok Cheongang stuck his head in and looked me up and down.
“Hmm.
Now that I think about it, why are you so fine?
You should have been unable to move and forced to circulate your energy for at least half an hour.”
Why am I fine?
Because I absorbed the Blazing Flame Divine Pill.
But I could not say that.
Under his suspicious gaze, my mouth went dry.
“You’re a strange one, the more I look at you.
Which sect are you from?”
“I’m from the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan...
I’m sure I’ve heard of it somewhere.”
Jeok Cheongang furrowed his brow for a moment, then exclaimed, “Ah!”
“Was it the Blade of Flowers?
That’s right.
That fellow Jin Baekyang was from the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
Blade of Flowers Jin Baekyang.
He was the Head Elder.
I never expected that name to come up here.
Under Jeok Cheongang’s demanding gaze, I licked my lips.
“That’s right.”
“I ran into him a few times in my travels.
He was a decent fellow.
He had a somewhat gloomy side, but everyone was like that back then.
He was also unfailingly courteous.”
All that remained to a person were their memories, especially for an old man like Jeok Cheongang, who did not have many years left to live.
But why did that memory have to be of the Head Elder?
Apparently, he remembered him quite fondly.
Then again, until recently, no one would have expected the Head Elder to do what he had done.

In reality, we had been locked in a relationship of killing or being killed.

Is that so?”

I’ve just come of age.”

Did the Blade of Flowers teach you?”

Well, he’s doing fine in his grave, I suppose.

Should I stop by and see him while I’m here?”

You can visit, but you won’t be seeing his face.

Surely he won’t treat me coldly.”
