chapters.title: Chapter 174
paragraphs: “Huh? Blade of Flowers Jin Baekyang—isn’t he the person you killed, Benefactor? Right?”
Only one thought crossed my mind.
I should’ve put a muzzle on that bastard ages ago.
Was he even human? No, he was an animal.
But it was already too late. Cheongpung was running wild like a pit bull off its leash.
“It’s a famous story. After a fierce battle, Benefactor drove his spear straight into the Blade of Flowers’s chest—bam! And the blood went splat!”
Please stop. That’s enough, you lunatic.
I had to shut him up, even now. I hurriedly opened my mouth, but before I could speak—
“I heard you even cursed at the Blade of Flowers. ‘Get your hands off me, you son of a bitch!’”
“...Where did you hear that?”
“Everyone I met seemed to know about it. When I told them I was close to Benefactor, lots of people came over and told me all kinds of things. The cook even packed me a ton of delicious food.”
No wonder he kept disappearing so often.
While staying with the Jin Family of Taiyuan, he must have wandered all over the place, eating plenty and listening to what people had to say.
And thanks to him, I’m fucked.
I swallowed hard and slowly turned my head.
Jeok Cheongang stood there with an utterly unreadable expression.
“It’s a misunderstanding.”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyebrow twitched.
“A misunderstanding?”
“Yes. Really. It truly is.”
“A misunderstanding. That’s possible. Rumors circulating through the Murim tend to get twisted and exaggerated.”
His dry voice continued.
“So you weren’t the one who killed the Blade of Flowers?”
“Uh... I was, actually. But the thing is—”
“Then there’s no need to hear any more.”
I could not finish my sentence.
Just a few steps away, Jeok Cheongang’s hands were blazing red.
Whoooosh.
I could feel it.
An overwhelming current of internal energy.
The cold shattered, and the scorching wind of a desert whipped around us. The heat forcing its way between my lips felt as though it would sear my lungs.
A memory from only a few months ago flashed through my mind.
The Flame Divine Palm?
That was it. The Flame Divine Palm.
But it was on an entirely different level from Jopil’s.
It was several times stronger. Stronger, stronger, and simply stronger.
Jeok Cheongang was no longer an old man with little time left to live.
He was the Fire King incarnate.
“You defied the sacred bonds of kinship and killed the Blade of Flowers. Are you even human?”
“W-wait! There are some very profound and complicated circumstances behind that...”
That was a mistake.
Instead of babbling about circumstances, I should have blurted out that the Head Elder had betrayed the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Profound and complicated circumstances?
Shit, you have to let me explain before you decide anything.
For a moment, I had forgotten who I was dealing with.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.

This was a man who had burned a thousand people to death for the simple offense of trespassing on his home and setting it on fire. Words like profound and complicated were light-years removed from him.
Whoooosh!
Damn old man...
No wonder they called him the Fire King. He was brutally straightforward and fiery as hell.
Feeling the heat of the Flame Divine Palm, I stared wide-eyed.
Is my life flashing before my eyes?
In a world slowed to a crawl, his flame-wreathed palm crept toward my chest.
If Jopil’s Flame Divine Palm had been beef-bone soup, this was spicy fish stew loaded with hot green chilies.
If I took a direct hit from that, I could not guarantee I would survive.
I have to block it.
The problem was, I could not move so much as a finger.
The whole world seemed to be moving in slow motion only because my brain had registered the threat of death. Jeok Cheongang had not slowed down, and I had not gotten any faster.
Damn it.
I desperately tried to raise my hand, but it was already too late.
Jeok Cheongang’s burning red palm filled my vision amid the darkness of despair.
Then—
Shiiiiing! Boom!
A streak of Sword Energy shot out of nowhere and slammed into Jeok Cheongang’s hand.
Brilliant violet Sword Energy.
It was Cheongpung.
Beyond the thunderous explosion, I heard his desperate cry.
“Benefactor!”
Even Cheongpung’s Sword Energy could not stop Jeok Cheongang’s Flame Divine Palm. It had only slowed it for the briefest instant.
But the crossroads between life and death was always decided in that instant.
Now!
The forty-five years of internal energy coiled within my dantian stirred awake.
Scorching Yang Qi flared like wildfire and surged through countless acupoints.
Its destination was my hands.
I thrust them forward with all my strength to meet Jeok Cheongang’s Flame Divine Palm.
Damn it. I don’t even have time to draw a weapon.
Of all the things I could have come up with against the Flame Divine Palm, I was using my bare hands.
It was clearly insane, but it was the best insanity I could manage in this situation.
I roared from the depths of my soul.
“Cheongpung, you son of a biiiiitch!”
The instant my hands met the Flame Divine Palm—
Gooooong.
A deafening blast of splitting air erupted.
The thunderous boom seemed to split the sky.
After a brief silence, things began to change.
Fssssss.
Everything crumbled into ash and scattered through the air.
The stone wall Jang Taebo had painstakingly built ten years ago. The few trees he had planted in one corner of the yard.
All of it.
Black ash fluttered down onto the old man’s white hair.
“W-what in the world...”
Jang Taebo could not stop trembling.
He had spent a long lifetime in the Murim—long enough for the mountains and rivers to have changed six times over, and then some.
He was merely a blacksmith who had never learned martial arts, but that was precisely why he had been able to meet so many people.
“I beg you. If that’s what you want, I’ll even give you my head!”
“Make me the finest sword under heaven.”
“Are you the Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild? I was sent by the Imperial Son-in-Law.”
From clueless martial artists to the leaders of renowned sects and great factions, even powerful figures from the imperial court had sought him out.
They came from every walk of life, but Jang Taebo’s answer was always the same.
“If you are worthy, I will make one for you.”
Jang Taebo believed that every blade had a soul.

For a blunt, rounded lump of metal to take shape, it had to endure thousands, tens of thousands, of hardships. It was bent countless times and beaten again and again. It was heated until it glowed, then cooled until it was cold.
Only once that long ordeal was over and it had finally taken shape did it gain a soul.
So it must also be my duty to choose a master worthy of the weapon.
Depending on whose hand wielded it, the weapon could become a killing blade or a life-giving blade.
Jang Taebo knew that better than anyone, which was why he never accepted a commission lightly.
One with a gentle nature. One overflowing with ambition. One determined to walk a path all his own...
No two people were alike. Countless people, each different from the next, had received weapons from him and returned to the Murim.
Some had died, while others survived.
But they all had one thing in common.
They were strong. Every last one of them.
They were masters capable of becoming the overlords of entire regions.
Strong enough to protect treasures coveted by all and use them as they saw fit.
Some had possessed martial arts that could be compared to those of the leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families.
But...
This is different. This man is different.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
The aura and martial arts erupting from that diminutive frame were beyond human.
Jang Taebo also realized that Jeok Cheongang would never need a weapon.
His martial arts have reached the heavens.
Whether he held something in his hands no longer mattered.
This was the Supreme Peak realm he had only vaguely imagined.
“Phew.”
Jang Taebo released the breath he had been holding. As the strength left his body, the object tucked inside his robe slipped to the ground.
So hard and light that it was difficult to believe it was a mineral, it gave off a faint glow even in broad daylight.
“Good grief!”
It was a treasure destined to be reborn as his final masterpiece—the greatest work of his life.
Jang Taebo hurriedly picked up the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron and clutched it to his chest.
Then he froze.
As he came to his senses, he suddenly remembered something he had forgotten.
His client.
“W-wait! Stop! I said stop!”
Jang Taebo scrambled to his feet and rushed forward.
A young man lay naked at Jeok Cheongang’s feet, every scrap of his clothing burned away. He was not moving at all.
“I-is he dead?”
Jeok Cheongang did not answer.
He merely looked back and forth between his hand and the young man, his face terrifyingly rigid.
“Say something!”
Jang Taebo burst out in fury and was just about to examine Jin Taekyung when a clear voice stopped him.
“He’s not dead. He only suffered an internal injury and lost consciousness for a moment.”
The owner of the voice continued.
“Right, Grandpa Jeok?”
When Jeok Cheongang finally answered, his voice was hoarse.
Every word revealed his surprise and the complicated emotions roiling inside him.
“I never intended to kill him in the first place.”
Just as Cheongpung and Jang Taebo sighed in relief, Jeok Cheongang added one short sentence.
“Until now, that is.”
“Don’t worry. I’ll decide what to do after I hear the full story.”
Jeok Cheongang stared strangely at the fallen Jin Taekyung.
“I have a great many questions for this boy.”
The words sounded almost threatening, prompting Jang Taebo to step forward.
Even witnessing the Fire King’s martial prowess firsthand had not shaken the resolve hardened by his long years.
“That sounds as though you intend to torture him.”
“I have no taste for that. But if it proves necessary...”

“Do you have any idea who that young man is? You may be a master counted among the Ten Kings, but if you think you can make an enemy of the entire Shanxi Murim and emerge unscathed, you are gravely mistaken!”
Jeok Cheongang gave a short laugh.
“There were once men who swallowed half the world with an army of one hundred thousand. Do you think I feared them?”
Jang Taebo was left speechless.
That was right. His opponent was the Fire King.
The old monster of Mount Jiuhua who had once fought alone against the Demonic Cult when it sought to rule the world.
Orthodox, unorthodox, or demonic—he belonged to none of them.
He had thrown his own weight onto the scales of war.
The reason was simple.
They had invaded his territory.
Jeok Cheongang stared at Jang Taebo with reddish eyes.
“I have one request. Please don’t ask anyone for help. I have no desire to burn down the Shanxi Murim at my age.”
He meant it.
And he possessed the power to make his words reality.
“Understood?”
“I-I’ll bear it in mind.”
“A wise decision.”
Jeok Cheongang grinned and turned away.
All the strength suddenly left Jang Taebo’s legs. As he began to fall, Cheongpung caught him and asked,
“Where are you going?”
“There’s an inn where you lot were staying, isn’t there? I’ll go ahead. Follow me.”
Cheongpung watched Jeok Cheongang’s back slowly recede and muttered plaintively,
“Whew. Grandfather was right. He really does have a strange personality.”
He said it so calmly that Jin Taekyung would have reached for a muzzle if he had heard.
Cheongpung turned to Jang Taebo and bowed deeply.
“Sorry for causing you so much trouble. We’ll be going now.”
Then he tucked Jin Taekyung under one arm and Hyuk Mujin under the other before trotting briskly away.
Jang Taebo stood there for a long while as though bewitched by a ghost.
Before long, he remembered the crucial fact that had momentarily slipped his mind.
Fire King, you goddamn old bastard.
There had to be a limit to this kind of outrageous behavior.
He had burned everything down, leaving nothing but the foundation stones.
Jang Taebo stared blankly at the ash drifting all around him, then let out a deep sigh.
“Fuck. This place is done for too.”
That was the moment his sweet retirement came to an end.

‘Get your hands off me, you son of a bitch!’”
“...Where did you hear that?”
“Everyone I met seemed to know about it.
When I told them I was close to Benefactor, lots of people came over and told me all kinds of things.
The cook even packed me a ton of delicious food.”
No wonder he kept disappearing so often.
While staying with the Jin Family of Taiyuan, he must have wandered all over the place, eating plenty and listening to what people had to say.
And thanks to him, I’m fucked.
I swallowed hard and slowly turned my head.
Jeok Cheongang stood there with an utterly unreadable expression.
“It’s a misunderstanding.”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyebrow twitched.
“A misunderstanding?”
“Yes.
Really.
It truly is.”
“A misunderstanding.
That’s possible.
Rumors circulating through the Murim tend to get twisted and exaggerated.”
His dry voice continued.
“So you weren’t the one who killed the Blade of Flowers?”
I was, actually.
But the thing is—”
“Then there’s no need to hear any more.”
I could not finish my sentence.
Just a few steps away, Jeok Cheongang’s hands were blazing red.
Whoooosh.
I could feel it.
An overwhelming current of internal energy.
The cold shattered, and the scorching wind of a desert whipped around us.
The heat forcing its way between my lips felt as though it would sear my lungs.
A memory from only a few months ago flashed through my mind.
The Flame Divine Palm?
That was it.
The Flame Divine Palm.
But it was on an entirely different level from Jopil’s.
It was several times stronger.
Stronger, stronger, and simply stronger.
Jeok Cheongang was no longer an old man with little time left to live.
He was the Fire King incarnate.
“You defied the sacred bonds of kinship and killed the Blade of Flowers.
Are you even human?”
“W-wait!
There are some very profound and complicated circumstances behind that...”
That was a mistake.
Instead of babbling about circumstances, I should have blurted out that the Head Elder had betrayed the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Profound and complicated circumstances?
Shit, you have to let me explain before you decide anything.
For a moment, I had forgotten who I was dealing with.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
This was a man who had burned a thousand people to death for the simple offense of trespassing on his home and setting it on fire.
Words like profound and complicated were light-years removed from him.
Whoooosh!
Damn old man...
No wonder they called him the Fire King.
He was brutally straightforward and fiery as hell.
Feeling the heat of the Flame Divine Palm, I stared wide-eyed.
Is my life flashing before my eyes?
In a world slowed to a crawl, his flame-wreathed palm crept toward my chest.
If Jopil’s Flame Divine Palm had been beef-bone soup, this was spicy fish stew loaded with hot green chilies.
If I took a direct hit from that, I could not guarantee I would survive.
I have to block it.
The problem was, I could not move so much as a finger.
The whole world seemed to be moving in slow motion only because my brain had registered the threat of death.
Jeok Cheongang had not slowed down, and I had not gotten any faster.
Damn it.
I desperately tried to raise my hand, but it was already too late.
Jeok Cheongang’s burning red palm filled my vision amid the darkness of despair.
Then—
Shiiiiing!
Boom!
A streak of Sword Energy shot out of nowhere and slammed into Jeok Cheongang’s hand.
Brilliant violet Sword Energy.
It was Cheongpung.
Beyond the thunderous explosion, I heard his desperate cry.
“Benefactor!”
Even Cheongpung’s Sword Energy could not stop Jeok Cheongang’s Flame Divine Palm.
It had only slowed it for the briefest instant.
But the crossroads between life and death was always decided in that instant.
Now!
The forty-five years of internal energy coiled within my dantian stirred awake.
Scorching Yang Qi flared like wildfire and surged through countless acupoints.
Its destination was my hands.
I thrust them forward with all my strength to meet Jeok Cheongang’s Flame Divine Palm.
Damn it.
I don’t even have time to draw a weapon.
Of all the things I could have come up with against the Flame Divine Palm, I was using my bare hands.
It was clearly insane, but it was the best insanity I could manage in this situation.
I roared from the depths of my soul.
“Cheongpung, you son of a biiiiitch!”
The instant my hands met the Flame Divine Palm—
Gooooong.
A deafening blast of splitting air erupted.
The thunderous boom seemed to split the sky.
After a brief silence, things began to change.
Fssssss.
Everything crumbled into ash and scattered through the air.
The stone wall Jang Taebo had painstakingly built ten years ago.
The few trees he had planted in one corner of the yard.
All of it.
Black ash fluttered down onto the old man’s white hair.
“W-what in the world...”
Jang Taebo could not stop trembling.
He had spent a long lifetime in the Murim—long enough for the mountains and rivers to have changed six times over, and then some.
He was merely a blacksmith who had never learned martial arts, but that was precisely why he had been able to meet so many people.
“I beg you.
If that’s what you want, I’ll even give you my head!”
“Make me the finest sword under heaven.”
“Are you the Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild?
I was sent by the Imperial Son-in-Law.”
From clueless martial artists to the leaders of renowned sects and great factions, even powerful figures from the imperial court had sought him out.
They came from every walk of life, but Jang Taebo’s answer was always the same.
“If you are worthy, I will make one for you.”
Jang Taebo believed that every blade had a soul.
For a blunt, rounded lump of metal to take shape, it had to endure thousands, tens of thousands, of hardships.
It was bent countless times and beaten again and again.
It was heated until it glowed, then cooled until it was cold.
Only once that long ordeal was over and it had finally taken shape did it gain a soul.
So it must also be my duty to choose a master worthy of the weapon.
Depending on whose hand wielded it, the weapon could become a killing blade or a life-giving blade.
Jang Taebo knew that better than anyone, which was why he never accepted a commission lightly.
One with a gentle nature.
One overflowing with ambition.
One determined to walk a path all his own...
No two people were alike.
Countless people, each different from the next, had received weapons from him and returned to the Murim.
Some had died, while others survived.
But they all had one thing in common.
They were strong.
Every last one of them.
They were masters capable of becoming the overlords of entire regions.
Strong enough to protect treasures coveted by all and use them as they saw fit.
Some had possessed martial arts that could be compared to those of the leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families.
But...
This is different.
This man is different.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
The aura and martial arts erupting from that diminutive frame were beyond human.
Jang Taebo also realized that Jeok Cheongang would never need a weapon.
His martial arts have reached the heavens.
Whether he held something in his hands no longer mattered.
This was the Supreme Peak realm he had only vaguely imagined.
“Phew.”
Jang Taebo released the breath he had been holding.
As the strength left his body, the object tucked inside his robe slipped to the ground.
So hard and light that it was difficult to believe it was a mineral, it gave off a faint glow even in broad daylight.
“Good grief!”
It was a treasure destined to be reborn as his final masterpiece—the greatest work of his life.
Jang Taebo hurriedly picked up the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron and clutched it to his chest.
Then he froze.
As he came to his senses, he suddenly remembered something he had forgotten.
His client.
“W-wait!
Stop!
I said stop!”
Jang Taebo scrambled to his feet and rushed forward.
A young man lay naked at Jeok Cheongang’s feet, every scrap of his clothing burned away.
He was not moving at all.
“I-is he dead?”
Jeok Cheongang did not answer.
He merely looked back and forth between his hand and the young man, his face terrifyingly rigid.
“Say something!”
Jang Taebo burst out in fury and was just about to examine Jin Taekyung when a clear voice stopped him.
“He’s not dead.
He only suffered an internal injury and lost consciousness for a moment.”
The owner of the voice continued.
“Right, Grandpa Jeok?”
When Jeok Cheongang finally answered, his voice was hoarse.
Every word revealed his surprise and the complicated emotions roiling inside him.
“I never intended to kill him in the first place.”
Just as Cheongpung and Jang Taebo sighed in relief, Jeok Cheongang added one short sentence.
“Until now, that is.”
“Don’t worry.
I’ll decide what to do after I hear the full story.”
Jeok Cheongang stared strangely at the fallen Jin Taekyung.
“I have a great many questions for this boy.”
The words sounded almost threatening, prompting Jang Taebo to step forward.
Even witnessing the Fire King’s martial prowess firsthand had not shaken the resolve hardened by his long years.
“That sounds as though you intend to torture him.”
“I have no taste for that.
But if it proves necessary...”
“Do you have any idea who that young man is?
You may be a master counted among the Ten Kings, but if you think you can make an enemy of the entire Shanxi Murim and emerge unscathed, you are gravely mistaken!”
Jeok Cheongang gave a short laugh.
“There were once men who swallowed half the world with an army of one hundred thousand.
Do you think I feared them?”
Jang Taebo was left speechless.
That was right.
His opponent was the Fire King.
The old monster of Mount Jiuhua who had once fought alone against the Demonic Cult when it sought to rule the world.
Orthodox, unorthodox, or demonic—he belonged to none of them.
He had thrown his own weight onto the scales of war.
The reason was simple.
They had invaded his territory.
Jeok Cheongang stared at Jang Taebo with reddish eyes.
“I have one request.
Please don’t ask anyone for help.
I have no desire to burn down the Shanxi Murim at my age.”
He meant it.
And he possessed the power to make his words reality.
“Understood?”
“I-I’ll bear it in mind.”
“A wise decision.”
Jeok Cheongang grinned and turned away.
All the strength suddenly left Jang Taebo’s legs.
As he began to fall, Cheongpung caught him and asked,
“Where are you going?”
“There’s an inn where you lot were staying, isn’t there?
I’ll go ahead.
Follow me.”
Cheongpung watched Jeok Cheongang’s back slowly recede and muttered plaintively,
“Whew.
Grandfather was right.
He really does have a strange personality.”
He said it so calmly that Jin Taekyung would have reached for a muzzle if he had heard.
Cheongpung turned to Jang Taebo and bowed deeply.
“Sorry for causing you so much trouble.
We’ll be going now.”
Then he tucked Jin Taekyung under one arm and Hyuk Mujin under the other before trotting briskly away.
Jang Taebo stood there for a long while as though bewitched by a ghost.
Before long, he remembered the crucial fact that had momentarily slipped his mind.
Fire King, you goddamn old bastard.
There had to be a limit to this kind of outrageous behavior.
He had burned everything down, leaving nothing but the foundation stones.
Jang Taebo stared blankly at the ash drifting all around him, then let out a deep sigh.
“Fuck.
This place is done for too.”
That was the moment his sweet retirement came to an end.

chapters.title: Chapter 175
paragraphs: In a shabby guest room, a diminutive old man silently gazed down at the young man lying on the bed.
Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Though he had yet to regain consciousness, Jin Taekyung’s face looked peaceful. At a glance, he might have been sound asleep.
He took the Flame Divine Palm, and this is all he suffered?
Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue inwardly.
The technique had been executed by his own hand—a Supreme Peak martial art.
He had held back, but even so, its power was not something a young punk who had only just broken through to Peak should have been able to withstand.
There was only one possible answer, and Jeok Cheongang already knew what it was.
This boy has cultivated the same kind of Scorching Yang Qi as I have.
But not all Scorching Yang Qi was the same.
In some ways, internal energy resembled a weapon. Its essence was one, but it could take many forms.
Advanced cultivation techniques each displayed their own distinct characteristics, like Huashan’s Zaha Divine Technique.
The same was true of the Fire Gate Clan, which Jeok Cheongang currently led as Sect Leader.
There’s no way this boy learned the Fire Gate Divine Technique.
For hundreds of years, the Fire Gate Clan had strictly upheld its tradition of passing its teachings down to a single successor.
As the current Sect Leader, Jeok Cheongang knew better than anyone that nothing had ever leaked during that succession.
And yet, Jin Taekyung bore traces of his school...
It must have been that, after all.
The Blazing Flame Divine Pill.
No matter how he considered it, that was the only answer.
Jeok Cheongang smiled bitterly, his expression so lonely that anyone who knew him would have doubted their own eyes.
“So this is how it ended.”
His aged voice echoed hollowly through the shabby guest room, then faded away.
For a long while, Jeok Cheongang’s gaze seemed to pursue something that could neither be seen nor grasped. At last, it settled on Jin Taekyung’s face.
His features were badly contorted, as though he were trapped in a nightmare.
“What is this old man to do with you...?”
At that moment, Jin Taekyung muttered something like a groan.
“Mmm... kimochiii.”
Kimo... what?
Jeok Cheongang could not understand the word, but something about hearing it made him deeply uncomfortable.
He watched Jin Taekyung twitch over and over, murmuring “kimochi” all the while, then slowly shook his head.
What a strange fellow.
He left only after “kimochi” turned into “yamete.”
Unable to endure any more, Jeok Cheongang fled the room with goose bumps prickling across his forearms.
...Is this some form of dark art after all?
His suspicions deepened.
When I opened my eyes, I saw a shabby ceiling.
A reddish oil lamp flickered nearby, and darkness had fallen beyond the window. A sigh of relief escaped me before I knew it.
“Pheeeew.”
I was alive.
I had suffered a minor Internal Injury, but I was grateful it was no worse than that.
No, considering that my opponent had been the Fire King, it was nothing short of a miracle.
Had he really not meant to kill me?
No matter what I tried, I was no match for the Fire King. The same went for Cheongpung.
And yet, here I was, lying on a bed...
“Are you awake?”
“Gah!”
I leaped up like a startled carp.
Something crouched in a dark corner had slowly risen to its feet.
“You scared me, you crazy bastard!”
Hyuk Mujin replied gruffly.
“Why are you so surprised? It’s not as if this is your first time seeing my face.”
“Have you looked at your face? You think anyone could get used to that?”
“What’s wrong with my face? I’m handsome enough. My parents even worried about me when I was little.”
“Because they thought you’d have trouble getting through life with that face?”
“No. They were worried I’d be kidnapped because I was too pretty for a boy.”
Was he out of his mind?
With looks like his, his parents should not have worried about him being kidnapped. They should have worried he would grow up to become the kidnapper.
“...Tell them they can stop worrying.”
“I’ll tell them later.”
Hyuk Mujin shuffled toward me, then gasped and collapsed onto the floor.
“Ah, aagh! Hold on.”
“What? What’s wrong?”
His face twisted in pain.
“A cramp. I-I’ve got a cramp.”
“...You’ve really done one thing after another today. Are you sure you’re a martial artist?”
“That can happen when you sit still for too long. And whose fault is it that I was stuck in that corner?”
“How is that my fault?”
“You kept making weird noises. Gimokji, yamakdae.”
The words were carved into my soul.
They were beyond familiar. They felt like old friends. I flinched and asked,
“...I said that?”
“Yes. It gave me goose bumps, so I went outside. Then Great Hero Jeok told me to get back in here and sit quietly unless I wanted to burn to death. He said to report to him the moment you woke up.”
Hyuk Mujin continued with an aggrieved expression.
“He said it might be some kind of dark art, so I should keep my ears covered. But you wouldn’t stop. You just kept going, ‘Oh? Ahh, gimokji, gimokji...’”
“...That’s enough, you bastard.”
This was the greatest humiliation of my life.
No wonder I had felt so electrified when I woke up. I must have been having a pretty good dream.
Just in case, I discreetly slipped a hand beneath the blanket.
Hmm. Clean. No problems.
With one problem taken care of, it was time to turn my attention to another.
In terms of importance, it was incomparably greater than the first.
My life was at stake, after all.
“Where’s that old geezer?”
There was no need to explain who I meant. Hyuk Mujin lowered his voice.
“He’s downstairs, drinking and carousing with Cheongpung.”
“He is? For how long?”
“I’m not sure. I only woke up a little while ago myself, but I asked the server, and he said they’d already been at it for more than three shichen.”
I did not even need to focus my internal energy.
My hearing had grown sharper after I reached Peak, and it carried the drunken shouts and singing from downstairs straight to my ears.
Listen to them having the time of their lives.
One was an old man who attacked first and asked questions later. The other was an oblivious idiot who had barged in and caused this whole disaster.
I wanted to smash those villains’ heads in with a liquor bottle and shout, “Justice has been served!” But I held myself back.
...More precisely, I had no choice but to restrain myself.
“Phew.”
Being powerless was a sin. A sin.
As I let out a deep sigh, Hyuk Mujin cautiously spoke up.
“Captain.”
“What?”
“I think we should head downstairs soon.”
“Why the hell would I go down there?”
“Great Hero Jeok said to bring you down as soon as you regained consciousness...”
“Great Hero, my ass. How is that old man a Great Hero?”
“You’d call him Great Hero if he were standing in front of you.”
He had me there.
But obeying and going downstairs would be no different from leaping straight into a tiger’s jaws.
I began pulling on the clothes draped over the table at the speed of light.
“What are you doing?”
“Getting ready to bolt.”
“What?”
“I said I’m running away. Why? You coming?”
Hyuk Mujin grabbed my arm in alarm.
“Why are you running away?”
“That old geezer could lose his temper and burn me to death at any moment. If you were me, wouldn’t you run?”
“Is this about what happened earlier?”
“If by that, you mean the Head Elder?”
“Yes. If that’s what you’re worried about, Cheongpung and I already...”
I firmly cut him off.
“You must have explained everything ages ago. The misunderstanding should be cleared up by now.”
“Oh, you know?”
“Do you think I’m an idiot?”
I had passed out around noon, so at least half a day had gone by. No matter how hot-tempered Jeok Cheongang was, he must have investigated enough to learn the truth.
Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin would have done their best to clear up the misunderstanding as well.
Hyuk Mujin tilted his head.
“Then isn’t everything fine? You have no reason to run.”
Every second counted.
Pretending to rummage through my clothes, I quickly pulled an item from my Inventory and waved it at him.
“Here’s your reason.”
Flame Divine Palm
Hyuk Mujin examined the cover of the weathered martial arts manual and muttered,
“Ah, shii...”
“All right, here’s a question. What exactly is the relationship between Jopil, who possessed the Fire Gate Clan’s Flame Divine Palm manual, and Jeok Cheongang?”
“You’re starting to see it too, aren’t you? I’d bet my wrist and my entire fortune that they were master and disciple. What are you willing to bet?”
Hyuk Mujin bet nothing.
Instead, he desperately spread the wings of an imagination full of dreams and hope.
“W-wait a second. The two of them might not be master and disciple.”
“If not master and disciple, then what? Father and son? Considering they both have such shitty tempers, that actually sounds plausible too. Right?”
“Jopil might have stolen Great Hero Jeok’s belongings.”
I snorted hard enough to nearly launch a booger out of my nose.
“You think the Fire King is some harmless old man from the neighborhood? Who would dare steal from that geezer?”
The Fire King had killed a thousand Demonic Cultists because they set fire near his home.
Jopil might have been crazy, but unless he had gotten Botox injected into his liver, he could not even have dreamed of doing such a thing.
After a moment’s hesitation, Hyuk Mujin nodded.
“...Fine. Let’s say Jopil was his Disciple.”
“I’m telling you, they were definitely master and disciple. And if you aren’t coming, let go of me. I’m busy.”
Hyuk Mujin ignored me and stubbornly continued.
“Even if Jopil was Great Hero Jeok’s Disciple, we were only doing our duty. Jopil was the one who attacked us and tried to kill us first.”
“Right. You and Cheongpung will be safe either way, so tell him that for me. I’ve got to get going.”
“Captain!”
“Now, Mujin. Let’s assume you’re right. Let’s say that foul-tempered old man admits his Disciple was at fault and lets the matter go. It’ll never happen, but let’s say he does.”
I peeled his hand away from my arm one finger at a time and asked,
“Then we’d still have to return everything Jopil stole, wouldn’t we?”
Hyuk Mujin nodded vigorously.
“Of course. If we kept it, we’d be asking to burn to death.”
“So what do you think would happen if we told him we couldn’t return it?”
“What? Captain, are you saying you want the Flame Divine Palm for yourself...?”
“Am I insane? Living a long and uneventful life is my philosophy. That’s why I even make my dumps thin and long on purpose!”
Under normal circumstances, he would have made a disgusted face and complained about my dirty talk. But now, he merely kept gulping dryly.
“Then what’s the problem?”
“The problem is that the Flame Divine Palm manual wasn’t the only thing Jopil had.”
I held up three fingers and began folding them down one by one.
“One, the Flame Divine Palm. Two, the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron sword. And finally, three...”
“The Blazing Flame Divine Pill.”
Hyuk Mujin’s jaw had already dropped at the mention of the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron sword. Now he looked at me uncertainly.
“...Do you mean that thing from back then? The one that massively boosts your internal energy but makes your body burst into flames?”
“Yeah. The one I was planning to give you along with the Flame Divine Palm manual a long time ago.”
“Where is it now? Where’s that thing?”
“Mujin.”
My eyes glistening, I gazed out the window toward the north—the direction of the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
“Remember when we went to the Mount Heng Sword Sect?”
“Why are you bringing that up all of a sudden?”
“The Red Wind Band Leader was stronger than I expected. How was I supposed to beat someone who’d defeated Cheol Mubaek and even Jin Mukyung?”
“H-hold on. Then, back then...?”
“Yeah. It worked like a charm.”
With the emotions of a woman three weeks pregnant who had just checked a pregnancy test, I stroked my stomach.
“I put it in here. The Blazing Flame Divine Pill.”
“They say it’s a secret divine elixir of the Fire Gate Clan. If I want to return it, I’ll have to cut open my stomach and drain the blood.”
“So stop holding me back. I’m casting off every shackle and restraint in this world and setting out to find a way to survive...”
At that moment, Hyuk Mujin moved with greater agility than ever before.
Tap-tap-tap—whoosh!
Clutching his ever-present satchel to his chest, he launched himself through the wide-open window.
In that moment, I saw a bird.
That bastard.
How dare he try to escape before me?
And he had even taken the satchel containing our silver nyang and food!
“Hey, Hyuk Mujin!”
By the time I hissed the words after him, it was already too late.
Hyuk Mujin glanced back at me with the serene eyes of a man who had attained enlightenment.
Then his body dropped straight down.
“Goddammit.”
I had to get out of there too.
I dashed to the window and was just about to throw myself outside when—
Crack! Thud!
Hyuk Mujin, who had been sprinting away for all he was worth, suddenly crumpled as though he had been shot.
The object that struck him squarely in the temple was one I knew very well.
“...A chicken bone?”
The next moment, an aged voice rose from below.
“You stupid fool. Can’t you tell a chicken from a duck?”
Step. Step.
A small shadow swayed in the light of the lantern hanging by the inn’s entrance.
A wrinkled face suddenly appeared. It looked up at me, my body draped over the window, and grinned.
“Where were you going?”
After witnessing 14,000,605 possible futures, I arrived at the most appropriate answer.
“To the privy.”
“Do you want to shit blood?”
“No.”
Yeah. I knew that would not work.

“What?
What’s wrong?”
His face twisted in pain.
“A cramp.
I-I’ve got a cramp.”
“...You’ve really done one thing after another today.
Are you sure you’re a martial artist?”
“That can happen when you sit still for too long.
And whose fault is it that I was stuck in that corner?”
“How is that my fault?”
“You kept making weird noises.
Gimokji, yamakdae.”
The words were carved into my soul.
They were beyond familiar.
They felt like old friends.
I flinched and asked,
“...I said that?”
“Yes.
It gave me goose bumps, so I went outside.
Then Great Hero Jeok told me to get back in here and sit quietly unless I wanted to burn to death.
He said to report to him the moment you woke up.”
Hyuk Mujin continued with an aggrieved expression.
“He said it might be some kind of dark art, so I should keep my ears covered.
But you wouldn’t stop.
You just kept going, ‘Oh?
Ahh, gimokji, gimokji...’”
“...That’s enough, you bastard.”
This was the greatest humiliation of my life.
No wonder I had felt so electrified when I woke up.
I must have been having a pretty good dream.
Just in case, I discreetly slipped a hand beneath the blanket.
Hmm.
Clean.
No problems.
With one problem taken care of, it was time to turn my attention to another.
In terms of importance, it was incomparably greater than the first.
My life was at stake, after all.
“Where’s that old geezer?”
There was no need to explain who I meant.
Hyuk Mujin lowered his voice.
“He’s downstairs, drinking and carousing with Cheongpung.”
“He is?
For how long?”
“I’m not sure.
I only woke up a little while ago myself, but I asked the server, and he said they’d already been at it for more than three shichen.”
I did not even need to focus my internal energy.
My hearing had grown sharper after I reached Peak, and it carried the drunken shouts and singing from downstairs straight to my ears.
Listen to them having the time of their lives.
One was an old man who attacked first and asked questions later.
The other was an oblivious idiot who had barged in and caused this whole disaster.
I wanted to smash those villains’ heads in with a liquor bottle and shout, “Justice has been served!” But I held myself back.
...More precisely, I had no choice but to restrain myself.
“Phew.”
Being powerless was a sin.
A sin.
As I let out a deep sigh, Hyuk Mujin cautiously spoke up.
“Captain.”
“What?”
“I think we should head downstairs soon.”
“Why the hell would I go down there?”
“Great Hero Jeok said to bring you down as soon as you regained consciousness...”
“Great Hero, my ass.
How is that old man a Great Hero?”
“You’d call him Great Hero if he were standing in front of you.”
He had me there.
But obeying and going downstairs would be no different from leaping straight into a tiger’s jaws.
I began pulling on the clothes draped over the table at the speed of light.
“What are you doing?”
“Getting ready to bolt.”
“What?”
“I said I’m running away.
Why?
You coming?”
Hyuk Mujin grabbed my arm in alarm.
“Why are you running away?”
“That old geezer could lose his temper and burn me to death at any moment.
If you were me, wouldn’t you run?”
“Is this about what happened earlier?”
“If by that, you mean the Head Elder?”
“Yes.
If that’s what you’re worried about, Cheongpung and I already...”
I firmly cut him off.
“You must have explained everything ages ago.
The misunderstanding should be cleared up by now.”
“Oh, you know?”
“Do you think I’m an idiot?”
I had passed out around noon, so at least half a day had gone by.
No matter how hot-tempered Jeok Cheongang was, he must have investigated enough to learn the truth.
Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin would have done their best to clear up the misunderstanding as well.
Hyuk Mujin tilted his head.
“Then isn’t everything fine?
You have no reason to run.”
Every second counted.
Pretending to rummage through my clothes, I quickly pulled an item from my Inventory and waved it at him.
“Here’s your reason.”
Flame Divine Palm
Hyuk Mujin examined the cover of the weathered martial arts manual and muttered,
“Ah, shii...”
“All right, here’s a question.
What exactly is the relationship between Jopil, who possessed the Fire Gate Clan’s Flame Divine Palm manual, and Jeok Cheongang?”
“You’re starting to see it too, aren’t you?
I’d bet my wrist and my entire fortune that they were master and disciple.
What are you willing to bet?”
Hyuk Mujin bet nothing.
Instead, he desperately spread the wings of an imagination full of dreams and hope.
“W-wait a second.
The two of them might not be master and disciple.”
“If not master and disciple, then what?
Father and son?
Considering they both have such shitty tempers, that actually sounds plausible too.
Right?”
“Jopil might have stolen Great Hero Jeok’s belongings.”
I snorted hard enough to nearly launch a booger out of my nose.
“You think the Fire King is some harmless old man from the neighborhood?
Who would dare steal from that geezer?”
The Fire King had killed a thousand Demonic Cultists because they set fire near his home.
Jopil might have been crazy, but unless he had gotten Botox injected into his liver, he could not even have dreamed of doing such a thing.
After a moment’s hesitation, Hyuk Mujin nodded.
“...Fine.
Let’s say Jopil was his Disciple.”
“I’m telling you, they were definitely master and disciple.
And if you aren’t coming, let go of me.
I’m busy.”
Hyuk Mujin ignored me and stubbornly continued.
“Even if Jopil was Great Hero Jeok’s Disciple, we were only doing our duty.
Jopil was the one who attacked us and tried to kill us first.”
“Right.
You and Cheongpung will be safe either way, so tell him that for me.
I’ve got to get going.”
“Captain!”
“Now, Mujin.
Let’s assume you’re right.
Let’s say that foul-tempered old man admits his Disciple was at fault and lets the matter go.
It’ll never happen, but let’s say he does.”
I peeled his hand away from my arm one finger at a time and asked,
“Then we’d still have to return everything Jopil stole, wouldn’t we?”
Hyuk Mujin nodded vigorously.
“Of course.
If we kept it, we’d be asking to burn to death.”
“So what do you think would happen if we told him we couldn’t return it?”
“What?
Captain, are you saying you want the Flame Divine Palm for yourself...?”
“Am I insane?
Living a long and uneventful life is my philosophy.
That’s why I even make my dumps thin and long on purpose!”
Under normal circumstances, he would have made a disgusted face and complained about my dirty talk.
But now, he merely kept gulping dryly.
“Then what’s the problem?”
“The problem is that the Flame Divine Palm manual wasn’t the only thing Jopil had.”
I held up three fingers and began folding them down one by one.
“One, the Flame Divine Palm.
Two, the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron sword.
And finally, three...”
“The Blazing Flame Divine Pill.”
Hyuk Mujin’s jaw had already dropped at the mention of the Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron sword.
Now he looked at me uncertainly.
“...Do you mean that thing from back then?
The one that massively boosts your internal energy but makes your body burst into flames?”
“Yeah.
The one I was planning to give you along with the Flame Divine Palm manual a long time ago.”
“Where is it now?
Where’s that thing?”
“Mujin.”
My eyes glistening, I gazed out the window toward the north—the direction of the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
“Remember when we went to the Mount Heng Sword Sect?”
“Why are you bringing that up all of a sudden?”
“The Red Wind Band Leader was stronger than I expected.
How was I supposed to beat someone who’d defeated Cheol Mubaek and even Jin Mukyung?”
“H-hold on.
Then, back then...?”
“Yeah.
It worked like a charm.”
With the emotions of a woman three weeks pregnant who had just checked a pregnancy test, I stroked my stomach.
“I put it in here.
The Blazing Flame Divine Pill.”
“They say it’s a secret divine elixir of the Fire Gate Clan.
If I want to return it, I’ll have to cut open my stomach and drain the blood.”
“So stop holding me back.
I’m casting off every shackle and restraint in this world and setting out to find a way to survive...”
At that moment, Hyuk Mujin moved with greater agility than ever before.
Tap-tap-tap—whoosh!
Clutching his ever-present satchel to his chest, he launched himself through the wide-open window.
In that moment, I saw a bird.
That bastard.
How dare he try to escape before me?
And he had even taken the satchel containing our silver nyang and food!
“Hey, Hyuk Mujin!”
By the time I hissed the words after him, it was already too late.
Hyuk Mujin glanced back at me with the serene eyes of a man who had attained enlightenment.
Then his body dropped straight down.
“Goddammit.”
I had to get out of there too.
I dashed to the window and was just about to throw myself outside when—
Crack!
Thud!
Hyuk Mujin, who had been sprinting away for all he was worth, suddenly crumpled as though he had been shot.
The object that struck him squarely in the temple was one I knew very well.
“...A chicken bone?”
The next moment, an aged voice rose from below.
“You stupid fool.
Can’t you tell a chicken from a duck?”
Step.
Step.
A small shadow swayed in the light of the lantern hanging by the inn’s entrance.
A wrinkled face suddenly appeared.
It looked up at me, my body draped over the window, and grinned.
“Where were you going?”
After witnessing 14,000,605 possible futures, I arrived at the most appropriate answer.
“To the privy.”
“Do you want to shit blood?”
“No.”
Yeah.
I knew that would not work.

chapters.title: Chapter 176
paragraphs: I feel like I’ve gone back to high school.
Like I got caught by the school disciplinarian while trying to sneak out of evening self-study. Of course, the despair I felt back then was nothing compared to this.
The person holding my ear right now wasn’t a school disciplinarian.
He was the Fire King.
Crack.
“Ah! Aaaagh! It hurts! Something just made a weird noise in my ear!”
Jeok Cheongang glared at me.
“Shall I make sure you never hear another sound?”
Judging by everything he had said and done so far, he was more than capable of following through.
I clamped my mouth shut and let Jeok Cheongang lead me along by the ear.
“Sit.”
“Yes, sir.”
I sat on a crude wooden chair and looked around.
The old inn was dark and gloomy. The owner was nowhere to be seen, and a server who looked barely twenty sat dozing at a table near the entrance.
Damn it. There aren’t even any other customers.
I must have been unconscious for longer than I thought. There were only four people on the first floor.
The dozing server, Jeok Cheongang, me—and Cheongpung, already dead drunk and sprawled face-down on the table, drooling.
It was the perfect place to die without anyone being the wiser.
No. They say that even in a tiger’s den, you’ll survive as long as you keep your wits about you.
Even so, I needed some kind of life insurance, just in case.
Unfortunately, the only brake capable of stopping Jeok Cheongang was currently fast asleep and snoring.
Cheongpung, you need to wake up if I’m going to survive this.
I was carefully stretching my leg beneath the table, preparing to step on Cheongpung’s foot, when—
“Let him sleep.”
“Huh?”
“I said leave him alone. Don’t bother the boy when he’s sleeping.”
At this point, he might as well have been a ghost.
I hadn’t made a sound or even moved noticeably, yet he knew exactly what I was doing beneath the table.
“Your answer?”
“...I’ll stay still.”
“You’re not entirely clueless, I see. You might live a long life yet.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered something that could have been either praise or an insult, then tilted the liquor bottle.
As the empty cup slowly filled, the cheap liquor’s sharp scent stung my nose.
“I have something to ask you.”
“I’ll explain everything in detail about the Head Elder—no, my great-uncle.”
“I’ve already heard. He committed more than enough crimes to deserve death. He was a fairly sharp fellow once, but time has ruined a lot of people...”
Jeok Cheongang downed his drink in one gulp and muttered bitterly,
“That child was like that, too.”
“Where did you meet him?”
The question came out of nowhere, but I understood immediately.
The “child” Jeok Cheongang had just mentioned was Jopil.
He already knew that Jopil and I were connected. The worst possible situation had become reality.
“If you’re thinking of lying, you’d better abandon the idea now. You’ll end up telling the truth anyway.”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice sank like an abyss, sending a shiver down my spine.
There was no point in lying or making excuses anymore. Right now, he was the prosecutor, the defense attorney, and the judge who could hand down any sentence he pleased.
Damn it.
My parched mouth tasted bitter. He wasn’t even releasing Scorching Yang Qi, yet I was so thirsty I could barely speak.
“Give me a drink too.”
“You cheeky bastard.”
Despite saying that, Jeok Cheongang readily filled my cup.
I hurriedly gulped down the strong liquor, and only then could I breathe again.
Right. It wasn’t over yet. The more dangerous the situation, the more I needed to keep my wits about me if I wanted to escape it.
I took a deep breath and began.
“It was about two months ago. That’s when I met Jopil.”
“Jopil?”
“Yes. One Question, One Kill, Jopil. He was a fairly famous wandering martial artist.”
“Judging by his alias, he probably wasn’t famous for anything good.”
“...You could say that.”
He hadn’t just been bad. He had been practically insane.
Back then, I had seen Jopil as nothing more or less than a man obsessed with killing. He had genuinely enjoyed it.
“Is this his face?”
Jeok Cheongang pulled a sheet of paper from inside his robe.
It was so old that it had yellowed with age and was crumpled all over, but the young man’s face drawn on it was still easy to recognize.
“Is that Jopil when he was young?”
“It seems it was him after all. So that’s what became of him.”
His words sounded more like a monologue than an answer to my question.
After remaining silent for a while, Jeok Cheongang suddenly spoke again.
“More than twenty years ago, a terrible epidemic swept through Anhui Province. Countless commoners died, and even more children were left orphaned. He was one of them.”
The moment had come for Jopil’s true identity, unknown to everyone, to be revealed. Depending on what Jeok Cheongang said next, my future would be decided.
I held my breath and listened.
Jeok Cheongang continued slowly. As the clear liquor rippled in his cup, memories of those days rose vividly to the surface.
“He was a child struggling desperately to survive. Even while a dozen or so people surrounded him and trampled him, he shoved a dirt-covered dumpling into his mouth.”
“I liked the fierceness in his eyes, and I pitied him too. I gave him the name Jangcheon—Vast Sky.”
That was how Jangcheon came to live in a hut deep within Mount Jiuhua.
He was the first outsider to set foot there in the fifty long years since Jeok Cheongang had seen his Master off.
“At first, he knew nothing. It wasn’t until a year later that he realized I was a martial artist. Soon afterward, he began begging me to teach him martial arts.”
To an orphan with no one in the world, who had lived amid contempt and hunger, martial artists might as well have been beings from the heavens.
The boy wanted to become a martial artist and change his life. That was why he desperately clung to the old man who had saved him.
“Please accept me as your Disciple.”
“No.”
“Master!”
“Master? Who said I was your Master? You lack both the physique and martial talent to learn our sect’s arts.”
“I’ll do it. I’ll find a way to prove myself. Even if it kills me, I won’t disappoint you, Master!”
“...Don’t be ridiculous.”
Jeok Cheongang thought Jangcheon would not last long.

But the boy’s determination was far more tenacious than he had expected. For an entire year, Jangcheon tried to persuade him every single day. Eventually, he even went so far as to injure himself and refuse food.
Each time, Jeok Cheongang was the one left sweating bullets.
“You fool. Why would you do something like this?”
“I want to learn martial arts. Please accept me as your Disciple.”
“...I can’t.”
“Is it because I’m lacking?”
“It is an unavoidable decision if I am to continue the sect’s lineage. This will be difficult for you too.”
“No matter how difficult it is, I can endure it!”
“No. If you insist on being this stubborn, I’ll have no choice but to send you down the mountain. Is that what you want?”
In truth, Jeok Cheongang was the one who did not want them to part.

With the infirmities of old age creeping up on him, it seemed he had grown lonely for human company. A year had been more than enough time for him to grow attached to the scarred, taciturn boy who had endured far too much for his age.
But...
“Then do it. I’m destined to die anyway, aren’t I?”
“What?”
“If I can’t serve you as my Master, I’ll kill myself. No—kill me now. Kill me with the same hand that saved me.”
“You little—!”
What was so important about martial arts?
Seeing Jangcheon ready to throw away his own life for them, Jeok Cheongang felt hurt and furious.
But at the same time, another thought occurred to him.
“His martial talent and physical aptitude may have been lacking, but with tenacity like that, I thought he was bound to achieve Great Completion one day.”
Jin Taekyung, who had been listening quietly, asked with an uneasy expression,
“That kind of tenacity... Is that why you accepted him as your Disciple?”
“Yes.”
Jeok Cheongang added with a sigh,
“It was a mistake.”
That was the most painful mistake he had made in all the hundred years since his birth.
“For several years, everything went smoothly. He improved so quickly that the concerns I’d had before accepting him as my Disciple seemed foolish.”
Jangcheon followed his Master’s instructions faithfully.
No—it was closer to absolute obedience.

He swung his sword like a madman all day long and devoted himself to training his stamina. Even when learning the smallest, most basic techniques, he poured his entire being into them as though he were practicing the greatest martial art under heaven.
With his Disciple training with such passion and devotion, Jeok Cheongang could not help but be deeply moved. He did everything in his power to help Jangcheon grow.
Jangcheon’s talent and physical aptitude were only slightly above average, but Jeok Cheongang gradually improved his constitution by cleansing his sinews and washing his marrow.
A Master and Disciple who trusted and relied on each other.
Remarkable achievements.
Everything seemed to be going perfectly.
“The problem came afterward.”
The old man remained old, but the boy grew into a young man.
Yet his martial arts failed to develop along with his body. Jangcheon grew furious with himself after spending years making no progress, and eventually, something happened.

“I still remember it clearly. I had more trouble sleeping than usual that night, so I was sitting on a rock when he came up from below. He’d been out of sight for several days, claiming he was in closed-door cultivation.”
Jin Taekyung tilted his head.
“What do you mean, he came up from below?”
“He had gone to the village. The wind carried the musk courtesans use.”
“Oh. A pleasure house?”

“I understood. He had spent more than ten years learning nothing but martial arts, barely ever leaving the mountain. What could I say when his own Master had been of so little help and cared only for his own cultivation?”
At the time, Jeok Cheongang had been immersed in training to open his upper dantian.

Opening the upper dantian meant entering the Martial Extremity realm. It would not only raise his martial arts to another level, but also treat the infirmities of old age that were steadily eating away at him.
“But it wasn’t easy. It required lengthy preparation, time, and enlightenment.”
As a result, Master and Disciple gradually began seeing less of each other.
Jeok Cheongang believed that his Disciple, who had always worked so hard, would attain enlightenment on his own, so he focused on cultivating his upper dantian.
He noticed Jangcheon’s trips down the mountain only on the occasional days when the wind carried a mixture of unfamiliar scents.
“Then one day, a visitor came.”
“A visitor?”
“The Azure Sky Sword King. I had never seen his face before, but I recognized him immediately. He was exactly as I’d heard.”
Jin Taekyung’s jaw dropped.
“The Azure Sky Sword King? One of the Ten Kings?”
“Yes. He was also the Grand Family Head of the Namgung Family.”
“Why did he come?”
Jeok Cheongang tilted the liquor bottle without a word.
He had already emptied several bottles by himself, yet his mind only grew clearer. So too did the words the Azure Sky Sword King had spoken when he appeared without warning.

“These days, the brats in my family have been throwing a fit. There’s some vicious bastard running wild in Anhui, but they say they can’t catch him. They begged me so desperately that I had no choice but to come see you.”
Jeok Cheongang had been bewildered.
The Namgung Family’s influence in Anhui was immense.
If even their power had proven insufficient, to the point that the Azure Sky Sword King himself had to step in, then just how powerful was this bastard?
“Then why did you come to me? Are you saying the bastard is some kind of Martial God?”
“If he were a Martial God, he wouldn’t be killing only innocent women and mediocre wandering martial artists. I saw him once from a distance, but I let him go.”
“What does that—”
“A Master should correct his Disciple’s mistakes, shouldn’t he?”
Not long after the Azure Sky Sword King left, Jeok Cheongang stood absentmindedly on the rock and caught a scent carried on the wind.
It was the smell of blood.

“If I can’t serve you as my Master, I’ll kill myself.
No—kill me now.
Kill me with the same hand that saved me.”
“You little—!”
What was so important about martial arts?
Seeing Jangcheon ready to throw away his own life for them, Jeok Cheongang felt hurt and furious.
But at the same time, another thought occurred to him.
“His martial talent and physical aptitude may have been lacking, but with tenacity like that, I thought he was bound to achieve Great Completion one day.”
Jin Taekyung, who had been listening quietly, asked with an uneasy expression,
“That kind of tenacity...
Is that why you accepted him as your Disciple?”
“Yes.”
Jeok Cheongang added with a sigh,
“It was a mistake.”
That was the most painful mistake he had made in all the hundred years since his birth.
“For several years, everything went smoothly.
He improved so quickly that the concerns I’d had before accepting him as my Disciple seemed foolish.”
Jangcheon followed his Master’s instructions faithfully.
No—it was closer to absolute obedience.
He swung his sword like a madman all day long and devoted himself to training his stamina.
Even when learning the smallest, most basic techniques, he poured his entire being into them as though he were practicing the greatest martial art under heaven.
With his Disciple training with such passion and devotion, Jeok Cheongang could not help but be deeply moved.
He did everything in his power to help Jangcheon grow.
Jangcheon’s talent and physical aptitude were only slightly above average, but Jeok Cheongang gradually improved his constitution by cleansing his sinews and washing his marrow.
A Master and Disciple who trusted and relied on each other.
Remarkable achievements.
Everything seemed to be going perfectly.
“The problem came afterward.”
The old man remained old, but the boy grew into a young man.
Yet his martial arts failed to develop along with his body.
Jangcheon grew furious with himself after spending years making no progress, and eventually, something happened.
“I still remember it clearly.
I had more trouble sleeping than usual that night, so I was sitting on a rock when he came up from below.
He’d been out of sight for several days, claiming he was in closed-door cultivation.”
Jin Taekyung tilted his head.
“What do you mean, he came up from below?”
“He had gone to the village.
The wind carried the musk courtesans use.”
“Oh.
A pleasure house?”
“I understood.
He had spent more than ten years learning nothing but martial arts, barely ever leaving the mountain.
What could I say when his own Master had been of so little help and cared only for his own cultivation?”
At the time, Jeok Cheongang had been immersed in training to open his upper dantian.
Opening the upper dantian meant entering the Martial Extremity realm.
It would not only raise his martial arts to another level, but also treat the infirmities of old age that were steadily eating away at him.
“But it wasn’t easy.
It required lengthy preparation, time, and enlightenment.”
As a result, Master and Disciple gradually began seeing less of each other.
Jeok Cheongang believed that his Disciple, who had always worked so hard, would attain enlightenment on his own, so he focused on cultivating his upper dantian.
He noticed Jangcheon’s trips down the mountain only on the occasional days when the wind carried a mixture of unfamiliar scents.
“Then one day, a visitor came.”
“A visitor?”
“The Azure Sky Sword King.
I had never seen his face before, but I recognized him immediately.
He was exactly as I’d heard.”
Jin Taekyung’s jaw dropped.
“The Azure Sky Sword King?
One of the Ten Kings?”
“Yes.
He was also the Grand Family Head of the Namgung Family.”
“Why did he come?”
Jeok Cheongang tilted the liquor bottle without a word.
He had already emptied several bottles by himself, yet his mind only grew clearer.
So too did the words the Azure Sky Sword King had spoken when he appeared without warning.
“These days, the brats in my family have been throwing a fit.
There’s some vicious bastard running wild in Anhui, but they say they can’t catch him.
They begged me so desperately that I had no choice but to come see you.”
Jeok Cheongang had been bewildered.
The Namgung Family’s influence in Anhui was immense.
If even their power had proven insufficient, to the point that the Azure Sky Sword King himself had to step in, then just how powerful was this bastard?
“Then why did you come to me?
Are you saying the bastard is some kind of Martial God?”
“If he were a Martial God, he wouldn’t be killing only innocent women and mediocre wandering martial artists.
I saw him once from a distance, but I let him go.”
“What does that—”
“A Master should correct his Disciple’s mistakes, shouldn’t he?”
Not long after the Azure Sky Sword King left, Jeok Cheongang stood absentmindedly on the rock and caught a scent carried on the wind.
It was the smell of blood.

chapters.title: Chapter 177
paragraphs: Why hadn’t I known?

Perhaps it was the faith I had placed in the Disciple I’d raised as my own flesh and blood. Perhaps it was indifference. But the scent of blood had unmistakably clung to Jangcheon as he staggered up the mountain that day.
“Where have you been?”
“Ah, Master.”
His eyes were flushed with drink—and something else.
“I went down to the village for a little while. I’ve been feeling restless lately, so I had a drink.”
“Drinking. Was that all?”
“It’s a little embarrassing to say. Hahaha! I’m sorry you had to see me like this.”
The pungent musk courtesans used stung Jeok Cheongang’s nose. But it was merely a veil meant to conceal the truth.
Beneath it, he could smell the faint scent of blood. The smell of death. The smell of a killer—a scent he had forgotten since the Great Faction War.
“You went to a pleasure house...?”
“As expected, I can’t fool you, Master. Yes. This useless Disciple was troubled, so I sought the company of women.”
The Disciple he had not seen in so long had become a completely different person.
The taciturn, unsmiling boy was gone. In his place stood a smooth-talking killer who concealed his murders without a trace of concern.
“But what brings you out at this late hour? Have you made any progress in your closed-door cultivation?”
“...It had been so long since I’d seen your face. I was waiting for you.”
He had apparently murdered dozens of innocent commoners in horrific ways.

His Disciple had committed a crime that made heaven and earth furious. The right thing to do would have been to sever his Sinews and Meridians and cripple his dantian at once. That was what a Master should do.
But—
“I see. I’m glad to see you too, Master.”
At Jangcheon’s faint smile, Jeok Cheongang found himself unable to speak. He felt neither anger nor betrayal. Something simply welled up from deep inside him, choking off his words.
In the end, there was only one thing he could say.
“It’s late. Go get some rest.”
Jin Taekyung listened to Jeok Cheongang’s story with disbelief written across his face.
“Wait. That’s it?”
“I wanted to believe in that child.”
“You already knew. You knew Jopil—or rather, Jangcheon—was lying.”
“I knew.”
“And you still let the bastard go?”
“Yes. Even so.”
The old man continued in a weary voice.
“Do you have any blood relatives?”
“Yes.”
“I have none. As far back as I can remember, I was alone. He was the same.”
Jeok Cheongang looked down at his hands. Age spots and wrinkles covered them, each one bearing the imprint of the years.

“My Master was a strict man. His training was harsh and painful, but as a child, I even liked that. I was happy simply knowing that someone cared about me and was there beside me. My Master was the only person I could rely on.”
But his time with his Master had been brief. Jeok Cheongang was left alone once more, and over the years, his loneliness slowly grew numb.
Until he met a child in the marketplace, fighting desperately to protect a single dumpling.
“I was the only person that child could rely on. Even if all under heaven pointed fingers at him, I had to believe in him.”
At some point, Jangcheon had become more than a Disciple to Jeok Cheongang.
He was his only son and his grandson. They shared no blood, but Jeok Cheongang loved him more deeply than family.
“But what that child did was too horrible. I had to make him stop. One way or another.”
Before that, however, he wanted to see his Disciple’s atrocities with his own eyes.
The fact that the Azure Sky Sword King had come in person meant that all the circumstantial and physical evidence was already in hand. But that alone was not enough.
“So I began following him in secret.”
From that day on, Jeok Cheongang followed his Disciple. Evading Jangcheon’s notice was easy, since he had yet to break through to the Peak realm.
Once, twice, ten times...
With each pursuit, the despair Jeok Cheongang had initially felt began to fade.

Like any other wastrel, Jangcheon merely visited pleasure houses, drank, and embraced women. When he returned to his hut flushed with liquor, he became a martial artist once more and diligently resumed his training.
Nothing seemed amiss.
“Then a thought occurred to me. Perhaps there had been some mistake. Perhaps the Namgung Family and the Azure Sky Sword King had misjudged him.”
Jin Taekyung stared at him incredulously.
“I think you’re the one who misjudged him, Sir Jeok.”
Jeok Cheongang laughed hollowly.
“Yes. I did. Like a fool, I desperately turned away from the truth.”
“So did you eventually see it for yourself?”
Jeok Cheongang silently raised the bottle and drank straight from it.
The ceiling looked blurry, not because the liquor was strong, but because the memory of that day had returned with perfect clarity.
Thud. Thud. Thud.
In a back alley of the red-light district, beneath the heavy darkness of night, muffled groans mingled with spurts of blood.
The back of the masked man stabbing and prodding someone’s limbs with a sharp dagger was more familiar than anything—and more foreign than ever.
“...Jangcheon.”
At the quiet call, the hand gripping the dagger abruptly froze. The masked man slowly turned, and his eyes met Jeok Cheongang’s.
At the sight of his Master after so long, the Disciple’s eyes curved into crescents.
“Ah, Master.”
“What... What are you doing?”
“What do you mean? Exactly what you see.”
Jangcheon grinned and drove the dagger down.
Thud. Thud. Thud.
The middle-aged man, his limbs bound, writhed in agony.
“Stop at once!”
“Why should I?”
“...W-What did you say?”

“It’s been a long time since I came down here, and all kinds of people are running wild. Wandering martial artists swaggering around because they know a few Third Rate martial arts, merchants with fat bulging from their bodies, and women whose only property they can sell is their own bodies. What a madhouse.”
Jangcheon flashed a white smile.
“This man is just one of them. What difference does it make if I kill one such person? He’s nothing more than a two-legged beast with no reason to live.”
Everything felt like a dream to Jeok Cheongang. The hope he had clung to while watching his Disciple for the past four months vanished like a bursting bubble.
“Why... Why would you do this?”
“Because I’m strong.”
Jangcheon continued, his voice brimming with excitement.
“Might makes right. Didn’t you teach me that, Master? Murim—no, the entire world—is like that. The weak die at the hands of the strong.”
“You killed innocent people for no better reason than that?”
“Innocent? How could you possibly know they were innocent, Master?”
“Then what terrible crimes did the people you killed commit?”
Jeok Cheongang wanted them to have deserved death.

He wanted them to have been corrupt merchants who sucked the lifeblood from others, or vicious ruffians who murdered as casually as they ate—not simple commoners who knew nothing of the world and spent their lives toiling like oxen.
But...
“How should I know?”
“Who in this world lives without sin? They were simply unlucky. The same goes for this man who happened to catch my eye.”
The world seemed to recede before Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.
The Disciple he loved like his own flesh and blood had already crossed a river from which there was no return.
Those who reached the far bank never came back. They lived out the rest of their days as blood-soaked killing fiends.
“Jangcheon.”
“Yes, Master.”
The face of the scrawny child he had met in the marketplace more than a decade ago overlapped with that of the blood-drenched young man before him.
“What in the world made you like this?”
“What do you mean?”
“You... You weren’t this kind of child. The weak die at the hands of the strong? Have you forgotten the person you once were, struggling desperately just to survive?”
“I haven’t forgotten. That’s why I am who I am now.”
“No. You were kind and diligent...”
“Master.”
Jangcheon gently cut him off.
It was the first time the Disciple had ever interrupted or contradicted his Master. But now, even open mockery lingered at the corners of Jangcheon’s mouth.

“I remember the day I first met you as clearly as if it were yesterday. I had gone hungry for days and was wandering the marketplace when I found a dirt-covered dumpling. Even as boys no better off than I was trampled me, I kept forcing it into my mouth.”
“That’s right. You did it to survive. Why can’t you remember that you were once weak too?”
Jangcheon’s lips twisted.
“Wangpal. Hong Sochil. So U-pyeong.”
“Three of the fifteen who tried to take my dumpling. Unfortunately, the others were already dead.”
Three names fell from his Disciple’s lips.
Their meaning was unmistakable. Those three no longer belonged to this world. And until the moment they breathed their last, they must have suffered unimaginable pain.

“They didn’t remember me, but I never forgot them for a single day. More than ten years ago, as I chewed that dirt-covered dumpling, I realized something. So this is the world. The weak are trampled, and the strong do the trampling. Then I must become strong. I must enjoy the rights of the strong.”
As Jangcheon recited the vow he had made that day in a chilling voice, Jeok Cheongang finally understood.
“You... You...”
“Yes. I never changed. Not once, from the day I first met you until now.”
His white teeth gleamed in the darkness. Jangcheon giggled.

“It was thrilling. At first, they begged me to spare them. Later, they screamed at me to kill them. But once they finally fell silent, I felt empty inside. Drinking myself senseless at a pleasure house and embracing a woman couldn’t make the feeling go away.”
He could only have been a born Slaughter Saint.
Only murder could fill that emptiness. Jangcheon would likely go on killing until the moment he drew his final breath.
“The timing was perfect. You happened to be so absorbed in your training that you neglected me, which allowed me to run wild to my heart’s content.”
Jeok Cheongang wanted to cover his ears. He wanted to cover his ears, close his eyes, and erase the memory of that day, which had been branded into his mind.
His body trembled with rage and betrayal toward the Disciple he had raised as his own kin.
But what tormented him most was the affection he still felt for that Disciple.

“Of course, I wasn’t entirely at ease either. Was it four months ago? I came back after taking care of some business and found you waiting for me. The moment I saw you acting unlike yourself, I knew I’d been found out.”
“Stop.”
“You trusted me far too completely to start following me for no reason, so someone must have tipped you off... Ah, it must have been the Namgung Family.”
“I said shut up!”
A tremendous wave of qi tore through the alley.
Confronted with a fury he had never before seen from his Master, Jangcheon’s eyes widened.
“Master?”
“You bastard! How dare you call me Master with that mouth? Do you still not understand what you’ve done?”
“Why are you acting like this? Surely you don’t intend to cast aside your only Disciple over something so trivial?”
“Trivial? Did you call this trivial?”
“Master, you’re like a father to me. I believed that even if everyone under heaven condemned my faults, you would understand. Because you’re my father.”
Father.
The word Jeok Cheongang had wanted so desperately to hear.
He gritted his teeth.
“You’re wrong.”
“Wrong?”
Jangcheon smiled faintly.
“Then why don’t you strike me dead right now? You had countless chances, both now and throughout the past four months.”
“That’s—”
“Am I wrong?”
Jeok Cheongang could not answer. Everything Jangcheon had said was true. He had deliberately looked away from the truth and tried to justify doing so.
Because no matter what it took, he had wanted to believe in his Disciple.
A long time passed before he finally spoke.
“I’ll sever your Sinews and Meridians.”
“My Sinews and Meridians. And then?”
“I’ll cripple your dantian. You’ll spend the rest of your life repenting for your crimes.”
“Facing a wall in meditation until the day I die. The very thought is horrifying.”
Despite his words, Jangcheon’s face was full of laughter.
“But did our sect’s rules change while this useless Disciple wasn’t looking? As I understand it, a case like this calls for immediate execution, no questions asked.”
“...This is my final act of mercy. Put that man down and step away at once.”
Jangcheon blinked as if he had forgotten something important.
The middle-aged man in his arms, his entire body drenched in blood, was still drawing ragged breaths.
“Ah, right. I’d forgotten about him.”
Slash.
Blood erupted in a fountain.
Jeok Cheongang stared at it with trembling eyes.
Jangcheon’s hand had moved without the slightest hesitation. The man’s throat had been cut. His body convulsed, then fell still.
“Is this your answer?”
“It’s already too late. Even if I saved him, he would spend the rest of his life crippled. Wouldn’t it be better to give him a clean death?”
“You... You’re no longer the child I knew.”
“I am exactly the child you knew, Master. You simply misunderstood me from the very beginning.”
“Enough. Your evil deeds end today.”
“Do you truly intend to cripple me and make me spend the rest of my life facing a wall?”
A faint fear showed on his Disciple’s face.
Jeok Cheongang clenched his fist until blood seeped from his palm. One move. A single move was all it would take to erase Jangcheon from this world.
But he knew he could not bring himself to do it.
Severing his Disciple’s Sinews and Meridians, crippling his martial arts, and imprisoning him was the best he could do.
“Do you regret it?”
“Regret?”
“Yes. Regret.”
It would change nothing, but Jeok Cheongang wanted to hear the answer from Jangcheon’s own lips.
Then, in the next instant, every trace of fear vanished from Jangcheon’s face.
“I was relieved.”
“What?”
“I couldn’t see or hear you, but I knew you had been watching me for the past four months. Why else do you think I did this right in front of you?”
Jangcheon’s face was reflected in Jeok Cheongang’s vacant eyes. He continued with perfect composure.
“You can’t kill me, Master. It wouldn’t matter if I killed not dozens but hundreds. Before I left, I wanted to confirm that one last time.”
“Before you leave? What do you mean?”
“There may be fathers who blame their children for their faults, but there is no father anywhere in this world who kills his own child with his own hands.”

“Thank you, Master. Thank you for raising me as your child rather than merely your Disciple. Thank you for trying to save a child like me until the very end. Thanks to you, my one path to survival has opened.”
Jeok Cheongang stood frozen as if his breath had stopped. Before him, Jangcheon gave a deep bow filled with genuine sincerity.
When he raised his head again, a small white porcelain vial was held between his lips.
“It’s Bone-Melting Powder.”
Bone-Melting Powder was a deadly poison that dissolved flesh and bone.
Even a tiny amount would be fatal if the vial shattered inside his mouth. Not even a celestial immortal could save him.
Jeok Cheongang roared in fury.
“Jangcheon! You bastard!”
“That bow I just gave you... was my final farewell. I’m leaving now. I’ll go far away and never return.”
“You think I’ll let you leave like this?”
“Then kill me. That’s the only way.”
“Kill me.”
Kill me.
Those were his Disciple’s final words.
Jeok Cheongang blinked. The ceiling had looked blurry for some time, and now something was running down his cheek.
“The inn is old. Rain must be leaking through.”
It was a winter night, one day before New Year’s Day.
