At first, they begged me to spare them.
Later, they screamed at me to kill them.
But once they finally fell silent, I felt empty inside.
Drinking myself senseless at a pleasure house and embracing a woman couldn’t make the feeling go away.”
He could only have been a born Slaughter Saint.
Only murder could fill that emptiness.
Jangcheon would likely go on killing until the moment he drew his final breath.
“The timing was perfect.
You happened to be so absorbed in your training that you neglected me, which allowed me to run wild to my heart’s content.”
Jeok Cheongang wanted to cover his ears.
He wanted to cover his ears, close his eyes, and erase the memory of that day, which had been branded into his mind.
His body trembled with rage and betrayal toward the Disciple he had raised as his own kin.
But what tormented him most was the affection he still felt for that Disciple.
“Of course, I wasn’t entirely at ease either.
Was it four months ago?
I came back after taking care of some business and found you waiting for me.
The moment I saw you acting unlike yourself, I knew I’d been found out.”
“Stop.”
“You trusted me far too completely to start following me for no reason, so someone must have tipped you off...
Ah, it must have been the Namgung Family.”
“I said shut up!”
A tremendous wave of qi tore through the alley.
Confronted with a fury he had never before seen from his Master, Jangcheon’s eyes widened.
“Master?”
“You bastard!
How dare you call me Master with that mouth?
Do you still not understand what you’ve done?”
“Why are you acting like this?
Surely you don’t intend to cast aside your only Disciple over something so trivial?”
“Trivial?
Did you call this trivial?”
“Master, you’re like a father to me.
I believed that even if everyone under heaven condemned my faults, you would understand.
Because you’re my father.”
Father.
The word Jeok Cheongang had wanted so desperately to hear.
He gritted his teeth.
“You’re wrong.”
“Wrong?”
Jangcheon smiled faintly.
“Then why don’t you strike me dead right now?
You had countless chances, both now and throughout the past four months.”
“That’s—”
“Am I wrong?”
Jeok Cheongang could not answer.
Everything Jangcheon had said was true.
He had deliberately looked away from the truth and tried to justify doing so.
Because no matter what it took, he had wanted to believe in his Disciple.
A long time passed before he finally spoke.
“I’ll sever your Sinews and Meridians.”
“My Sinews and Meridians.
And then?”
“I’ll cripple your dantian.
You’ll spend the rest of your life repenting for your crimes.”
“Facing a wall in meditation until the day I die.
The very thought is horrifying.”
Despite his words, Jangcheon’s face was full of laughter.
“But did our sect’s rules change while this useless Disciple wasn’t looking?
As I understand it, a case like this calls for immediate execution, no questions asked.”
“...This is my final act of mercy.
Put that man down and step away at once.”
Jangcheon blinked as if he had forgotten something important.
The middle-aged man in his arms, his entire body drenched in blood, was still drawing ragged breaths.
“Ah, right.
I’d forgotten about him.”
Slash.
Blood erupted in a fountain.
Jeok Cheongang stared at it with trembling eyes.
Jangcheon’s hand had moved without the slightest hesitation.
The man’s throat had been cut.
His body convulsed, then fell still.
“Is this your answer?”
“It’s already too late.
Even if I saved him, he would spend the rest of his life crippled.
Wouldn’t it be better to give him a clean death?”
“You...
You’re no longer the child I knew.”
“I am exactly the child you knew, Master.
You simply misunderstood me from the very beginning.”
“Enough.
Your evil deeds end today.”
“Do you truly intend to cripple me and make me spend the rest of my life facing a wall?”
A faint fear showed on his Disciple’s face.
Jeok Cheongang clenched his fist until blood seeped from his palm.
One move.
A single move was all it would take to erase Jangcheon from this world.
But he knew he could not bring himself to do it.
Severing his Disciple’s Sinews and Meridians, crippling his martial arts, and imprisoning him was the best he could do.
“Do you regret it?”
“Regret?”
“Yes.
Regret.”
It would change nothing, but Jeok Cheongang wanted to hear the answer from Jangcheon’s own lips.
Then, in the next instant, every trace of fear vanished from Jangcheon’s face.
“I was relieved.”
“What?”
“I couldn’t see or hear you, but I knew you had been watching me for the past four months.
Why else do you think I did this right in front of you?”
Jangcheon’s face was reflected in Jeok Cheongang’s vacant eyes.
He continued with perfect composure.
“You can’t kill me, Master.
It wouldn’t matter if I killed not dozens but hundreds.
Before I left, I wanted to confirm that one last time.”
“Before you leave?
What do you mean?”
“There may be fathers who blame their children for their faults, but there is no father anywhere in this world who kills his own child with his own hands.”
“Thank you, Master.
Thank you for raising me as your child rather than merely your Disciple.
Thank you for trying to save a child like me until the very end.
Thanks to you, my one path to survival has opened.”
Jeok Cheongang stood frozen as if his breath had stopped.
Before him, Jangcheon gave a deep bow filled with genuine sincerity.
When he raised his head again, a small white porcelain vial was held between his lips.
“It’s Bone-Melting Powder.”
Bone-Melting Powder was a deadly poison that dissolved flesh and bone.
Even a tiny amount would be fatal if the vial shattered inside his mouth.
Not even a celestial immortal could save him.
Jeok Cheongang roared in fury.
“Jangcheon!
You bastard!”
“That bow I just gave you... was my final farewell.
I’m leaving now.
I’ll go far away and never return.”
“You think I’ll let you leave like this?”
“Then kill me.
That’s the only way.”
“Kill me.”
Kill me.
Those were his Disciple’s final words.
Jeok Cheongang blinked.
The ceiling had looked blurry for some time, and now something was running down his cheek.
“The inn is old.
Rain must be leaking through.”
It was a winter night, one day before New Year’s Day.

chapters.title: Chapter 178
paragraphs: “The inn is old. Rain’s leaking in.”
I stared up at the blameless ceiling.
“It is a little run-down.”
Of course, no rain was falling. The ink-dark sky was perfectly still.
It wasn’t the inn that was old, but Jeok Cheongang’s heart. Remembering the painful events of long ago had sprung a leak in his eyes.
I thought the old man had neither blood nor tears in him.
Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
I had never imagined that this irascible Supreme Peak master had a past like this. I also had to revise my assessment of Jopil, whom I had dismissed as merely insane.
He was even crazier than I thought.
He had thoroughly used and discarded the Master who had saved him from the brink of death. From what I’d heard, he clearly hadn’t felt a shred of guilt, even at the very end.
I was shocked that anyone could be filled with such pure malice—and relieved that Jopil no longer existed in this world.
“But he still managed to escape alive. The Namgung Family must have been keeping a close eye on him.”
The Namgung Family—a staple of martial arts novels.

They were one of the Five Great Families, an organization said to rival the Nine Sects and One Gang. I might not know the details, but hunting down and killing a single fugitive should have been nothing to them.
Unless someone had helped him.
“Could it be...?”
At my question, Jeok Cheongang calmly nodded.
“I went to the Azure Sky Sword King and asked for his help. It was the last duty I could perform.”
The Disciple had abandoned his Master and left, yet the Master had protected him to the very end.
The more I heard, the more unbelievable their Master-Disciple relationship became.
“...That’s incredible.”
“Incredible? I raised a Slaughter Saint like him as my Disciple, then let him loose upon the world because I was blinded by personal affection. It was a foolish choice.”
Jeok Cheongang continued with a self-deprecating laugh.
“The Azure Sky Sword King told me the same thing. He said I would regret it. He was right. Every moment of the past ten years has been filled with regret.”
“If you could go back to that day, what would you do?”
His answer came without hesitation.
“I would save him. And I would regret it all over again. Even if I were given a hundred chances, the man I was then would make the same choice every time.”
The me back then would have done the same?
That was a loaded choice of words. It also meant that the Jeok Cheongang of today was different.
Could it be...?
Perhaps those ten years had been his time to prepare.
To prepare himself to personally kill the Disciple who might still be committing atrocities somewhere in the world.
If that was the case...
A thought flashed through my mind, and I asked carefully—very carefully.
“Speak.”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice was low. His fathomless gaze seemed to see through everything, and my heart began to pound.
I swallowed, then opened my mouth.
“I believe there’s something you want to ask me.”
We hadn’t sat down face-to-face just to reminisce about the past.
He had questions for me, and I had questions for him.
We each had things to ask and answers to give. And I wasn’t the one holding the sword hilt.
“I’ll answer you. Whatever you ask.”
Jeok Cheongang, the one holding the sword hilt, silently ran his fingers over his empty wineglass.
The silence seemed as though it might never end. Fifteen minutes? Half an hour? Half a shichen? I had no idea how much time passed.
A cold wind howled outside, but whether from tension or something else, my entire body was drenched in sweat.
At last, the long silence broke.
“...Is he dead?”
His voice was terribly hoarse. He was trying to sound calm, but the question held a jumble of emotions.
When I nodded, the old man’s gray eyes trembled.
“I see. So that’s how it ended.”
Jeok Cheongang unconsciously tried to tip back his wineglass, then noticed that it was empty and gave a hollow laugh.
“I suspected as much. I sensed traces of our sect in you.”
It was because of the internal energy I had gained from the Blazing Flame Divine Pill. Just as his internal energy had led me to suspect that he was the Fire King, mine had told him the same thing.
“Did he die peacefully?”
“That...”
I pictured Jopil thrashing as blood streamed from his seven apertures.
After drawing on even his innate qi, he had fought me to the death and died with half his upper body blown away.
When I hesitated, Jeok Cheongang waved a wrinkled hand.
“Enough. It was my fault for asking a pointless question. What peaceful death is there in a battle between martial artists?”
“His suffering would have been brief.”
“A man who spent his life inflicting pain on countless others received a better death than he deserved.”
Despite his words, his expression was bitter.
If Jeok Cheongang had found Jopil, he would have used the finest move at his disposal.
He would have granted him the swiftest, most painless death possible.
Maybe that was why he returned to the world.
But Jeok Cheongang had failed to achieve his goal. Jopil had encountered me before his former Master could reach him, and lost his life.
How would Jeok Cheongang react—
“I owe you a debt.”
“Pardon?”
“Did you not hear me? I said I owe you.”
“No, I heard you. It’s just...”
I was dumbfounded.
Never in my wildest dreams had I expected those words to come from him so easily.
As I blinked at him, wondering what on earth was happening, Jeok Cheongang continued.
“Someone had to stop that child. You did in my stead what I should have done ten years ago. And...”
Jeok Cheongang’s lips suddenly twitched, as though he had never said anything like this to anyone before.
After a brief hesitation, he finally spoke.
“I’m sorry. I sincerely apologize to all of you for acting so rashly before.”
My voice burst out before I could stop it.
“Whoa.”
“Whoa?”
“Ah, it’s nothing. I was so surprised that it just slipped out.”
“Is it truly so astonishing for this old man to apologize?”
It seemed plenty astonishing to me. Besides, he’d looked incredibly uncomfortable saying it, so what was he complaining about?
“...Well, you see...”
I trailed off awkwardly, then saw Jeok Cheongang’s face beginning to contort and quickly changed my tune.
“The renowned Fire King, Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, personally apologizing to a junior as young as me! I can only bow before your magnanimity and humility.”
Just look at his face. Jekyll and Hyde were fighting it out right there.
Every muscle in Jeok Cheongang’s face conveyed his fierce inner struggle over whether or not to hit me. Eventually, he sighed.
“I cannot make heads or tails of you. You may leave now.”
“Yes, sir.”
“And take those children with you.”
Cheongpung was fast asleep with his forehead pressed against the table, while Hyuk Mujin was still sprawled facedown in the courtyard.
Before Jeok Cheongang could change his mind, I quickly gathered up the two deadweights and headed for the second floor. Then I remembered something.
Oh, right. I have to return the Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual and the sword.
I had already swallowed the Blazing Flame Divine Pill, so there was nothing I could do about that, but I still needed to return the other items.
I desperately wanted to settle everything between Jeok Cheongang and me once and for all today.
“Um, Sir Jeok. I’m sorry, but there’s one more thing I need to tell you...”
I turned back, my voice as tiny as an ant, then stopped short.
Glug, glug.
Left alone, Jeok Cheongang was pouring drinks.
One glass, then another. He placed the second wineglass before the empty seat across from him and began drinking in silence.
I watched him for a moment, then suddenly thought:
He looks small.
The back of the giant known as the Fire King looked small and lonely.
I quietly turned away and climbed the stairs.
Once the presence behind him had disappeared, Jeok Cheongang muttered,
“You deserved to die.”
Jangcheon had killed dozens in Anhui alone. There was no telling how many people had fallen victim to his Disciple over the past ten years.
“You called it Might Makes Right, didn’t you? You’re the same. In the end, you died at the hands of someone stronger than you.”
No one remained strong forever, just as no one remained weak forever.
Even Jeok Cheongang, a Supreme Peak master, was weaker than someone.
Yet some people forgot that fact. Drunk on their own strength—or on blood—they strayed down the wrong path.
“What a pathetic fool.”
Jeok Cheongang drained his drink. His Disciple’s words from that day long ago seemed to echo in his ears.
I have never changed. Not once, from the day I first met you until now.
Over the past ten years, he had turned those words over in his mind countless times. That single sentence had lodged near his heart like a dagger and tormented him.
“Did you truly never change? Not even once?”
They had spent many years together. At times, Jeok Cheongang had been a strict teacher; at others, he had cared for his Disciple like a loving father.
No—he had believed that was what he had been.
But it had all been an illusion. If it had truly been otherwise, Jangcheon would have chosen a very different path.
“How could rice paper be black from the beginning?”
Being born into this world was like receiving a blank sheet of rice paper.
A person passed through countless moments between birth and death.
When death finally arrived, those moments came together to complete a single painting. The painting Jangcheon had created was... entirely ink-black.
Jeok Cheongang had watched it from the closest distance, yet he hadn’t known.
“Cheon.”
The old man stared at the seat across from him, where a wineglass had been set. One by one, phantomlike figures appeared in the empty chair.
A child hunched over as he stuffed dumplings into his mouth. A boy clutching the wooden sword his Master had made for him, his cheeks flushed bright red.
His limbs lengthened, and his gaze sharpened. Before long, a tall young man stood glaring at the old man.
Kill me.
That day, Jeok Cheongang had been unable to answer his Disciple’s cutting words.
But if he ever met his Disciple again, there was something he had desperately wanted to say.
“I’m sorry. I’m so sorry.”
Whoooosh.
A cold wind slipped through the door of the old inn and brushed across the wineglass.
“Benefactor!”
I awoke to a terrible racket. Cheongpung, practically bursting with excitement, was bouncing up and down.
“This is my pavilion, so why... Ah.”
Right. This wasn’t the Jin Family of Taiyuan. It was an inn.
At the same time, the events of the previous day flashed through my mind like a panorama. It wouldn’t have been an exaggeration to say I had crossed the boundary between life and death.
Well, that aside—
“Stop jumping around. There’s enough dust in here already.”
“I’m allowed to jump today!”
How was anyone supposed to sleep through this?
Hyuk Mujin, who had been curled up like a shrimp in one corner of the floor, blearily opened his eyes.
“Is this... paradise?”
That bastard started talking nonsense the moment he woke up.
It was absurd, but then I remembered that yesterday, after trying to escape on his own, he had been knocked unconscious by a duck bone Jeok Cheongang flicked at him.
“You awake?”
“Captain?”
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes widened when he saw me. Then he sighed.
“So this isn’t paradise.”
“...What the hell is that supposed to mean, you bastard?”
“It was a joke. A joke. I’m just glad to see you alive again.”
“Says the guy who tried to run away on his own.”
“Come on. Why do you have to put it like that?”
Grinning shamelessly, Hyuk Mujin looked around. More precisely, he looked at Cheongpung, who was running laps around the room like a train.
“What’s all this commotion so early in the morning? What good thing happened to make him run around like that?”
“No idea. He says he’s allowed to jump today.”
“He must’ve eaten something tasty.”
It was obviously bullshit, but since we were talking about Cheongpung, its credibility skyrocketed.
Giving him a doubtful look, I asked Cheongpung,
“What day is it today?”
Cheongpung, who had been circling the room and driving me crazy, stopped dead.
“Benefactor, you don’t even know that?”
“...Let’s refrain from saying things like that. It hits ten times harder coming from you.”
“It’s the first day of the new year. New Year’s Day!”
Hyuk Mujin and I nodded at the same time.
“Ah, so it’s New Year’s Day.”
“Right. It’s already New Year’s Day.”
“I thought it was something els—”
“Yeah. A whole year has already pass—”
After a brief silence, a profound realization struck us.
Ah. The Jin Family of Taiyuan.
At that moment, Wipeng’s threat from before I left the family rang vividly in my ears.

How was anyone supposed to sleep through this?
Hyuk Mujin, who had been curled up like a shrimp in one corner of the floor, blearily opened his eyes.
“Is this... paradise?”
That bastard started talking nonsense the moment he woke up.
It was absurd, but then I remembered that yesterday, after trying to escape on his own, he had been knocked unconscious by a duck bone Jeok Cheongang flicked at him.
“You awake?”
“Captain?”
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes widened when he saw me.
Then he sighed.
“So this isn’t paradise.”
“...What the hell is that supposed to mean, you bastard?”
“It was a joke.
A joke.
I’m just glad to see you alive again.”
“Says the guy who tried to run away on his own.”
“Come on.
Why do you have to put it like that?”
Grinning shamelessly, Hyuk Mujin looked around.
More precisely, he looked at Cheongpung, who was running laps around the room like a train.
“What’s all this commotion so early in the morning?
What good thing happened to make him run around like that?”
“No idea.
He says he’s allowed to jump today.”
“He must’ve eaten something tasty.”
It was obviously bullshit, but since we were talking about Cheongpung, its credibility skyrocketed.
Giving him a doubtful look, I asked Cheongpung,
“What day is it today?”
Cheongpung, who had been circling the room and driving me crazy, stopped dead.
“Benefactor, you don’t even know that?”
“...Let’s refrain from saying things like that.
It hits ten times harder coming from you.”
“It’s the first day of the new year.
New Year’s Day!”
Hyuk Mujin and I nodded at the same time.
“Ah, so it’s New Year’s Day.”
“Right.
It’s already New Year’s Day.”
“I thought it was something els—”
“Yeah.
A whole year has already pass—”
After a brief silence, a profound realization struck us.
Ah.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan.
At that moment, Wipeng’s threat from before I left the family rang vividly in my ears.

chapters.title: Chapter 179
paragraphs: It really was New Year’s Day.
It had only been two days since Wipeng had given me strict instructions before I left the Jin Family of Taiyuan, yet I had completely forgotten.
Hyuk Mujin swallowed a hollow breath and spoke.
“W-What do we do?”
“What do you mean, what do we do? Even if we’d remembered, we wouldn’t have made it back in time.”
This was the Fire King we were talking about.
Considering the mood yesterday, if I’d told him I had family business and needed to leave, he would have sent me off with a hearty laugh.
Straight down the road to the underworld, of course.
“Great Hero Wipeng is going to kill me.”
I patted the ashen-faced Hyuk Mujin on the shoulder.
“Don’t worry. He can’t kill me.”
“Oh, me neither!”
Such was the sorrow of having no powerful backer.
Still, I had no intention of deliberately dragging my feet.
Today was the day the Jin Family of Taiyuan would rise as the undisputed ruler of Shanxi Province. The youngest son of the family couldn’t afford to be late.
“Pack your things. We’re leaving right now.”
Not that I had much to pack. One travel bundle was everything I owned.
We were ready in no time and headed downstairs. The inn had been decked out in red for New Year’s Day, and despite the early hour, it was bustling with people.
Two men stood out among the crowd.
“Oh, you’re up?”
“Tsk, tsk. Young fellows shouldn’t sleep so much.”
“Exactly. When I was young, there were plenty of days when I couldn’t even get one shichen of sleep.”
“One whole shichen? Why, back in my day...”
The two old men raised their hands in greeting, then went right back to passing wine cups between themselves.
Their flushed faces and the wine jar beside them showed they had already been drinking heavily this early in the day.
Hyuk Mujin, following behind me, whispered in a small voice,
“What kind of combination is that?”
“No idea.”
One was a giant of an old man, larger than most strapping young men. The other was so small and frail that a stiff breeze might have carried him away.
The Fire King was one thing.
But when did Jang Taebo get here?
Had he come because of the commission?
In any case, the two old men—each a master in his own field—seemed to have grown quite close.
“It’s pretty chaotic in here. Can’t we just slip out?”
“Slip out, my ass. Don’t you remember getting knocked unconscious with a duck bone yesterday?”
“That was a duck bone? Damn, no wonder my skull was ringing.”
“If we pretend nothing happened and leave, he’ll crack it open.”
“I’d rather avoid that.”
“So? Want to make a run for it?”
Hyuk Mujin sighed gloomily.
“Phew. What a rotten way to start the new year.”
I couldn’t have agreed more. No one in the world would want to run into Fire King Jeok Cheongang first thing on New Year’s Day.
“Grandpas, do you have any dumplings?”
“There’s plenty of meat, too. Eat up.”
“Yaaay!”
...Except that guy.
Hyuk Mujin and I trudged forward with heavy hearts, like oxen being led to the slaughterhouse.
Cheongpung, who was shoveling food into his mouth at the speed of light, beamed and held out several plates.
“Hewe! It’s delishush! Try shome!”
“...You eat plenty.”
“Thanksh, I will!”
Someone like him was a Peak master. The sheer unfairness of reality filled me with despair for the future of the Murim.
Jang Taebo spoke up.
“So, what are you all planning to do now?”
“We’re going back to our family first. We have some business to take care of.”
“Ah, I see. You said there was going to be a gathering at the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
At present, every move the Jin Family of Taiyuan made was a hot topic throughout Shanxi Province.

The Jin Family of Taiyuan, once treated as an old tiger past its prime, had reclaimed the throne of Shanxi Murim after many years. It was only natural that the interest and expectations surrounding them were extraordinary.
Even Jang Taebo, a homebody living in a tiny place like Jang Family Village, had heard about it.
“That’s all anyone talks about whenever people gather these days. Even ordinary people with nothing to do with the Murim are flocking there for the spectacle. That tells you everything.”
“Will that many people really come?”

“A grand feast always draws all sorts of hangers-on. Shanxi Province may be a frontier region, but this is about becoming the hegemon of an entire province. I may not be a martial artist, but I’ve seen and heard enough in my time. Just wait and see. Ah, and...”
Jang Taebo lowered his voice.
“Don’t worry about the commission.”
The commission.
His words suddenly reminded me of something I hadn’t had the chance to ask before.
“By the way, is there anything else you need?”
“What do you mean?”
“Well, there must be something.”

Even the neighborhood laundromat charged a fee for repairs. Jang Taebo was a master artisan renowned throughout the world. He might not have been as skilled as he was in his prime, but I didn’t believe his abilities had vanished over the past ten years.
His work had to command an appropriate price...
Realizing what I meant, Jang Taebo stroked his white beard.
“You mean you want to compensate me?”
“To be honest, I can’t give you as much as you might be expecting.”
“Then just give me ten thousand nyang.”
Ten thousand nyang was a hundred silver nyang. It was certainly an enormous sum, but considering his fame, it felt like nothing more than a special discount.
I nodded readily. It wasn’t my money, anyway.
“I’ll prepare it and send it to your home.”
“Ten thousand silver nyang? You’d have to tear out every last pillar holding up the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“...Ten thousand silver nyang?”
“Of course. Did my worth look that cheap to you?”
“That’s a whopping million nyang.”
“Not a whopping million. A mere million. You’ll be getting the greatest divine weapon under heaven. What does a little money matter?”
Of course it mattered.
How much would a million nyang be worth in the real world? Hundreds of billions of won? Trillions?
Jang Taebo let out a quiet laugh at my expression.
“I don’t need it.”
“I’m sorry, but would you consider a quick deal for ten thousand nyang—pardon?”
“I said I don’t need it. What would I do with that much money? I couldn’t spend it all before I died. Having an opportunity like this come my way while I’m still alive is payment enough.”
Was this the spirit of a true artisan?
What a shining example, this Jang Taebo. Every blacksmith under heaven should follow his example and Taebo accordingly.
As I trembled with emotion, Hyuk Mujin cut in with an admiring look.
“Then why don’t you take the ten thousand nyang for now and give it to me?”
That bastard could write an autobiography. He could call it A Hundred Ways to Get Yourself Beaten to Death.
I smacked him on the back of the head, then bowed politely to Jang Taebo.
“Then I’ll leave it in your hands.”

“I’m the one who should be asking a favor. I can’t promise how long it will take, but I’ll create something that will make the world tremble. Until then, make sure you acquire the strength and qualifications worthy of wielding it.”
“I’ll do my best.”
“Good. Then that settles it. I’ll have to place my trust in you.”
Jang Taebo nodded, then paused.
“Ah. Could I ask one more favor?”
“Build my house again. It all burned down, and I don’t even have anywhere to sleep.”
The home he had bought after retiring—the precious place where he had spent his golden years in peace—had vanished overnight.
At the sorrow in Jang Taebo’s voice, my gaze drifted to the side of its own accord.
Jeok Cheongang, who had been quietly sipping his wine while we talked, looked up.
“What are you staring at?”
There was no trace of the emotional, solemn Jeok Cheongang from last night. I subtly averted my gaze.
“...Nothing.”
“If you have something to say, say it. This old man isn’t so petty.”
“Are you really sure?”
“Go ahead.”
The moment he finished speaking, the space beneath the table began to heat up.
It wasn’t as though the innkeeper were a modern man who had brought in an electric heater...
Fuck. Flame Divine Palm.
Tears welled in my eyes as I answered.
“I was just thinking that you looked a good ten years younger than usual today.”
Jeok Cheongang frowned.
“What? Ten years?”
Damn it. Subtracting ten from a hundred still left ninety.
I hurriedly revised my answer.
“Twenty years...”
“Twenty years?”
“Thirty years...”
In the space of barely three seconds, Jeok Cheongang had grown thirty years younger. He nodded in satisfaction.
“I thought you were a fellow with nothing but shit in your head, but you do have some fairly plausible thoughts after all.”
Hyuk Mujin looked like he had something to say, but he clamped his mouth shut.
Apparently, he had no desire to make A Hundred Ways to Get Yourself Beaten to Death his final work.
Instead, he kept poking me in the side, looking desperate to leave this place immediately.
Of course, I feel the same way.
But before we could go, there was one last thing I needed to settle.
I spoke in the most respectful tone I could manage.
“I have several items in my possession.”
Jeok Cheongang, his face flushed as he tipped back his wine cup, let out a quiet laugh.
“Were you ever planning to return them?”
“Of course I did.”
“That’s right. If you don’t return them, you’ll see something ugly.”
The old man could see straight through people’s hearts like a ghost.
I forced a smile and placed the items I had already taken out on the table.
The Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual I had obtained from Jopil, and the Unnamed Sword made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
“As you already know, Great Hero Jeok, the Blazing Flame Divine Pill...”
“You gobbled it up.”
“Yes. That’s right.”
A wrinkled finger tapped against the table. Jeok Cheongang continued in a dry voice.
“Where is the Treasured Jade?”
“Pardon?”
“The treasured jade. The jade.”
Treasured jade? As in some sort of treasure or gemstone?
Jeok Cheongang didn’t seem like the type to obsess over ordinary jewelry, so it had to be extremely important.
But since I hadn’t even known it existed, I could only stare at him in bewilderment.
“These are the only things I received.”
“Received? You didn’t collect them yourself?”
“No. There were circumstances. They were handed to me right after I woke up.”
“Do you suspect any of the people involved?”
Gong Yacheong and Socheon had handed Jopil’s belongings over to me. Neither of them was the sort to quietly pocket something behind everyone else’s back.
The same went for the members of the reconnaissance squad who had been there. I didn’t know what had happened, but that didn’t change my trust in them.
“They wouldn’t have. No, absolutely not.”
Jeok Cheongang studied me for a moment before speaking.
“Then it must be one of two things. Someone deceived you, or that child lost it.”
“What a nuisance. This has become troublesome.”
Jeok Cheongang had likely returned to the world not only to find his Disciple, but also to recover the Fire Gate Clan’s treasures that had been scattered because of him.
The Treasured Jade seemed to be one of them.
It was a treasure that even the Fire King was willing to endure the trouble of searching for at all costs.
Damn it. I never even got to see it.
Just as a creeping sense of danger began to outweigh my curiosity about what the jade actually was, Jeok Cheongang spoke.
“It can’t be helped. Keep them for now.”
That casual remark brought my thoughts to a complete halt.
Wait. Did he mean...
“You want me to keep these?”
“Yes.”
“Both of them?”
“All three. Have you forgotten the one in your stomach? Anything that originated from our sect must be reclaimed, one way or another.”
“I’m joking.”
“Phew.”
“Tsk, tsk. You’re still young, but your nerve is already the size of a bean.”
Bean or cannonball, I didn’t care.
I wanted nothing more to do with that terrifying old man. Ever.
I took a deep breath and opened my mouth.
“I’m sorry, but I’ll have to decline—”
“If you refuse, I’ll reclaim them right now. All three.”
“This time, I’m serious.”
Once again, the space beneath the table grew scorching hot. It was Flame Divine Palm, of course.
What the fuck?
I was trying to return the items to their rightful owner. And I couldn’t even do that?
Overcome with resentment and indignation, I demanded, “Why are you doing this to me?”
“Do you expect an old man like me to carry those cumbersome things around? I don’t have the strength for that.”
“What if someone takes them from me?”
“Then this old man will kill you.”
“What if I learn the martial art?”
“Then you’ll die even more painfully.”
What kind of bullshit situation was this?
Leaving me standing there in a daze, the Fire King rose from his seat.
Cheongpung, who was still cramming food into his mouth, looked up.
“Gwandpa, awe you leaving?”
“...You’re even worse than your grandfather. Slow down.”
After exchanging a silent glance of farewell with Jang Taebo, Jeok Cheongang turned away and tossed out one meaningful remark.
“Let’s meet again soon.”
I didn’t want to see him.
Ever.

paragraphs: New Year’s Day.
Jin Wikyung’s reaction upon seeing the sunlight on the first day of the new year was short and simple.
“Fantastic.”
Wolhwa, who had been tilting her teacup with graceful composure, let out a quiet laugh. She had arrived at the Jin Family of Taiyuan the previous night.
With the family currently barring all outsiders from entering, admitting her was a show of respect for their alliance.
“Are you really that happy?”
“How could I not be?”
“I suppose you have every reason to be, considering everything that’s happened. Two years ago, I never imagined a day like this would come.”
“That hurts to hear.”
Wolhwa covered her mouth in exaggerated dismay.
“My goodness, shouldn’t I be the one saying that? We’ve been waiting for you for so long.”
“I’ll keep my promise. Without fail.”
“I hope so. It would be troublesome if you went back on your word a second time.”
“Let’s stop. I’m tired.”
“That makes two of us.”
The previous night had been a long one. After an intense back-and-forth, they had finally found common ground that gave each of them what they wanted.
Both sides needed the other’s help if they wished to wield influence in Shanxi Murim.
Having finally obtained what she wanted, Wolhwa gave him a prim smile.
“Still, we did give you a valuable piece of information, didn’t we?”
Jin Wikyung replied with a disgruntled look.
“Oh, that information? I heard our family’s Datong Branch played some part in the matter as well.”
“We were the first to bring you the information. We were also the ones who promptly sent a messenger eagle.”
“That much... I’ll admit.”
Wolhwa suddenly narrowed her eyes.
“But aren’t you worried?”
“About what?”
“The Heavenly Wind Band.”
The news that the Heavenly Wind Band, which had been prowling around Datong, had been annihilated was certainly welcome. But it was also profoundly shocking.
One person had single-handedly wiped out hundreds of mounted bandits, including a Peak master? Unless that person was a Supreme Peak master, it would have been nearly impossible.
Wolhwa ran one long finger along her teacup.
“Who do you think it was?”
“Who knows? We’ll have to find out in time.”
Jin Wikyung suppressed a laugh. The world might be vast and full of reclusive eccentrics, but Supreme Peak masters were anything but common.
When he had first heard the news about the Heavenly Wind Band, only one name had flashed through his mind.
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.
It was most likely him.
Considering the relationship they had built over the years, he ought to tell Wolhwa. But the matter was far too significant to share even with the Chief Branch Leader of the Lower District Sect.
“Don’t worry too much. Our family is keeping a close eye on the situation.”
“For someone saying that, you look awfully relaxed.”
“How could I be relaxed? I merely assume that whoever annihilated the notoriously vicious Heavenly Wind Band wasn’t a master of demonic, heterodox arts.”
Wolhwa narrowed her eyes at his feigned ignorance.
But she couldn’t press him any further. If the Jin Family of Taiyuan had truly possessed ties to a Supreme Peak master, its rise to its current position would have been far easier.
“Well, in any case, you have my sincere congratulations.”
“Thank you.”
“But someone else has been awfully quiet.”
Knowing exactly whom Wolhwa meant, Jin Wikyung shook his head.
“He’s been dissatisfied since birth.”
A prickly voice asked,
“Are you talking about me?”
“Who else would I be talking about?”
Wipeng, who had been leaning diagonally against the wall of the office, opened his mouth.
“I wholeheartedly agree with my lord. It truly is a fantastic day.”
“What’s gotten into you? Whenever I say something like that, you lecture me about dignity and propriety.”
“What else am I supposed to call a fantastic day?”
His subordinate, usually as strict and fussy as an old schoolmaster, was humoring him for once. Jin Wikyung smiled in satisfaction.
“Exactly. That’s how important this occasion will be.”
“Can you hear the murmuring from far away? I hear that not only the influential martial artists of Shanxi Murim, but even commoners who heard the news have come.”
“Oh, is that true?”
“Indeed. We’ve also received a letter of congratulations from the Heavenly Sword True Person, the Sect Leader of Huashan.”
“Oh!”
“The Three Plum Blossom Elites should be arriving soon as well.”
Jin Wikyung already knew all of this, but it still felt good to hear it again.

The Nine Sects and One Gang were pillars of the Murim world, and their influence was immense. Even if only part of that great alliance was represented, it was practically equivalent to the entire orthodox faction vouching for the legitimacy of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Of course, he couldn’t deny that the Sword Saint and Cheongpung had played a significant role in that.

“And that’s not all. Isn’t Prince Shangshan, a descendant of the Son of Heaven, coming as well? This means that both the government and the Murim have acknowledged our family as the undisputed hegemon of Shanxi Province.”
“Of course! Absolutely!”
As Jin Wikyung’s spirits soared, Wipeng smiled.
“Do you know what the even better news is?”
“You’re really going all out today. What is it? Tell me already!”
The next moment, the smile at the corners of Wipeng’s mouth vanished without a trace.

“At this gathering, where countless martial artists and commoners, distinguished guests from the Nine Sects and One Gang, and even a descendant of the imperial family are coming, both Young Masters are absent.”
“I can at least understand the Second Young Master. Enlightenment doesn’t come whenever one wants it to, so secluded training is understandable. I’m a martial artist too. But!”
Wipeng continued with a fierce glare.
“The Third Young Master absolutely cannot be let off the hook. Leaving at a time like this as though none of it concerned him was bad enough, but now all word from him has stopped completely.”
Jin Wikyung quietly averted his gaze. Wolhwa, his only lifeline, merely shrugged as if she knew nothing and watched the spectacle unfold.
“He’ll come.”
“What do you mean, he’ll come? He left last year saying he’d be right back.”
Jin Wikyung opened his mouth to object, then stopped. The way Wipeng phrased it sounded strange, but it wasn’t wrong.
Wipeng ground his teeth and continued.
“Going off to make a weapon when we’re facing such a momentous occasion... I’m an idiot for trusting the Third Young Master even for a moment.”
“Now, now.”
“Am I wrong?”
“Now, hold on!”
“Why? What about it?”
Jin Wikyung flinched at Wipeng’s bulging eyes. Then salvation arrived in the form of a voice from outside the office.
“Lesser Family Head, the preparations are complete.”
“...There you have it.”

Wipeng’s lips moved as though he still had more to say, but he released a deep sigh instead. This was hardly the first time something like this had happened. They had to deal with the business at hand first.
“This time, you must give the Third Young Master a proper talking-to.”
“Of course I will.”
Jin Wikyung grinned and left the office.
Fifty martial artists radiating sharp auras stood in formation before the pavilion. Every one of them was at least a First Rate master, and they stared at their lord with unwavering composure.

An eight-cheok-tall giant, Jin Wikyung was the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. In place of the absent Family Head, he had led the family for the past two years and finally set it upon a firm foundation.
His tightly closed lips parted.
“Let’s go.”
Wipeng, Wolhwa, and the fifty martial artists followed him. As they crossed the quiet grounds of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, their numbers continued to swell.
Fifty became a hundred, a hundred became two hundred, and two hundred became three hundred...
The Jin Family of Taiyuan had suffered as though its limbs had been torn away in the previous war, but its recovery had been swift, and its growth even swifter.
Our family has grown stronger.
The One Pavilion, Two Halls, and Three Teams advancing alongside him were proof of that.
They were the arms, legs, waist, and torso of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, stronger and sturdier than ever before.
Remembering the countless sacrifices and efforts that had brought them to this day, Jin Wikyung felt a surge of emotion.
“Lesser Family Head.”
Before he knew it, they had reached the Gate Guard Pavilion.
The gate guards standing watch at the main entrance bowed with crisp, disciplined movements. Beyond the solid stone walls, the cheers of countless people rang out.
“Wow, this really is fantastic.”
“My lord, give the order.”
Wolhwa smiled brightly, while Wipeng wore a more solemn expression than ever.
Jin Wikyung took in their faces and drew a deep breath. The next moment, his dignified voice rang out.
“Open the gates.”

It marked the beginning of the grand banquet that would continue for the next three days—and served as the signal flare announcing that the Jin Family of Taiyuan had become the hegemon of Shanxi Murim.

The area in front of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s gates was packed with people. There were martial artists wearing swords and blades, merchants hoping to seize an opportunity, and commoners who belonged to neither group.
Even though it was broad daylight, firecrackers celebrating the first day of the new year went off now and then.
Boom! Boom-boom!
“Waaaaah!”
While hundreds upon hundreds of people laughed and chatted in the festive atmosphere, a handful wore faces fit for a funeral.
“Damn it.”
“What kind of situation is this?”
“I ought to just—”
The five middle-aged men—the heads of the five sects collectively known as the Five Gates of Shanxi—couldn’t smooth out their crumpled expressions.
Of the five, Woo Hwangtae, chief of the Seongun Escort Bureau, was in the worst state by far, frantic with worry thanks to his worthless son.
They wouldn’t even grant me an audience.
He had arrived five days earlier and requested a meeting countless times.
He had come to clean up the mess caused by his son, Woo Jintae.

But the carefully prepared letters and gifts he sent had been turned away without ever crossing the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s threshold. His pride had taken a beating, but in the end, he had resorted to coming in person.
“I am Woo of the Seongun Escort Bureau.”
The Seongun Escort Bureau had endured for three generations, and everyone in Shanxi Province knew its name. After all, it had flaunted the enormous fortune it had amassed through any means necessary.
Yet the gate guard’s response had been indifferent.
“You can’t meet him right now.”
“Come now, man. What do you mean? I’m telling you, I’m the chief of the Seongun Escort Bureau!”
“Whether you’re a bureau chief or a sect leader, I don’t know or care. I follow orders.”
Had he ever suffered such humiliation in his life?

Like Woo Jintae, he had spent his entire life enjoying every advantage his family’s prestige afforded him. He had suffered a few setbacks and had occasionally been ignored by those of higher status, but he could endure that much.
But to be treated this way by a mere gate guard!
Every time Woo Hwangtae thought about it, the back of his head throbbed.
Those fucking bastards. No matter how powerful they are, how dare they treat someone like this?
Even his son, who had a child of his own, had returned so badly beaten that it was difficult to tell whether he was still human or some blue-skinned beast.
Father and son had both been utterly humiliated. It was too embarrassing to complain to the other sect leaders.
“Huff... Hooo...”
As Woo Hwangtae exhaled through his flushed face, the other heads of the Five Gates of Shanxi watched him cautiously.
“Chief Woo, are you all right?”
“If you’re feeling unwell, perhaps we should come back tomorrow...”
Woo Hwangtae snapped at them.

“Would you be all right, Sect Leader Song? My son was beaten like a street dog, and now we’re expected to apologize on top of that. And Lord Tae, if I retreat now, what do you think the Jin Family of Taiyuan will make of it? Do you even hear yourselves?”
The two men who had spoken flinched after drawing his ire, while the other two breathed sighs of relief.
But inwardly, all four were thinking the same thing.
This damned merchant. I ought to just...
They were only tolerating him because they still needed the Seongun Escort Bureau’s support.
They remembered clearly what their sons had told them.
The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi said he would make the Seongun Escort Bureau an example.
Chief Woo and that man are both formidable... Unless they’re the Nine Sects and One Gang, do they really think they can swallow the whole bureau in one bite?
Given the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s recent power, they might be able to.
For now, we watch.

If the balance tipped even slightly, they would have to switch sides. The four sect leaders were each waiting for the right moment, and as long as their own families survived, they were perfectly willing to keep smiling at Woo Hwangtae.
“Ha-ha, Chief Woo. Calm yourself.”
“Indeed. You and we have all been wronged, haven’t we? We understand how you feel.”
“Let’s head inside. We can’t stand here watching forever.”
“Here, these pills came from a renowned physician. They can calm even the fiercest temper. Let’s each chew one before we go in.”
Woo Hwangtae released a heated sigh and was about to toss the pill into his mouth when—
“Wow, this place is crawling with people. Absolutely crawling.”
Along with the booming voice, something shoved against his arm. The pill dropped, and someone immediately stepped on it.
That was the limit of Woo Hwangtae’s patience. He glared at the culprit, his eyes blazing.
The man stood a full two heads taller than everyone around him. Between his cow-like eyes and the way he was picking his nose, he looked every inch a country bumpkin.
“You! Stop right there!”
The huge man stopped in his tracks.
“Huh? Me?”
“Yes, you bastard! If you bump into someone, you should apologize immediately!”
“Ah. There were so many people, I didn’t notice. Sorry ’bout that.”
The man promptly bowed and turned away, but that only made Woo Hwangtae’s temper flare hotter.
His son’s humiliation. The memory of being disregarded by the gate guard for days. And now the behavior of this oversized country bumpkin.
The fuse had been lit.
“You ox-headed bastard! Stop right there!”
The giant flinched.
“What did you just say?”
“I called you an ox-headed bastard. You’re lower than an ox, you son of a bitch!”
“That’s one of the things I hate most.”
“If you hate it, what are you going to do about it?”
The giant snorted a plume of breath before opening his mouth.
“Can I hit him?”
“You bastard, I’ll kill—!”
Just as Woo Hwangtae was about to strike, a clear voice came from behind him.
“No.”
The speaker was a clean-cut young man.
Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong, had stopped his Junior Brother just before he exploded. He smiled at Woo Hwangtae.

chapters.title: Chapter 181
paragraphs: “You cause trouble whenever I take my eyes off you, even for a moment.”
After lightly scolding his Junior Brother, Baek Museong bowed his head to Woo Hwangtae.
“It seems there was a minor misunderstanding between you. I hope you’ll be generous enough to forgive him.”
His voice was as gentle as his appearance.

Woo Hwangtae was closer to a merchant than a martial artist. His martial arts were First Rate, but he could pride himself on having a Peak-level eye for people and situations, honed through years of running an Escort Bureau.
Under normal circumstances, one look at Baek Museong might have brought a certain phrase to mind.
The extraordinary hidden within the ordinary.
Unfortunately, Woo Hwangtae was not in his right mind.

Baek Museong had stepped in out of nowhere, and his clean-cut appearance made him seem like an easy mark. His polite voice carried the composure of a powerful man, but to Woo Hwangtae, it sounded merely insolent.
“What was that? You want me to generously forgive him?”
His voice seethed with rage as he raised an eyebrow.
“How dare you tell me what to do?”
“That was not my intention, but if I’ve offended you, I apologize.”
“Apologize? Hah. You little pup.”
Crack.
Once anger took hold, it naturally clouded a person’s judgment.
Woo Hwangtae clenched his fists and stepped forward, but the other Sect Leaders hurriedly tried to restrain him.
“Chief Woo, it would be best to stop here.”
“Sect Leader Song is right. Nothing good will come of making a scene.”
“Some arrogant bastards who crawled in from God knows where insult me, and you expect me to take it? Do you all look down on me too?”
“No, that’s not what we meant.”
“Then what are you trying to say?”
His tone was now only a hair short of openly speaking down to them. The Sect Leaders of the Five Gates of Shanxi frowned inwardly, but they still had to prevent an unnecessary conflict.
“We only mean that this is the wrong time and place. Have you forgotten our situation?”
“If you insist, I won’t stop you, but... there’s no need to cause a scene when we’re already in the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s bad books.”
“We understand that you’re angry, but please think of our position too. We’re all trying to survive here.”
Again. Again with the damned Jin Family of Taiyuan!

Woo Hwangtae barely swallowed the curses threatening to burst from his mouth. If not for the countless eyes and ears around him, he would have spewed every insult he knew and smashed everything in sight.
But his last shred of reason held him back.
“Nggh.”
After barely calming himself, Woo Hwangtae glared at Baek Museong, who still stood there looking perfectly composed.
“I’d like nothing more than to beat you to death with a single blow right now, but... I’ll let it pass as a country bumpkin’s mistake. Get lost before I change my mind.”
Baek Museong regarded him for a moment, then bowed his head.
“Thank you for your consideration.”
“Hmph. Lucky bastards.”
But Woo Hwangtae was the lucky one.
If Baek Museong hadn’t sent a Sound Transmission a moment earlier, he would have been hovering between life and death by now.
“Second, stop.”
Chulwoo, the second of the Three Plum Blossom Elites and known as the Defeated Flower Fist, stopped dead just as he was about to launch himself forward.
A voice no one else could hear slipped between his teeth.
“He wasn’t satisfied with going after me—he even went after you, Senior Brother.”
“It doesn’t matter.”
“It matters to me. Can’t I hit him once? Just once?”
“That sounds like you want to beat him to death.”
“...I’ll hit him gently. Just once. Really.”
“That sounds like you want to gently beat him to death. Have you forgotten Master’s strict order not to attract unnecessary attention?”
Chulwoo wrestled with himself for a moment before lowering his tightly clenched fist.
“Whew. This is driving me crazy.”
Baek Museong gave his shoulder an approving pat.
“You showed restraint. This too is training.”
“How is this training? What’s the point of learning martial arts if I can’t use them when the time comes?”
“Indiscriminate killing will only ruin you. Martial arts are meant to cultivate essence, qi, and spirit, not to kill people.”
“Every time I look at you, I get confused. Am I a disciple of Huashan or a monk from Shaolin Temple?”
“Could someone with your personality possibly become a monk? I already pity all the wooden fish you’d smash.”
Baek Museong let out a quiet laugh, and Chulwoo sighed.
He deeply respected his Senior Brother, but the man was simply too kindhearted. That was the problem.
“Those bastards should have their mouths smashed in...”
“Hey, watch your mouth!”
“All right, all right.”
Chulwoo watched Woo Hwangtae’s back as he grew smaller in the distance and smacked his lips.
I’ve memorized his face. Just let me catch him once.
Baek Museong knew exactly what his Junior Brother was thinking. He shook his head.
“Enough foolish thoughts. Find the youngest.”
“Did Eunhyang disappear again?”
“Yes. Just like you did.”
Chulwoo flinched.
“I-I went to take a leak.”
“That’s right. But why did someone who went to take a leak end up picking a fight in the middle of a crowd?”
“It happened on my way back after I’d finished. Wait, Senior Brother, do you not believe me? I haven’t washed my hands yet. Want to smell them?”
“...Never mind.”
Baek Museong rubbed his temple. He cherished his Junior Brothers more than anyone, but they were exceptionally difficult to handle.
At least Chulwoo was big enough to find quickly. Their youngest Junior Disciple, Eunhyang, was practically invisible in a crowd like this.
“Do you see anything?”
Chulwoo, who was at least two heads taller than everyone else, swept his gaze around.
“Not really. There are too many people.”
Even a Peak master’s eyes would struggle to find a small girl amid the endless, bustling mass.
The crowd was so large that merchants had even set up stalls here and there.
“By the way, was the Jin Family of Taiyuan always this big? I’d never even heard of it before we came.”
“Those in the know do. The current Sect Leader, the Shanxi Extraordinary Hero, is fairly well known, and so is the Heaven Shaking Sword, isn’t he?”
“I don’t know about the Shanxi Extraordinary Hero, but the Heaven Shaking Sword... Is that the fellow who’s supposedly one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes?”
“Don’t call him that. Watch your mouth.”
“He’s just a bookworm who goes to an academy. In my opinion, Senior Brother is much more...”
“Hey. Where did you learn that nasty habit of judging people before you’ve even met them? He is clearly a remarkable talent.”
“Well, for someone from Shanxi Province, being that good is practically a dragon rising from a ditch.”
Chulwoo answered indifferently, then suddenly frowned.
“Wasn’t there someone else besides the Heaven Shaking Sword? Some other dragon—or was it a loach?”
“A dragon? Do you mean the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
“Ah, right. The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.”
“I hear he’s quite talented, though not as much as the Heaven Shaking Sword.”
“Dragon or loach, I’ve heard about him nonstop on the way here. I should at least take a look at his face.”
The corner of Baek Museong’s mouth lifted as he watched Chulwoo clench his fists.
“Do you want to spar with him?”
Chulwoo scratched the back of his head.
“Not particularly. I’d win anyway.”
“Competitive spirit is a good thing, but avoid causing trouble if you can.”
“What trouble could there be? Since we came all this way, I just want to see what he can do.”
Baek Museong studied his Second Junior Brother.
Despite what Chulwoo said, his curiosity was obvious.
After spending years cooped up on Huashan, facing the same people every day, he seemed excited to finally be out in the world.
“You’ll see him soon enough. Of course, we need to find the youngest first.”
The final words came out almost as a sigh.
The gates of the Jin Family of Taiyuan were already open, and the invited guests were streaming inside like clouds.
Baek Museong was wondering whether he would have to climb a tree when—
“Senior Brother, it’s all right if I make a little noise, isn’t it?”
“What?”
Chulwoo grinned and drew a deep breath.
The next instant, a thunderous shout erupted.
“Eun—hyang!”
Baek Museong had no time to stop him. Chulwoo’s voice was every bit as tremendous as his body.
The people around them clapped their hands over their ears and dropped to the ground, while the countless people who had been laughing and chatting abruptly fell silent.
As a hush descended over the crowd like a bucket of cold water—
“Big Brothers! I’m over here!”
Far in the distance, Chulwoo spotted a young girl eagerly jumping up and down in place. He spoke triumphantly.
“Ha-ha! Senior Brother, I found her!”
“...Yes, well done. Very well done.”
Baek Museong put a hand to his head.
Just then—
Whoosh.
Hundreds of people began murmuring as they parted like a field of reeds before the wind.
At the end of the open path stood a man like an iron tower. Chulwoo muttered without realizing it,
“Is that a man or a bear?”
“He’s a man. If not for him, the Jin Family of Taiyuan would not be what it is today.”
Baek Museong respectfully offered a cupped-fist salute to the bear-like man, Jin Wikyung.
Thud-thud-thud-thud!
The scenery whipped past us. Hyuk Mujin, riding beside me, shouted over the pounding hooves.
“We were definitely slow on the way there, but we’re incredibly fast coming back. Is it because we took our time two days ago?”
“Everything happens for a reason.”
“What reason?”
“We move faster when no one tries to stuff his face while riding a horse.”
“Ah.”
Cheongpung had looked gloomy the entire trip. Before we left, I had stopped him from packing a mountain of food.
“I’m hungry.”
I answered coldly.
“Endure it.”
A Peak master’s digestion was Peak-level too. Cheongpung crapped as much as he ate, then ate as much as he crapped.
And since he ate often, he naturally had to crap often...
Damn it. This is disgusting. I’ll stop there.
“How far are we?”
“We just passed the ninth village, so... We should arrive in half a shichen at the earliest, or one full shichen at the latest.”
The sunlight pouring down made my eyes sting. I looked up at the sun as it slowly climbed toward the middle of the sky.
“So we’ll arrive around noon?”
“Probably.”
“We’re late, aren’t we?”
“Of course we’re late. Isn’t that why we’re riding like hell, trying to be a little less late?”
Fair point.
Instead of answering, I spurred my horse onward. With every stride, the long bundle strapped across my back thumped against the horse’s back.
Ugh, what a pain.
The bundle contained the Unnamed Sword.
I was supposed to have returned it to Jeok Cheongang, but instead, I had somehow ended up taking it back.
As long as I lived in a Murim where the law was damn far away and fists were painfully close, I had no choice.
It’s not like I can put it in my inventory either.
I could at least claim I had tucked the Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual inside my clothes. But if an entire sword suddenly popped out of my pocket, there would be no explaining that away.
If I were alone, it might be different. But with other people watching, it would be the perfect way to get accused of practicing demonic, heterodox arts.
I really got myself into a mess this time.
It wasn’t that I resented being saddled with a troublesome object. I simply hated the thought of having to meet Fire King Jeok Cheongang—that terrifying old man—again.
“Let’s meet again soon.”
Meet again, my ass.
Every time I remembered what he had said a few shichen ago, my stomach churned.
Hyuk Mujin, who had been sneaking glances at me from time to time, asked,
“Why do you look like that?”
“I was thinking about the Fire King.”
“Ugh. Life’s too short for anything but happy thoughts, so why imagine something that horrible?”
“If you were me, wouldn’t you think about him? He said he’d be back soon.”
“Speaking of which, could you give me some time off? I suddenly miss my family.”
“You bastard. You’re trying to save yourself.”
“You never know what might happen. Before I die, I should at least see my parents’ faces one more time.”
“That doesn’t sound like something an unfilial son who hasn’t shown his face in years should say.”
“I’d like to take this opportunity to become a good son.”
“Nope.”
I dismissed Hyuk Mujin’s bullshit and looked up at the sky with a sigh.
“Even the heavens are heartless. Why did that old man have to leave this thing with me?”
“He said it was a pain to carry around.”
“For such a petty reason?”
“With him, I can completely believe it.”
That was surprisingly convincing.
“I could lose it before he comes back. Or I could quietly pocket it for myself.”
“You, Captain?”
Hyuk Mujin laughed as if he had just heard a brilliant joke.
“If you were that kind of person, what have you been doing all this time? If you hadn’t been on the verge of death, you probably would’ve just kept the Blazing Flame Divine Pill too.”
“That’s...”
He had a point.
“Just hide it somewhere no one will notice. Who knows? Maybe that great Fire King will teach you a move in return.”
“Teach me, my ass. I’m sure he’d love to teach the man who killed his Disciple.”
The absurdity drew a quiet laugh from me.

The Fire Gate Clan was said to pass its arts down to a single successor and never teach outsiders. Even setting personal feelings aside, the idea that he would teach martial arts to an outsider like me was ridiculous.
“Your nonsense is only funny in moderation, you idiot.”
“Well, now that you mention it, I suppose you’re right.”
At that moment, Cheongpung—who had been drooping like a corpse and endlessly repeating that he was hungry—spoke up.
“Isn’t he trying to take you as his Disciple, Benefactor?”
“Maybe not? I think he is. Grandpa Jeok seemed to be watching you closely, Benefactor.”
“Me?”
“Captain?” Hyuk Mujin asked.
Our gazes met in midair. Hyuk Mujin looked utterly baffled. I was probably making the same face.
We both let out disbelieving laughs.
“That’s great. Congratulations in advance, Captain.”
“Yeah. Thanks.”
Me? Someone he’d known for barely a day or two?
The idea was so absurd it didn’t even qualify as a joke.
“Maybe not? Or am I right?”
As Cheongpung tilted his head over his own bizarre suggestion, Hyuk Mujin raised a finger and pointed into the distance.
“Can you see it?”
I could.
People were walking down a well-kept road. Farther ahead lay a broad expanse of land surrounded by a teeming crowd.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan.
I was back after three days away.

paragraphs: Step. Step.
Under countless watchful eyes, two men walked toward each other. When they finally came face-to-face, they exchanged cupped-fist salutes.
“I am Jin Wikyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“I’m Baek Museong of Huashan.”
Huashan.
And Baek Museong.
Those two names alone carried tremendous weight.
Exclamations erupted from every direction, instantly shattering the silence.
“Huashan!”
“Baek Museong! It’s Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong!”
Though ordinary civilians were mixed in among them, a considerable number of those gathered here today were martial artists.
The name of Huashan and the epithet Huashan’s Lone Crane carried immense prestige.
“My heavens, why did Huashan’s Lone Crane come here?”
“Was the Jin Family of Taiyuan really this influential?”
“W-Wait. If Huashan’s Lone Crane came here, then...”
The people who had been talking over one another began scanning the area. Before long, they spotted the man and woman beside Baek Museong, and another round of exclamations broke out.
“That young man must be the Defeated Flower Fist. He’s enormous, just like I heard.”
“The Flower Sword Phoenix is here too! She’s even beautiful!”
“Whoa! It’s the Three Plum Blossom Elites!”
Chulwoo and Eunhyang looked bewildered by the unexpectedly fervent reception.
Both had accompanied their Master, the Heavenly Sword True Person, into the martial world a few times, but neither had ever received cheers like these.
“What the hell? Am I really this famous? They even know my epithet?”
“Senior Brother Chul, did you hear that? Someone just called me beautiful.”
Chulwoo’s expression turned stern.
“You heard wrong. Pay it no mind.”
“...You’re seriously annoying.”
They had trained together under the same Master since childhood and grown up like brother and sister. Jin Wikyung smiled faintly as they glared daggers at each other.
“You two seem close.”
“They’re still immature and constantly causing trouble. They have a long way to go.”
“Ha-ha. The Defeated Flower Fist and the Flower Sword Phoenix are both outstanding young prodigies. Surely that can’t be true.”
“You flatter us.”
A faint smile touched Baek Museong’s lips. Though this was their first meeting, he found himself liking Jin Wikyung.
Perhaps it was because of the man’s distinctive way of putting people at ease. Or perhaps it was his familiar bulk, which reminded Baek Museong of Chulwoo.
“Let us go inside. This is hardly the place for an important conversation.”
“I agree.”
They had already drawn attention unintentionally.
If even a single word about the Sword Saint slipped out with so many people watching, there would undoubtedly be an uproar.
“Well, then.”
Jin Wikyung dipped his head and led the way.
Baek Museong followed amid the cheers and countless stares, only to stop short.
He could no longer sense his junior disciples behind him.
What is it?
Baek Museong glanced back and saw Chulwoo standing tall as an iron tower, staring intently at something.
“Second.”
At Baek Museong’s call, Chulwoo slowly turned his head.
“Yes, Senior Brother.”
“Is something wrong?”
“No. Nothing.”
Eunhyang, who was standing beside Chulwoo, abruptly cut in.
“That’s not true. Senior Brother Chul was staring at someone just now.”
“Do you know that person?”
Chulwoo immediately shook his head. His massive frame subtly blocked Eunhyang from view.
“As if. Other than going out a couple of times with our Master, I’ve been cooped up at headquarters the whole time.”
“That is... true.”
“My stomach suddenly started hurting, so I was only looking for a privy.”
“Really?”
“Yes. So, if you don’t mind, could I stop by the privy before we go?”
“How long has it been since you last took a piss?”
Chulwoo deliberately hardened his expression.
“If you take care of the big business first, the small business gets taken care of at the same time. But you can’t take care of the big business while doing the small business.”
“...Uh, sure.”
Baek Museong felt vaguely uneasy.
Perhaps it was because his Second Junior Brother, who usually rambled on without making a lick of sense, had answered so smoothly.
“Second, are you thinking about something else—”
He could not finish.
Jin Wikyung had stopped and was looking back at them in puzzlement.
“Young Hero Baek, is something the matter?”
“Oh, no. My junior disciple said he had an urgent matter.”
“What sort of matter?”
“Well... he needs to relieve himself.”
“Oh.”
The people who had been listening closely snickered. Chulwoo scratched the back of his head awkwardly.
“I apologize.”
“Not at all. You must be exhausted after traveling all the way to our family. You should take this opportunity to rest properly.”

Baek Museong considered it for a moment, then nodded. The important conversation was between him and Jin Wikyung anyway. Better to let his junior disciples rest than have them standing beside him and yawning their heads off.
“Great Hero Jin has given you permission, so go ahead.”
“Big Bro—no, Senior Brother. Can I go too?”
“Yes. Do you dislike it?”
“Yes. I just want to stay beside Senior Brother.”
Eunhyang nodded vigorously, and Jin Wikyung smiled.
“Then that settles it. Young Hero Baek?”
“Ah, yes. Let us go.”
Baek Museong resumed walking, still looking unconvinced. Before long, however, he put the matter out of his mind.
Surely nothing could happen in such a short time.
As Chulwoo watched the group recede into the distance, a martial artist from the Jin Family of Taiyuan approached him.
“I’ll guide you to the privy.”
“What do I need a privy for?”
“Pardon?”
“We’re surrounded by mountains. I can just take a dump by the side of the road. Don’t you agree?”
The people surrounding them burst into loud laughter.

There was a common prejudice that members of the Nine Sects and One Gang would be arrogant and rude. But Chulwoo’s refreshing banter made everyone feel as if a weight had been lifted from their chests.
“Of course. That’s right.”
“Though this is the frontier, the mountain scenery around here is beautiful. Go take care of your business while enjoying the view!”
“Hey, Defeated Flower Fist! Since fate brought us together, would you like me to recommend a scenic spot?”
Chulwoo threw back his head and roared with laughter.
“Ha-ha-ha! A scenic spot? Sounds good. But I don’t want to go to the place where you took a dump. Let’s see...”
Chulwoo casually swept his gaze over the crowd, then raised a finger and pointed at one man.
“How about that Brother over there guides me?”
The middle-aged man who had been staring blankly at Chulwoo all this time jolted in surprise.
“M-Me?”
“That’s right. You.”
The middle-aged man was Woo Hwangtae, and his face turned the color of shit.
“Slow down a little. Let’s take it easy from here.”
“Why?”
“Can’t you see the horse is foaming at the mouth? And if we arrive panting and out of breath, everyone will look at us and think, Ah, that bastard was late.”
“That makes a strange amount of sense.”
We gradually eased up on the reins. As we descended the hill, the Jin Family of Taiyuan slowly came into view below.
“By the way, there sure are a lot of people.”
“Seriously. From what I heard, they weren’t supposed to invite anywhere near that many.”
Even a rough count put the crowd camped out before the main gate of the Jin Family of Taiyuan well over several hundred.
Though we were still quite far away, we could even hear faint cheers.
Did an idol show up or something?
I drew on my internal energy and focused on my ears. My hearing, now several times sharper than usual, picked up every cheer from the crowd.
Hyuk Mujin quietly watched me for a moment before asking, “What’s going on? Did they say an important guest arrived?”
“Huashan’s Last Crane and the Plum Blossom Cutoff, apparently.”
“...Those are epithets?”
“Don’t ask me. That’s what I heard.”
We were still pretty far away, so there was a limit to what I could make out.
Still, what kind of epithets were those? Did the Plum Blossom Cutoff have some sort of grudge against Huashan?
At that moment, Cheongpung, who had been lying facedown across his horse’s neck, spoke.
“Benefactor. They said Huashan’s Lone Crane and the Three Plum Blossom Elites.”
“Oh, really?”
“Yes. I heard them clearly.”
He could hear that from this distance?
Cheongpung was the strongest martial artist among us, so he was probably right.
“I see.”
While I merely nodded without much interest, Hyuk Mujin was so shocked that he nearly fell off his horse.
“H-Huashan’s Lone Crane! The Three Plum Blossom Elites!”
“Are they famous?”
“Famous? That’s putting it mildly! They’re the direct disciples of the Heavenly Sword True Person, the Sect Leader of Huashan!”
“Is this one of those things where you’d have to be an idiot not to know them?”
“No martial artist could possibly not know them!”
“Oh, really?”
I casually pointed behind me. Cheongpung was staring wide-eyed and clapping.
“Wow, those are cool epithets. But where did they say they were from?”
“Shaolin Temple, maybe?”
Was he insane?
This was coming from the youngest Junior Brother of Huashan’s Sect Leader himself.
After a long silence, Hyuk Mujin finally spoke.
“Huashan’s Lone Crane. The Three Plum Blossom Elites. You really haven’t heard of them?”
“I like Huashan! I like plum blossoms even more!”
“...Right.”
Style was temporary, but class was forever.
It wasn’t even “I like Dad, but I like Mom more.” What the hell was this?
Was Huashan filed away in his head as Dad and plum blossoms as Mom?
While I pondered the workings of Cheongpung’s mind, Hyuk Mujin finally collected himself and reached a conclusion.
“Anyway, they’re insanely famous.”
“I see.”
“I see.”
“...Is that really all the reaction you’ve got?”
“What kind of reaction were you expecting?”
“Most people would react like I did.”
“So I’m supposed to be so shocked that I fall off my horse?”
Hyuk Mujin climbed back into the saddle and launched into an impassioned speech.
“That’s how big a deal they are! The Heavenly Sword True Person’s disciples! The future of Huashan!”
“I see. They’re no joke.”
I turned toward Cheongpung.
“May I ask your grandfather’s full name?”
“His surname is Mae, and his given name uses the characters Jong and Hak. Mae Jonghak.”
“And his epithet?”
“The Sword Saint.”
“Did you hear that, Mujin?”
“Yes.”

Hyuk Mujin nodded with a blank expression, then came to his senses. His eagerness to make us understand how extraordinary Huashan’s Lone Crane and the Three Plum Blossom Elites were was almost palpable.
“Great Hero Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint, doesn’t count. Honestly, that would be like an adult joining a children’s fight.”
“So what’s your conclusion?”

“Huashan’s Lone Crane is already a master who has surpassed the level of a young prodigy. At this rate, becoming the next Sect Leader won’t be a problem. The other two members of the Three Plum Blossom Elites are objects of admiration among young martial artists too.”
They really were impressive. From the way he talked about young prodigies, they still seemed to be quite young, yet the public considered them at least world-class.
“Then why am I not particularly impressed?”
“That... I’m not sure.”
Hyuk Mujin thought about it carefully, then his expression suddenly went flat.
“Now that I think about it, I’m not exactly bursting with excitement either.”
“Really?”
“Yes. Huashan’s Lone Crane used to be my idol.”
Cheongpung abruptly cut in.
“Isn’t it because of Grandpa Jeok?”
“Huh?”
“Eh?”
“He’s incredibly strong. And he’s trying to take you as his Disciple.”
The second part was complete bullshit, but the first part was right.
If the Sword Saint, Mae Jonghak, was something above the clouds that I could not even properly picture in my mind, the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was a monster that had revealed itself in the flesh.
After experiencing a monster larger than a hundred-story building, it was only natural that a monster the size of a four-story commercial building would make less of an impression.
Cheongpung looked straight at me and continued slowly.
“You’re plenty strong, Benefactor.”
“...What?”
“I mean it.”
Something tickled in one corner of my chest, but he was undeniably right about that too.
It wasn’t that I thought I could fight Huashan’s Lone Crane right now without falling behind.
I was certain I could catch up to him before long.
It had taken me only a few months to go from a Third Rate martial artist who knew nothing about martial arts to a Peak master.
I couldn’t even begin to imagine how much I might grow in another year or two.
To me, Huashan’s Lone Crane was a milestone along the road—not an impassable wall.
“Thanks for saying that.”
Cheongpung answered with a sunny smile.
“You’re welcome. Grandpa said weak martial artists without firm resolve need constant attention.”
Fuck me. It had just been a pep talk.
I was wrestling with the urge to split open the crown of Cheongpung’s head when—
“H-Hey, Young Hero Chul!”
“Hah, listen to this old coot calling me Young Hero Chul. Didn’t you call me a cow’s head earlier?”
“N-No, Great Hero Chul! I committed a grave discourtesy, -so!”
“Committed-so? -so? Cow? You just called me a cow again, didn’t you?”
“Eeeeeek! Isn’t that taking it too far? Do you even know how old I am?”
“Yes, Elder. Let’s head up there and have a little talk.”
A young man with a massive build reminiscent of Jin Wikyung was dragging a middle-aged man behind him.
Just as they were about to enter the mountainside beside the hill, the young man spotted us and stopped.
“Brother over there, do you need something?”
He means me, right?
