paragraphs: A hulking man reminiscent of a Minotaur glared at me with enormous, bulging eyes.
“Brother over there, do you need something?”
He was telling me to pretend I hadn’t seen anything and move along.
It was no different from something a third-rate thug in a movie might say, but according to Qi Sense, this hulking man was neither a third-rate thug nor some inept wandering martial artist.
System Level: 95 — Chulwoo
He’s as skilled as he looks.
In Murim terms, he was a Peak master. In modern terms, he was at least an A-rank Hunter.
If a guy like that were a thug, forget the police—the people’s cane. Even the people’s sledgehammer wouldn’t be enough.
Where did this guy come from?
For a moment, the epithets I’d just heard—Huashan’s Lone Crane and the Three Plum Blossom Elites—flashed through my mind, but that was as far as it went.
No matter how I looked at him, he seemed more like the Majang-dong Knifeman or Seocho-dong Twin Axes than a crane or a plum blossom. Those sorts of nicknames suited him much better.
When I merely stared without answering, the hulking man—Chulwoo—frowned.
“Didn’t you hear me? Are you deaf? Or mute?”
Before I could say anything, Hyuk Mujin jumped in.
“What an outrageous fellow. How dare you speak so rudely to our Young Master?”
“And pretending not to hear someone is polite?”
“Ahem!”
“What are you ahem-ing about? How important do you think you are, refusing to answer when someone speaks to you?”
“You insolent bastard! Do you need a beating to come to your senses?”
I stopped Hyuk Mujin as he reached for his sword scabbard.
“That’s enough.”
“Please don’t stop me. Someone like him needs to be taught a harsh lesson!”
“He’s stronger than you.”
“Ah. I don’t think this is my place to step in.”
Chulwoo opened his mouth with an incredulous expression.
“Is he your subordinate?”
“For now.”
“You must have a hard time.”
“Every day is a battle against my own patience.”
After looking our group up and down, Chulwoo clicked his tongue.
“You look like martial artists, so you’d be better off going on your way. This man wronged me badly.”
Chulwoo grabbed this man by the collar and lifted him. He was so strong that the heavyset middle-aged man shot straight into the air.
“Eeeek! H-Help me!”
Above the terrified middle-aged man’s head floated the Level window I had detected earlier with Qi Sense.
System Level: 60 — Woo Hwangtae
That was a name that made me crave hangover soup.
It also sounded vaguely familiar.
Woo Hwangtae, Woo Hwangtae... Where have I heard that before?
While I was thinking, Chulwoo shook Woo Hwangtae violently by the collar.
“What do you mean, help you? Don’t drag innocent people into this. Just take a few hits and get it over with.”
“G-Great Hero, please don’t do this. Let’s resolve it through conversation. Conversation.”
“Conversation?”
“Y-Yes! Conversation!”
“Conversation sounds good. Then let’s go somewhere without any people around and have a nice, intimate chat.”
He clearly meant to have a physical conversation.
Woo Hwangtae, who was being dragged away against his will, screamed,
“I-I was invited here by the Jin Family of Taiyuan! I’m supposed to have a private audience with the Lesser Family Head!”
“So was I. And I’m a simple, crude man by nature, so I don’t particularly care whether you’re meeting the Lesser Family Head or the Family Head.”
“Eeeeeek!”
This wouldn’t do. Someone was going to die before I remembered his name.
I had no desire to get dragged into an unnecessary dispute, but simply walking past didn’t sit right with me either.
From the sound of it, he’s a fairly important guest.
The fact that he was supposed to meet privately with Jin Wikyung bothered me, as did Chulwoo’s casual disparagement of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
I smacked my lips and stepped forward.
“Excuse me.”
“All that fat and you still have to make people’s lives difficult... Did you call me?”
“Yes.”
“What do you want?”
“It’s nothing important.”
Chulwoo paused, and I continued.
“It’s a good day. Wouldn’t it be better to talk things out?”
“You want me to stop?”
“I’m sorry for sticking my nose where it doesn’t belong, but wouldn’t it look bad for the Jin Family of Taiyuan if its guests started fighting on a day like this?”
“Listen, Young Hero.”
Chulwoo rubbed his neck with an annoyed expression. At the same time, he dropped what little politeness remained in his speech.
“This is personal. If you get involved, you’ll only make trouble for yourself.”
“I’m already tired of this. What can you do?”
“You’re getting awfully informal.”
“Yep. Right back at you.”
“How old are you?”
“Twenty.”
“Twenty? Ha. Still green. Nice and green.”
“How old are you?”
“I’m twenty-five, you young bastard.”
Good grief. I was surprised twice.
Once by the boomer attitude of a twenty-five-year-old, and again by the fact that his face belonged to a man in his mid-twenties.
Even if he had been fed protein supplements instead of breast milk as a baby, he shouldn’t have ended up like this. I asked with considerable astonishment,
“Twenty-five? Is your name Benjamin or something? You’re living your life backward all by yourself.”
Benjamin Chulwoo glared at me.
“What kind of bullshit is that?”
“It’s not bullshit. It’s a fact. Looking that old must have made life tough.”
“Old? Shut up! Everyone around me says I look young!”
“Everyone around you? Number one, your mother. Number two, your father. Number three, your grandmother. Pick one of the three. Oh, let’s make number four your youngest aunt.”
“You beardless little brat...”
“Pull down your pants. I want to see whether you’ve got hair on your dick.”
“You little—!”
“Woof, woof-woof! Woof-woof-woof!”
Chulwoo released Woo Hwangtae’s collar. Trembling as he looked back and forth between earth and sky, he drew a deep breath.
“You... Hoo. Hoooo.”
“Are you angry, Benjamin?”
“Shut that damn mouth!”
He seemed to have completely lost his temper.
I didn’t mean to take it this far.
I had merely returned each insult as it came, and somehow this was where we had ended up.
Snorting like a frenzied Minotaur, Chulwoo finally managed to force the words out. With great difficulty. Tremendous difficulty.
“Y-You bastard, what the hell are you?”
“What kind of bastard do you think I am?”
“A bastard who’s gone mad wanting to die.”
Crack.
Bones shifted with an ugly crunch inside his fist, which was as thick as a shovel handle.
Chulwoo ground his teeth and glared at me.
“Do you even know what it means to interfere in someone else’s personal gratitude and grudges in Murim?”

“I already apologized for sticking my nose where it doesn’t belong. But if guests start throwing punches, what does that make the people who invited them? You ought to consider our family’s position too.”
“Our family?”
“Yeah. Our family.”
“Are you perhaps a member of the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
“I’m no household parasite, if that’s what you mean.”
“Make one more wordplay joke, and I’ll put you in bed for three years.”
“Watch your mouth—unless you want your family observing three years of mourning.”
Chulwoo smiled thinly. It wasn’t a smile born of amusement. It was the kind of smile that appeared on its own when someone’s anger had reached the top of his head.
“My Senior Brother warned me over and over... but I can’t let you off. Time for you to take a few hits.”
Boom!
Before he could finish speaking, an enormous roar rang out, and the ground shattered.
The two-meter-tall giant launched himself like a cannonball. The time it took him to reach the tip of my nose was no more than an instant.
“It’s going to hurt.”
Whoosh!
With a chilling voice, the air scattered.
No—it was crushed.
It was nothing more than a simple punch, with no form or martial principle added to it. The force contained in that fist exploded with enough momentum to shatter a thousand-geun boulder.
But...
It doesn’t matter if it doesn’t hit me.
Bang! B-bang!
I bent backward as if lying down. The fist tore through the air a handspan above me, compressed air exploding from its tip. A tree about ten feet away went flying as if caught in a typhoon.
Wow. This guy was serious.
I had to marvel at the sheer power.
If an ordinary First Rate master had taken that blow, it would not have ended with mere pain. Once Chulwoo lost his temper, he seemed unable to see anything else.
“Hey, hey. Take it easy. Take it easy.”
“You rat-like bastard!”
Whoosh! Whoooosh!
One punch, two punches, three. Each time I easily dodged another blow, my suspicion hardened into certainty.
I think I can win.
Even a thousand-geun boulder had to be hit before it could be shattered.
No matter how powerful an attack was, it meant nothing if it failed to connect.
Moreover, Chulwoo had only just entered the Peak realm and couldn’t even project Fist Energy. If our martial insight was comparable, I had an overwhelming advantage.
Because I possessed a special power no one else had.
Stats.
Whoooosh! Bang!
After yet another wild swing, Chulwoo exploded in frustration.
“What the hell!”
“You’re too worked up. Take a deep breath and relax. Then you might manage to touch a single hair on my head.”

Meanwhile, I had completely regained my composure. Hyuk Mujin and Cheongpung were watching from the sidelines as if none of this concerned them, while Woo Hwangtae stared at our exchange with his mouth hanging open.
Given how things were going, Chulwoo also seemed considerably flustered.
“What the hell are you?”
“A member of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“There’s no way someone like you could be in this backwater... Wait.”
Chulwoo stared intently at me, then suddenly narrowed his eyes.
“Are you the Heaven Shaking Sword?”
“I’m somewhat related to him. As far as I know, we came out of the same womb.”
“Then... are you the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
I grinned.
“Bingo.”
He might not have known what bingo meant, but he understood that it meant yes and clenched his fist.
“I knew you had some skill.”
“Try hitting me at least once before saying that. You said it would hurt, but this just feels refreshing.”
“I’ll admit it. You may not be a dragon, but you could at least qualify as an imugi.”
“Good grief, that’s a harsh assessment.”
“Your mouth has reached the realm of transcendence.”
“It’s all psychological warfare. Take a look at yourself. Your eyes are rolled back, and you keep swinging at thin air.”
“Don’t get the wrong idea. I simply had no desire to use my sect’s martial arts against a nameless small fry like you.”
“Which sect is that? The Dodong Sect?”
“You don’t need to know.”
He spat out a wad of phlegm and muttered,
“Damn it, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. That takes the fun out of it.”
Same for me.
He was obviously a disciple of a fairly well-known sect, but if we fought until one of us fell, both of us would have to deal with the backlash.
“I’m holding back because of my eldest brother.”
“I’ll let you off because of my Senior Brother.”
We spoke at nearly the same time and glared at each other.
“Oh? Look at this bastard.”
“Bastard? You little brat, how dare you speak to an adult that way!”
“Adult, my ass. Do you even know how old I am, calling yourself an adult?”
“What else is someone who’s barely twenty supposed to be but a child?”
“That’s not what I meant...!”
If I added my age in Murim to my age in the modern world, I was practically fifty. But there was no chance of getting that across to him.
I swallowed the words that were about to burst out.
“Forget it. What’s the point of talking to a guy like you? Anyway, in Murim, the strong are the adults.”
“What? Are you saying I’m weaker than you?”
“Obviously. Didn’t you feel the difference between us just now?”
“You son of a bitch! I could chew you up and still not feel satisfied!”
“Try hitting me, if you can.”
“You think I can’t?”
Just as Chulwoo raised his fist with a heavy snort, someone’s voice abruptly cut in.
“It would be best if you both stopped now.”
Wipeng descended with an elusive movement technique and swept us with a chilly gaze.
His eyes passed over Cheongpung, Hyuk Mujin, and Woo Hwangtae, who was a complete mess after being dragged around, before finally shooting toward Chulwoo and me like arrows.
“Defeated Flower Fist. Third Young Master.”
“No, Great Hero Wipeng. It’s not like that. The circumstances...”
“That’s right. I was merely...”
His voice, colder than the bitter winds and snow of the north, froze our next words solid.
“Are you both determined to bring utter shame upon your respective schools?”
Chulwoo and I quietly shut our mouths.
“How long has Defeated Flower Fist been gone?”
“Dunno. Feels like it’s been more than half an hour.”
“Why isn’t he back?”
“Maybe he’s blocked up.”
“A Daoist from Huashan?”
“Why would that matter? If he’s a Daoist from Huashan, does that mean his shit should come out smoothly too?”
“I suppose you’re right.”
Just as the theory that Chulwoo was constipated was all but confirmed, the people who spotted a party of riders coming down the hill burst into cheers.
Among them was a face no martial artist in Shanxi Province could possibly fail to recognize.
“It’s the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi!”
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi! He’s coming with the Defeated Flower Fist!”
“Wooaaah!”
The appearance of two young and outstanding men sent the crowd into a frenzy.
The two young prodigies whom everyone believed would become future leaders of Murim walked side by side, waving their hands.
Every time they did, cheers erupted from all directions, along with hands reaching out to touch even their clothing.
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi!”
“The Defeated Flower Fist!”
“Well now, they look pretty close. Were they acquainted?”
“Does that matter? Real talent recognizes real talent. There’s nothing strange about them forming a deep friendship in such a short time.”
“Now that you mention it, that makes sense. They look great together.”
While everyone watched them with warm smiles, the beaming Jin Taekyung and Chulwoo exchanged words in voices so low they were barely audible.
“I let you off earlier. You know that, right? You couldn’t even touch me.”
“Bullshit. I didn’t use even half my strength.”
“I didn’t use even a third.”
“I misspoke. I didn’t use even one-tenth.”
“My mistake too. Truth is, I didn’t use even one percent.”
“Now that I think about it, neither did I.”
“Is this guy completely insane?”
“Who are you to say that?”
Amid the thunderous cheers, a fierce exchange unfolded—one only Peak masters could hear.

“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi! Look this way just once!”
“Eeeek! Young Hero Jin!”
“Waaah!”
They say even a mutt has the advantage on its home turf.
No matter how famous the Three Plum Blossom Elites were, they couldn’t beat the pride of Shanxi Province—the son of Taiyuan—on his own turf.
As I beamed and waved, Chulwoo whispered to me.
“Look at the corners of your mouth. Enjoying yourself?”
“Look at the corners of yours. Are you crying?”
“You Shanxi bumpkin.”
“Yeah, next mountain man.”
“You little—”
“What, you—”
Just as sparks were about to fly again, a thread of Sound Transmission pierced my ear.
Third Young Master!
Wipeng was glaring at me with a fierce expression. He looked like he wanted to slap me right then and there.
He must have sent a similar Sound Transmission to Chulwoo, because the man added a curt remark with a dissatisfied expression.
“I let you off.”
I answered with a derisive snort.
When the crowd’s cheers first told me that Chulwoo was a fairly prominent young prodigy of Huashan, I’d been rather surprised.
But that was all.
So what if he’s one of the Three Plum Blossom Elites?
I’d already seen more than enough of Huashan’s martial arts, thanks to a certain someone trudging along beside me.
“I’m hungry. I’m hungry.”
Cheongpung was a strange guy no matter how many times I saw him, but there was no denying that he was a Peak master who had mastered Huashan’s supreme secret arts.
Thanks to him, I was confident I could counter whatever martial arts Chulwoo used. The only thing Chulwoo had over me was Huashan’s backing.
Ah, no. I take that back.
Now that I thought about it, the difference in our backgrounds was pretty serious. No matter how far the Jin Family of Taiyuan had risen, the Nine Sects and One Gang were overwhelmingly powerful.
Fuck. I lose.
The Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were essentially Murim’s version of a corporate alliance.
A bunch of already powerful conglomerates had banded together to gang up on everyone else. Who could possibly stand against that?

Fortunately, for all their talk of being the orthodox faction, they didn’t encroach on the neighborhood markets. That was why small and medium-sized companies like the Jin Family of Taiyuan still had room to climb.
Seen that way, Huashan is clearly paying close attention to this matter.
Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong.
If everything Hyuk Mujin had told me was true, Baek Museong was practically the next Sect Leader of Huashan—recognized as such by everyone, including himself.
There was one person among Huashan’s young prodigies who could be considered his only equal, though...
“Benefactor, I’m really hungry. Do you have any dumplings left?”
“No. I don’t.”
“Oh. Aaaah...”
Cheongpung was a lost cause.
Huashan’s Daoists would probably convert to Islam before that guy became the Sect Leader of Huashan.
Even I, an outsider, couldn’t help thinking, What kind of person is this? How much worse must it be for the people of Huashan?
He’s the kind of guy who’ll experience everything the world has to offer, then decide he’d like to try being Huashan’s Sect Leader too. Yeah.
As I imagined this highly plausible future, Chulwoo spoke with an irritated look.
“What, are you possessed by the ghost of someone who died craving dumplings? Please shut up and walk.”
Chulwoo flinched as Wipeng, Hyuk Mujin, and I all turned to stare at him.
“W-What? Why are you suddenly looking at me like that?”
“Hey, don’t tell me...”
“Young Hero Chul, you don’t know?”
“Come on, surely not. You’re one of the Three Plum Blossom Elites. There’s no way you wouldn’t know.”
As our reactions came one after another, Chulwoo’s ox-like eyes darted around.
“What? Why is everyone acting like this?”
Why else? Because he couldn’t recognize an elder of his own sect.
In terms of seniority, Cheongpung was the Sword Saint’s Disciple and the youngest Junior Brother of the Heavenly Sword True Person, Huashan’s current Sect Leader.
That made him Chulwoo’s master’s Junior Brother—in other words, his Martial Uncle.
Actually, now that I think about it, maybe he wouldn’t know.
The Sword Saint, Mae Jonghak, had raised Cheongpung while living in seclusion. Only a select few within Huashan could possibly know his face and identity.
I clicked my tongue at Chulwoo, who was standing right in front of his Martial Uncle without recognizing him.
“Tsk, tsk. It really is darkest beneath the lamp.”
“What the hell are you talking about?”
“Never mind. You’ll find out soon enough.”
“Damn it, this is driving me insane.”
As Chulwoo pounded his chest in frustration, we left the cheering crowd behind and passed through the main gate of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
At once, more than a hundred pairs of eyes turned toward us, accompanied by whispers from every direction. The atmosphere was completely different from the one outside the gate.
“That young man...”
“That’s the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. He’s every bit as handsome as I’d heard.”
“The Defeated Flower Fist is here too. Isn’t he the Heavenly Sword True Person’s second Disciple?”
“Then who are the two young men beside them?”
“I couldn’t tell you.”
More than a hundred men and women of all ages mingled inside. Their clothes and bearing spoke of wealth and leisure.
The power players of Shanxi Province.
Some were Sect Leaders, while others were wealthy merchants. Every one of them possessed enough influence and ability to earn a formal invitation to this gathering.
At first glance, it almost looks like an aristocratic ball.
A strange feeling came over me as I walked on.

These people could be considered Shanxi Province’s ruling class, yet they were merely supporting players at this gathering. Their curious, admiring gazes made something tickle in one corner of my chest.
Then it happened.
“My name is Jang Se-pal. I lead a small sect called the Hequ Sect.”
“Ah, yes. Hello.”
“I’ve long admired the reputation of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi from the bottom of my heart, and...”
The middle-aged martial artist launched into a long-winded speech about how honored he was to meet me. Then people began swarming toward us like a horde of Zombies.
“Greetings. I run a small martial arts academy near Yangcheon...”
“Pardon? Oh, yes.”
“Young Hero Jin, I have something important to discuss with you. Perhaps we could move somewhere else...”
“Right now? That might be difficult.”
“This is my daughter. She wanted to meet the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi at least once, so I brought her along. If you happen to find her appealing...”
“Yes, yes.”
“Oh! Then shall I send a matchmaker at once?”
“Wait, wait! I answered that wrong!”
What the hell was going on?
Requests for handshakes—or rather, a barrage of fist-and-palm salutes—poured in from every direction. I was on the verge of losing my mind.
If Wipeng hadn’t stepped forward at just the right moment, I would have ended up accepting every favor and marriage proposal wrapped in flowery language.
“Everyone, restrain yourselves!”
The shout of a Peak master infused with internal energy made the people flinch, and we took the opportunity to escape. Chulwoo clicked his tongue as though he’d had enough.
“That was excessive. Are all the people of Shanxi like that?”
Of course not. This was a special case.
Wipeng was the only member of our group who hadn’t been flustered. He spoke with his usual calm expression.
“This will happen often from now on, so you should gradually get used to it.”
“I’m supposed to experience things like this often?”
“You’re a direct descendant of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, after all.”
“I almost got married five times just now.”
“That’s only natural for a promising young prodigy without a partner.”
“I heard someone claim they were betrothed to me while we were still in the womb... Is that true?”
“What does it matter whether it’s true or false? Look on the bright side.”
My hair stood on end.
I’d spent twenty-seven years in the modern world without ever dating anyone, and now I was afraid I might suddenly end up in an arranged marriage.
In Murim, thousands of miles from home, no less.
No. I have Song-i.
Veins bulging in my neck, I shouted,
“Marriage is incredibly important! You can’t just brush it aside like that! Love between a man and a woman! Pure feelings! Don’t I get any of that?”
“No. You don’t.”
“Why?! How come?!”
Wipeng looked me up and down as if I were an insect.
“Is that something a man who’s been frequenting pleasure houses since he was sixteen should say? Did you scatter your conscience along with your silver nyang?”
“Let’s keep moving quietly. Our Lord is waiting.”
If I’d actually been to one, at least I wouldn’t have felt so wronged.
Fuck, I’d never even been to a pickup bar, let alone a pleasure house.
As I kept silent and wept tears of blood inside, Chulwoo sidled over and asked,
“Is that true?”
“What is?”
“That you’ve been visiting pleasure houses since you were sixteen.”
“None of your business. Why are you suddenly asking?”
Chulwoo flinched and began to ramble.
“Well, how should I put it? Personal curiosity, perhaps. The curiosity of a man who has steadfastly walked only the path of a martial artist...”
“You want to visit a pleasure house?”
“Ahem!”
“Finish walking the path of a martial artist. Don’t go wandering down side paths for no reason.”
I had barely finished answering with utter disdain when a voice cut in.
“Jin Taekyung is absolutely right. How long has it been since you descended from the main sect? Have you already forgotten the duty of a martial artist?”
The tone was stern, yet tinged with amusement.
The unfamiliar voice belonged to a clean-cut man. He approached with steady steps and respectfully offered a fist-and-palm salute.
But it wasn’t directed at me or Wipeng.
“Baek Museong, First-generation Disciple of Huashan, pays his respects to his Martial Uncle.”
Cheongpung remained silent for a moment before answering.
“Who are you?”
He looked to be around sixty.
The old man had a slender frame and strikingly narrow eyes.
A deeply hoarse voice rasped through his chapped lips.
“So you were utterly humiliated by some nameless nobody?”
“E-Elder, that isn’t what happened...”
The three men standing before him were sweating profusely.
They were known as the Three Hands of Zhongnan, but in the presence of an elder of their sect, they had to watch every word and every movement.
All the more so when that elder was the Roaring Fury Swordsman, a master counted among the five strongest in the Zhongnan Sect and a man notorious for his fiery temper.
“Then what happened? No matter how I listen to this, all these old ears hear is that you bastards smeared shit all over the name of the great Zhongnan Sect.”
The Three Hands of Zhongnan trembled beneath his piercing gaze.
Just as the Roaring Fury Swordsman was about to unleash his thunderous reprimand, one of the men, who had kept his mouth tightly shut the entire time, suddenly spoke.
“He wasn’t a nameless nobody.”
“What?”
Gong Ilhyuk, the man with a splint on his arm, continued.
“He said he was the Sword Saint’s Disciple.”
The revelation was so shocking that the Roaring Fury Swordsman fell speechless. After a moment, he asked in disbelief,
“...The Sword Saint?”
“Yes.”
“The Sword Saint, who has lived in seclusion all these years, raised a Disciple?”
“We suspected it at first, but... it seems to be true.”
“Your evidence?”
“Li Feng, a lay Disciple of Huashan, serves in the military of Shanxi Province. Judging by his reaction, there can be little doubt.”
“Li Feng?”
The old man’s already wrinkled brow furrowed further.
His memory wasn’t sharp enough to recall some lay Disciple of Huashan.
“Is that all?”
At the lukewarm response, Gong Ilhyuk hurriedly continued.

“He has mastered Huashan’s supreme secret arts to the Peak level despite being barely twenty. He displayed one martial art after another that only the main sect’s direct Disciples are permitted to learn...”
After hearing the entire account of what had happened, the Roaring Fury Swordsman silently rubbed his sword scabbard.
The Sword Saint’s Disciple. The Sword Saint’s Disciple.
The Sword Saint had been in seclusion for decades.
No one even knew whether he was alive or dead, yet now his Disciple had suddenly appeared in Murim?
It was hard to believe, but the Roaring Fury Swordsman was already inclined to accept it.
At the very least, I should confirm it for myself.
After remaining silent for a long while, the Roaring Fury Swordsman abruptly rose from his seat. An order fell on the startled Three Hands of Zhongnan.
“Guide me.”
“W-Where do you mean?”
“Could you mean the Sword Saint’s Disciple...?”
Unlike the other two, who stood there flustered, Gong Ilhyuk’s eyes flashed.
“As far as I know, that bastard is traveling with a scion of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“A scion of the Jin Family of Taiyuan? You mean that Jin Taekyung fellow you mentioned earlier?”
“Yes. He’s half a day’s journey from here.”
The Roaring Fury Swordsman clicked his tongue.
“You cunning bastard. That’s why you came looking for this old man, isn’t it?”

“The name of the great Zhongnan Sect has fallen into the dirt because of these inept Disciples. Elder, aren’t you the person who cares about our sect more than anyone? I happened to hear that you were in the area on business, so...”
“Cut it out. From what you’ve told me, this Jin Taekyung fellow sounds like an incredibly arrogant bastard too.”
“That’s right. A bastard like him needs to be taught a harsh lesson.”
As if the thought had only just occurred to him, Gong Ilhyuk added,
“I hear the Jin Family of Taiyuan is holding a gathering.”
“A gathering?”
“They invited every sect in Shanxi Province so they could flaunt their power.”
“They trampled on our sect, and now they’re holding a gathering?”
Anger flared in the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s eyes.
“I’ve heard enough. Lead the way.”
“I obey, Elder.”
A smug smile spread across Gong Ilhyuk’s lips.

“Second.”
“Enough. Wait, did you plan all this just to mess with me?”
“It’s the truth.”
“Senior Brother, I’m not that gullible. Now that I think about it, the people of the Jin Family of Taiyuan are quite the pranksters too. Did all of you really conspire just to fool me? Ha ha ha!”
What was this, some Korean-Chinese co-produced drama?
There was no way Huashan and the Jin Family of Taiyuan had joined forces to stage some hilarious hidden-camera prank just to fool this one guy.
“Ha ha ha.”
When no one—not even me—reacted, Chulwoo’s laughter gradually dwindled, then stopped altogether.
“...You’re serious?”
Baek Museong rubbed his temple as he answered.
“Yes.”
“Not a single word of it is a lie?”
“I told you, it’s true.”
Chulwoo whipped his head toward Cheongpung.
“Excuse me, Young Hero. What’s your name?”
“Cheongpung.”
Chulwoo’s pupils trembled. He’d clearly remembered what he’d said to Cheongpung only moments ago.
“D-Dumpling.”
“Dumpling?”
“N-Nothing. Then is this really Martial Uncle Cheongpung?”
“Without a doubt.”
I almost wished I had some popcorn.
Leaving Chulwoo to slap his own cheeks over and over as if wondering whether he was dreaming, Baek Museong spoke.
“I apologize, Martial Uncle Cheongpung.”
Cheongpung answered with an innocent expression.
“No, it’s fine.”
“You failed to recognize an elder of our sect and showed him grave disrespect. You ought to apologize a hundred times over. Is that not so?”
“Please forgive me, Martial Uncle.”
Chulwoo bowed his head gloomily. Judging by his expression, he would need some time to accept that the dumpling ghost was his Martial Uncle.
Of course, Cheongpung didn’t care in the slightest.
If anything, he was more curious about his relationship with these new faces.
“But who are all of you?”
“We are all Disciples of Huashan, just like Martial Uncle Cheongpung.”
“Oh. But I’m just Grandpa’s grandson.”

The Sword Saint hadn’t merely passed his martial arts on to Cheongpung as a Disciple. He had raised him as his grandson. That was why Cheongpung had only the vaguest understanding of sects and martial artists.
Yet even at that response, Baek Museong’s gentle smile never faltered.
“My Master goes by the title of Heavenly Sword True Person. In terms of seniority, he is your eldest Senior Brother.”
“My eldest Senior Brother?”
“Yes. Your Master—or rather, your grandfather—the Sword Saint had three Disciples before you. Have you ever heard about them?”
Cheongpung murmured uncertainly.
“I don’t really know. I think Grandpa mentioned them once, but...”
“He even came to visit you with several others ten years ago.”
Cheongpung thought hard, then suddenly exclaimed,
“Ah! That scary-looking old man!”
He’d just called the Sect Leader of Huashan a scary-looking old man. Regardless of everyone else’s shock, Cheongpung beamed now that the mystery had been solved.
“He’s my eldest Senior Brother?”
“Precisely.”
“Ohhh. I see. I thought he was a bad person. It looked like he was trying to kick Grandpa and me out.”
“You may be unfamiliar with the circumstances of our sect, Martial Uncle. You can learn about those things little by little.”
What admirable patience.
Even if Baek Museong had slapped Cheongpung across the ear in the middle of their conversation, he probably would’ve been acquitted at the first trial. Yet his smile never faltered.
No wonder there’s a crane in his epithet.
As I was thinking that, Cheongpung turned to me with a bright smile.
“Benefactor, they say they’re my Martial Nephews!”
“Ah, yes. Congratulations.”
“Do you want to be my Martial Nephew too, Benefactor?”
“Why? If you don’t want to be my Martial Nephew, I can make you my Martial Uncle.”
This crazy bastard was spouting nonsense.
Not only was that not something Cheongpung could decide on his own, but becoming Cheongpung’s Martial Uncle would make me a junior fellow Disciple of the Sword Saint, Mae Jonghak.
For all I knew, I could even order the Sect Leader of Huashan to run cigarette errands for me.
That actually sounded pretty good.
I was about to nod as if under a spell when—
“Ha ha. Young Hero Cheongpung certainly knows how to tell a joke.”
Wipeng’s mouth was smiling, but his eyes said something entirely different.
His murderous glare snapped me back to my senses.
“No, it’s fine. I’m all right.”
“Really? What a shame.”
The other two members of the Three Plum Blossom Elites stood with their mouths hanging open in disbelief, but Baek Museong merely smiled.
“You may not be able to formally enter the sect, but we can certainly welcome you as an honored guest.”
I blinked.
“Was that a formal invitation?”
“Of course. An exceptional young prodigy like Young Hero Jin is always welcome. And...”
His gentle voice continued.
“You could also keep Martial Uncle Cheongpung company on his journey back to our sect.”
Cheongpung, who had been bouncing excitedly, went still.
“Huh? Go back?”
“Yes, Martial Uncle Cheongpung.”
Baek Museong offered a deep fist-and-palm salute. When he spoke again, his voice was stern and solemn.
“It is the Sect Leader’s order. Please return to Huashan.”
Watching Cheongpung disappear into the main hall of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, Chulwoo clicked his tongue.
“What kind of man—or rather, Martial Uncle—is he?”
Even Eunhyang, who bickered with Chulwoo at every opportunity, nodded this time.
“Exactly. I didn’t know anyone could refuse our Master’s order.”
“There is one person. Grandmaster.”
“Senior Brother Chul, he doesn’t count.”
Chulwoo scratched the back of his head awkwardly.
“Well, that’s true.”
The Sect Leader’s authority was absolute. Even someone who outranked him in sect seniority couldn’t openly refuse his orders.
Challenging the Sect Leader’s authority was tantamount to tarnishing the sect’s name.
The larger the sect, the more rigidly that hierarchy was enforced.
“But to refuse him flat-out... Whew. I knew he was unusual, but he’s even more extraordinary than I expected.”
“You’ve only seen a tiny fraction of it. Earlier, I even called him Dumpling—no, never mind.”
Chulwoo shook his head, then cautiously asked,
“What are you planning to do now, Senior Brother?”
“I’m not sure.”
Baek Museong, who had been lost in thought, finally spoke.
“I didn’t expect Martial Uncle Cheongpung to refuse so stubbornly.”
“At this point, shouldn’t the Disciplinary Hall step in instead of us?”
“Why do you think so?”
“He disobeyed our Master’s order.”

Even the slightest violation of Huashan’s rules resulted in a summons from the Disciplinary Hall. If the Disciplinary Hall, which dealt with every infraction without mercy, passed judgment, Cheongpung would be treated as a serious criminal.
Seeing his Junior Brother huff indignantly, Baek Museong let out a quiet laugh.
“Martial Uncle did not violate the rules.”
“Pardon?”
“What do you mean?”
“The rules apply only to Disciples of our sect. Would a Disciple of Qingcheng Sect be punished for violating Shaolin’s rules?”
“Does that make any sense?”
“Of course it does. But Martial Uncle Cheongpung is... our Martial Uncle. He’s Grandmaster’s Disciple.”
“If only that were truly the case.”
Baek Museong added with a sigh,
“Strictly speaking, Martial Uncle Cheongpung is little different from an outsider. This happened because he never underwent the initiation ceremony.”

Everyone underwent an initiation ceremony, whether they were a main-sect Disciple or a lay Disciple. Only then did they officially become a Disciple of Huashan and have their name entered into the sect registry.
But Cheongpung was different.
“Who could have known Grandmaster would do something like that?”
Baek Museong remembered what had happened ten years ago with perfect clarity.

After the Sword Saint had lived in seclusion for many years, his Master, the Heavenly Sword True Person, had led several people in searching Huashan himself. At last, they discovered a residence where a ten-year-old boy was swinging a sword.
“It was unbelievable.”
No one knew when the boy had arrived, where he’d come from, or how he’d been raised. Yet he had already learned Huashan’s supreme secret arts.
But even the boy’s astonishing accomplishments were soon overshadowed by the Sword Saint’s even more astonishing words.
“You want me to initiate him?”
“Yes, Master. I intend to conduct the initiation ceremony and accept him as a main-sect Disciple. The order may be backward, but we cannot ignore a once-in-a-millennium genius like him—”
“Ignore him.”
“Pardon?”
“I said to continue ignoring him. When the time comes, I’ll send him over myself.”
“M-Master!”
“And don’t come looking for him again. Not unless you want me to burn this whole place down.”
“Set fire to Huashan? Are you saying we should all die together?”
“Oh. Now that you mention it, I suppose we would. Anyway, that’s how it is. I’ll take care of Cheongpung.”
Chulwoo and Eunhyang both gaped at him.
“D-Did he really say that?”
“Are you sure you’re not exaggerating?”
“I wish I were... but you both know what happened afterward.”
Cheongpung, whom the Sword Saint had promised to send when the time was right, had slipped out into the world without anyone noticing, while the Sword Saint himself had vanished without a trace.
“The truth is, our Master isn’t worried about Grandmaster. He’s worried about Martial Uncle Cheongpung.”
Cheongpung had already displayed unbelievable accomplishments ten years ago. But the world—and Murim in particular—overflowed with schemes and treachery.
It was far too dangerous for someone who wasn’t a Disciple of Huashan to wander the world while possessing Huashan’s secret arts.
“We must bring Martial Uncle Cheongpung back. For his sake, and for the sake of our sect. Do you understand?”
The two nodded at his resolute tone, then suddenly spoke up.
“But, Senior Brother...”
“How are we supposed to bring him back? By force?”
“That...”
Baek Museong hesitated before letting out a deep sigh.
“First, we need to bring the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi over to our side.”
All three of them remembered Cheongpung’s final words at the same time.
“I’m staying with my Benefactor!”
The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung.
This unexpected obstacle made Baek Museong’s head throb.
What did he do for Martial Uncle to call him his Benefactor? Did he save his life or something?
A bond that had begun with a few candied hawthorn skewers was proving far more tenacious than expected.
The moment we entered the main hall, Wipeng demanded,
“What on earth did you do?”
“What do you mean?”
“I’m talking about Cheongpung.”
Everyone’s gaze naturally turned toward Cheongpung.
He was cramming the refreshments from the table into his mouth until his cheeks bulged.
“I didn’t really do anything.”
“Cheongpung defied the Sect Leader’s order. He said he would stay with the Third Young Master.”
“So?”
“What do you mean, ‘so’? Don’t you understand that one wrong move could strain the relationship between our family and Huashan?”
Was this like a parent blaming his top-student son’s friend when the boy’s grades dropped?
I shrugged.
“I’ll try to persuade him.”
“You must. You absolutely must persuade him.”
Wipeng’s voice rang with firm resolve. He whipped his head toward Jin Wikyung, who sat in the place of honor.
“My lord, please say something as well.”
“Very well.”
Jin Wikyung put on a solemn expression and spoke.
“My youngest. Your face has grown so haggard in just a few days. Was the journey uncomfortable? Do you have any idea how worried I was...?”
“Stop. I was insane to trust you, my lord.”
“Don’t be so hard on him. My youngest will take care of it.”
“This is driving me mad. As of today, I’m leaving the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Ha ha ha. You certainly know how to tell a joke.”
“Did that sound like a joke?”
“Yes. It was very funny.”
“I’m not amused. I haven’t been amused since the Third Young Master failed to return by noon yesterday as promised.”
Jin Wikyung’s eyes widened.
“Oh, that reminds me, my youngest.”
“As you promised last time, please give him a thorough scolding.”
“What’s that sword strapped to your back? It looks like you had it made while you were away. Let me see it.”
Unable to contain his anger, Wipeng shot to his feet.
“I’m really leaving. It’s been awful knowing you. Let’s never meet again.”
“Ha ha ha. What’s gotten into him today? Why does he keep making me laugh?”
“Damn it. Draw your sword.”
“Taekyung, Wipeng seems eager to see your new sword. Why don’t you draw it for him?”
“Aaaaaah!”
With his eyes rolling back, Wipeng let out a shriek and placed his hand on the sword hilt.
But my next words froze him in place.
“Since the Fire King gave it to me, I think it would be best not to touch it if possible.”
Jin Wikyung and Wipeng blinked silently before finally managing to speak.
“F-Fire what?”
“Third Young Master, what nonsense did you just say?”
“The Fire King. Fire King. He left a sword in my care. Oh, and a martial arts manual too.”
Thunk. Clang.
In the suffocating silence, the sound of Wipeng dropping his sword rang out like thunder.

chapters.title: Chapter 186
paragraphs: Jin Wikyung and Wipeng.
The longer my story went on, the more openly their emotions showed.
Shock. Disbelief. Then shock all over again.
“Th-That’s really true?”
I’d been talking for so long that I was exhausted.
“It’s one hundred percent pure truth. Believe me.”
Wipeng, who had been sitting there in a daze, suddenly lunged at me.
“Third Young Master, if any of this is a lie, I swear one of us is going to die—and then the other one will too.”
“I told you, it’s one hundred percent true. One hundred percent!”
“No, but still...”
“Not a single speck of falsehood. One hundred fucking percent!”
Wipeng faltered, his face saying, Why do I suddenly feel so dirty?
I waved the sword and martial arts manual at him.
The last thing I could do was give him time to think it over.
“If you still don’t believe me, inspect them yourself. The Flame Divine Palm manual and a sword made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron!”
“Gasp! Put those away. Now!”
A vampire wouldn’t have reacted that strongly to a cross shoved in its face.
“What’s wrong?”
Wipeng stared at me in horror.
“You’re telling me to inspect the Flame Divine Palm manual? Are you trying to get our entire family wiped out?”
“Oh, right. There was that.”
Anyone who stole a look at the Fire King’s signature martial art would get a taste of the heat—enough to set their entire body on fire.
“Anyway, it’s all true. There are witnesses right here. Isn’t that right?”
Hyuk Mujin, who had been sitting in the corner like a corpse, cautiously raised his hand.
“Forgive me for speaking out of turn, but it is all true.”
Cheongpung, busy cramming some unidentifiable snack into his mouth, spoke with a solemn expression.
“Uh-oh-wa-uh-oh!”
I doubted that testimony would carry much weight. More importantly, how long was that bastard planning to keep eating? Was his stomach some kind of bottomless jar?
“Wipeng, it seems Taekyung is telling the truth.”
At Jin Wikyung’s words, Wipeng nodded, his expression complicated.
“Yes. As difficult as it is to believe... I don’t see how we can doubt him.”
“The Fire King. The Fire King himself...”
Jin Wikyung let out a long breath. After a moment’s hesitation, he picked up the Unnamed Sword from the table.
Shing.
A pure-white blade slid free of its rough scabbard.
As Jin Wikyung studied the frost-sharp edge, he murmured, “It smells of blood.”

Without needing an Item description window like I did, he had accurately read the weapon’s condition. He slid the sword back into its scabbard.
“Taekyung.”
“Yes.”
I straightened.
If Jin Wikyung called me Taekyung instead of my youngest, it meant he was about to say something serious.
“Do you know what these objects are?”
“Precious treasures, aren’t they? The kind that would be difficult to obtain even for a thousand pieces of gold.”
A Supreme Peak martial art with the power to dominate the world and a peerless sword forged from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
The Murim martial artists I knew would risk their lives to obtain these things.
Jin Wikyung shook his head.
“Wrong.”
“What?”
“These are ghostly objects. They take away a person’s soul and drive them mad.”
“Oh.”
“Do you know the name of that ghost?”
I muttered the answer.
“Greed.”
“Yes. Greed. A tenacious, dangerous creature that dwells in every human heart.”
I knew.
I had experienced it myself. How could I not know?
On that day several years ago, greed had taken root in my heart, and because of it, I had lost people close to me.
“I don’t know why the Fire King entrusted such dangerous objects to you, but... everything concerning them must be kept absolutely secret. Do you understand?”
His eyes and posture were directed solely at me, but the warning was meant for everyone in the room.
Me, Hyuk Mujin, and finally Cheongpung.
As though we had made a promise, we answered at the same time.
“Yes.”
“I’ll keep that in mind, Lesser Family Head.”
“Ah-uh-ah-hae-ho, ma-ah-hae-oh.”
That damn mouth of his. I ought to just—

Sunlight struck the rough scabbard strapped across Taekyung’s back and shattered into fragments.
“The weather is fucking beautiful.”
“Didn’t you say it was fantastic earlier?”
“That was then. They mean nearly the same thing anyway.”
“This one sounds rather different.”
“Don’t nitpick when you know perfectly well what I mean. Come to think of it, why are you still here when you said you were leaving?”

“After everything else, now the Fire King has appeared.”
“I hear he is extraordinarily eccentric. I’m worried his wrath may fall upon our family.”
“Then we’ll have to turn that danger into an opportunity.”
Jin Wikyung ran his fingers over his teacup. To anyone watching, he would have appeared lost in thought, but his lips were moving almost imperceptibly.
How is that matter progressing?

“The tea has gone cold. Shall I have them bring you another cup?”
We haven’t discovered anything yet.
“It’s fine. This is still drinkable.”
What about the surviving remnants?
“You’ll ruin your health if you keep doing that.”
Most of them died during the interrogation.

Only three?
Wipeng sighed and nodded.
They had a far more powerful restriction placed on them than expected. I’m sorry to say this, but... my abilities aren’t enough.

Stop the interrogations. Keep them alive by any means necessary. For now, those men are our only physical evidence.
As you command.
Jin Wikyung closed his hand around the cold teacup.
The trembling surface of the tea reflected a distorted, featureless face.
Just like them.
Dark Heaven...
He didn’t know where, how, or why they had done such a thing.
He was flailing at empty air without learning a single thing.
Yet one suspicion in Jin Wikyung’s mind was steadily hardening into certainty.
They are extremely dangerous. Targeting Shanxi Province was only the beginning.
The Head Elder had endured for years, biding his time. Yet the outcome was far too paltry for a grand design decades in the making.
Jin Wikyung had realized that only after the thrill of victory faded.
This was... too easy.
It had been the perfect opportunity to seize an entire province.
Yet Dark Heaven had never shown themselves, as though this alone had been enough for them.
What in the world are they after?
For now, there was no way to know.
He could only hope he had overestimated them.
“My lord?”
“Ah.”
“You’ve been away from your seat for too long. The guests are waiting.”
“...Is that so?”
At Wipeng’s prompting, Jin Wikyung drained his teacup in one gulp and rose.
“Let’s go.”
The gathering was for the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
For now, they could allow themselves to savor the joy of victory.
Winter days were short. I had only just returned to the Jin Family of Taiyuan, but the sun was already beginning to set.
Come to think of it, I haven’t trained properly in days. Not unless circulating my qi counts.
I was loosening up by practicing martial arts in the training ground attached to my pavilion when some unexpected guests arrived.
“Benefactor!”
“Benefactor!”
What was that, an echo?
I turned toward the voices.
“I’m here!”
Cheongpung was smiling brightly, his mouth covered in a thick layer of some mysterious sauce. And then there was...
“Benefactor! It’s me, Socheon!”
“It has been a while, Young Hero Jin.”
“Huh?”
They were Gong Yacheong and Socheon, survivors of the Sakju Branch.
A sudden rush of happiness swept over me at the sight of those familiar faces.
It feels like someone’s missing, though.
As I tilted my head, a whining voice rose from below the stone wall blocking my view.
“Me too! Soyul wants to see Uncle too!”
“Wait a moment.”
Gong Yacheong bent down, scooped something up, and hoisted it onto his shoulders.
It was Soyul. The little girl beamed and waved at me.
“Uncle!”
“Oh, you’ve grown a lot.”
“You’ve grown a lot too, Uncle!”
“Thanks. But I’m not an uncle.”
“Anyone can tell you’re an uncle!”
“...Right.”
What did it matter whether I was an uncle or not?
Chuckling, I walked over to them.
“Has everyone been well?”
Gong Yacheong answered with a faint smile.
“Of course.”
He still looked somewhat gaunt, but there was color in his face. He was clearly doing far better than when he had been poisoned and hovering at death’s door.
The kids seem to be doing well too.
Socheon was at the age when children shot up, and he had grown another half a handspan since I’d last seen him. Soyul’s cheeks were nice and plump.
And Cheongpung’s stomach had swollen into a round little belly from all the food he’d eaten.
Right. Eat well and grow big.
Twenty was still a growing age, after all.
“What brings all of you here?”
Socheon answered as though he’d been waiting for me to ask.
“Martial Artist Hyuk requested it. The banquet is about to begin, but he has to report for guard duty, so he asked us to deliver the message in his place.”
“Oh, the banquet.”
I vaguely remembered hearing about it earlier. There was supposed to be a grand banquet that evening.
Cheongpung, who had been licking the sauce from around his mouth, suddenly looked shocked.
“Gasp! Really?”
“...What? Didn’t you come here because you already knew?”
“No. If I’d known, I would’ve eaten less!”
Soyul also opened her eyes wide in shock. The candied treat in her hand slipped to the ground.
“No! Soyul’s full too!”
From their reactions, I could make a pretty good guess where the two of them had met.
“So, when does it start?”
“Less than half an hour from now, Benefactor.”
“Benefactor, hurry! I’ve never been to a banquet before!”
“Where is it?”
“In front of the new Grand Training Ground, Benefactor.”
“They said it’s in front of the Grand Training Ground, Benefactor!”
“Oh, there.”
I set down the practice spear in my hand and firmly secured the bundle beside me across my back.
The bundle, of course, contained the sword entrusted to me by the Fire King.
“Let’s all go.”
I started walking, only to stop short. I’d just remembered something I’d been meaning to say.
“Oh, and one more thing...”
“Please speak, Benefactor.”
“What is it, Benefactor?”
I heaved a deep sigh.
“Only one of you should call me Benefactor. It’s confusing.”
They were like a pair of parrots.
Without taking even a second to think, the two Benefactor parrots nodded.
“I’ll remember that, Benefactor.”
“Okay, Benefactor.”
No, think before you answer.
The Grand Training Ground.
True to its name, it was the largest training ground in the family, and it was packed shoulder to shoulder with people.
“What the hell? Why are there so many?”
I thought only invited guests were allowed in.
Cheongpung answered my question.
“I heard from the cook earlier that the Lesser Family Head said everyone should celebrate together on such a wonderful day, so he ordered them to let in all the people waiting outside too.”
“All of them?”
“Yes. The cook got really angry. He said the Lesser Family Head didn’t have any sense and shouldn’t run his mouth when he wasn’t going to help with the cooking.”
Soyul, happily sucking on a candied treat, chimed in.
“That’s right! He even gave Soyul a candied treat and told her not to tell anyone!”
“...Then why are you telling us?”
“Gasp!”
I shook my head and kept walking.
Before I had gone more than a few steps, a martial artist from the Jin Family approached.
“We will escort the two Young Masters to their seats.”
“I don’t mind watching from anywhere. I suppose that isn’t allowed?”
“No, Young Master. It is the Lesser Family Head’s order.”
Given the occasion, there was no helping it.
I exchanged brief farewells with Gong Yacheong and the others, then followed the martial artist to the seat prepared for me.
Mine was one of the places of honor reserved for a select few distinguished guests.
Which, of course, meant...
“Martial Uncle Cheongpung, Young Master Jin. We meet again so soon.”
The Three Plum Blossom Elites were among them.
Baek Museong had his junior disciples seated on either side of him. He greeted us with a fairly friendly expression.
“We didn’t get a proper chance to introduce ourselves earlier, did we? I’m Eunhyang.”
System Level: 75 Eunhyang
She was probably around the same age as my younger sister, Hayeon.
No sooner had I finished greeting her than a sullen voice cut in.
“Damn it. You’re sitting next to me?”
It was Chulwoo, a massive man whose bulk made the seat itself look cramped.
“Why? Don’t like it?”
“Would you?”
“I don’t like it either. That’s why I said it. Guess we agree on something.”
“Don’t say something so disgusting!”
“Then switch seats.”
“With whom?”
“Lots of people besides you would love to sit there. Switch with anyone standing down below.”
“You son of a bitch!”
“Did you just insult my parents? In the Jin Family of Taiyuan? Are you trying to pull a Jin-rula here?”
Chulwoo trembled with rage, but Baek Museong immediately rebuked him.
“You fool! What kind of outrageous language is that?”
“No, Senior Brother. It’s just...”
“Quiet. Young Hero Jin, I apologize on behalf of my Junior Brother. I also offer my apologies to Martial Uncle Cheongpung.”
Cheongpung, who had been hiding behind me, cautiously poked his head out.
“I’m fine, Martial Nephew.”
I smiled gently as well.
“I’m fine too. His blood is bound to run hot at that age. We should be understanding.”
“You’re five years younger than me, you little punk! What did you just say?”
“Young Hero Baek, if it isn’t too much trouble, could you switch seats with me? I’m a little afraid to sit beside him...”
“Second!”
“Whoo. Whoo-hoo.”
I dropped into the seat beside the snorting Chulwoo.
Chulwoo to my right, Cheongpung to my left.
What a spectacular arrangement.
Where is Jin Wikyung?
I looked around, but there was no sign of Jin Wikyung or Wipeng.
Then—
Boom!
The martial artists of the Jin Family surrounding the Grand Training Ground began striking their weapons.
There were more than three hundred of them. A blade-sharp aura and wave-like spirit surged from their ranks.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Like drums pounding across a battlefield, the sound grew louder and louder until it swallowed every other noise.
And then...
BOOM!
With the loudest thunderclap yet, the human curtain split apart.

His blood is bound to run hot at that age.
We should be understanding.”
“You’re five years younger than me, you little punk!
What did you just say?”
“Young Hero Baek, if it isn’t too much trouble, could you switch seats with me?
I’m a little afraid to sit beside him...”
“Second!”
“Whoo.
Whoo-hoo.”
I dropped into the seat beside the snorting Chulwoo.
Chulwoo to my right, Cheongpung to my left.
What a spectacular arrangement.
Where is Jin Wikyung?
I looked around, but there was no sign of Jin Wikyung or Wipeng.
Then—
Boom!
The martial artists of the Jin Family surrounding the Grand Training Ground began striking their weapons.
There were more than three hundred of them.
A blade-sharp aura and wave-like spirit surged from their ranks.
Boom!
Boom!
Boom!
Like drums pounding across a battlefield, the sound grew louder and louder until it swallowed every other noise.
And then...
BOOM!
With the loudest thunderclap yet, the human curtain split apart.

chapters.title: Chapter 187
paragraphs: Hundreds of martial artists stood there, radiating an aura as sharp as frost. Along the path they had opened, one man approached.
Step. Step.
The commoners who had come to watch, the nameless martial artists dressed in worn uniforms, and finally the powerful figures who moved Shanxi Province—
Everyone held their breath and watched that one man.
Jin Wikyung.
This is like something out of a movie.
Clad in a martial uniform embroidered with a silver wyvern, Jin Wikyung strode forward without hesitation. His commanding presence and effortless authority overwhelmed everyone present.
The silence Jin Wikyung had created was broken by his voice.
“Our family first put down roots in Taiyuan three hundred years ago.”
His shout, infused with profound internal energy, carried far and wide.
“Our beginnings were undeniably humble.”

It had been an age of chaos. Natural disasters struck one after another, and the empire that had seemed eternal lost its strength. Warlords raised their banners throughout the land and declared themselves kings, plunging the realm into war.
Blood instead of water soaked the parched earth, while grain waiting to be harvested was trampled beneath horses’ hooves.
At the end of that long war, a man who had wandered the realm stopped in the ruined capital of an old dynasty.
That was the beginning of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
“Our ancestor, Grand Patriarch Jin Muryang, took in orphans and cared for widows and the elderly. Though he raised the banner of martial strength, he never forgot humanity.”
The small seed soon sprouted. Those who gathered beneath the banner of the Jin Family of Taiyuan became its branches, its trunk, and its strong, deep roots.
The family that had begun so humbly grew into a towering tree whose reach extended across all of Shanxi Province.
“Yet even our family could not escape the rise and fall of fortune.”
Everything had slowly changed with the passage of time. After enduring one event after another, both great and small, the towering tree began to wither.
Mistaken decisions by its leaders, invasions by foreign enemies, betrayals by allies, natural disasters beyond human power to prevent...
Before long, its many branches had broken and its lush leaves had fallen.
“But!”
A thunderous shout burst forth. His voice boiled like lava.
“We survived.”
Though the branches broke and the leaves fell, the roots remained whole.
“We may have been shaken, but we were never uprooted.”
As long as the roots remained, the tree would grow again. It would regain its vitality and put forth lush new leaves as though nothing had ever happened.
Just as it was doing now.
“As the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, I swear this.”
Boom!
Hundreds of weapons struck the ground. Invisible heat rose from the martial artists of the Jin Family of Taiyuan as they dropped to one knee.
“We! The Jin Family of Taiyuan!”
It was a vow to the family’s countless members, to everyone gathered here, and to the enemies who had yet to bare their fangs.
“Three hundred years ago and three hundred years from now, we will remain here unchanged!”
Boom! Boom!
“I ask you all!”
His blazing eyes swept across the crowd. Taking in faces filled with excitement and anticipation, fear and guilt, Jin Wikyung shouted,
“Are you ready to lay a new foundation alongside our family?”
A tremendous roar erupted from the crowd, centered on the martial artists of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
“Loyalty!”
Boom, boom-boom-boom-boom-boom!
Just then, a clear voice rang out from somewhere.
“May we also join the Jin Family of Taiyuan on the path it has chosen?”
The voice had come neither from the place of honor where I sat nor from the seats reserved for distinguished guests below.
The vast crowd surrounding the Grand Training Ground parted, revealing the owner of the voice.
That’s...
Instead of a flowing court dress, she wore a comfortable martial uniform. With features mature beyond her years, she respectfully saluted Jin Wikyung with clasped fists.
“I am Lee Seowol of the Mount Heng Sword Sect. I have arrived in response to the Lesser Family Head’s summons.”
The middle-aged man who had been standing beside her like an iron tower revealed his identity in a rough voice.
“I am First Elder Cheol Mubaek. I pay my respects to the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
The martial artists of the Mount Heng Sword Sect standing behind them shouted in unison.
“We pay our respects to the Lesser Family Head!”
A stir swept through the crowd.
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had appeared when it stood on the very brink of destruction.
Its new Sect Leader was the late Blood Wolf Sword’s only daughter, while the man at her side who called himself First Elder was Cheol Mubaek, the Tiger of Mount Heng.
Yet amid everyone else’s astonishment, Jin Wikyung remained perfectly calm.
Of course he did. He was the one who had sent me to deliver their invitation for New Year’s Day.
“This is the first time I’ve met you in person, Young Lady. Did you receive the formal invitation I sent last time?”
“Yes. And in addition...”
Lee Seowol answered calmly, then raised her head and looked in my direction.
“I received a kindness I could never hope to repay.”
Every gaze that swung my way made my face prickle.
Naturally. There probably wasn’t a single person in Shanxi Province who didn’t know that Jin Mukyung and I had saved the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
After giving me a faint smile, she turned back to Jin Wikyung.
“I would like to hear your answer to the question I asked earlier.”
Lee Seowol drew a deep breath. Her eyelids trembled.
“May we... join the Jin Family of Taiyuan as well?”
Jin Wikyung answered without a moment’s hesitation.
“Of course.”
“Now it is my turn to ask. Are you prepared to walk alongside our family?”
Thump.
Instead of answering, Lee Seowol dropped to one knee. Cheol Mubaek and the martial artists under his command did the same.
“I, Lee Seowol, second Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, swear before Heaven and Earth.”
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had once commanded Shanxi Murim. Now its new Sect Leader, inheritor of its orthodox lineage, knelt before Jin Wikyung.
No. She knelt before the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
“Our sect pledges its loyalty to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Loyalty!”
They were few in number, but their shout was thunderous. Jin Wikyung took Lee Seowol by the shoulder and helped her to her feet.
His manner of speech had shifted naturally as well.
“I grant you permission.”
On the first day of the new year, the Jin Family of Taiyuan accepted the Mount Heng Sword Sect as its vassal.
“Waaaaaaah!”
“Jin Family of Taiyuan! Jin Family of Taiyuan!”
Cheers upon cheers.
The crowd of more than a thousand people enthusiastically chanted the name of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
It really was that impressive.
First came a speech that set the listeners’ blood boiling, followed by the Mount Heng Sword Sect’s oath of loyalty.
What an ending.
The real banquet hadn’t even begun, but everyone present must have realized it by now.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan was the hegemon of Shanxi Province, possessed of both overwhelming power and mercy.
Chulwoo, seated beside me, was no exception.
“...Whoa.”
The guy who had seemed simpleminded and proud to a fault now wore an expression of genuine admiration.
The kid knows a thing or two.
It was childish, but I couldn’t help puffing out my chest a little. I was a member of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, after all, and I’d contributed quite a bit to making this day possible.
“Ahem, ahem. Looks like you were moved.”
“It was incredible. My heart pounded the entire time.”
Chulwoo continued, his voice brimming with excitement.
“How can anyone be so beautiful?”
“Not to brag, but the Jin Family of Taiyuan has become a pretty big deal in Shanxi—what did you say?”
What had I just heard?
After some hesitation, I asked uneasily,
“You’re not talking about my eldest brother, are you?”
“What?”
“You know, that sort of thing. I covet that man’s muscles. I want to do bench presses with him while we strip off each other’s Under Armour. Something like that...”
“What the hell are you talking about?”
Chulwoo frowned. Judging by his expression, that wasn’t what he meant.
“Good. That’s a relief. I thought you were gay.”
“Gay? What’s that?”
“Well, to put it metaphorically, I suppose it’s the process by which a pair of Diglett meet and become Dugtrio.”
“I can’t understand a word you’re saying. Explain it simply.”
I came up with the simplest term possible.
“Male homosexuality.”
“You little bastard...!”
Chulwoo was about to raise his fist when he stopped short. Baek Museong, his Senior Brother, was sitting right beside him.
The Huashan’s Lone Crane buff was damn useful.
I grinned and asked,
“So who exactly is beautiful?”
“The woman! That woman from the Mount Heng Sword Sect!”
“Oh, Young Lady Lee Seowol?”
Strictly speaking, she was the Sect Leader, but calling her Young Lady still felt more natural.
At my familiar tone, Chulwoo’s eyes lit up.
“Y-You know her?”
“We have a little history.”
“What kind of history?”
A history that began with a sexual harassment scandal and ended with a marriage proposal, I suppose.
“It’s a pain to explain. The whole story is pretty eventful. But don’t tell me...”
I trailed off and looked at Chulwoo.
“You’re interested in Young Lady Lee?”
“Interested?”
Chulwoo shot to his feet, and I felt slightly reassured.
“Right? You kept talking about your heart pounding, so I thought you were actually interested in—”
“This isn’t interest! It’s love.”
“Three children should be about right. Two boys and one girl.”
“...Sure. Keep going.”
“We’ll raise a yellow dog too. I heard that children who grow up with a dog develop better emotionally. We’ll have a happy family.”
I was about to call him an idiot when I suddenly stopped.
I feel like I’ve seen this scene before.
Where had I seen it?
For some reason, something about it hit a sore spot.
And why was I suddenly thinking about Song-i and Uncle Kkeokjeong back in the real world?
That’s strange.
I pushed the question aside and spoke.
“Are you done?”
“I’m not done yet.”
“Then let’s pretend you are and listen to me. This is important.”
My serious tone gave Chulwoo pause.
“Important?”
“Yeah. How old are you?”
“Twenty-five.”
“Do you know how old Young Lady Lee is?”
“No.”
“She’s seventeen. Ah, the year just changed, so she’s eighteen now.”
“So?”

“What do you mean, so, you goddamn monster? Forget the seven-year age gap—she’s still eating school lunches and doing late-night study sessions! She’s only just choosing between humanities and sciences! What about her school grades?”
Chulwoo stared at me in bewilderment.
“What are you talking about? She’s at the perfect age to marry.”
“Ah, sorry. I got carried away.”
As the older brother of a younger sister who was still in school, I couldn’t help putting myself in her shoes. I kept forgetting this was Murim.
“Anyway, think it through. Don’t let some fleeting emotion carry you away.”
“No.”
Chulwoo answered firmly, his expression turning dreamy.
“I knew the moment I saw her. My heart, which had lain still my entire life, finally began to beat.”
“...So you were dead for twenty-five years?”
“Dead? Yes, you’re right. Before I met her, I was little more than a corpse.”
“Can you really not die? Please die.”
“I can’t. Without her permission, I can neither die nor live.”
“...Wow. What a load of bullshit.”
Baek Museong and Eunhyang, who had been listening to our conversation, shook their heads.
“Here we go again.”
“Big Brother, didn’t you say something similar to that pretty third-generation Disciple last year?”
He’s a repeat offender?
What are you, some kind of serial confession demon?
Just as Chulwoo was about to explode at Eunhyang for exposing his embarrassing past—
“Young Master Jin.”
A lovely voice reached my ears. I turned and saw a woman climbing the stairs.
No. A girl.
Lee Seowol.
It was her.
