chapters.title: Chapter 188
paragraphs: Dressed in a martial uniform, she looked more mature—and more beautiful—than the last time I’d seen her.
A faint fragrance drifted toward me as she drew closer.
Honestly, I can see why Chulwoo fell for her.
And not just Chulwoo. Half the men gathered at the Jin Family of Taiyuan were probably weighing their chances of confessing to her.
And a girl like that proposed to me.
She was still just a kid, and her proposal had been little more than an offer of political marriage, but I couldn’t help feeling strange about it.
At last, she stopped in front of me and greeted me.
“It’s good to see you again. Have you been well?”
“Yes. What about you, Young Lady Lee?”
The words had barely left my mouth when I realized my mistake. Her family had been killed, and her sect had nearly been annihilated. There was no way she could have been well.
While I floundered, Lee Seowol answered.
“I’ve been well. Thanks to you, Young Master Jin.”
With a light smile, she added,
“And I’ll continue to be.”
There was a steely resolve in her voice. It was as though the crisis that had nearly destroyed her sect, and the difficult decision to swear loyalty, had helped her grow.
I answered sincerely.
“I hope so.”
Lee Seowol gave me a faint smile and nodded. That was when—
“H-Hey, Taekyung!”
“...What are you doing?”
I stared at Chulwoo in disbelief. He had thrown an arm around my shoulders, his expression and tone painfully awkward.
“You’re in the way. Get your arm off me.”
“H-Hahahaha! What’s gotten into you? We’re childhood friends. What’s a little thing like this between us?”
“Weren’t we sworn enemies?”
“M-My friend, your jokes have improved tremendously! Hwa-ha, hahahaha!”
“Does that sound like a joke to you?”
“Ah! By the way, who might this beautiful lady be?”
“...So that’s what this was about.”
The fabric of space-time cringed. Having flawlessly delivered the worst performance imaginable, Chulwoo bowed ninety degrees to Lee Seowol.
“Hello! It is an honor to meet you!”
“Ah... yes. It’s an honor to meet you too.”
“If I may introduce myself, I am this man’s friend of ten years—”
To help the flustered Lee Seowol, I added,
“We met for the first time today.”
“Although we only met today, we have already forged a bond worthy of friends of ten years—”
“We’re not close at all.”
“S-Since fate has brought us together, perhaps you’d care to sit beside me—”
“He’s hitting on you because he thinks you’re pretty. Don’t fall for it.”
Chulwoo ground his teeth. Lee Seowol’s eyes widened.
“Oh, really?”
“Yes. Can’t you tell just by looking at him?”
There was such a thing as being too oblivious. If she couldn’t pick up on something this obvious, she was in trouble.
I sighed, and Lee Seowol stepped closer.
“No. I meant the other thing.”
“Pardon?”
“Do you think I’m pretty, too, Young Master Jin?”
“Wait. Hold on.”
Her voice was alluring, and her eyes sparkled.
What’s gotten into her? Why is she acting like this?
Chulwoo watched the two of us, his gaze sinking into gloomy despair.
“Waaaaah!”
“Drink! Drink!”

The atmosphere at the Grand Training Ground was incredible, to put it mildly. The dance troupe—or rather, the dancers—brought in from Honghwaru captivated everyone with their dazzling movements, while the crowd ate, drank, and made merry.
Even the honored guests, who had looked uncomfortable at first, began to relax.
Those bastards should be on their knees with their heads to the floor, and even that wouldn’t be enough.
Many of the honored guests owed the Jin Family of Taiyuan a debt, yet they had remained neutral during the recent war.
Neutral was a generous way to put it. They had backed out because they feared retaliation from the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
They must feel safe now that we’ve accepted the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
In front of those very people, Jin Wikyung had embraced the Mount Heng Sword Sect, the Jin Family’s greatest enemy, and seated Lee Seowol in a place of honor.
It meant he had no intention of holding them accountable for what had happened.
Naturally, the atmosphere among the honored guests warmed at once. Swift oaths of loyalty followed, along with a barrage of gifts.
“Lesser Family Head, the Sangdo Sect and I wish to cast our lot with the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Oh, how kind of you.”
“This is a small gift I prepared as a token of my sincerity.”
“Thank you, Sect Leader Hwang.”
“Great Hero Jin, I lead the merchant guild...”
“It is a humble offering, but please accept it...”
It didn’t take long for luxury goods, gold, and silver treasures to pile up like a mountain. I doubted Jin Wikyung would ever have to worry about the family budget again after today.
Once things had settled down, Jin Wikyung approached me.
“How was it?”
I gave him a thumbs-up.
“It was impressive. But is it really all right for you to come over already? It looks like some people haven’t even had a chance to speak with you.”
“That is precisely why they will grow anxious.”
“What?”
“How do you think those who failed to speak with me today will feel?”
“I don’t know. Like they’ve fallen far behind everyone else?”
“Correct.”
Jin Wikyung took a sip of his drink and winked at me.
“The more desperate they become, the more they will offer. This is only the first day. I am looking forward to the final day even more.”
“Damn.”
He was going to bleed them dry.
The Sect Leaders of the Five Gates of Shanxi, who were staring this way as though someone had lit a fire under their asses, would undoubtedly be the highlight of the final day.
“But, my youngest.”
Jin Wikyung lowered his voice.
“Why is the Defeated Flower Fist acting like that?”
At some point, Chulwoo had moved to the far end of the honored seats. He kept glancing our way with a gloomy expression.
He would glare at me with blazing eyes, then heave a deep sigh whenever Lee Seowol and I exchanged a few words.
“Uh, well...”
How was I supposed to explain this? Lee Seowol was sitting nearby, so I had to watch what I said.
If I’d known this would happen, I would’ve practiced Sound Transmission beforehand.
Reaching the Peak realm had made Sound Transmission available for me to acquire through practice. It hadn’t granted me the skill on the spot.
“He looks unwell. Is he hurt?”
He was probably hurting, all right. In his heart.
“I guess he’s just in a bad mood.”
I gave a vague answer. Just then, the music filling the Grand Training Ground abruptly stopped, and people began to murmur.
Who’s that now?
A young man strode confidently through the flustered dancers. After surveying his surroundings, he gave a respectful fist-and-palm salute toward the honored seats.
More precisely, toward Jin Wikyung.
“My name is Choo Dohwan of the Iron Blood Sect of Henan.”
Jin Wikyung’s eyes widened.
“Could you be Choo Dohwan, the Iron Fist?”
“It is merely an undeserved reputation.”
“I have heard much about you. But what brings a Disciple of the Iron Blood Sect here without prior notice?”
Even I had heard of the Iron Blood Sect of Henan a couple of times. It was a well-known sect.
Judging by his sect alone, he must rank among the top three honored guests here.
With everyone’s attention focused on him, Choo Dohwan revealed why he had stepped forward.
“I have come to request a duel.”
“A duel? Now?”
“Yes. I apologize for the imposition, but I ask that you grant my request.”
Of course he ought to apologize. What kind of occasion did he think this was?
Surprisingly, however, very few people frowned. Most had already had a few drinks and seemed to regard this as an exciting surprise event.
“Hmm.”
“If you refuse, I will offer a sincere apology and withdraw.”
At least he knew his manners. Baek Museong, who had been watching the exchange, added,
“I too have heard the name Choo Dohwan, the Iron Fist. They say that, as befits a Disciple of the Iron Blood Sect, he excels in fist-and-foot martial arts and is a man of upright character.”
“You could choose Baek Museong as your opponent.”
Baek Museong smiled faintly.
“My junior brothers and I would be happy to accept.”
“Are you certain?”
“Of course. On such a fine day, I can only be grateful for the chance to enliven the festivities as a guest.”
His answer carried both the composure of a powerful man and impeccable courtesy. Jin Wikyung rose from his seat.
“I accept Young Hero Choo’s request.”
“Thank you.”
But Jin Wikyung didn’t stop there.
“Furthermore, anyone who wishes to participate in the duels may step forward! The final victor will receive one hundred silver nyang and a fine weapon worthy of the prize!”
“Waaaaah!”
Cheers erupted at his generous gesture, rowing while the tide was coming in. After all, there was nothing more entertaining in the world than watching a fight.
The eyes of the young martial artists, still brimming with youthful vigor, lit up at the thought of testing themselves.
“Then, Young Hero Choo!”
Jin Wikyung drew everyone’s attention with his booming voice, then asked Choo Dohwan,
“Name your first opponent.”
“The opponent I wish to face is...”
A Disciple of the Iron Blood Sect, famous for his fist-and-foot martial arts. His epithet was the Iron Fist, for heaven’s sake.
It’s obvious.
Just as I expected, Choo Dohwan named a particular person.
“Chulwoo, the Defeated Flower Fist!”
Chulwoo, who had been sitting there in a daze, rose to his full height. His gloom-soaked eyes settled on Choo Dohwan.
“Sounds good.”
“Let us determine which of us is stronger!”
I looked at the Level window floating over Choo Dohwan’s head and thought,
He’s going to get beaten to death.
System Level 65 Choo Dohwan
And my prediction soon became reality.
Wham! Wham! Wham!

There were no forms or techniques involved. The difference between the Peak realm and First Rate was like the difference between heaven and earth, and Choo Dohwan had nothing that could bridge that gap.
Thud!
“Guh! H-How can it be this easy?”
“Are you really the Iron Fist? Why are you so soft?”

Chulwoo, meanwhile, rampaged like a monster. His martial arts were on a higher level, and he had been born with tremendous strength, size, and toughness. It took him only fifty exchanges to knock his opponent senseless.
And honestly, he seemed to have gone pretty easy on him.
“You know how to throw a punch, but it won’t work on me anyway. Give up here.”
Choo Dohwan gritted his teeth.
“No! It isn’t over until it’s over!”
“What a stubborn bastard.”
Whoosh! Crack! Thump!
Well, now it really was over.
Once Choo Dohwan lost consciousness, the waiting martial artists of the Jin Family of Taiyuan brought over a stretcher and carried him away.
“Whaaaat?”
“As expected of the Defeated Flower Fist!”
“The Iron Fist Choo Dohwan is a fairly well-known master, but even he’s no match for one of Huashan’s Three Plum Blossom Elites.”
Under the simple rules they had established, the winner had to continue accepting challenges. If no challengers remained, the winner could name an opponent.
Lee Seowol, who had somehow claimed the seat beside me, whispered,
“Do you think anyone else will challenge him?”
I snorted quietly.
“After seeing what happened to the Iron Fist? Do you really think anyone will come forward? I’ll bet my wrist that nobody does.”
Just then, a man wearing a heroic headband suddenly stepped forward and shouted,
“I am Hwang Jinsu of Hwang Family Manor! I challenge the Defeated Flower Fist!”
Ah, shit. I should’ve kept my mouth shut.
Crack! Thud!
As I wallowed in regret, Hwang Jinsu of Hwang Family Manor collapsed, scattering teeth everywhere.
A Level 25 had stepped forward. Of course that was the result.
“What about now?”
“Didn’t you just see what happened? He got it even worse than the Iron Fist. Bones can be set, but teeth are finished. Completely finished.”
“And your wrist...”
“Fine, I’ll bet it. I bet my left wrist before, so this time it’s my right. Just watch. Nobody’s coming forward now. Seriously.”
A wandering martial artist in a bamboo hat stepped forward.
“I am Gal Mo. I may be a nameless wandering martial artist, but would you care to exchange a few moves?”
“No need to ask. Come on up.”
Did that bastard smear honey on his fists or something? Why do the challengers keep coming?
After knocking down fifteen or so people in about half an hour, Chulwoo roared,
“Is there no one who can stand against me?”
Despite fighting so many duels in such a short time, he was still bursting with energy. The difference in skill was so vast that even the other martial artists now looked thoroughly daunted.
Thinking this was my chance, I spoke up.
“Nobody’s coming out now. Really, nobody. I’ll bet my wrist.”
Lee Seowol helpfully replied,
“You already bet those earlier. Both of them.”
“Then my left ankle.”
“You bet that on the fifth match.”
“Oh, then what about my right ankle?”
“You already bet that on the sixth.”
“My neck...”
“The eighth match...”
Damn it. So this was what a corpse with its eyes open looked like.
As I sat there in a daze, Lee Seowol let out a small laugh.
“It’s all right. I won’t collect.”
“...Were you planning to?”
“If you do me one favor.”
“What favor?”
Just as Lee Seowol was about to open her mouth—
“Shan! Xi! Sleeping! Dragon!”
A tremendous shout shook the Grand Training Ground. Having defeated every challenger, Chulwoo stared at me and crooked a finger.
“Jin Taekyung, come out.”
At the same time, a System alert rang out.
Ding.

System Level 95 Chulwoo has chosen you as his duel opponent! Quest: There Is a Man Who Loved You So Much has been created. - Would you like to accept the Quest? - Refusing will incur a massive penalty!
I could say this with absolute certainty: that was the most fucked-up quest title I had ever received.

chapters.title: Chapter 189
paragraphs: System Quest There Is a Man Who Loved You So Much A man’s burning love for a woman has manifested as jealousy and rage. He seeks to win her love by defeating you. Grade: Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Task: Win the duel (Incomplete) Reward: EXP and Fame Failure: Acquire the Title Weak Male —Would you like to accept the Quest? —If you refuse the Quest, the Title Weak Male will be granted.
Wow. This is bullshit.
Of course, the penalty for refusing would suck twice as much.
Not like I have a choice.
I clicked my tongue and rose from my seat, drawing everyone’s attention.
“Young Master Jin!”
“Young Master Jin.”
“Young Hero Jin, you don’t need to go out there.”
“That’s right. Has Senior Brother Chul gone crazy? Why is he suddenly acting like this?”
Wolhwa, Lee Seowol, Baek Museong, and even Eunhyang, whom I’d barely exchanged a few words with, all looked at me with concern.
I was the only one who didn’t think much of it.
“It’s fine. We’ll have a good, clean fight.”
Wolhwa sighed.
“Young Master Jin, do you know who you’re up against?”
“Of course. Chulwoo, the Defeated Flower Fist.”
“I don’t think you do. The Defeated Flower Fist is considered a prodigy even within Huashan. Think carefully about why he’s called one of the Three Plum Blossom Elites.”
“Probably because he’s good at fighting.”
“No, that’s not what I... Whew. Fine. I give up. Do whatever you want.”
Wolhwa was out.
Baek Museong and Eunhyang stepped forward next.
“I don’t mean to underestimate Young Hero Jin, but my Second Junior Brother is, how should I put this? He’s...”
“A mad bull. When Senior Brother Chul loses his temper, dealing with him is a real nightmare.”
“Eunhyang!”
“What? I’m not wrong.”
In short, they were saying someone like me was no match for Chulwoo.
That’s what you think.
I thought otherwise. I still didn’t know whether it was arrogance or confidence. I just...
I don’t think I’ll lose.
I was certain of it. Certain that I could defeat the man shouting at me.
“Come! Out! Right! Now!”
“I’m coming, you bastard.”
With more than a thousand people gathered around the Grand Training Ground watching me, I walked toward Chulwoo.
“We must stop the duel.”
At Baek Museong’s words, Jin Wikyung shook his head.
“My younger brother has already accepted the Defeated Flower Fist’s challenge. The duel will end after that.”
“Great Hero Jin.”
“I don’t know what happened between them, but there seems to be some bad blood. Wouldn’t this be a good opportunity for them to clear the air?”
Baek Museong sighed inwardly at Jin Wikyung’s carefree response.
Does he not understand the situation?
From what Baek Museong could see, Chulwoo was absolutely furious. He looked ready to break several of Jin Taekyung’s limbs before he stopped.
This is bad.

They had to stop this now. Baek Museong had heard more than enough rumors about the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi on the journey here, but in his eyes, Jin Taekyung was no match for his Second Junior Brother.
The names Defeated Flower Fist and Three Plum Blossom Elites had not been earned through his Master’s reputation alone.
“He could be seriously injured. Shouldn’t we intervene before something happens?”
“Who?”
“...Pardon?”
“The duel hasn’t even begun yet. Nor has its outcome been decided.”
Baek Museong realized he had been mistaken. Jin Wikyung understood the situation better than anyone.
They were simply operating under different assumptions.
“Great Hero Jin. Don’t tell me...”
“That’s right.”
Jin Wikyung gave a low laugh. His gaze remained fixed on the back of his younger brother as he walked toward the dueling platform.
“That boy will win. Just as he always has.”
Baek Museong was left speechless. The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi was undeniably a remarkable prodigy, but he couldn’t match Chulwoo in experience, martial arts, or internal energy.
Baek Museong had watched Chulwoo since childhood. He could say that with absolute certainty.
The Lesser Family Head is wrong. The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi can’t stand against my Second Junior Brother.
Baek Museong shook his head, but the water had already been spilled. If they backed down now, the prestige of both sects would be dragged through the dirt.
I’ll have to intervene at the right moment.
As he watched the dueling platform with a grave expression, he overlooked one fact.
Munch, munch. Smack, smack.
Cheongpung—the man who called Jin Taekyung his Benefactor—was silently watching the situation unfold.
“Waaaaah!”
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi! Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi!”
“Defeated Flower Fist! Defeated Flower Fist!”
The moment I stepped onto the dueling platform, cheers erupted from every direction. The response was on a completely different level from when the previous challengers had appeared.
“Oh, so everyone knows the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. Just so you know, he’s. Damn. Strong.”
“Waaaaah!”
As I enthusiastically waved to the crowd, Chulwoo glared at me.
“You should wave too. There are no stars without fans. Don’t you know that?”
“Wave while you still can. You’ll spend the next three months staring at the ceiling of a medical clinic.”
“Let me ask you something. Why the fuck are you giving me shit?”
“You’re asking because you don’t know?”
I shrugged.
“Did you get rejected before you could even confess?”
“Who got rejected!”
Chulwoo shouted, his face flushed.
“If you hadn’t interfered, we’d already be living happily with three children!”
“...Isn’t that a little too fast?”
There were limits to how much you could speed things up. They hadn’t even known each other for half a shichen. How were they supposed to get married and have three children already?
What is he, a Command Center? He’ll hit a population of two hundred in no time.
As Cheongpung had said, even if a goose brought them by rocket delivery, it would take half a day. And since there were three children, they’d have to come as a bundle.
“It’s fine to spread your imagination’s wings, but leave me out of it. I don’t have anything to do with this Young Lady, so this is unfair.”
“Nonsense! I saw the way she looked at you!”
“The way she looked at me? What kind of look was it?”
“It was... It was... Urgh.”
Unable to continue, Chulwoo groaned and widened his eyes.
“I promise you this. You won’t be leaving here on your own two feet.”
“I’m a nice guy, so I’ll let you crawl out on all fours.”
“I’ll smash that insolent mouth of yours!”
With a roar, Chulwoo charged.
I swung my spear shaft at the punch flying toward me with a fierce aura.
Whoosh! Boom!
The violent impact sent me sliding backward. The force was unbelievable for a collision between flesh and steel.
At some point, a pair of dull-black gauntlets had appeared on his hands.
“Those Items look pretty nice. Mind if I check them out?”
“You bastard!”
Whoosh!
He truly was a mad bull.
The only difference was that he had fists instead of horns—and those fists weren’t just swinging blindly.
“Hup!”
I held my breath and swung my spear. The paths of the gauntlets and spearhead intersected, spraying sparks.
Clang-clang-clang!
I pressured him with the spear’s advantage in reach, while Chulwoo pressured me with his natural reflexes and strength.
Whoosh!
A steel-hard leg whipped toward my waist.
He was astonishingly fast and flexible for his size. I retreated and thrust my spear toward his neck.
Bang! Krrrck!
His toes cut through empty air, while his gauntlet blocked the spearhead. Chulwoo seized the blade and grinned.
“Got you.”
Krrrck!
At the same moment, an immense force yanked the spear toward him. He had probably been aiming for this from the start.
A spearman without his spear was no better than a scarecrow with its eyes open.
Of course...
I expected this much.
I released my grip and charged at Chulwoo. The triumph on his face turned to shock.
Unable to overcome the force of his own pull, both of his hands shot overhead with the spear still clutched between them.
“Give me back my spear.”
Crack!
“Guh!”
Something broke. Chulwoo staggered after taking my knee to the face.
Next came his solar plexus.
Thud!
“Ghn!”
Struck in a vital spot, he dropped the spear and stumbled backward. In the meantime, I calmly retrieved it.
“You bastard!”
Chulwoo finally overcame the pain and straightened up. The moment I saw him, a quiet laugh escaped me.
“Y-You’re laughing?”
“Your nose is bleeding.”
“You’re really dead—what? A nosebleed?”
He hurriedly wiped the bridge of his nose with the back of his hand, and his face twisted in outrage.
“How dare you injure my face?”
“It’s fine. You’re so ugly, no one will notice.”
“That makes it worse! Won’t I become even uglier now?”
What the hell was with this guy? He was surprisingly self-aware.
“Gaaaaah!”
Chulwoo let out a furious roar, his eyes flashing.
“For my Senior Brother’s sake, I was going to end this without going too far... But not anymore.”
“Do it properly. That’s why I came out here.”
“Fine. I’ll fight you seriously.”
As if to prove his words, a faint light shimmered around Chulwoo’s gauntlets.
“Fist Energy?”
It was still incomplete, but it was unmistakably Fist Energy. A vicious smile spread across his lips.
“It’s too late for regrets.”
Whoosh! Slice!
Sparks flew as the spearhead was cleanly severed. Chulwoo drew upon every bit of internal energy in his body, and his fists blurred.
Swish! Swish-swish-swish!
A razor-sharp gale raged around me. Each time I swung my spear against the wind raised by his fists, another handspan was sliced away.
Though incomplete, the cutting power of his materialized qi was tremendous.
Slice! Slice! Slice!
In less than a split second, the steel spear in my hands had been reduced to a sharpened metal rod the length of my forearm.
“Damn. I thought I was finally getting used to it.”
At this point, it wasn’t a spear anymore. It was a short flute. A short flute.
Grumbling, I swung the steel flute through the air.
“Man, it suddenly got so light that I can’t adjust.”
Chulwoo must have found the sight amusing, because he burst into laughter.
“Ha-ha-ha! You pathetic bastard. What are you planning to do with that?”
“None of your business.”
“Are you admitting defeat already?”
“Admitting defeat, my ass. Who says I lost?”
“What gives you such confidence after losing even your weapon? If you think my Senior Brother or your brother will save you, you’re mistaken.”
I let out a quiet laugh.
“You’d better not regret this. If you ask for a draw now, I might consider it.”
“What? A draw?”
“Yeah. On the condition that you stop hitting on this Young Lady.”
“You lunatic.”
“Then negotiations are over.”
I strode toward him, casually swinging the steel flute that could no longer be called a spear.
“Come here. Let’s fight.”
A spearman was fearlessly approaching a master of fist-and-foot martial arts—and without even a proper weapon in his hands.
The crowd surrounding the Grand Training Ground began to murmur at the sight.
Chulwoo frowned as though he were looking at some bizarre creature.
“What the hell are you?”
“Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. You know that.”
“Are you acting cocky because you have some hidden move up your sleeve?”
“Who knows?”
“You aren’t planning to use some underhanded trick, are you?”
An underhanded trick.
In a way, I supposed it was something like that.
After all, it was a method permitted only to me—one no one else could see.
Open Status Window.
Only thirty paces remained between Chulwoo and me.
The System responded.
Ding.

System Status Window Level 71 Jin Taekyung Class: Peak Master Fame: 2,500 (+250) Titles: 5 (Title effects active) Returnee (All stats +10) Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi (All stats +15, Fame +200) Scion of a Prestigious Family (All stats +5, Fame +50) Gambler (Combat-related stats +10% in one-on-one combat) Intermediate Trainee (Training speed +20%) Strength: 255 (+55) Stamina: 207 (+50) Agility: 250 (+55) Intelligence: 40 (+30) Charm: 40 (+30) Internal Energy: 45 years Toughness: 200 (+50) Remaining Points: 70 - Certain stats have been temporarily increased by the Gambler effect. - Assign the remaining points.
The Gambler effect. And the seventy points I’d gained by breaking through the wall of the Peak realm.
I stepped forward without hesitation. Twenty paces away, I could see the bewilderment on Chulwoo’s face.
“Lunatic.”
“I hear that a lot.”
Fifteen paces.
I muttered inwardly.
Assign twenty points to Strength.
Whoosh.
An invisible wind swept through me, carrying new strength into my body. My Strength, temporarily pushed past 300, churned like an active volcano.
Assign fifty points to Agility.
A second wind blew.
The very next step felt strange, as though the foot I’d just moved belonged to someone else.
Was I always this light?
It felt as though I’d stepped into an entirely new world.
I took a deep breath.
Chulwoo, not me, was the first to close the remaining ten paces.
“Damn it, I told you to surrender! Don’t blame me for what happens now!”
Whoosh!
I knew this martial art. It was called Crouching Tiger Fist because it was said to subdue tigers.
Just as its ferocious opening strike was about to slam into my chest—
Whoosh.
A third wind blew.
It began at my toes and ended at my fingertips.
“Hey, Level 95.”
Swish.
I jabbed the pointed steel flute into the back of Chulwoo’s neck.
By then, I was already perched on his shoulder.
“Looks like I’ve gotten a lot stronger.”

He seeks to win her love by defeating you.
Grade: Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Task: Win the duel (Incomplete) Reward: EXP and Fame Failure: Acquire the Title Weak Male —Would you like to accept the Quest?
—If you refuse the Quest, the Title Weak Male will be granted.
Wow.
This is bullshit.
Of course, the penalty for refusing would suck twice as much.
Not like I have a choice.
I clicked my tongue and rose from my seat, drawing everyone’s attention.

I was the only one who didn’t think much of it.

We’ll have a good, clean fight.”
Wolhwa sighed.

The Defeated Flower Fist is considered a prodigy even within Huashan.

“Probably because he’s good at fighting.”
“No, that’s not what I...
Whew.
Fine.
I give up.
Do whatever you want.”
Wolhwa was out.

“Eunhyang!”
“What?
I’m not wrong.”
In short, they were saying someone like me was no match for Chulwoo.
That’s what you think.
I thought otherwise.
I still didn’t know whether it was arrogance or confidence.
I just...

chapters.title: Chapter 190
paragraphs: Crash!
Baek Museong's body shot upward as though it had been bounced into the air.
The chair he had been sitting in moments ago clattered loudly across the ground, but he paid it no attention. Neither did anyone else present.
“What in the...”
“What happened?”
“W-What just happened?”
They had thought it was over. Jin Taekyung had displayed far greater skill than expected, but in the end, he had lost his weapon to Chulwoo's Fist Energy.
A spearman without a spear against a Peak fist fighter. The outcome was obvious.
No—it had seemed obvious.
Until a moment ago.
“How did that happen?”
At Lee Seowol’s question, Baek Museong’s lips twitched. It was still difficult to believe, but for an instant, he had lost sight of Jin Taekyung’s movements.
All he had seen was a pale blur.
I feel as though I’ve been bewitched by a ghost.
Something impossible had happened.
After remaining silent for a moment, Baek Museong opened his mouth. His voice came out tinged with embarrassment.
“I don’t know.”
Another wave of shock rippled through the crowd. Eunhyang, who had observed Baek Museong more closely than anyone else, widened her eyes.
“Big Brother—no, Senior Brother.”
“It’s true. Don’t say a word.”
He had entered Huashan at the age of five, become the Disciple of the Heavenly Sword True Person, and earned the reputation of being Huashan’s greatest prodigy.
Though only thirty, his standing was already equal to that of the Elders, if not greater.
Huashan’s greatest prodigy... Even a passing dog would laugh.
With a bitter smile, Baek Museong turned his head. A brightly smiling figure entered his view.
Ten years ago, a single meeting with Cheongpung had taught him the truth.
Baek Museong was not Huashan’s greatest prodigy.
“Martial Uncle Cheongpung.”
“Go ahead, Martial Nephew.”
Cheongpung answered without turning his head. His eyes remained fixed on the Grand Training Ground, gleaming with interest.
“Please tell me. How did he move?”
Under everyone’s expectant gaze, Cheongpung opened his mouth.
“He was fast.”
Everyone promptly deflated. Fast? That was not the simple, obvious answer they had wanted.
Baek Museong spoke in an anxious voice.
“That isn’t what I meant.”
“I know. But that’s all there is to it.”
“...What do you mean?”
“My Benefactor has learned only one footwork technique and one spear technique. They’re rough but practical martial arts. Neither could be called a divine art.”
Cheongpung smiled brightly.
“He was simply fast. Much faster than Martial Nephew Chulwoo.”
Baek Museong was left speechless.

Jin Taekyung had learned no supreme martial art and possessed no peerless internal energy. To Baek Museong, he had been nothing more than a young prodigy from a frontier martial family with exceptional martial talent.
How can such a thing be possible?
The human body had limits. Murim martial artists were special because martial arts and internal energy allowed them to surpass those limits.
Yet Cheongpung was saying that Jin Taekyung had surpassed those limits without any particularly extraordinary martial arts.
Baek Museong blurted out a vehement denial.
“Impossible.”
Cheongpung shook his head.
“It’s possible for my Benefactor.”
“He read the pattern of Crouching Tiger Fist and counterattacked after only two days. If Martial Nephew Chulwoo had known that, he would have tried something else.”
“Crouching Tiger Fist—in two days?”
Crouching Tiger Fist was unquestionably an advanced martial art. True to its name, it was fierce enough to subdue a tiger, and its forms were exceptionally intricate.
Even Huashan Disciples whose talent had already been recognized needed a full year merely to learn its structure and forms.
Yet Jin Taekyung had done it in only two days.
My second junior brother was bound to lose.
Baek Museong’s eyelids trembled faintly.
He thought he finally understood why the young Martial Uncle before him wished to remain at Jin Taekyung’s side.
There was another monster.
Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
He was exactly what the name implied. Though he remained hidden in the shadows of the frontier for now, it would not be long before he spread his wings and soared into the open sky.
I was far too arrogant.
Baek Museong clenched his fists. His nails dug into his skin, but the shame hurt more than the pain.
Had he become drunk on the name of Huashan?
Before the duel had even begun, he had already decided who would win and who would lose.
I’m always telling my junior disciples to be humble, yet I failed to practice it myself.
It had been a day that gave him much to reflect upon.
Baek Museong let out a quiet sigh and offered Jin Wikyung a clasped-fist salute.
“Great Hero Jin, I apologize for my earlier rudeness.”
“Ah, no.”
Jin Wikyung’s expression was stiff as he accepted the apology.
As far as Baek Museong knew, Jin Wikyung treasured his two younger brothers like precious jewels. Baek Museong had belittled Jin Taekyung right in front of him, so naturally he would be angry.
Baek Museong continued politely.
“My Junior Brother and I have both learned a great deal. The winner appears to have been decided, so I believe we may end the duel here.”
“That would be best.”
Jin Wikyung nodded gravely and rose from his seat.
A murmur too quiet for anyone to hear slipped between his lips.
“...Wow. He actually did it.”
Jin Wikyung had never expected him to really win.
The Grand Training Ground was as quiet as though everyone had been drenched in cold water. The commoners and martial artists alike wore expressions as if they had seen a ghost.
Though I couldn't see his face, Chulwoo was probably wearing a similar expression. The guy who had been frozen like a statue asked in a trembling voice,
“H-How?”
“By being good.”
“C-Could that have been Shifting Form and Position?”
“Your hyung’s pretty fast, you know. Surprised?”
“You dodged Crouching Tiger Fist that easily...”
“You were much slower than your Martial Uncle. You'd better train hard when you get back.”
It was true. Compared to Cheongpung’s Crouching Tiger Fist, Chulwoo’s was far slower, and his movements were much broader.
I could see the entire pattern. There was no reason I couldn’t evade it—especially with an Agility stat that had broken through 300.
“Destructive power only matters if your movements are fast and precise enough to hit your opponent. Got it?”
“...How dare you lecture me?”
“How dare I? Lecture you? You still haven’t figured out what’s going on?”
I snorted quietly and poked the back of Chulwoo's neck with the steel flute.
Its sharp edge dug into his skin, and his massive body shuddered. Oh, this was fun.
“Rest easy! Huashan’s Serial Confession Man has been dealt with by the Taiyuan Jin Family’s Steel Flute Murderer!”
“You bastard!”
“Ah-ah, don’t move. I’d rather not draw blood.”
“You’re dead the moment you come down.”
“Maybe. But the duel seems to be over, so try again next time.”
Just then, I spotted Jin Wikyung rising from his seat.
Chulwoo would never surrender of his own accord, so it seemed Jin Wikyung intended to end the duel here.
His voice, reinforced with internal energy, rang throughout the Grand Training Ground.
“You both fought well!”
“Waaaaah!”
The crowd finally came to its senses and answered with a deafening cheer.
They had witnessed a duel between Peak masters with their own eyes—something difficult to see even if you were willing to pay for it. Their reaction was understandable.
“All right, that’s enough. Good work.”
The Quest had been much easier than expected.
The moment I pulled the steel flute away from Chulwoo’s neck with a cheerful smile—
Grab!
A hand as large as a pot lid clamped around my wrist.
“Huh?”
“It isn’t over yet!”
For a moment, I had forgotten what kind of man Chulwoo was.
A man blinded by love. A man who had spent twenty-five years dead inside until his heart finally began to beat. A man who could neither live nor die without Lee Seowol’s permission...
In short, a madman. “Fucking bastard” was a close synonym.
There’s no way a guy like that would give up so easily.
Whatever else could be said about him, he had been born with one extraordinary gift: divine strength. Even Cheongpung had to concede that much to him.
Chulwoo spoke with absolute confidence.
“Once I get my hands on someone, it’s over.”
Sure, I'd let my guard down, but weren't this bastard's manners absolute shit?
Ah, a man blinded by love.
I let out a heavy sigh.
“Chul-thetic, Pawoo.”
“Are those your last words?”
“No. Words of wisdom.”
“You spout nonsense whenever you get the chance. Give up on Young Lady Lee, and I’ll let you off here.”
“Did I ever tell you?”
“What?”
“Young Lady Lee proposed to me.”
“You goddamn soooooon of a—!”
A scream erupted from the crowd.
Veins bulged across Chulwoo’s entire body as he tried to slam me into the ground with tremendous force.
Tried to.
“What are you doing?”
“Hnnnnngh!”
His flushed face turned pale, then purple.
An immense force dragged at my wrist, but I didn’t budge an inch.
“Oh, you’re pretty strong.”
Between the temporary boost from the Gambler Title and the points I had just allocated, the strength now coursing through my body far surpassed human limits.
Not even Chulwoo, with his enormous frame and innate divine strength, could overpower me.
“At this level, your Strength stat must be well over 200.”
“W-What is this?”
“Bastard.”
My grinning face was reflected in his horrified eyes.
“Your hyung’s Strength alone is over 300. I was stronger than you even before I allocated those points.”
Fist Energy? It meant nothing if it couldn’t hit me. Strength, speed—I surpassed him in every respect. Even if we had kept fighting as we were, I would have won in the end.
Even so, there was a simple reason I had bothered allocating the points.

“You son of a—!”
Thwack!

Boom!

Ding.

“No.”

“Zhongnan Sect.”

“Z-Zhongnan Sect?”
The old man at the front stared at Hyuk Mujin with blazing eyes.
“Jin Taekyung and Cheongpung. Take me to those two bastards at once.”

Baek Museong's body shot upward as though it had been bounced into the air.
The chair he had been sitting in moments ago clattered loudly across the ground, but he paid it no attention.
Neither did anyone else present.
“What in the...”
“What happened?”

Jin Taekyung had displayed far greater skill than expected, but in the end, he had lost his weapon to Chulwoo's Fist Energy.
A spearman without a spear against a Peak fist fighter.
The outcome was obvious.
No—it had seemed obvious.
Until a moment ago.
“How did that happen?”
At Lee Seowol’s question, Baek Museong’s lips twitched.
It was still difficult to believe, but for an instant, he had lost sight of Jin Taekyung’s movements.
All he had seen was a pale blur.
I feel as though I’ve been bewitched by a ghost.
Something impossible had happened.
After remaining silent for a moment, Baek Museong opened his mouth.
His voice came out tinged with embarrassment.
“I don’t know.”
Another wave of shock rippled through the crowd.
Eunhyang, who had observed Baek Museong more closely than anyone else, widened her eyes.
“Big Brother—no, Senior Brother.”
“It’s true.
Don’t say a word.”
He had entered Huashan at the age of five, become the Disciple of the Heavenly Sword True Person, and earned the reputation of being Huashan’s greatest prodigy.
Though only thirty, his standing was already equal to that of the Elders, if not greater.
Huashan’s greatest prodigy...
Even a passing dog would laugh.
With a bitter smile, Baek Museong turned his head.
A brightly smiling figure entered his view.
Ten years ago, a single meeting with Cheongpung had taught him the truth.
Baek Museong was not Huashan’s greatest prodigy.
“Martial Uncle Cheongpung.”
“Go ahead, Martial Nephew.”
Cheongpung answered without turning his head.
His eyes remained fixed on the Grand Training Ground, gleaming with interest.
“Please tell me.
How did he move?”
Under everyone’s expectant gaze, Cheongpung opened his mouth.
“He was fast.”
Everyone promptly deflated.
Fast?
That was not the simple, obvious answer they had wanted.
Baek Museong spoke in an anxious voice.
“That isn’t what I meant.”

But that’s all there is to it.”
“...What do you mean?”

Neither could be called a divine art.”
Cheongpung smiled brightly.
“He was simply fast.

Jin Taekyung had learned no supreme martial art and possessed no peerless internal energy.
To Baek Museong, he had been nothing more than a young prodigy from a frontier martial family with exceptional martial talent.
How can such a thing be possible?
The human body had limits.
Murim martial artists were special because martial arts and internal energy allowed them to surpass those limits.
Yet Cheongpung was saying that Jin Taekyung had surpassed those limits without any particularly extraordinary martial arts.
Baek Museong blurted out a vehement denial.
“Impossible.”
Cheongpung shook his head.

If Martial Nephew Chulwoo had known that, he would have tried something else.”
“Crouching Tiger Fist—in two days?”
Crouching Tiger Fist was unquestionably an advanced martial art.
True to its name, it was fierce enough to subdue a tiger, and its forms were exceptionally intricate.
Even Huashan Disciples whose talent had already been recognized needed a full year merely to learn its structure and forms.
Yet Jin Taekyung had done it in only two days.
My second junior brother was bound to lose.
Baek Museong’s eyelids trembled faintly.
He thought he finally understood why the young Martial Uncle before him wished to remain at Jin Taekyung’s side.
There was another monster.
Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
He was exactly what the name implied.
Though he remained hidden in the shadows of the frontier for now, it would not be long before he spread his wings and soared into the open sky.
I was far too arrogant.
Baek Museong clenched his fists.
His nails dug into his skin, but the shame hurt more than the pain.
Had he become drunk on the name of Huashan?
Before the duel had even begun, he had already decided who would win and who would lose.
I’m always telling my junior disciples to be humble, yet I failed to practice it myself.
It had been a day that gave him much to reflect upon.
Baek Museong let out a quiet sigh and offered Jin Wikyung a clasped-fist salute.
“Great Hero Jin, I apologize for my earlier rudeness.”
“Ah, no.”
Jin Wikyung’s expression was stiff as he accepted the apology.
As far as Baek Museong knew, Jin Wikyung treasured his two younger brothers like precious jewels.
Baek Museong had belittled Jin Taekyung right in front of him, so naturally he would be angry.
Baek Museong continued politely.
“My Junior Brother and I have both learned a great deal.
The winner appears to have been decided, so I believe we may end the duel here.”
“That would be best.”
Jin Wikyung nodded gravely and rose from his seat.
A murmur too quiet for anyone to hear slipped between his lips.
He actually did it.”
Jin Wikyung had never expected him to really win.
The Grand Training Ground was as quiet as though everyone had been drenched in cold water.
The commoners and martial artists alike wore expressions as if they had seen a ghost.
Though I couldn't see his face, Chulwoo was probably wearing a similar expression.
The guy who had been frozen like a statue asked in a trembling voice,

“By being good.”

Surprised?”

I could see the entire pattern.

You still haven’t figured out what’s going on?”

chapters.title: Chapter 191
paragraphs: As the unconscious Chulwoo was carried away, Jin Wikyung stepped forward.
“Does anyone else wish to challenge him?”
I had literally wiped the floor with Chulwoo, who had been so overwhelmingly strong. There was no chance anyone else would step up.
When no one came forward, Jin Wikyung shouted with an expression of pure delight,
“Then the final winner of this duel tournament is the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung!”
Ding.
System You became the final winner of the Jin Family of Taiyuan Duel Tournament Sudden Event! Fame increased! - You gained EXP! Level Up! You acquired 10 bonus points as an event Reward!
With that unexpected alert, the Grand Training Ground erupted into absolute madness.
“Waaaaah!”
“Long live the Jin Family of Taiyuan! Long live the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi!”
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi defeated the Defeated Flower Fist!”
“Kiyah-hoo!”
Who was that? Now there was a man who knew how to party.
In any case, the atmosphere in the Grand Training Ground grew hotter than anything a rock festival could offer.
A child hurled his candied fruit into the air, while a white-haired old man let out a wild cry and snapped his cane over his knee.
“Waaaaah!”
“Hiyah!”
The martial artists were even worse.
Shanxi Murim had long been treated as a backwater. I had merely defeated one Serial Confession Man, but to them, it was as good as winning a battle of pride against Shaanxi Murim.
“Lady of the House! Bring me a bottle of strong liquor!”
“That dumpling I ate twenty years ago finally went down! Order whatever you want! Everything’s on me today!”
Don’t call the Lady of the House. And don’t order everything.
It was all coming out of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s pockets anyway, but the people drunk on Shanxi pride had completely lost their minds.
They’re going wild.
Since a large portion of them were martial artists, carrying weapons was standard. I was worried that someone might get drunk on the excitement and cause trouble.
Sure enough, some lunatic suddenly shouted,
“Everyone, draw your swords!”
Clang-clang-clang!
Hundreds of weapons were drawn in a flash of reflected light.
“Wave them in order, starting from the front!”
“Waaaaah!”
Clang-clang-clang! Clang-clang-clang!
Wait, were they doing the wave here?
As I watched this cutting-edge new cheering culture unfold, I muttered in disbelief,
“This is a complete...”
“Shitshow.”
I had started the sentence, but I hadn’t said the second half.
An elderly voice pierced my ears with perfect clarity. I looked around, but all I could see were excited people.
Who was that?
Even amid the cacophony, the voice had sounded as though its owner were standing right beside me. Whoever he was, he was a master—and one with profound internal energy at that.
Just as several of us turned to search for the speaker—
“Ha!”
Gooooong.
Was this what the lion’s roar I had read about in martial arts novels sounded like?
The ground rumbled and the air trembled. The more fainthearted commoners passed out or collapsed screaming.
“Eeeeeek!”
“Gah!”
The festive Grand Training Ground descended into chaos in an instant.
The commoners trembled, and the martial artists stood frozen. Through the crowd, scattered as though a bomb had gone off, an old man strolled leisurely into view.
“Much better.”
He was tall and gaunt. His sharp gaze swept across the gathering before meeting mine.
I was standing in the middle of the duel platform, and a young man who remained perfectly fine while staring back at him was bound to stand out.
The old man looked me up and down, then spoke.
“Is it you?”
“Excuse me?”
“Cheongpung or Jin Taekyung. Which one are you?”
What the hell was going on?
Countless thoughts flashed through my mind. I made my decision in that brief instant.
“Neither.”
“You’re not?”
“No. You must have mistaken me for someone else.”
Whatever was going on, I might as well deny everything and see what happened.
One glance told me enough. I didn’t know who he was or where he had come from, but he certainly didn’t seem to have any warm feelings toward me.
“Is that so?”
“I’ve never heard either name in my life.”
The old man beckoned behind him.
“Come here.”
“Yes, Elder.”
Four people who had been obscured by the crowd emerged. As it happened, I had met every one of them before.
One face in particular was impossible to mistake.
Hyuk Mujin?
Wasn’t he supposed to be standing guard? What was he doing over there?
Pale as a sheet, Hyuk Mujin came forward as though the three middle-aged men beside him were dragging him along. Their faces were familiar too.
What were their epithets again?
Oh, right. The Three Hands of Zhongnan.
Just as I finally remembered the extras’ collective epithet, the unidentified old man spoke to the four of them.
“Find them.”
Hyuk Mujin and Gong Ilhyuk, the middle-aged man with a splint on his arm, pointed at me simultaneously.
“Captain! Please save me!”
“That’s him! He’s Jin Taekyung!”
Well, I was caught.
After a brief silence, the old man asked me,
“Are you really Jin Taekyung?”
I bowed as politely as I could.
“Nice to meet you. My name is Jin Taekyung.”
“...What kind of lunatic is this?”
As the old man stared at me in disbelief, three people landed lightly with a rush of wind.
Jin Wikyung, Baek Museong, and Cheongpung.
“I am Jin Wikyung, Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. May I ask this Senior’s name?”
“Ahem. You’re the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
The question had been directed at the old man, but Gong Ilhyuk was the one who stepped forward.
Jin Wikyung frowned at the interruption.
“That is correct. And who might you be?”

“I am Gong Ilhyuk, one of the Three Hands of Zhongnan. I am a second-generation Disciple of the Great Zhongnan Sect, and Great Hero Gong Iljung, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord and Sect Leader, is my father’s cousin.”
He was still going on about his father’s cousin.
It made me want to slap him across the mouth with the hind leg of a boiled chicken.
Upon learning Gong Ilhyuk’s identity, Jin Wikyung muttered almost as if groaning.
“The Zhongnan Sect?”
Gong Ilhyuk was a well-connected hack who threw his weight around, but the name of the Zhongnan Sect was another matter.
The Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were the towering powers that moved the present-day Murim.
Emboldened by the momentum, Gong Ilhyuk continued smugly,
“And this gentleman is Great Hero Song Il, an Elder of our sect.”
That old man is an Elder of the Zhongnan Sect?
I had expected him to be a master, but it seemed his status was even more impressive than I had imagined. Jin Wikyung and Baek Museong’s expressions hardened.
“The Roaring Fury Swordsman...!”
“This junior of Murim, Baek Museong, pays his respects to Senior Song.”
The old man—the Roaring Fury Swordsman—silently looked down at the two of them as they hurriedly paid their respects.
His voice carried the composure and arrogance of a powerful man.
“Baek Museong? Are you Huashan’s Lone Crane?”
“Yes. It is an epithet far too generous for me.”
“So it seems. You’re inferior to your Master in his youth.”
What an insufferable old bastard.
Still, I had to admit his clout was extraordinary.

Not only had the Roaring Fury Swordsman casually belittled Baek Museong, who was practically an object of admiration, in front of everyone, but he had also spoken of Huashan’s Sect Leader, the Heavenly Sword True Person, as though he were some old neighborhood friend.
His seniority in Murim seemed every bit as formidable as his martial arts.
“I will continue striving.”
“Hm. You certainly know how to make yourself sound good. But if the Heavenly Sword True Person sent you...”
As he watched Baek Museong bow his head without another word, the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s eyes flashed.
His gaze had shifted to Cheongpung, who stood there looking blank.
“So it’s you. The Sword Saint’s heir.”
Cheongpung asked with a puzzled expression,
“You know my grandfather?”
“Of course. How could I possibly not know him?”
Judging by the old man’s expression, theirs probably hadn’t been a pleasant relationship.
As the situation grew more serious, Jin Wikyung asked with a stiff face,
“May I ask what brings you here?”
“I came to collect a debt.”
“A debt?”
“Yes. A debt owed for daring to mock the Great Zhongnan Sect and injure one of our Disciples.”
His blade-sharp gaze shot toward Cheongpung and me.
Gong Ilhyuk stepped forward, waving his splinted arm.
“Do you see this? I suffered this injury at Prince Shangshan’s residence, where I had gone by invitation. A physician examined it and said I would need at least six months to recover.”
Cheongpung spoke with an apologetic expression.
“I hit you gently... Did it hurt that much?”
Cruel bastard. He was killing Gong Ilhyuk twice over.
Gong Ilhyuk’s face flushed red at the public humiliation.
“You bastard! You ambushed me, yet you still have the nerve to say that!”
I muttered in disbelief,
“Ambushed, my ass. You grabbed him by the collar first and got your ass handed to you.”
“Shut your mouth! When I think of how you two mocked our sect and what you did to me, I wouldn’t be satisfied even if I chewed you up and swallowed you!”
That was how a fight between children turned into a fight between adults.
Jin Wikyung and Baek Museong’s faces twisted sharply.
“Chew him up and swallow him? Did you just say that to our youngest?”
“How dare you call him a bastard! Great Hero Gong, watch your words! Though our sects may differ, there is still such a thing as seniority in Murim. How could you...”
“Heh heh heh.”
At the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s grating laughter, Jin Wikyung and Baek Museong fell silent.
“Seniority, you say. You chose your words well.”
“This old man is the Senior Brother of our sect’s Sect Leader, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord. I am of the same seniority as the Heavenly Sword True Person of Huashan, so there should be no problem.”
Bringing up seniority had been a mistake.

The Roaring Fury Swordsman’s martial arts were formidable enough, and now he was crushing them beneath the sheer weight of his seniority. Neither Jin Wikyung nor Baek Museong could contend with him. Not even Cheongpung, the Sword Saint’s Disciple, could.
“Am I wrong?”
When no one answered, the Roaring Fury Swordsman turned to Cheongpung.
“You injured a Disciple of the Zhongnan Sect. Are you prepared to face the consequences?”
This was why words were so frightening.
There was no explanation of how it had happened. Only the result remained.
Baek Museong hurriedly interjected.
“Senior, we must first establish the rights and wrongs of this matter.”
Cheongpung shrank in on himself and muttered,
“I only gave him a gentle tap.”
“Are you saying you didn’t do it?”
“That’s not what I mean. I did hit him, but I didn’t know he would be hurt that badly.”
Gong Ilhyuk seized the opening and lunged in.
“It was an obvious attempt to kill!”
“Did you hear that?”
“It really wasn’t.”
As Cheongpung fumbled for words, the Roaring Fury Swordsman continued in a cutting voice.
“I will formally lodge a complaint with Huashan over this matter, so don’t you dare think you can wriggle out of it.”
“Elder, the government and Murim do not interfere in each other’s affairs. Furthermore, the officials present at the time were favorably disposed toward them. I fear they may give false testimony.”
“You are right. I will take measures.”
It was all rigged from the start.
Baek Museong bit down hard on his lip at the unfair treatment, and the next target of their arrows was obvious.
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan will seal its gates until our sect sends someone.”
“...What did you just say?”
Jin Wikyung said what I wanted to say for me. No—everyone nearby who had heard the Roaring Fury Swordsman must have been thinking the same thing.
Seal our gates?
What kind of bullshit was that?
It was true that I had humiliated Gong Ilhyuk a little.
But that had been directed solely at Gong Ilhyuk. I could swear that I had never said anything to mock or insult the Zhongnan Sect.
And they wanted the Jin Family to seal its gates over that?
Even with the condition that it would last only until the Zhongnan Sect sent someone, the order itself was already a humiliation.
“That is unjust!”
At Jin Wikyung’s shout, the Roaring Fury Swordsman raised his eyes.
“What did you say?”

“How can you order us to seal our gates before even investigating what happened and determining who was at fault? Is this the way of the Nine Sects and One Gang—or rather, the way of the Zhongnan Sect?”
“How dare you!”
“Our family will not accept this!”
“If you refuse to accept it?”
Ssssss.
A tremendous aura rose from the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s entire body like wildfire.
It felt as though a sword were pointed directly between my brows. My skin prickled.
“If you refuse, what will you do?”
“This is Murim. Have you forgotten?”
A surge of irritation suddenly welled up inside me.
I already knew how the world worked. I had experienced it more times than I cared to remember.
People ignored you because you had no money, looked down on you because you lacked powerful backing, and scorned you because your talent was insignificant.
It’s the same here.
Murim and the modern world were different, yet so much alike.
Those with power turned lies into truth and truth into lies.
They pressured the weak and crushed them underfoot. To people like that, it was all natural. All inevitable.
Just like the Roaring Fury Swordsman standing before me.
Drip. Drip.
Blood trickled from the fist I had clenched without realizing it.
I stared down at the drops landing one by one on the ground and exhaled a hot breath.
“Ah, fuck. This is fucking bullshit.”
No one had dared to speak, so everyone heard the profanity that burst from my mouth.
It felt as though something invisible had shattered with a sharp crack.
The Roaring Fury Swordsman asked with an expression of disbelief,
“...What did you just say?”
Swearing had been a mistake. Since I was the reason this had happened, I should have swallowed it no matter what.
That was the best way to resolve the situation smoothly.
But...
“It’s fucking bullshit. I said it’s fucking bullshit. You fucking assholes. There’s a limit to how much you can throw your weight around.”
I couldn’t take it anymore.
They could call me thoughtless or a young fool who knew nothing about the world.
I had no desire to replay all the things I had been sick of experiencing in reality here in Murim.
I apologized to Jin Wikyung.
“I’m sorry. I know I’m supposed to put up with it even when it’s fucking bullshit, but they were being so fucking shitty about it that it felt twice as fucking shitty, and I couldn’t let it slide.”
Jin Wikyung, who looked half dazed, went through an astonishing range of expressions.
His face twisted, then relaxed. After showing several different expressions in a short span of time, he finally let out a quiet laugh.
“Honestly, I thought it was fucking bullshit too.”
Those words pulled the trigger.
Flames hotter than lava poured from the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s eyes.
“You bastards... must be desperate to die.”
Shing.
As he spat the words through clenched teeth, he drew his sword. Layer upon layer of Sword Energy enveloped the snow-white blade.
It burned more fiercely than any Sword Energy I had ever seen.
The instant it pointed at me—
“If you kill that guy, you die too.”
At the clear, ringing voice that came from somewhere, the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s body abruptly froze.

I had literally wiped the floor with Chulwoo, who had been so overwhelmingly strong.

Fame increased! - You gained EXP!

“Waaaaah!”

A child hurled his candied fruit into the air, while a white-haired old man let out a wild cry and snapped his cane over his knee.
“Waaaaah!”
“Hiyah!”

Shanxi Murim had long been treated as a backwater.

“Lady of the House!

“That dumpling I ate twenty years ago finally went down!

Don’t call the Lady of the House.
And don’t order everything.
It was all coming out of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s pockets anyway, but the people drunk on Shanxi pride had completely lost their minds.
They’re going wild.
Since a large portion of them were martial artists, carrying weapons was standard.
I was worried that someone might get drunk on the excitement and cause trouble.
Sure enough, some lunatic suddenly shouted,
“Everyone, draw your swords!”
Clang-clang-clang!
Hundreds of weapons were drawn in a flash of reflected light.
“Wave them in order, starting from the front!”
“Waaaaah!”
Clang-clang-clang!
Clang-clang-clang!
Wait, were they doing the wave here?

“Shitshow.”
I had started the sentence, but I hadn’t said the second half.
An elderly voice pierced my ears with perfect clarity.
I looked around, but all I could see were excited people.
Who was that?
Even amid the cacophony, the voice had sounded as though its owner were standing right beside me.
Whoever he was, he was a master—and one with profound internal energy at that.
Just as several of us turned to search for the speaker—
“Ha!”
Gooooong.
Was this what the lion’s roar I had read about in martial arts novels sounded like?
The ground rumbled and the air trembled.
The more fainthearted commoners passed out or collapsed screaming.
“Eeeeeek!”
“Gah!”
The festive Grand Training Ground descended into chaos in an instant.
The commoners trembled, and the martial artists stood frozen.
Through the crowd, scattered as though a bomb had gone off, an old man strolled leisurely into view.
“Much better.”
He was tall and gaunt.
His sharp gaze swept across the gathering before meeting mine.
I was standing in the middle of the duel platform, and a young man who remained perfectly fine while staring back at him was bound to stand out.
The old man looked me up and down, then spoke.
“Is it you?”
“Excuse me?”
“Cheongpung or Jin Taekyung.
Which one are you?”
What the hell was going on?
Countless thoughts flashed through my mind.
I made my decision in that brief instant.
“Neither.”
“You’re not?”
“No.
You must have mistaken me for someone else.”
Whatever was going on, I might as well deny everything and see what happened.
One glance told me enough.
I didn’t know who he was or where he had come from, but he certainly didn’t seem to have any warm feelings toward me.

The old man beckoned behind him.

Wasn’t he supposed to be standing guard?
What was he doing over there?
Pale as a sheet, Hyuk Mujin came forward as though the three middle-aged men beside him were dragging him along.
Their faces were familiar too.
What were their epithets again?
Oh, right.
The Three Hands of Zhongnan.

Well, I was caught.

The Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were the towering powers that moved the present-day Murim.

chapters.title: Chapter 192
paragraphs: “Ah, fuck. This is fucking bullshit, seriously.”
...What?
Song Il thought he was dreaming.

Who was he? He was Song Il, the Roaring Fury Swordsman. Even now that his junior brother, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, had become Sect Leader, he still treated Song Il with the utmost courtesy and respect.
And yet—what the fuck? Fucking bullshit?
Did I hear that wrong?
The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung. The youngest son of the tiny Jin Family of Taiyuan.
A brat who had only just turned twenty with the new year.
He couldn’t believe that such a brat had said those words to him—a Great Zhongnan Sect Elder and one of the heroes of the Great Faction War.
No. He couldn’t accept it.
“What did you just say?”
Any hope that he had misheard was crushed the next moment by Jin Taekyung’s reply.
“It’s fucking bullshit. I said it’s fucking bullshit! You fucking assholes! There’s a limit to how much you can throw your weight around.”
After cursing up a storm, Jin Taekyung turned to Jin Wikyung.
“I’m sorry. I know I’m supposed to put up with it even when it’s fucking bullshit, but they were being so fucking shitty about it that it felt twice as fucking shitty, and I couldn’t let it slide.”
“Honestly, I thought it was fucking bullshit too.”
Those words from Jin Wikyung were the finishing touch.
The disbelief in Song Il’s eyes slowly gave way to light. A blazing light.
It was an immense fury he hadn’t felt in a very long time.
“You bastards...”
Hot breath escaped between Song Il’s teeth as he lost all reason.
“You must be desperate to die.”
Shing.

His treasured sword, which had cut down countless enemies, emerged from its scabbard. It didn’t matter whether the Jin Family of Taiyuan belonged to the orthodox faction, the unorthodox faction, or even practiced demonic, heterodox arts.
If Song Il had thought about the consequences before causing trouble, he never would have earned the title Roaring Fury Swordsman.
I’ll kill every last one of you.
Song Il truly intended to kill them. As though to prove it, powerful Sword Energy surged like waves.
He had trained in the Zhongnan Sect’s ultimate technique, the Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords, all his life.
Although he had not achieved Great Completion, it was more than enough to carve these insolent fools into chunks of meat with a single sword strike.
I’ll kill you first.
He had already decided who would die first.
The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung. He would chew up that young brat’s tongue and swallow it.
Just as Song Il was about to unleash his Sword Energy, his eyes bloodshot—
“If you kill that guy, you die too.”
At the voice that came from somewhere, Song Il’s body abruptly froze.
Not because of what the words meant. Because he couldn’t determine where they had come from.
I can’t tell? Me?
That was impossible.
But the voice that followed made it clear that this was real.
“A man your age, picking on a child like this. Tsk, tsk.”
Front, back, above, below, left, right.
Song Il couldn’t distinguish where the voice was coming from. Its owner was nowhere and everywhere at once.
Th-this is...
At last, Song Il realized the identity of the voice, and his body trembled.
Six-Harmonies Voice Transmission!

If Sound Transmission, the art of conveying sound through internal energy, was the exclusive province of Peak masters, Six-Harmonies Voice Transmission was a martial art permitted only to those who had reached the realm beyond it.
Supreme Peak. A great realm that only a tiny fraction of the chosen few could enter.
How could someone like that...
Why? Why was such a person interfering with him?
Song Il shouted as if having a fit.
“Who are you! I am Elder Song Il of the Great Zhongnan Sect, the Roaring Fury Swordsman! Show yourself at once!”
“‘This old man’? ‘Elder’? Hahahahahaha!”
Thunderous laughter rang out from every direction, backed by internal energy so vast that no one dared guess at its limits.
The commoners who had never learned martial arts fell flat on their faces, crying out to the Jade Emperor, while the martial artists trembled in awe.
“Can you not hear me!”
“Ha, hahaha! Ah, I’m laughing so hard my stomach’s going to split.”
“You insolent bastard!”
Having lost his composure to anger and fear, Song Il caught sight of Jin Taekyung.
Unlike the people staring around in shock, Jin Taekyung alone was gazing into the empty air. There was even an enigmatic smile on his lips.
Almost as though he were mocking Song Il.
That bastard!
Ssssss!
The Sword Energy that had faltered for a moment surged again. Pointing his sword at Jin Taekyung, Song Il looked around and shouted,
“Show yourself at once! Or I’ll kill this bastard!”
The laughter that had shaken heaven and earth abruptly stopped.
“What? Kill that guy?”
“I’ll count to three.”
A triumphant smile spread across Song Il’s lips.
He didn’t know where the voice’s owner was, but the troublemaker’s weakness was Jin Taekyung. The fluster in the other man’s voice was proof.
“One!”
“Heh, look at you. You’ve grown even more vicious since I last saw you.”
Since they last met?
Song Il’s mind raced. Judging by those words, they had clearly met before, but...
Wait. Could that voice be...
Song Il flinched as someone came to mind, but quickly gritted his teeth.
That was impossible. There was no way that old monster was still alive.
As though trying to shake off his fear, he shouted even louder.
“Two!”
“Phew. Fine, I understand. I’ll come out now, so wait right there! But if you touch even a single hair on him, I’ll make you pay!”
Song Il’s strength left him all at once.
His gamble had worked. The unidentified Supreme Peak master wanted Jin Taekyung alive. And he was farther away than Song Il had expected.
“Fifty jang. Stay at least fifty jang away. If you come any closer, this bastard is as good as dead—”
At that exact moment—
“Three.”
Song Il doubted his own eyes and ears.
Barely three jang away, Jin Taekyung calmly spoke again.
“I said three. You fucking old bastard. Are you deaf?”
“You bastard. Are you desperate to die?”
“Try killing me. If you can.”
“...What?”
“You know what? If you can’t kill me with one sword strike, you’re next.”
“Let’s see who dies.”
Jin Taekyung smiled brightly and spread both arms.
“He’s coming.”
He was coming. Those two words sent a chill down Song Il’s spine.
Song Il unconsciously took a step back.
Then—
Whoosh.
A faint rush of wind pierced his ears. A presence was rapidly closing in from behind at an unbelievable speed.
This is...
Every hair on Song Il’s body stood on end. The instincts he had honed by crossing the threshold of death countless times whispered to him.
It’s already too late. Fall back. Now.
But—
I am Song Il, the Roaring Fury Swordsman!
Sssshhhhh!
The Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords, which he had brought to nine-tenths mastery, erupted. His Sword Energy split into twenty-four streams and shot forward.
In the slowed world, Jin Taekyung’s figure was reflected in Song Il’s wide-open eyes.
Swish, swish, swish, swish, swish!
He narrowly evaded the twenty-four streams of Sword Energy as they closed in from every direction.
The only price he paid for evading the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s strike was torn clothing and scattered drops of blood.
“This is impossible—!”
Song Il, still in shock, was given no chance to attack again.
Something firm and hot clamped around his wrist just as he tried to unleash the second form.
Clench!
“You fucking bastard... Didn’t I tell you not to touch a single hair on him?”
A low voice. Two eyes blazing so fiercely that their red seemed to burn blue.
Only then did Song Il realize that he could no longer hear the wind.
And that he had touched someone he never should have touched.
“Y-you... How could you...”
“The Zhongnan brat has grown a lot. You can’t even recognize an adult anymore.”
The old monster who had inflicted an unforgettable humiliation upon him long ago had stepped out of his memories and now stood before him.
Song Il let out a shrill scream.
“Fire King—!”
A terrifying smile appeared on Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled lips.
“Yes. It’s me.”
On New Year’s Day, the Fire King descended upon the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
The weight of that name pressed down upon the entire training ground.
One God, Three Saints, Ten Kings.
They were gods, stars, and kings who towered above the countless martial artists of Murim. Absolute beings who stood closest to the title of greatest under heaven.
Jeok Cheongang wore shabby clothes and had a slight frame, but his presence was that of a giant.
And the giant’s eyes turned toward me.
“You crazy bastard. Are you desperate to die?”
I never thought that voice could sound so welcome. I sank to the ground on the spot.
“Whew. I almost died for real.”
“You would have if this old man hadn’t stepped in.”
“Yes, thank you. I won’t forget this kindness.”
At my soulless reply, Jeok Cheongang glared at me.
“You lost your fear in half a day. Do you want to die?”
Only half a day?
Come to think of it, I had parted with Jeok Cheongang that very morning.
The first day of the new year had been so eventful that it felt as though a month had passed.
I answered in an exhausted voice.
“If you’re going to kill me, please put it off as long as possible.”
“That is the plan.”
Jeok Cheongang turned his head and added,
“First, I’ll deal with this insolent bastard.”
Insolent bastard?
How many people in the world could call the Senior Brother of the Zhongnan Sect’s Sect Leader—and an Elder at that—something like that?
“Ah, ah...”
Song Il, the Roaring Fury Swordsman, was trembling from head to toe.
Judging by the way Jeok Cheongang kept calling him a brat, they must have known each other in the past. Apparently, it hadn’t been a particularly warm relationship.
“It’s been a long time. So, did those broken bones heal properly?”
“H-how could you...”
“‘You’? Was that directed at me?”
The Fire King blinked as though he were looking at some fascinating creature, then let out a hollow laugh.
“You’ve grown a lot.”
Smack.
It was a sight money couldn’t buy.

Jeok Cheongang slapped the Roaring Fury Swordsman across the face with his wrinkled hand. His hand moved so slowly it seemed to take forever, yet the Roaring Fury Swordsman didn’t dare evade it even though he could see it coming.
“I remember when I first saw you. You were barely twenty, a young pup.”
Smack.
“You were arrogant and rude, causing all kinds of trouble while hiding behind your sect’s prestige. And now you’re an Elder of the Zhongnan Sect?”
Smack.
“Once, I saved you when you were about to die, and what you said afterward was truly something. Was it, ‘Why are you stealing someone else’s battle credit?’”
Smack.
“If it hadn’t been for your Master’s request, I would have broken your neck instead of your leg.”
Smack, smack, smack!
The ordinary slaps carried not a trace of internal energy, yet the half-gray-haired Roaring Fury Swordsman shrank like a beaten child.
The ease and arrogance of a powerful man had vanished from his eyes, replaced by humiliation, fury, and fear.
Jeok Cheongang spat out the words with the expression of a man looking at a bug.
“You fucking moron. Did all those years go straight up your ass?”
What should I do?
I was starting to like the old man more and more.
Jin Wikyung and Hyuk Mujin were already gazing at Jeok Cheongang with love in their eyes.

“You call yourself an Elder of the Nine Sects and One Gang, yet you threaten commoners and use your power to arbitrarily order a sect to seal its gates? If your Master saw this, he would be wailing in the afterlife.”
“Who is the Sect Leader now?”
The Roaring Fury Swordsman answered in a stammering voice.
“M-my junior brother. The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord...”
“Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord? I’ve never heard that title in my life. Is that why a piece of trash like you struts around calling himself an Elder of the Zhongnan Sect?”
What audacity—to treat the Sect Leader of the Zhongnan Sect like some nobody.
As if having his sect insulted weren’t enough, the Roaring Fury Swordsman had suddenly been reduced to a piece of trash. His face twisted violently.
When he silently lowered his head to hide his humiliation and anger, Jeok Cheongang’s tiger-like eyes widened.
“Is your mouth just for decoration? Why aren’t you saying anything?”
“...Great Hero Jeok. I-I merely...”
“Shut your mouth!”
I made up my mind.
I was going to create a fan club.
At this very moment, the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was practically the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s idol.
Is this what it feels like to bathe in a hot spring filled with soda?
Even my white blood cells seemed to fizz with carbonation.
It felt like chugging a can of beer so cold it had begun to ice over after finishing a raid on a sweltering summer day.
Wave after wave of exhilarating refreshment swept through my entire body.
Fire. King. Is. The. Best.
Of course, that was from the perspective of someone watching.

The Roaring Fury Swordsman had been publicly humiliated in front of countless commoners and martial artists alike. His body shook. Perhaps that was why the humiliation and anger he felt in that instant overcame his fear of the Fire King.
“T-this is a matter between our sect and the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“What?”
“I’m saying that this is not a matter for Great Hero Jeok to involve himself in.”
“This old man has no business involving himself?”
Jeok Cheongang studied the Roaring Fury Swordsman, who had forced out those words in a trembling voice.
His tightly clenched fist twitched as if he were deciding where to hit him so everyone would agree he had chosen the perfect spot.
Hit him! Please, just hit him once!
As though he had heard my encouragement, Jeok Cheongang raised his hand high.
Then, the next moment, his wrinkled finger pointed at me.
“Do you see that bastard?”
What the hell? Why was I suddenly involved?
Just as confusion spread across every face, mine included, the Fire King continued.
“I entrusted the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure to that boy.”
Silence descended upon the Grand Training Ground.
Wordless shock spread endlessly through the crowd.

This is fucking bullshit, seriously.”

Song Il thought he was dreaming.
Who was he?
He was Song Il, the Roaring Fury Swordsman.
Even now that his junior brother, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, had become Sect Leader, he still treated Song Il with the utmost courtesy and respect.
And yet—what the fuck?
Fucking bullshit?
Did I hear that wrong?
The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung.
The youngest son of the tiny Jin Family of Taiyuan.
A brat who had only just turned twenty with the new year.
He couldn’t believe that such a brat had said those words to him—a Great Zhongnan Sect Elder and one of the heroes of the Great Faction War.
No.
He couldn’t accept it.
“What did you just say?”
Any hope that he had misheard was crushed the next moment by Jin Taekyung’s reply.
“It’s fucking bullshit.
I said it’s fucking bullshit!
You fucking assholes!
There’s a limit to how much you can throw your weight around.”
After cursing up a storm, Jin Taekyung turned to Jin Wikyung.
“I’m sorry.
I know I’m supposed to put up with it even when it’s fucking bullshit, but they were being so fucking shitty about it that it felt twice as fucking shitty, and I couldn’t let it slide.”
“Honestly, I thought it was fucking bullshit too.”
Those words from Jin Wikyung were the finishing touch.
The disbelief in Song Il’s eyes slowly gave way to light.
A blazing light.
It was an immense fury he hadn’t felt in a very long time.
“You bastards...”
Hot breath escaped between Song Il’s teeth as he lost all reason.
“You must be desperate to die.”
Shing.
His treasured sword, which had cut down countless enemies, emerged from its scabbard.
It didn’t matter whether the Jin Family of Taiyuan belonged to the orthodox faction, the unorthodox faction, or even practiced demonic, heterodox arts.
If Song Il had thought about the consequences before causing trouble, he never would have earned the title Roaring Fury Swordsman.
I’ll kill every last one of you.
Song Il truly intended to kill them.
As though to prove it, powerful Sword Energy surged like waves.
He had trained in the Zhongnan Sect’s ultimate technique, the Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords, all his life.
Although he had not achieved Great Completion, it was more than enough to carve these insolent fools into chunks of meat with a single sword strike.
I’ll kill you first.
He had already decided who would die first.
The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung.
He would chew up that young brat’s tongue and swallow it.
Just as Song Il was about to unleash his Sword Energy, his eyes bloodshot—
“If you kill that guy, you die too.”
At the voice that came from somewhere, Song Il’s body abruptly froze.
Not because of what the words meant.
Because he couldn’t determine where they had come from.
I can’t tell?
Me?
That was impossible.
But the voice that followed made it clear that this was real.
“A man your age, picking on a child like this.
Tsk, tsk.”
Front, back, above, below, left, right.
Song Il couldn’t distinguish where the voice was coming from.
Its owner was nowhere and everywhere at once.
Th-this is...
At last, Song Il realized the identity of the voice, and his body trembled.
Six-Harmonies Voice Transmission!

If Sound Transmission, the art of conveying sound through internal energy, was the exclusive province of Peak masters, Six-Harmonies Voice Transmission was a martial art permitted only to those who had reached the realm beyond it.
Supreme Peak.
A great realm that only a tiny fraction of the chosen few could enter.
How could someone like that...
Why?
Why was such a person interfering with him?
Song Il shouted as if having a fit.
“Who are you!
I am Elder Song Il of the Great Zhongnan Sect, the Roaring Fury Swordsman!
Show yourself at once!”
“‘This old man’?
‘Elder’?
Hahahahahaha!”
Thunderous laughter rang out from every direction, backed by internal energy so vast that no one dared guess at its limits.
The commoners who had never learned martial arts fell flat on their faces, crying out to the Jade Emperor, while the martial artists trembled in awe.
“Can you not hear me!”
“Ha, hahaha!
Ah, I’m laughing so hard my stomach’s going to split.”
“You insolent bastard!”
