Unlike the people staring around in shock, Jin Taekyung alone was gazing into the empty air.
There was even an enigmatic smile on his lips.

That bastard!
Ssssss!
The Sword Energy that had faltered for a moment surged again.

The laughter that had shaken heaven and earth abruptly stopped.

A triumphant smile spread across Song Il’s lips.

The fluster in the other man’s voice was proof.

chapters.title: Chapter 193
paragraphs: The Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure.
The moment that unfamiliar phrase sprang from the Fire King’s mouth, the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s eyes bulged as though they were about to tear apart.
“W-what do you mean?”
“You’re not even seventy, and your ears are already clogged? I’ll say it one more time, so listen carefully.”
Jeok Cheongang jerked his chin toward me, looking irritated.
“This old man entrusted our sect’s sacred treasure to that brat. Got it?”
What do you mean, got it?
I looked around in bewilderment. Everyone, including Jin Wikyung and Baek Museong, was staring back and forth between Jeok Cheongang and me in shock.
Amid all this chaos, the only person unaffected spoke up.
“Benefactor, what’s the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure? Show me too.”
I couldn’t answer Cheongpung’s question.
I don’t know either, you little shit.
The Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure? What was he talking about?
I swore I had never heard or seen such an item.
The only things I had received from Jeok Cheongang were the martial arts manual for the Flame Divine Palm and a sword...
Wait.
“Could it be?”
Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue at my questioning look.
“You’ve been carrying it on your back this whole time and still didn’t know? What a moron.”
I felt as if someone had struck me in the back of the head with a hammer.
I hurriedly untied the knot holding it firmly in place. When I unwound the layers of cloth, an old, crude scabbard appeared.
The Unnamed Sword.
The very thing Jopil had stolen from his Master, only for me to take it from him.
I gripped the hilt and drew.
Shing!
With a sound that made every hair on my body stand on end, the pure-white blade slid free.
It shone in the surrounding darkness like some holy sword from legend, drawing gasps from the crowd.
So this really is... the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure?
Until now, I had never once questioned it.
Why Jopil had stolen it from Jeok Cheongang. Why, unlike the Flame Divine Palm or the Blazing Flame Divine Pill, it bore the strange description Unnamed Sword.
I was staring blankly at the blade when—
“T-this is impossible!”
It was the Roaring Fury Swordsman. Unlike him, overwhelmed by extreme confusion and excitement, Jeok Cheongang’s expression was perfectly calm.
“What is?”
“T-that...”
“This old man entrusted the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure to that brat. Even with a head full of nothing but shit, surely you understand what that means.”
That snapped me back to my senses.

I had been so absorbed in the sword that I had momentarily forgotten what it meant for a sect’s sacred treasure to be entrusted to someone—especially the treasure of the Fire Gate Clan, whose lineage had been passed from one person to the next for hundreds of years.
At the same time, Cheongpung’s words from barely half a day ago flashed through my mind.
Aren’t you trying to take Benefactor as your Disciple?
At the time, I had dismissed it as ridiculous nonsense and laughed it off.
But now...
Fuck. I don’t know either.
As I swallowed dryly, the Roaring Fury Swordsman pointed a finger at me.
Before he could speak, however, Jeok Cheongang’s terrifying gaze locked him in place.
“This old man said he entrusted our sect’s sacred treasure to him.”
That was all.
But his opponent was none other than the Fire King.
The Roaring Fury Swordsman had no courage left to argue. He chewed on his lip, then suddenly glared at me.
“You bastard. You’re lucky.”
Why is this old man starting shit with me again?
Jeok Cheongang said nothing. Did he expect me to handle this much on my own?
I shrugged at the Roaring Fury Swordsman.
“You’ve got the wrong man. I’m actually really unlucky.”
If I were fucking lucky, would I have met a piece of shit like you?
The situation had been a hair’s breadth from exploding when Jeok Cheongang appeared, so I wasn’t sure whether to call it great misfortune or great fortune.
“Anyway, it was nice meeting you. Have a safe trip home.”
“You cunning bastard. Why don’t you try what you did earlier?”
“What I did earlier? Oh, you mean when I said it was fucking bullshit?”
Before the Roaring Fury Swordsman could respond, I bowed my head.
“I apologize for that. I’ve never been able to tolerate injustice. Please forgive a slip of the tongue from a junior far beneath you. Great. Hero.”
The Roaring Fury Swordsman trembled. Blood dripped from his tightly clenched fists.
Looking at him, I saw myself from only a few minutes earlier. The difference between us was that I had refused to submit to the Roaring Fury Swordsman, while he had submitted to the Fire King.
Those who rely on power kneel before greater power. Realizing that fundamental truth of the world again was satisfying, but not entirely.
If anything, it left me bitter.
This leaves a bad taste in my mouth.
If Jeok Cheongang hadn’t been here, the humiliation and fury that man now felt would have belonged to me and the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
If a few of the people here joined forces, defeating the Roaring Fury Swordsman himself wouldn’t be difficult. But the Zhongnan Sect stood behind him.
I hated admitting it, but the gap between us and them was vast. For now, it was a gap we could never bridge.
For now.
I had been a perpetual F-rank Hunter, yet I had still made it this far. No one knew what the future held.
Maybe one day, the Jin Family of Taiyuan would stand shoulder to shoulder with the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families.
Okay, am I getting a little ahead of myself?
It was like the head of some rural township running for President.
I let out a quiet laugh at the thought, and the Roaring Fury Swordsman ground his teeth.
“How dare you laugh at me?”
“My face just naturally looks like it’s smiling.”
“Shut that mouth of yours!”
The instant his furious shout rang out, Jeok Cheongang’s right foot shot forward like lightning and slammed into the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s shin.
A Supreme Peak master’s joint kick.
Thud!
“Guh!”
“You shut up. How dare a young bastard like you raise his voice in front of an elder?”
“What do you think you’re doing?”
“Look at this bastard. I tried to end things nicely, and now you’re begging for a beating?”
Wham!
“Urgh!”
Wow. That one really landed.
With an even duller impact than before, the Roaring Fury Swordsman clutched his shin and collapsed.
Even an Elder of the Great Zhongnan Sect is helpless against him.
The man was over sixty and held a lofty position, but his opponent was simply beyond comparison.
Age, martial arts, status—there was no catching up to the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, in any of them.
“Carrying on like that is a disease. You’ve done enough, so get the hell out of here.”
“...Very well.”
The Roaring Fury Swordsman glared resentfully at me as he rose, his body covered in dirt. Then Jeok Cheongang’s cold voice followed.
“And I will let today’s events pass, so you will never speak of this matter again. Do you understand?”
I really should start a fan club.

But with Jeok Cheongang mediating, things were different.
Though I’m not sure whether to call this mediation or a threat.
Resentment over what had happened today would remain, but at least he wouldn’t be able to bring official pressure against us.
Even if he did, having the Fire King as a sturdy shield took a great deal of the pressure off.
“Why aren’t you answering?”
The Roaring Fury Swordsman’s face twisted horribly now that his little scheme had been seen through. Jeok Cheongang, of course, couldn’t have cared less.
“Say it yourself. Right now.”
“...Understood. I swear it on my name.”
“What name do you have worth staking? Swear it in the name of the Zhongnan Sect.”
“Grrk... Understood.”
Only then did a satisfied smile appear on Jeok Cheongang’s lips. He chuckled and patted the Roaring Fury Swordsman on the shoulder.
“Where did a young bastard like you learn to grind his teeth like that? Maybe I should yank out every last one of them.”
“Hohoho! But this old man is getting on in years. I couldn’t possibly do such a thing in front of all these people. Hahahaha!”

Jeok Cheongang, who had been laughing like a fiend, turned to me.
“You’re not blameless either. Whatever the circumstances, how could you hurl such abuse at an elder so far above you in age? Are you out of your mind?”
I immediately bowed my head. Whatever else had happened, that much was true, and I also thought it was time to settle matters with the Roaring Fury Swordsman, an Elder of the Zhongnan Sect.
“I’m sorry.”
“Even if he ate his age through his asshole, he’s over sixty. It wouldn’t be strange for him to have a grandchild your age.”
“...Ah. Yes.”
“No matter how much of a bastard he is, he’s still your elder and a great Senior of Murim. No matter how filthy and unfair it feels, you must show him the proper respect from now on.”
“Great Hero Song, I sincerely apologize.”

Is this what comes with age?
Take a look at that verbal skill forged over a hundred years.

“I won’t see you out.”
“Let’s go!”

A thread of Sound Transmission filled with killing intent reached my ears.
— I don’t know what connection you have to that old man... but as long as I’m alive, I will definitely punish you and the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

“Yes? Where are you going?”

With that gruff reply, he disappeared with a bowlegged gait.

Whoooosh! Boom!
Dozens of streams of Sword Energy sliced through trees and shattered rocks. After venting his fury for quite some time, he finally turned it on the Three Hands of Zhongnan, Gong Ilhyuk included.
“You damned idiots...”
“E-Elder.”
“Do you know what kind of humiliation this old man suffered because of you?”
“I-I’m sorry. Please forgive your foolish Disciples.”
The Three Hands of Zhongnan froze.
Gong Ilhyuk was the most terrified of them all. If he hadn’t incited the Roaring Fury Swordsman to come to the Jin Family of Taiyuan, none of this would have happened.
“E-Elder, please calm down and hear me out.”
“I turned a blind eye a few times because you’re related by marriage to my Junior Brother, the Sect Leader, and now it seems you’ve forgotten your place.”
Clench!
The Roaring Fury Swordsman’s gaunt hand closed around Gong Ilhyuk’s throat.
“Guh... I-I’m the Sect Leader’s...”
“Do you think my Junior Brother, the Sect Leader, would so much as blink if this old man punished the likes of you? You worthless piece of trash.”
Gong Ilhyuk’s face went deathly pale.
Then—
Thump. Thump. Thud.
His body went limp, his head lolling to one side. The other two members of the Three Hands, who had been frozen with fear, also crumpled helplessly to the ground.
“W-why did these bastards suddenly...”
The Roaring Fury Swordsman, briefly confused, turned his head. He stared intently into the darkness before speaking.
“Do you still have business here?”
“Why else would I have come looking for you?”
Along with that calm voice, a small old man emerged.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
He clicked his tongue as he looked at the fallen Three Hands of Zhongnan.
“Tsk, tsk. Seems I ended up saving those bastards without meaning to. Maybe I should have come a little later.”
“Why have you come back?”
“It’s been so long. It seemed a shame to let you go just like that.”
The Fire King smiled faintly and added,
“There was also something I forgot.”
“Something you forgot? What do you mean...”
At that moment, Jeok Cheongang’s figure vanished like a phantom.
At the same time, Sword Energy erupted from the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s waist.
Sh-sh-sh-sh-shk!
A dense net of Sword Energy spread across a three-jang radius, slicing through bone and flesh the instant it touched them.

Crack!

“Gyaaah! You fucking old bastard!”
“When will you finally become a proper human being?”

Boom!
An unavoidable palm strike.

“Cough... F-Flame Divine Palm...”
“Raise your head and look at me.”
The old man’s voice was so cold that it made the title Fire King seem meaningless.
The Roaring Fury Swordsman barely managed to lift his head and found himself staring into a pair of eyes where blue ghostly flames flickered.
“F-Fire King.”
“That’s right. This old man is the Fire King.”

He was an opponent the Roaring Fury Swordsman could never hope to resist.
Deep despair settled over the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s face.
“Are you... are you planning to kill me?”
“If killing you could put an end to everything, this old man would have done it long ago.”
“Then...”
“Remember just one thing.”
The Fire King slowly parted his lips.
“You may kill Jin Taekyung. You may even wipe out the Jin Family of Taiyuan, and I will stand by and watch. But if that happens, I will go to the Zhongnan Sect.”

“I will smash the Zhongnan Sect’s signboard and burn down Mount Zhongnan. If you abandon your main sect and flee, I will chase you to the ends of the earth and kill every last one of you. I will do so until the day my breath stops.”

His voice was steeped in terror, and the Three Hands of Zhongnan could say nothing.

sentences.text: The Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure.
The moment that unfamiliar phrase sprang from the Fire King’s mouth, the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s eyes bulged as though they were about to tear apart.
“W-what do you mean?”
“You’re not even seventy, and your ears are already clogged?

Jeok Cheongang jerked his chin toward me, looking irritated.

Got it?”

I looked around in bewilderment.
Everyone, including Jin Wikyung and Baek Museong, was staring back and forth between Jeok Cheongang and me in shock.
Amid all this chaos, the only person unaffected spoke up.
“Benefactor, what’s the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure?
Show me too.”
I couldn’t answer Cheongpung’s question.
I don’t know either, you little shit.
The Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure?
What was he talking about?
I swore I had never heard or seen such an item.
The only things I had received from Jeok Cheongang were the martial arts manual for the Flame Divine Palm and a sword...
Wait.
“Could it be?”
Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue at my questioning look.
“You’ve been carrying it on your back this whole time and still didn’t know?
What a moron.”
I felt as if someone had struck me in the back of the head with a hammer.
I hurriedly untied the knot holding it firmly in place.
When I unwound the layers of cloth, an old, crude scabbard appeared.
The Unnamed Sword.
The very thing Jopil had stolen from his Master, only for me to take it from him.
I gripped the hilt and drew.
Shing!
With a sound that made every hair on my body stand on end, the pure-white blade slid free.
It shone in the surrounding darkness like some holy sword from legend, drawing gasps from the crowd.
So this really is... the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure?
Until now, I had never once questioned it.
Why Jopil had stolen it from Jeok Cheongang.
Why, unlike the Flame Divine Palm or the Blazing Flame Divine Pill, it bore the strange description Unnamed Sword.
I was staring blankly at the blade when—
“T-this is impossible!”
It was the Roaring Fury Swordsman.
Unlike him, overwhelmed by extreme confusion and excitement, Jeok Cheongang’s expression was perfectly calm.
“What is?”
“T-that...”
“This old man entrusted the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure to that brat.
Even with a head full of nothing but shit, surely you understand what that means.”
That snapped me back to my senses.

I had been so absorbed in the sword that I had momentarily forgotten what it meant for a sect’s sacred treasure to be entrusted to someone—especially the treasure of the Fire Gate Clan, whose lineage had been passed from one person to the next for hundreds of years.
At the same time, Cheongpung’s words from barely half a day ago flashed through my mind.
Aren’t you trying to take Benefactor as your Disciple?
At the time, I had dismissed it as ridiculous nonsense and laughed it off.
But now...
Fuck.
I don’t know either.
As I swallowed dryly, the Roaring Fury Swordsman pointed a finger at me.
Before he could speak, however, Jeok Cheongang’s terrifying gaze locked him in place.
“This old man said he entrusted our sect’s sacred treasure to him.”
That was all.
But his opponent was none other than the Fire King.
The Roaring Fury Swordsman had no courage left to argue.
He chewed on his lip, then suddenly glared at me.
“You bastard.
You’re lucky.”
Why is this old man starting shit with me again?
Jeok Cheongang said nothing.
Did he expect me to handle this much on my own?
I shrugged at the Roaring Fury Swordsman.
“You’ve got the wrong man.
I’m actually really unlucky.”
If I were fucking lucky, would I have met a piece of shit like you?
The situation had been a hair’s breadth from exploding when Jeok Cheongang appeared, so I wasn’t sure whether to call it great misfortune or great fortune.
“Anyway, it was nice meeting you.
Have a safe trip home.”
“You cunning bastard.
Why don’t you try what you did earlier?”
“What I did earlier?
Oh, you mean when I said it was fucking bullshit?”
Before the Roaring Fury Swordsman could respond, I bowed my head.
“I apologize for that.
I’ve never been able to tolerate injustice.
Please forgive a slip of the tongue from a junior far beneath you.
Great.
Hero.”
The Roaring Fury Swordsman trembled.
Blood dripped from his tightly clenched fists.
Looking at him, I saw myself from only a few minutes earlier.
The difference between us was that I had refused to submit to the Roaring Fury Swordsman, while he had submitted to the Fire King.
Those who rely on power kneel before greater power.
Realizing that fundamental truth of the world again was satisfying, but not entirely.
If anything, it left me bitter.
This leaves a bad taste in my mouth.
If Jeok Cheongang hadn’t been here, the humiliation and fury that man now felt would have belonged to me and the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
If a few of the people here joined forces, defeating the Roaring Fury Swordsman himself wouldn’t be difficult.
But the Zhongnan Sect stood behind him.
I hated admitting it, but the gap between us and them was vast.
For now, it was a gap we could never bridge.
For now.
I had been a perpetual F-rank Hunter, yet I had still made it this far.
No one knew what the future held.

Okay, am I getting a little ahead of myself?

chapters.title: Chapter 194
paragraphs: “Ahh, that hit the spot.”
Jeok Cheongang, who had said he was stepping away for a moment to relieve himself, returned fifteen minutes later. Something felt suspicious, and I narrowed my eyes.
“Why are you looking at me like that?”
“Did you really just go relieve yourself?”
“Do you need to smell me before you’ll believe me?”
“But it took you fifteen minutes. Could it be that—”
“This old man has virility to spare.”
How virile did you have to be to spend fifteen minutes pissing?
At that point, it wasn’t a stream. It was a fire hose.
When I stared at him in disbelief, Jeok Cheongang glared at me.
“What? You got a problem?”
“Of course not.”
A problem? Me?
Considering all the help he had given me today, I could bow to him a hundred times and it still wouldn’t be enough.
And then there’s the other thing...
I pushed aside the thought that had suddenly occurred to me.
The Fire Gate Clan’s divine artifact. The Fire King’s Disciple.
I also pretended not to hear the voices that had been whispering nonstop ever since.
Disciple? That’s ridiculous.
It was something I had never once considered before.
Why would a man accept as his new Disciple someone he had known for only a day—someone who had killed the Disciple he had cherished like a son?
Even if that Disciple had been a colossal son of a bitch.
As I was thinking about it, Jin Wikyung approached and respectfully cupped his hands toward Jeok Cheongang.
“I, Jin Wikyung, a junior of Murim, pay my respects to the Fire King Jeok Cheongang, whose fame resounds throughout the world.”
“Are you from the Jin Family?”
Jeok Cheongang looked Jin Wikyung up and down, then nodded as if he had figured it out.
“Then you’re this brat’s father?”
“What?”
“Raise your son properly. The boy’s young, but he’s already hotheaded and causing trouble. His manners are terrible, too.”
Jin Wikyung answered with the darkest expression I had ever seen on his face.
“He’s my younger brother.”
“Hm?”
“I’m Taekyung’s eldest brother.”
Jeok Cheongang’s face turned serious.
“Don’t joke around. I understand wanting to look young, but if you get too greedy, Heaven will punish you.”
“It’s the truth. I am Jin Wikyung, the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“How old are you, by any chance?”
“Now that the year has turned, I’m thirty-six.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered in disbelief.
“You look forty-six.”
Admittedly, his face was somewhat—quite a lot, actually—more weathered than his age suggested. Even I had mistaken him for my father at first.
At least his hair was still thick, but there was no cure for a face that had taken a 160-kilometer-per-hour fastball from time itself.
Seeing the sadness on Jin Wikyung’s face, Jeok Cheongang tried to comfort him.
“It’s all right. What matters in a man is his ability. You’ve got a pretty wife and adorable children, so what more do you need? Heh heh.”
“I’m still single.”
“...At thirty-six?”

In modern times, that would only be around the age when people started thinking seriously about marriage. But in Murim, where early marriage was common, thirty-six was old enough to have grandchildren.
The bachelor Jin Wikyung gave a terse answer.
“Yes.”
This silence ran a little long. The Fire King furrowed his brow, relaxed it, then flared his nostrils before finally heaving a deep sigh.
“Damn it. I could really use a drink.”
I let out a quiet laugh. It was a feast day, after all. What kind of feast would it be without alcohol? There was alcohol everywhere.
“Would you like a drink?”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened.
“You insolent brat. Are you making fun of this old man?”
“What?”
“Bring me the whole crock.”
A mood was like a spark. Once it went out, it was difficult to rekindle.
Yet even after the uninvited guests from the Zhongnan Sect had poured cold water over everything, the spark had not died.
No—in the presence of the Fire King, it blazed even more fiercely.
“Wooooo!”
“Drink! Come on, let’s drink!”
“I never thought I’d live to see the Fire King in person!”
“When the Fire King gets flustered, he goes Left Fire King, Right Fire King!”
I didn’t know who that was, but that bastard had nearly put out the spark just now.
At my signal, Hyuk Mujin, who had been standing by, quietly slipped away to hunt down the mood killer.
Meanwhile, Jeok Cheongang was receiving greetings from countless people.
“Great Hero Jeok! It’s the honor of a lifetime to meet you!”
“Please do us the honor of visiting our sect sometime...”
“Please grant us your guidance!”
It was truly a sea of people.
The name of the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was practically synonymous with living legend.
Moreover, his whereabouts had been unknown for decades, so most people had long accepted his death as fact.
And now the Fire King, whom everyone had thought dead, had appeared—not in the Central Plains or on Mount Jiuhua, but right here at the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Shanxi Province.
Of course everyone’s going to lose their minds.
Perhaps this was what it would be like if the legendary singer once called the Emperor of Pop came back from the dead.
Yet despite the enthusiasm of his local Shanxi fans, Michael Cheongang looked thoroughly displeased.
Jin Wikyung seemed to notice, too, and sent me a Sound Transmission.
—My youngest.

The only people who could hold a lengthy conversation with the eccentric Jeok Cheongang were Cheongpung and me. But there was no telling where Cheongpung’s thoughts might wander, so in the end, I had no choice but to act as the messenger.
“Are you uncomfortable?”
“Look at the state I’m in. Wouldn’t you be uncomfortable if you were me?”
Jeok Cheongang glared at the wine crock beside him. Quite a bit of time had passed, yet hardly any of it was gone.
It wasn’t that he disliked alcohol. He simply hadn’t had time to drink.
“Damn it. It shouldn’t be this hard to have a single drink.”
People kept asking him to accept them as Disciples, while Sect Leaders and merchants begged to host him as an honored guest.
One heavily pregnant woman had even asked if she could touch his nose. She wanted to receive the Fire King’s qi so she could give birth to a great person, or something like that.
Was he a dol hareubang or something?
It was enough to make even the onlookers snicker. How much worse must it have been for the man at the center of it all?
Frankly, given Jeok Cheongang’s personality, the fact that he had endured this much was impressive in itself.
“Why don’t we move somewhere I prepared in advance? It’s quiet there.”
“Ugh. Forget it.”
“You said you were uncomfortable.”
“I said forget it. Why are you so damn talkative?”
Even while grumbling, Jeok Cheongang stubbornly refused to leave. I tilted my head.
What’s going on?
We had known each other for only a short time, but I had gotten a fairly good sense of his personality.
It was obvious that he hated noisy places and found people’s attention bothersome. That was probably why he had spent his entire life on Mount Jiuhua.
Then why?
I watched Jeok Cheongang carefully.
In front of him, the owner of a merchant association with considerable influence in Shanxi Province was bowing and scraping.
“Great Hero Jeok! I’ve long heard of your reputation, which shakes the entire world. When I was young, I admired you so much...”
“Get to the point.”
“I have always admired you from the bottom of my heart, so I prepared a small token of my sincerity.”
“A small token?”
“Yes. It’s something I acquired recently, but I suppose every item has its destined owner.”
The merchant took a small wooden box from inside his robe and opened the lid. Inside was a ring set with clear jade.
“It is a Poison-Averting Ring.”
“A fairly valuable item. It must have been difficult to obtain.”
The merchant waved his hands dramatically.
“Having the honor of seeing your noble face, how could price possibly matter? It only cost a thousand silver nyang. Heh heh.”
A thousand silver nyang for a single ring. It ranked among the most expensive gifts the Jin Family of Taiyuan had received so far.
Jeok Cheongang, however, merely nodded without much interest.
“Well, since you’re giving it to me, I’ll accept it gratefully. Who are you, and where are you from?”
“I’m in charge of the Yangcheon Merchant Association...”
“Yangcheon? That’s near Hebei.”
The merchant had been interrupted before he could even give his name, but he bowed as if he had received a great honor.
“Yes. We are trying to begin trading with the Hebei Peng Family, but it has not been easy.”
That was the merchant’s real purpose.
It was why he had sought out Jeok Cheongang even after offering a token of sincerity that was anything but small.
In short, he wanted Jeok Cheongang to help him establish a business relationship with the Hebei Peng Family.
“The Peng Family, huh? Who’s the Family Head these days?”
“It is Great Hero Peng Cheolyeong, the Iron Blood Saber.”
“I’ve never heard of him. Is he the Thunderbolt Saber King’s son?”
“Yes, yes. The Thunderbolt Saber King retired from the front lines and passed the position of Family Head to him.”
“This old man once had a drink with the Thunderbolt Saber King in his younger days. All right, I understand.”
That was the end of the conversation. The merchant set down the wooden box and left with a grin stretching from ear to ear.
Beneath the box lay a stack of bank drafts that had not been there moments ago.
I took advantage of the merchant’s retreat to whisper to Jeok Cheongang.
“You know the Thunderbolt Saber King?”
As his title suggested, the Thunderbolt Saber King was one of the Ten Kings, a Supreme Peak master just like Jeok Cheongang.
Jeok Cheongang took a sip of wine before answering.
“I told you. We had a drink together.”
“Wow.”

He talked about the Thunderbolt Saber King as if he were some old neighborhood friend. Every time he did something like this, I was reminded all over again of just how extraordinary Jeok Cheongang was.
When I gaped at him in admiration, Jeok Cheongang puffed out his chest.
“I flattened that bastard’s nose years ago.”
“...What?”
“I was having a drink with the Sword Saint when he barged in without a word and picked a fight. We fought, and I taught him a lesson.”
What the hell was he talking about?
“Weren’t you two friends?”
“Me? With that guy?”
Jeok Cheongang furrowed his brow.
“Why would I associate with an uncultured bastard like him? We never saw each other again after that.”

“Later, some strange rumor even started going around. They said the Peng Family’s man and I had exchanged over a hundred moves before acknowledging each other and withdrawing. The bastards from the Hebei Peng Family must have pulled some kind of trick.”
I was dumbfounded, and so was everyone around me.
The story about the Thunderbolt Saber King was absurd enough, but if it was true, the merchant’s request had just gone up in smoke.
“Th-then the Yangcheon Merchant Association won’t be able to trade with the Hebei Peng Family, will they? Mentioning Great Hero Jeok’s name will only make things worse.”
Jeok Cheongang blinked.
“The Yangcheon Merchant Association? What’s that?”
“Ah, you mean that guy from earlier? Why should I care about him?”
“But you said you’d help him trade with the Hebei Peng Family.”
“He asked me to meet him, so I met him. It’s also true that I had a drink with the Thunderbolt Saber King. Was there even a shred of falsehood in anything this old man said?”
I wasn’t sure about that, but he certainly didn’t seem to possess even a shred of conscience.
His shamelessness was so impressive that I almost respected him for it.
Fire King, are you even human?

He had more than one or two victims. Before long, the people who had believed Jeok Cheongang’s empty promises and offered him a “small token of sincerity” would realize that it had all been complete bullshit and pound the ground in despair.
At this point, this is organized fraud.
Not that any of the victims would come forward.
No one was brave enough to approach the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, and demand their gifts back.
“We would be honored if you would visit our sect sometime...”
“Hmm. I’ll stop by one day.”
Meaning after he died and found himself wandering the netherworld.
“This is my small token of sincerity...”
“I’ll accept it.”
No. He really is just taking it.
As I watched the treasures, elixirs, and bank drafts pile up like a mountain, I finally realized something.
Was this why he stayed?
It was clearly a grand plan to make one big haul in his old age.
Eventually, after dealing with dozens of suckers, Jeok Cheongang spoke.
“Hmm. This is quite a haul. Aren’t there any more?”
Jin Wikyung answered with an exhausted expression.
“Yes. It seems that everyone who was likely to come has already arrived.”
“A shame. I could have squeezed more out of them.”
Just look at the greed on this old man.
Jeok Cheongang gazed at the spoils he had earned by drinking instead of sweating, then stretched his arms high above his head.
“Good grief, this is tiring.”
“Why are you looking at me like that?”
I subtly averted my gaze from Jeok Cheongang’s round eyes.
“It’s nothing. I was just admiring you.”
“From where I’m standing, that doesn’t look like admiration.”
“I’m serious. There’s nothing wrong with having a lot of wealth.”
“Is that so?”
Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh, then casually tossed out a remark.
“Then you take it.”
“What?”
“I’m saying I’ll give all of it to you.”
“All of that?”
“It’s completely useless to this old man, but it’s different for you. Scatter it in the street or do whatever you want with it. I won’t care, so take it.”
What was going on?
I stared at Jeok Cheongang in bewilderment.
Why all of a sudden?
He had already helped me immensely. Naturally, I couldn’t help wondering why he was showing such extraordinary favor to both me and the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Could it really be what I thought? Could he truly mean it?
I swallowed dryly and opened my mouth.
“Great Hero Jeok, by any chance...”
At that moment, Jeok Cheongang rose from his seat and spoke with a drunken expression.
“Ahh, I’m drunk. I’m going inside to rest. See you tomorrow.”
I watched Jeok Cheongang stagger away, then turned my gaze back to the wine crock.
The moon was reflected in the crock, which he had not even emptied a quarter of.

chapters.title: Chapter 195
paragraphs: Calling the banquet held on New Year’s Day a resounding success still felt like an understatement.

By embracing the Mount Heng Sword Sect, Jin Wikyung had made a bold move that won the loyalty of dozens of small and mid-sized sects. The Zhongnan Sect’s intervention and the appearance of Fire King Jeok Cheongang, whom everyone had believed dead, had left them all stunned.
And...
I was one of them.
I ate, drank, and moved from place to place. Wherever I went, people’s eyes followed my every move.
Half a day ago, those gazes had meant interest in the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
Not anymore.
The Fire King’s Disciple. The heir to the Fire Gate Clan.

I heard those words everywhere. People talked endlessly about what it meant that Jeok Cheongang, the current Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan, had entrusted me with the sect’s sacred treasure—and why he had protected the Jin Family of Taiyuan even at the cost of making an enemy of the Zhongnan Sect.
This already seems to be half-confirmed as fact.
To be honest, I didn’t understand Jeok Cheongang’s intentions either.
That was why I was here.
Everyone was still distracted, and I had managed to slip away unnoticed. This was my chance.
“Phew.”
I took a deep breath.
I stood before the pavilion where Jeok Cheongang had been given lodging. Someone must have ordered everyone to stay away, because there wasn’t so much as a mouse near the large building.
“Great Hero Jeok. Are you there?”
A reply came from beyond the door.
“I’m sleeping.”
“I came because there’s something I wanted to ask you.”
“I said I’m sleeping.”
“...How are you answering me if you’re asleep?”
“I’m sleepwalking.”
Was that an answer or a whinny?
It made no sense, but if the Fire King said that was how it was, then that was how it was. I pulled myself together and tried again.
“Um, there’s something I can’t stop wondering about.”
“Is this old man responsible for satisfying your curiosity?”
“No, but...”
“If you know that, go wash your feet and get some sleep.”
Talk about an impenetrable defense.
But I couldn’t back down now.
I began creeping ever so carefully toward the firmly closed door.
“Take one more step, and you won’t live to see tomorrow’s sunrise.”
“...How did you know?”
“To this old man, your presence is no different from a clap of thunder.”
“Come on. Couldn’t you let me in now? It’s still winter, and it’s rather chilly out here.”
“Would you like this old man to warm you up with the Flame Divine Palm?”
Just hearing that made my insides feel warm.
When I shut my mouth, silence fell. After a while, Jeok Cheongang broke it with a single sentence.
“I went to Jeongyang.”
“Ah.”
Even an insignificant bead could hold special meaning for someone. Jeongyang was like that.
Jeongyang was merely one of the dozens of counties and towns in Shanxi Province, but Jeok Cheongang had a reason to visit a mountain path there.
Jopil.
On the day snow came pouring from the sky, a man who had lived as Jangcheon died under the name Jopil.
“I stayed for a long time at the place you told me about. Some passersby saw an old man wandering around the foot of the mountain and asked why I was there.”
His subdued voice continued.
“I told them that a blood relative had died right there. That I had come because I wanted to recover whatever remained of his body.”
“That was when I realized something. Even if I had met that boy before you did, I could never have killed him. I would have let him go again, only to regret it afterward.”
It was difficult to imagine what expression Jeok Cheongang wore on the other side of the door.
After hesitating, I asked, “Did you find his body?”
“Nothing was left.”
Several months had already passed.

Jopil had spent his entire life walking a path of blood. The subordinates who might have recovered his body had died alongside him, so whatever remained had likely been buried by the capricious weather or devoured by hungry beasts.
“It is nothing but an old man’s selfish desire. Ugly and futile.”
Glug.
The sound of liquor filling a cup seemed unusually loud.
“I thought you said you were drunk earlier.”
“You crafty brat. Why ask when you already know?”
The candlelight flooding the pavilion outlined his silhouette.
Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh, then tossed back his drink.
“Ahh. Good.”
His voice sounded refreshed, as though that one cup had washed away his troubles.
It occurred to me that Jeok Cheongang had gone to the place where Jopil died to free himself from the regret and lingering attachment that still held him.
I deliberately brightened my voice.
“I was taught that good things should be shared.”
“I was taught from a young age that anyone who coveted what belonged to others should be burned with the Flame Divine Palm.”
“What terrifying person taught you that?”
“My Master.”
That was the Volcano Gate Clan for you. Ruthless.
They burned everyone with the Flame Divine Palm, no matter who it was.
I didn’t know the history of the Fire Gate Clan or the names of its past Sect Leaders, but looking at Jeok Cheongang, I could make a rough guess.
An old sect of thugs.
They said beans grew where beans were planted and red beans where red beans were planted.
Like master, like disciple. Jopil was the exception, of course.
Anyway, this isn’t what I came here to talk about.
I was watching the silhouette inside the pavilion while trying to read the situation when Jeok Cheongang suddenly spoke.
“From now on, the Fire Heaven Sword is yours.”
“Fire... what?”
“The Fire Heaven Sword. The sword I entrusted to you.”
I had just learned the Unnamed Sword’s true name, but that wasn’t the issue right now. I was so shocked that I stammered.
“B-but that’s the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure.”
“Ah, the sacred treasure.”
Jeok Cheongang tipped back yet another cup of liquor before continuing.
“That was a lie.”
“What?”

“It isn’t a sacred treasure. One of our sect’s Sect Leaders used it about a hundred years ago, and later generations inherited it from him. It’s old, but it was already renowned as a divine weapon back then, so it should still be useful.”
What the hell was he talking about?
I stood there with my mouth hanging open at this shocking truth I had never expected.
“That was all a lie? You’re messing with me, right?”
“Messing with you? Why would I bother with a little pup like you?”
“You said it in front of everyone! ‘I entrusted that boy with the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure!’”
“I did. Because we were in front of everyone.”
Jeok Cheongang continued in an indifferent voice.

“I had to go that far to get people talking. ‘That boy must have a deep connection to the Fire King. Perhaps he is the Fire King’s Disciple, since he was entrusted with the sacred treasure. If anyone touches the Jin Family of Taiyuan, that terrifying Fire King will step in.’ Rumors like that will spread far and wide.”

“Do you really think this old man would entrust our sect’s sacred treasure to a young brat like you? Our arts are passed down to only one successor per generation, so no one else knows the truth. If I say it is a sacred treasure, then it is a sacred treasure.”
“So keep the sword. That way, those Zhongnan bastards won’t dare make a move.”
Is this a dream?
As I stood there in shock, a System notification rang in my ears, delivering the final blow.
Ding.

The updated information was exactly as Jeok Cheongang had said.
It was the beloved sword of the tenth Sect Leader. No matter how hard I looked, there wasn’t a single mention of it being the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure.
Even the “true power” hidden within the sword could only be drawn out by someone who had inherited the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy.
In other words, other than the fact that it was made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, the sword was a corpse.
I really thought it was a sacred treasure. I spent so much time worrying about what I’d do if he said he wanted to make me his Disciple...
As I stared blankly at the holographic window, Jeok Cheongang added as though he were doing me a great favor.
“Think of it as a long-term loan. If this old man forgets about it and dies, you may keep it. Ah, and hand over the Flame Divine Palm manual right now.”
“Damn old man... Gasp.”
I had only meant to think it, but the words slipped out of my mouth.
I clapped my mouth shut in alarm. At that very moment, the firmly closed pavilion door burst outward.
Crack!
A pair of eyes blazing with fire glared at me.
“You little pup. What did you just say?”
“I-I-I misspoke.”
“Misspoke? Then this old man will make a little mistake with his hand, too.”
Whoosh!
A palm glowed red-hot, radiating overwhelming heat.
I spun around without looking back. In the same instant, I pulled the Flame Divine Palm manual from my Inventory and threw it.
“Gasp! The manual! The Flame Divine Palm manual!”
If he reached out now, the manual would turn to ash.
Jeok Cheongang, startled, hastily pulled back his fist. I took advantage of the opening and ran with all my might.
“I’m sorry! I’m really sorry! Please spare me!”
“You damned bastard! Stop right there!”
His roar thundered behind me.
Jeok Cheongang watched Jin Taekyung flee as though his tail were on fire and let out a quiet laugh.
The anger that had filled his face only moments ago had vanished without a trace.
“You little fool. No matter how far you run, you are still in the palm of this old man’s hand.”
He could catch Taekyung whenever he wished.
But Jeok Cheongang merely clasped his hands behind his back and turned away.
Jin Taekyung had killed Jangcheon, the Disciple Jeok Cheongang had cherished like a son.
Yet Jeok Cheongang bore him no hatred.
If anything, Taekyung was one of the people to whom Jeok Cheongang owed a sincere apology.
Everything had begun with the wrong choice Jeok Cheongang had made ten years ago.
“He called me a damn old man.”
Despite being cursed by a little pup, Jeok Cheongang wasn’t offended.
No, if anything, he felt relieved.
“That’s right. I am a damn old man. A senile old man, too. Heh heh. Heh heh heh.”
After his Master died, no one had dared criticize or curse Jeok Cheongang to his face.
He was the Fire King, a great martial artist who had single-handedly written himself into legend.
And yet, hearing that one remark from Jin Taekyung made him feel as though something that had been blocked for a long time had suddenly burst open.
“How refreshing. Truly refreshing.”
As people grow older, they become lonelier day by day. Not because they have no one with whom to share their warmth, but because they have no one to lean on.
Jeok Cheongang could serve as someone else’s support, but he had grown too old to lean on anyone himself.
“To be someone’s support...”
Jeok Cheongang was a rough, sharp thorn tree. He had lived a long life and crossed paths with countless people, but he had never allowed anyone to lean on him.
There had been only one exception.
Jangcheon.
“What about you? Did you ever feel, even for a moment, that this Master was a dependable support?”
As Jeok Cheongang thought of him, his gaze clouded over. But his chest no longer hurt as much as it once had, nor did his eyes grow hot.
The dead had already returned to a handful of earth.
At the place where his Disciple had fallen in a spray of blood, Jeok Cheongang had drunk a bottle of liquor and poured out an entire crockful.
He had wept freely, shedding the tears he had been unable to shed for the past ten years and letting the grief in his heart flow out with them.
“I’m sorry. Today will be the last time I think of you.”
If there was to be a next time, it would be in the next life.
He might still think of his dead Disciple from time to time. But those thoughts would no longer be regrets about the past.
They would be memories.
“This is enough. This is how it should be.”
After pacing around the courtyard for a long while, Jeok Cheongang suddenly stopped.
The image of Jangcheon that had been flickering before his eyes vanished, replaced by someone he had never expected to think of.
Why him?
Open, well-defined features. A confident smile that somehow managed to be irritating.
The way he cautiously gauged Jeok Cheongang’s mood, yet still took every cutting remark in stride.
Did I get angry without realizing it because he called me a damn old man?
Jeok Cheongang was frowning when—
Sizzle.
The sound of something burning filled the air, followed by a thin trail of smoke.
Realizing where the sound had come from, his eyes flew open.
“Th-the manual!”
The cover of the Flame Divine Palm manual was already half-burned.
Jeok Cheongang let out a furious roar.
“Jin Taekyung! You damned bastard!”

chapters.title: Chapter 196
paragraphs: “W-What happened here?”
A middle-aged merchant—the third generation of his family to run a textile shop in the center of Taiyuan, Shanxi Province—stood with his mouth hanging open.
“T-The silk...”

The bolts of silk that should have filled the shop had vanished without a trace. Various furnishings lay broken, and the proprietor, who should have been busy welcoming customers, was sprawled on the floor, drenched in sweat.
“Thieves! We’ve been robbed!”
The merchant’s vision went dark, and the strength drained from his legs.
He already operated several textile shops, but this was his largest store in Taiyuan, the flagship passed down from his grandfather and a symbol of his family’s legacy.
And someone had robbed it. Every last bolt of silk was gone!
I knew things had been going too well.
For the past four months, the merchant had traveled from province to province, inspecting his stores and closing a major contract.
Yet after all that time away, he had returned to find his flagship store in ruins. Unable to withstand the shock, he sank to the floor.
That was when—
“Tsk, tsk. This place is a mess, too. Honestly, martial artists...”
A middle-aged man had been clicking his tongue as he looked around the shop. When he noticed the merchant sitting on the floor, his eyes widened.
“Oh? When did you get back? I heard you had a big deal to close this time. You’re back earlier than I expected.”
But the merchant was already half out of his mind. He heard none of it except for one word that kept echoing in his ears.
“H-Here, too?”
“Huh?”
The merchant seized the middle-aged man by the collar and shook him violently.
“You said this place was a mess, too!”
“Y-Yeah, I did. But could you let go of my collar while we talk?”
“What happened? Mounted bandits? Thieves? Did a war break out and the authorities requisition everything? And what do martial artists have to do with it?”
“I said let go of me first!”
The middle-aged man finally tore himself free, then inspected his clothes with a grumble.
“Damn it. These are new.”
“If you don’t tell me right now, you’ll die and I’ll die with you.”
“All right, all right.”
“So what happened?”
The middle-aged man’s answer was simple.
“It all sold.”
“...What?”
“We weren’t robbed. It’s gone because everything sold out, my friend. So get a grip.”
The merchant stared blankly at him before finally managing to speak.
“Have you lost your mind? How does that make any sense? Who would buy more than a thousand bolts of silk?”
“Government officials, merchants, martial artists. Every last one of them came rushing in and cleaned the place out.”
“Why do you think? They all want to make an impression on the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan? The one I know?”
“Of course the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Who else? The Mount Heng Sword Sect?”
“Why are you bringing up the Mount Heng Sword Sect? Did something happen?”
“...You really haven’t heard?”
“I just got back after four months. I came straight here without even seeing my wife!”
“W-Wait! Please calm down. I’ll tell you everything.”
Not wanting his new clothes ruined, the middle-aged man gave him a quick summary of everything that had happened over the past few months.
Fifteen minutes later, after hearing the whole story from the war between the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect to the present day, the merchant muttered in a daze.
“All that happened?”
“I told you. Shanxi is in an uproar over the Fire King’s arrival. And it isn’t just Shanxi Province. The city is crawling with outsiders who came to meet him.”
The middle-aged man continued, his face flushed with excitement.
“I’ve been doing business in Taiyuan for over twenty years, but I’ve never seen a boom like this.”
“For all that, the streets didn’t look any busier than usual...”
“Do you think people would still be loitering in the streets when the sun has been high in the sky for hours? They packed up their things ages ago and ran to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Good heavens. It’s hard to believe.”
“I even cleared out my entire stock.”
“A-Already?”
“Why are you so surprised? Mine was nothing compared to yours. And I heard this next part from someone reliable...”
The middle-aged man lowered his voice to a conspiratorial whisper.
“The gathering was originally supposed to last three days, but it may be extended. The rumors are spreading fast, and the real big shots are beginning to move.”
“The real big shots?”

“The Murim’s prestigious major sects have started mobilizing. Seok Family Manor, said to be foremost in the merchant world, and His Highness Prince Shangshan, the City Lord, both went to the Jin Family of Taiyuan early this morning.”
“Even His Highness Prince Shangshan?”
“That’s why those officials who usually drag their feet are scrambling now. A member of the imperial family is coming. They have to show their faces and offer some token of sincerity, don’t they?”
“Of course. And they’d better arrive before everyone else.”
“What kind of place is Taiyuan? It may not rival the Central Plains, but it’s unquestionably the greatest commercial city in Shanxi Province. You can buy almost anything here.”
“Local procurement. I see.”
“And the more people come looking for something, the scarcer it’ll become. Prices will rise, too.”
The merchant’s eyes flashed. He had realized this would not end in a day or two.
His earlier confusion and despair had already vanished. Now mountains of silver nyang danced before his eyes.
This is an opportunity.
He could establish connections with people from the Murim, the merchant world, and the government. If he played his cards right, he might land an enormous deal.
After finishing his calculations, the merchant turned to the middle-aged man.
“I filled several warehouses just in case. I’ll let you have part of the stock at a reasonable price, so tell me straight. Who should I approach?”
Having just found his chance to make a killing, the middle-aged man grinned broadly.
“First, remember three people: the Fire King, Jin Wikyung, the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, and the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung.”
“...The Fire King and the Lesser Family Head, I understand. But why that good-for-nothing Jin Taekyung?”
“Hey now. He’s the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi these days. Before long, he’ll become an incredible master capable of influencing the entire world.”
“What are you talking about?”
“Tsk, tsk. How can a merchant be this completely out of touch?”
The middle-aged man savored the merchant’s bewildered expression. At last, he revealed the fact he had saved for this very moment.
“The Fire King has taken the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi as his Disciple.”
“What? Is that true?”

“I told you it was. Two days ago, an Elder of the Zhongnan Sect who didn’t know about it caused a scene, then went back after getting thoroughly beaten. He even entrusted the Sleeping Dragon with his sect’s divine artifact.”
“Th-Then...”
“It wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say that half the people heading to the Jin Family of Taiyuan right now are going to make an impression on the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, not the Fire King.”
The Fire King was unquestionably one of the greatest Supreme Peak masters in the world, but he was old—very old—and had no real power base to speak of.
Jin Taekyung was different.
He was only twenty-one, possessed outstanding martial talent, and had the powerful Jin Family of Taiyuan behind him.
No, wait.
It was the other way around now. The Jin Family of Taiyuan had gained an extraordinary source of support.
They now had the renowned Fire King, as well as Jin Taekyung, who might one day grow into a Supreme Peak master comparable to his teacher.
The merchant’s face flushed with excitement.
“It’s like giving wings to a tiger.”
“So we have to climb aboard before it flies away.”
This was an opportunity worth staking his entire fortune on.
Having finally made up his mind, the merchant spoke.
“I need to meet the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi at once.”
“That’s the right answer. But right now, you’d have trouble meeting him even if you showed up carrying a fortune in gold.”
“Why?”
“I don’t know. According to the Jin Family of Taiyuan, he suddenly entered closed-door cultivation.”
“Closed-door cultivation? That thing martial artists do? Why now, of all times?”
The middle-aged man let out a deep sigh.
“Exactly. I hear the Heaven Shaking Sword has also shut himself away, muttering about enlightenment or something.”
“Good heavens. Isn’t there any way around this?”
“I don’t know. Things have grown too big too quickly. The Jin Family of Taiyuan is practically bursting at the seams, so it seems they’ve started being selective about whom they let in.”
“Didn’t you say you were fairly close with one of the Jin Family’s Squad Leaders? I heard you slipped him a few bribes, too.”
“He’s dead. He died in the last war.”
“Oh dear.”
With powerful figures from every sphere already on the move, it would not be easy for ordinary merchants like them to get involved.
The two men put their heads together and racked their brains until the merchant suddenly spoke.
“I do know someone over there.”
“Oh! Someone you know well?”
“I know him very well. He’s a boy my wife gave birth to.”
The middle-aged man frowned at the merchant’s answer.
They had known each other long enough to be intimately familiar with each other’s family affairs.
“You mean your eldest son?”
“That’s right. That unfilial bastard hasn’t shown his face once in years. Judging by the fact that my wife hasn’t said anything, he must still be alive somehow...”
The middle-aged man nodded, plainly disappointed.
“Well, this is as good a time as any to contact him. Who knows? He might be making a name for himself as a proper martial artist.”
The merchant let out a derisive laugh.
“The son of a textile merchant, a martial artist? As if. He’s probably waiting hand and foot on someone.”
“If that someone happens to be the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, wouldn’t that be a good thing?”
“Impossible. If it turns out to be true, then from this day forward, my family name won’t be Hyuk. It’ll be Gyeon—gyeon as in dog!”
“Achoo!”
With the sound of a sneeze, my back suddenly felt cool.
Lying facedown on the bed with my upper body bare, I spoke quietly.
“Mujin, do you want to die?”
Hyuk Mujin, who had been wiping my back with a cloth soaked in cold water, answered.
“Oh, I’m sorry. My nose suddenly started itching.”
“Do that one more time. It’ll be the last sneeze of your life.”
“...Yes, sir.”
“Good. Keep wiping.”
Swish. Swish.
Every pass of the cold cloth across my back sent a dull throb of pain through me.
That was only natural. My entire upper body was covered in black-and-blue bruises.
Damn it. It’s been two days, and I’m still like this.
This had never happened before. Until now, I had recovered from most injuries in no time with sleep mode and by circulating my qi.
Every time I leveled up, I had poured points into Muscles and Bones and Sinews and Meridians. Ordinary blows shouldn’t have been able to damage me.
But...
That’s a Supreme Peak master for you.
None of it meant a damn thing against the Fire King.

The next thing I knew, I was waking up in unimaginable pain in the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s infirmary. After they moved me back to my pavilion, I spent the next two days confined to bed.
“That damn old man.”
“Gasp!”
Hyuk Mujin sucked in a sharp breath.
“Captain, have you lost your mind? He’ll really kill you.”
“Let him. What are people outside saying?”
“Officially, we’ve settled on calling it closed-door cultivation. It would be rather bad if rumors spread that the Fire King beat up the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.”
“What about my eldest brother?”
“Would the Lesser Family Head have any other choice? After hearing the initial report, he got extremely angry for a moment and went to see Great Hero Jeok, but...”
“He went to see him?”
“He saw the burned Flame Divine Palm manual, apologized several times, and left.”
“What did he have to apologize for? Did I set it on fire? Jeok Cheongang did that himself. And did he really have to beat me this badly over a little singeing?”
“I caught a glimpse of it, and it was more than a little singed. Almost half the cover with the title on it had burned away. The Flame Divine Palm had become just the Flame.”
“Anyway, I think we should stop talking about this. I don’t know about you, Captain, but I’m terrified. If Great Hero Jeok suddenly walks in, we’re both dead, aren’t we?”
“That’s true.”
Hyuk Mujin’s foresight was remarkable. Barely a moment after he finished speaking, the door flew open.
“Gasp!”
“Guh!”
“...You bastards. What was that reaction?”
“N-Nothing.”
The small, elderly man, Jeok Cheongang, narrowed his eyes and looked at us. Then he snorted.
“Fine. Since this old man didn’t hear anything, I’ll let it slide this once.”
Surprisingly willing to let the matter go, he jerked his chin at Hyuk Mujin.
“You, get out. You’re in the way.”
I didn’t know what he intended to do, but I had a feeling I would be better off with Hyuk Mujin in the room.
Hyuk Mujin responded to my desperate gaze—the gaze of a man who wanted to live a long life.
“Yes, sir. I’ll take my leave. Good luck!”
“Very well.”
...Son of a bitch.
Hyuk Mujin scurried out, leaving me consumed by anxiety.
There was something ominous about the way Jeok Cheongang was staring at my bare upper body.
“Wh-What is it?”
Surely not.
But Jeok Cheongang’s eyes gleamed with an inexplicable heat.
“Take off your pants.”
“Gasp. Wh-What do you mean?”
“Strip. Don’t leave a single scrap of cloth on your body.”
I desperately covered my chest. My voice trembled with shame and fear.
“B-But there’s someone I like.”
“...What does that have to do with anything?”
What a Western mindset!
I was screwed. There was no way out.
As I froze in place, Jeok Cheongang shouted:
“Ah, I’m going to cleanse your sinews and wash your marrow, so take off your clothes and lie down already!”
You should’ve said so from the start.

sentences.text: “W-What happened here?”
A middle-aged merchant—the third generation of his family to run a textile shop in the center of Taiyuan, Shanxi Province—stood with his mouth hanging open.
“T-The silk...”
The bolts of silk that should have filled the shop had vanished without a trace.

“Thieves!

The merchant’s vision went dark, and the strength drained from his legs.

For the past four months, the merchant had traveled from province to province, inspecting his stores and closing a major contract.

A middle-aged man had been clicking his tongue as he looked around the shop.

“Oh?

I heard you had a big deal to close this time.
You’re back earlier than I expected.”
But the merchant was already half out of his mind.
He heard none of it except for one word that kept echoing in his ears.
“H-Here, too?”
“Huh?”
The merchant seized the middle-aged man by the collar and shook him violently.
“You said this place was a mess, too!”
“Y-Yeah, I did.
But could you let go of my collar while we talk?”
“What happened?
Mounted bandits?
Thieves?
Did a war break out and the authorities requisition everything?
And what do martial artists have to do with it?”
“I said let go of me first!”
The middle-aged man finally tore himself free, then inspected his clothes with a grumble.
“Damn it.
These are new.”
“If you don’t tell me right now, you’ll die and I’ll die with you.”
“All right, all right.”
“So what happened?”
The middle-aged man’s answer was simple.
“It all sold.”
“...What?”
“We weren’t robbed.
It’s gone because everything sold out, my friend.
So get a grip.”
The merchant stared blankly at him before finally managing to speak.
“Have you lost your mind?
How does that make any sense?
Who would buy more than a thousand bolts of silk?”
“Government officials, merchants, martial artists.
Every last one of them came rushing in and cleaned the place out.”
“Why do you think?
They all want to make an impression on the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan?
The one I know?”
“Of course the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Who else?
The Mount Heng Sword Sect?”
“Why are you bringing up the Mount Heng Sword Sect?
Did something happen?”
“...You really haven’t heard?”
“I just got back after four months.
I came straight here without even seeing my wife!”
“W-Wait!
Please calm down.
I’ll tell you everything.”
Not wanting his new clothes ruined, the middle-aged man gave him a quick summary of everything that had happened over the past few months.
Fifteen minutes later, after hearing the whole story from the war between the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect to the present day, the merchant muttered in a daze.
“All that happened?”
“I told you.
Shanxi is in an uproar over the Fire King’s arrival.
And it isn’t just Shanxi Province.
The city is crawling with outsiders who came to meet him.”
The middle-aged man continued, his face flushed with excitement.
“I’ve been doing business in Taiyuan for over twenty years, but I’ve never seen a boom like this.”
“For all that, the streets didn’t look any busier than usual...”
“Do you think people would still be loitering in the streets when the sun has been high in the sky for hours?
They packed up their things ages ago and ran to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Good heavens.
It’s hard to believe.”
“I even cleared out my entire stock.”
“A-Already?”
“Why are you so surprised?
Mine was nothing compared to yours.
And I heard this next part from someone reliable...”
The middle-aged man lowered his voice to a conspiratorial whisper.
“The gathering was originally supposed to last three days, but it may be extended.
The rumors are spreading fast, and the real big shots are beginning to move.”
“The real big shots?”
“The Murim’s prestigious major sects have started mobilizing.
Seok Family Manor, said to be foremost in the merchant world, and His Highness Prince Shangshan, the City Lord, both went to the Jin Family of Taiyuan early this morning.”
“Even His Highness Prince Shangshan?”
“That’s why those officials who usually drag their feet are scrambling now.
A member of the imperial family is coming.
They have to show their faces and offer some token of sincerity, don’t they?”
“Of course.

“What kind of place is Taiyuan?

You can buy almost anything here.”
“Local procurement.
I see.”

Prices will rise, too.”
The merchant’s eyes flashed.

This is an opportunity.
He could establish connections with people from the Murim, the merchant world, and the government.
