chapters.title: Chapter 197
paragraphs: Cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow.
The name literally meant shedding one’s hair and cleansing one’s bones and muscles. It was a procedure performed only by prestigious sects with long histories.
By using internal energy to reshape the bones and muscles and purge the waste accumulated within the body, it transformed a person’s constitution into one better suited to learning martial arts.
Cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow had to be performed steadily over multiple sessions. The problem was that both the requirements and the process were extremely demanding.
After hearing Jeok Cheongang’s explanation, I asked, “Is it really that difficult?”
Jeok Cheongang nodded.
“You’re artificially changing the body you were born with. Did you really think that would be easy and convenient? If it were, there wouldn’t be anyone in this world who wasn’t a master.”
Fair enough.
An ordinary person had to grit their teeth and work out for months just to carve out a six-pack.
Changing your very bones, muscles, and constitution would obviously be far more difficult.
“Cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow requires three things.”
He said it was incredibly difficult, but there are only three?
That thought vanished the instant Jeok Cheongang continued.
“First, an internal-energy master with at least two jiazi of internal energy.”
“...Yikes.”
The difficulty level was brutal right from the start.
Two jiazi amounted to a full one hundred and twenty years. How many people under heaven could possibly possess that much internal energy?
There had to be very few, and Jeok Cheongang, standing right in front of me, was one of them.
He raised two wrinkled fingers.
“Second, money.”
“Why do you need money?”

“Because you need elixirs for the recipient to absorb. The practitioner must guide and circulate the qi filling the recipient’s body. Every sect has its own method, but it is no exaggeration to say the process costs a thousand gold.”
“It would be difficult for anyone outside the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families.”
“Not merely difficult. Extremely difficult. Was it Baek Museong? That Huashan-something fellow seems to have undergone it.”
This was an investment in the most literal sense. Sects selected promising young talents with bright futures and performed the procedure on them.
If Baek Museong was a blue-chip stock, Huashan would certainly have considered him worth the investment.
“Then what about Cheongpung?”
“Do you think the Sword Saint would have simply stood by and watched? He must have refined the boy’s body bit by bit from a very young age.”
Damn it. I’m the only one who missed out.

I had thought the Jin Family of Taiyuan was at least a silver spoon by Murim standards. But compared to the diamond-spoon babies who underwent the procedure as casually as double-eyelid surgery, we were nothing.
“What’s the third and final requirement?”
“Endurance.”
“Huh?”

“Cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow changes the bones, muscles, and constitution one was born with. The bones and muscles twist and settle back into place, and the process inevitably causes tremendous pain.”
“How painful are we talking?”
Jeok Cheongang answered without hesitation.
“Painful enough to kill you.”
“...Painful enough to kill me?”
“People really do die.”
“Gasp.”
“In the Sichuan Tang Clan, they fill a jar with more than a thousand different venomous creatures, and then...”
The longer Jeok Cheongang talked, the more my stomach seemed to shrivel. I swallowed hard.
“T-That’s only how the Sichuan Tang Clan does it, right?”
“Of course. Our sect has its own secret method.”
“You don’t stack up more than a thousand logs, make me climb on top, and set them on fire or something...?”
“I guess not. Sorry.”
“What the hell do you think our sect is?”
Jeok Cheongang glared at me with round, bulging eyes before shaking his head.

“Cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow cannot be prepared overnight. Today, this old man will merely straighten your bones and muscles with internal energy. Whether you stuff yourself with elixirs afterward is your concern.”
“Ah. Okay.”
Come to think of it, Jeok Cheongang had arrived empty-handed. If he had intended to perform the procedure properly, he would have brought elixirs and all the other necessities.
“Should I take off my clothes, then?”
“Ask me that one more time, and I’ll strip off your skin as well.”
I stripped off every piece of clothing I was wearing at the speed of light.
Jeok Cheongang’s gaze roamed over my completely naked body, and a strange look entered his eyes.
“This is...”
“Yes?”
“Ah, never mind. It’s nothing.”
What was that? Why did the atmosphere suddenly become so ominous?
As I wondered what was wrong with the old man, I realized something and grinned.
“Come on, now. We’re all friends here. Why are you acting like that?”

“Honestly, this size is absolutely not normal. I was shocked myself when I first saw it. Do you know the Amazon? There’s something called a black anaconda there. It’s just—whoosh. Really enormous. Whew.”
“I understand that you’re surprised, but you still can’t touch it. Got it?”
Whoosh—whack!
With a short rush of wind, a tightly clenched fist slammed into my temple.
Ding.
System Status effect: Unconsciousness has been removed.
I came to with the System notification, stared up at the familiar ceiling, and muttered, “Damn, you could’ve just said you wouldn’t touch it. Why hit me?”
Did he really want to touch it that badly? Was he upset because I turned him down so firmly?
I rubbed my throbbing temple and sat up. Several System messages I had not yet read were floating before my eyes.
“Huh? The cleansing is already over?”
I looked around, but Jeok Cheongang was nowhere to be seen.
Apparently, he had finished the procedure in a flash and left while I was unconscious. At least, that was what the messages suggested.

System Cleansing the Sinews and Washing the Marrow has been successfully completed. Muscles and Bones and Sinews and Meridians have increased by 5 each. Strength, Stamina, and Agility have increased by 1 each.
A weak murmur of admiration escaped me.
It was definitely good. I was undoubtedly better off than before. This was the sort of improvement that would normally require one level-up and plenty of steady training.
But...
“Is that really all?”
Form is temporary, but class is forever.
It might have been a makeshift procedure performed without proper preparation, but cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow was still cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow.
I had expected some incredible effect. Instead, I was so disappointed that I was practically bewildered.
“What the hell?”
In Murim novels, these things were practically cheat codes.
Bone Transformation and cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow were practically basic requirements for any protagonist.
Even a sickly weakling could undergo both, turn into a thug, and run rampant through the Murim.
So what was wrong with me?
“Did he just half-ass it?”
Just then, the door opened, and Hyuk Mujin cautiously poked his head inside.
“May I come in—gasp.”
As I pulled on the clothes scattered across the floor, I said:
“Just so we’re clear, if you get any strange ideas, I’ll crack your skull. And by skull, I mean your head.”
“Then why are you naked?”
“The old man worked on my body.”
“Your body? With you completely naked?”
“...You’re making that sound weird.”
Hyuk Mujin flinched and hurriedly waved his hands.
“N-No. That’s not what I meant. Great Hero Jeok looked so strange when I ran into him earlier that I came to see if something had happened.”
“His expression was strange?”
“His face was completely rigid. He looked like he’d been startled by something, or maybe like he was angry.”
“Really?”
“Yes. He looked so frightening that I couldn’t even bring myself to speak to him.”
“Why?”
“How would I know?”
I tilted my head. Had something happened all of a sudden?
Jeok Cheongang walked along, lost in thought.
People who recognized him bowed from every direction, but his mind was filled with only one person.
Jin Taekyung.
His assessment of the young man had changed several times over the past few days.

First, he had been an interesting fellow. Then he had become an infuriating bastard who burned his sect’s martial arts manual. And today, the moment Jeok Cheongang saw Jin Taekyung’s naked body for the first time, a new thought had occurred to him.
What a strange fellow.
Even at a glance, Jin Taekyung possessed exceptional bones and muscles. They were so remarkable that it seemed a waste for him to languish in a backwater like this.
But once Jeok Cheongang saw the body hidden beneath his clothes with his own eyes, he realized it was beyond anything he had expected.
How can a body be this perfectly balanced?
The human body grew over time, but balance was another matter.
One’s everyday posture and even the smallest habits in how one dressed, ate, and lived could throw that balance off.
A swordsman who wielded his sword with his right hand would naturally have more muscle and greater strength in his right arm.
It was as natural as water flowing downhill.
But Jin Taekyung was different.
...What is this fellow?
The length and angle of every bone. The shape and form of every muscle.
Every part of him was in perfect balance.
It was as though some unknown, omnipotent being had drawn one half of Jin Taekyung on a blank sheet of paper, folded it over, and then opened it again.
Could he have undergone cleansing steadily since childhood? No. Even cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow couldn’t achieve this.

In the past, Jeok Cheongang had agonized and conducted extensive research for Jangcheon, whose bones and muscles were lacking. Eventually, he had found the best possible method and performed the procedure on him.
The treatment had succeeded, but that experience had taught Jeok Cheongang one thing.
Even cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow has its limits.
The phrase perfect balance did not belong anywhere near the human body.
Even if one spent ten thousand gold instead of a thousand, minute flaws would remain. But Jin Taekyung was different.
Jeok Cheongang had kneaded and touched his unconscious body from head to toe.

He had felt the tough, elastic skin and the strength filling both the surface and the depths of his body. He had circulated his internal energy through Taekyung’s body and confirmed the broad, sturdy Sinews and Meridians within.
And then he had been stunned.
How can a body like this exist?
It was perfect. He almost wondered if this was what the legendary Bone Transformation he had only heard about would look like.
Jeok Cheongang had met several Supreme Peak masters in his life, including the peerless master Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint.
But he could say this without hesitation: Of all the bones and muscles he had ever seen, Jin Taekyung’s were the finest under heaven.
Could it be...
Jeok Cheongang had been staring blankly for some time when a thought flashed through his mind, making his entire body tremble.
The Murim held sayings passed down like legends from the distant past.
The Heavenly Martial Physique, said to be born through a caprice of Heaven once every several hundred—or perhaps even a thousand—years, was one of them.
The Heavenly Martial Physique? I must be out of my mind.
But the longer Jeok Cheongang examined Jin Taekyung’s body, the deeper his suspicions grew and the more tangled his thoughts became.
It would not have been an exaggeration to say that there was nothing about that body in need of correction.
Once he finished the mere formality that could barely be called cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow, his concerns only deepened.
If that boy truly possesses the Heavenly Martial Physique, what would happen if he learned martial arts even greater than those he knows now and absorbed elixirs?
His thoughts continued chasing one another long after he left the pavilion.
At last, the desire coiled deep within Jeok Cheongang’s heart raised its head.
“What if... I taught that boy?”
The mutter escaped him before he realized it, and Jeok Cheongang was startled.
A Disciple?
His only Disciple had betrayed their sect and was no longer of this world.
The wound from that betrayal had not even healed, and he was already thinking of taking another Disciple.
Worse, he was over a hundred years old, and the infirmities of old age had already begun to cloud his mind.
Even if I don’t do it, Mae Jonghak could find a worthy talent and carry on our sect’s legacy.
He had told no one, but Jeok Cheongang had planned to seek out the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak as soon as he left the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Mae Jonghak possessed martial arts counted among the strongest under heaven and had no selfish ambitions. Jeok Cheongang planned to entrust the Fire Gate Clan’s succession to him.
And now, at this late hour, I entertain such an absurd thought? Jeok Cheongang, you stupid bastard. You fool.
Jeok Cheongang was sighing heavily and staring up at the sky when a voice reached him.
“Great Hero Jeok. Is something troubling you?”
The polite voice belonged to Jin Wikyung, a giant of a man.
Jeok Cheongang, who had been thinking of Jin Taekyung at that very moment, flinched.
“Uh, yes?”

It was already the third day since Jeok Cheongang had begun staying at the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Seeing him act so unlike himself, Jin Wikyung asked cautiously, “Is there perhaps something making you uncomfortable...?”
“N-No. It’s nothing.”
“Then I’m relieved.”
Jeok Cheongang waved a hand while gazing toward a distant mountain.
“There’s nothing wrong with this old man. I’m perfectly fine, so go about your business.”
“Um, did you perhaps have something you wished to say to me?”
“I said I don’t.”
“Are you certain?”
“I said I am! Stop worrying about it and be on your way.”
“...Great Hero Jeok?”
“Ah, what is it?”
When Jeok Cheongang finally exploded, Jin Wikyung hesitated before speaking.
“Great Hero Jeok, you are standing directly in front of my office.”
“Would you care to come in for a cup of tea and a conversation?”
After a brief silence, Jeok Cheongang cleared his throat.
“Ahem. Give me liquor instead of tea.”
Whatever his mind might have said, Jeok Cheongang’s feet had been honest.

sentences.text: Cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow.
The name literally meant shedding one’s hair and cleansing one’s bones and muscles.
It was a procedure performed only by prestigious sects with long histories.
By using internal energy to reshape the bones and muscles and purge the waste accumulated within the body, it transformed a person’s constitution into one better suited to learning martial arts.
Cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow had to be performed steadily over multiple sessions.
The problem was that both the requirements and the process were extremely demanding.
After hearing Jeok Cheongang’s explanation, I asked, “Is it really that difficult?”
Jeok Cheongang nodded.
“You’re artificially changing the body you were born with.
Did you really think that would be easy and convenient?
If it were, there wouldn’t be anyone in this world who wasn’t a master.”
Fair enough.
An ordinary person had to grit their teeth and work out for months just to carve out a six-pack.
Changing your very bones, muscles, and constitution would obviously be far more difficult.
“Cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow requires three things.”
He said it was incredibly difficult, but there are only three?
That thought vanished the instant Jeok Cheongang continued.
“First, an internal-energy master with at least two jiazi of internal energy.”
“...Yikes.”
The difficulty level was brutal right from the start.
Two jiazi amounted to a full one hundred and twenty years.
How many people under heaven could possibly possess that much internal energy?
There had to be very few, and Jeok Cheongang, standing right in front of me, was one of them.
He raised two wrinkled fingers.
“Second, money.”
“Why do you need money?”
“Because you need elixirs for the recipient to absorb.
The practitioner must guide and circulate the qi filling the recipient’s body.
Every sect has its own method, but it is no exaggeration to say the process costs a thousand gold.”
“It would be difficult for anyone outside the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families.”
“Not merely difficult.
Extremely difficult.
Was it Baek Museong?
That Huashan-something fellow seems to have undergone it.”
This was an investment in the most literal sense.
Sects selected promising young talents with bright futures and performed the procedure on them.
If Baek Museong was a blue-chip stock, Huashan would certainly have considered him worth the investment.
“Then what about Cheongpung?”
“Do you think the Sword Saint would have simply stood by and watched?
He must have refined the boy’s body bit by bit from a very young age.”
Damn it.
I’m the only one who missed out.
I had thought the Jin Family of Taiyuan was at least a silver spoon by Murim standards.
But compared to the diamond-spoon babies who underwent the procedure as casually as double-eyelid surgery, we were nothing.
“What’s the third and final requirement?”
“Endurance.”
“Huh?”
“Cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow changes the bones, muscles, and constitution one was born with.
The bones and muscles twist and settle back into place, and the process inevitably causes tremendous pain.”
“How painful are we talking?”
Jeok Cheongang answered without hesitation.
“Painful enough to kill you.”
“...Painful enough to kill me?”
“People really do die.”
“Gasp.”
“In the Sichuan Tang Clan, they fill a jar with more than a thousand different venomous creatures, and then...”
The longer Jeok Cheongang talked, the more my stomach seemed to shrivel.
I swallowed hard.
“T-That’s only how the Sichuan Tang Clan does it, right?”
“Of course.
Our sect has its own secret method.”
“You don’t stack up more than a thousand logs, make me climb on top, and set them on fire or something...?”
“I guess not.
Sorry.”
“What the hell do you think our sect is?”
Jeok Cheongang glared at me with round, bulging eyes before shaking his head.
“Cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow cannot be prepared overnight.
Today, this old man will merely straighten your bones and muscles with internal energy.
Whether you stuff yourself with elixirs afterward is your concern.”
“Ah.
Okay.”
Come to think of it, Jeok Cheongang had arrived empty-handed.
If he had intended to perform the procedure properly, he would have brought elixirs and all the other necessities.
“Should I take off my clothes, then?”
“Ask me that one more time, and I’ll strip off your skin as well.”
I stripped off every piece of clothing I was wearing at the speed of light.
Jeok Cheongang’s gaze roamed over my completely naked body, and a strange look entered his eyes.
“This is...”
“Yes?”
“Ah, never mind.
It’s nothing.”
What was that?
Why did the atmosphere suddenly become so ominous?
As I wondered what was wrong with the old man, I realized something and grinned.
“Come on, now.
We’re all friends here.
Why are you acting like that?”
“Honestly, this size is absolutely not normal.
I was shocked myself when I first saw it.
Do you know the Amazon?
There’s something called a black anaconda there.
It’s just—whoosh.
Really enormous.
Whew.”
“I understand that you’re surprised, but you still can’t touch it.
Got it?”
Whoosh—whack!
With a short rush of wind, a tightly clenched fist slammed into my temple.
Ding.
System Status effect: Unconsciousness has been removed.
I came to with the System notification, stared up at the familiar ceiling, and muttered, “Damn, you could’ve just said you wouldn’t touch it.
Why hit me?”
Did he really want to touch it that badly?
Was he upset because I turned him down so firmly?
I rubbed my throbbing temple and sat up.
Several System messages I had not yet read were floating before my eyes.
“Huh?
The cleansing is already over?”
I looked around, but Jeok Cheongang was nowhere to be seen.
Apparently, he had finished the procedure in a flash and left while I was unconscious.
At least, that was what the messages suggested.
System Cleansing the Sinews and Washing the Marrow has been successfully completed.
Muscles and Bones and Sinews and Meridians have increased by 5 each.
Strength, Stamina, and Agility have increased by 1 each.
A weak murmur of admiration escaped me.
It was definitely good.
I was undoubtedly better off than before.
This was the sort of improvement that would normally require one level-up and plenty of steady training.
But...
“Is that really all?”
Form is temporary, but class is forever.
It might have been a makeshift procedure performed without proper preparation, but cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow was still cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow.
I had expected some incredible effect.
Instead, I was so disappointed that I was practically bewildered.
“What the hell?”
In Murim novels, these things were practically cheat codes.
Bone Transformation and cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow were practically basic requirements for any protagonist.
Even a sickly weakling could undergo both, turn into a thug, and run rampant through the Murim.
So what was wrong with me?
“Did he just half-ass it?”
Just then, the door opened, and Hyuk Mujin cautiously poked his head inside.
“May I come in—gasp.”
As I pulled on the clothes scattered across the floor, I said:
“Just so we’re clear, if you get any strange ideas, I’ll crack your skull.
And by skull, I mean your head.”
“Then why are you naked?”
“The old man worked on my body.”

With you completely naked?”

chapters.title: Chapter 198
paragraphs: An awkward atmosphere hung inside the office.
Jin Wikyung and Jeok Cheongang stole glances at each other as they sipped their tea and liquor.
Great Hero Jeok came here in person. What could this be about?
Has he been possessed by a ghost? Of all places, why did he have to come here?
But even silence had its limits.
After draining several cups in quick succession, Jeok Cheongang finally spoke. Since he was already here, he might as well clear up his questions about Jin Taekyung before leaving.
“I just came from seeing that fellow.”
“Ah, you mean Taekyung.”
Jin Wikyung immediately understood and carefully gauged his mood.
He had already heard the whole story. Jeok Cheongang had helped the Jin Family of Taiyuan because of the emotional debt he carried toward his dead Disciple.
But he was worried that the anger caused by the martial arts manual incident two days ago might not have faded yet.
“Is this perhaps about the martial arts manual?”
“This old man has already erased that from his memory. No matter how precious a manual may be, people are more important. Don’t you agree?”
“What? What’s with that expression?”
“Oh, it’s nothing.”
After beating him into a pulp, he’s talking about how people are more important now?
Jin Wikyung swallowed the words hovering at the tip of his tongue.
“In any case, I thought I might have hit him a little too hard, so I went to treat his body by cleansing his sinews and washing his marrow.”
“C-Cleansing his sinews and washing his marrow? You mean the cleansing I know of?”
Jeok Cheongang nodded at Jin Wikyung’s wide-eyed stare.
“Is there another kind?”
“N-No. I was simply too surprised.”
“Surprised?”
“How could I not be? Someone as extraordinary as Great Hero Jeok performed cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow on my younger brother. This is a tremendous blessing for our family.”
As Jeok Cheongang gazed at Jin Wikyung’s delighted face, he realized something.
“I see. I suppose you might not have known.”
“Pardon?”

You can only see as much as you know. Even Jeok Cheongang, one of the most renowned Supreme Peak masters in the world, had never imagined that Jin Taekyung’s bones and muscles could be that exceptional.
How, then, could Jin Wikyung have known?
Perhaps it was fortunate that I found out now.
Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue softly before speaking.
“The effect of cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow was minimal.”
“What do you mean? How could cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow have no effect?”
“That isn’t what I mean. It would be more accurate to say that Jin Taekyung doesn’t need it. It’s too early to make a definite judgment, but...”
Jeok Cheongang added in a low voice:
“I suspect he may possess the Heavenly Martial Physique.”
For a brief moment, shock flashed across Jin Wikyung’s face.
But a moment later, he nodded calmly, prompting Jeok Cheongang to ask, “Did you already know?”
“I didn’t. Things simply make sense now.”
“Understand what?”
“Taekyung’s astonishingly rapid progress in martial arts. If he possesses the Heavenly Martial Physique—if it truly is that Heavenly Martial Physique—then everything can be explained.”
“Astonishingly rapid?”
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his brow and continued.

“That fellow has certainly accomplished a great deal for someone his age, but not enough to call it astonishing. If anything, compared to the legends of the Heavenly Martial Physique, his progress seems lacking.”
His voice rang with certainty.
And for good reason. In his youth, Jeok Cheongang had been every bit as accomplished as Jin Taekyung—more so, if anything.
The Supreme Peak masters who now dominated the Murim had displayed their genius from childhood. Compared to them, Jin Taekyung’s current realm was nothing out of the ordinary.

“The Heavenly Martial Physique is exactly what its name implies: bones and muscles bestowed by Heaven. Once every several hundred years—perhaps even once every thousand—a whim of Heaven causes a god to dwell within the body of a mere human. But the boy is only...”
“At the beginning of the Peak realm.”
“Exactly. The world is vast, and talented people are everywhere. Cheongpung alone is proof of that.”
Everything Jeok Cheongang said was true.
The people sheltered by the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were not the only ones who existed.
There were undoubtedly young talents whose names had not yet reached the Central Plains, as well as people who had buried themselves in the countryside while training in martial arts.
If someone scoured every corner of the world, they would likely uncover several Supreme Peak masters approaching the level of the One God, the Three Saints, and the Ten Kings.

“That is why this old man cannot be certain. The boy is undoubtedly exceptional, but... this is not enough. Perhaps the legend is only a legend. Or perhaps his martial talent is inferior to his physique.”
“How interesting.”
“What is?”
“I thought the exact opposite.”
Jin Wikyung smiled faintly at Jeok Cheongang’s questioning expression.
“My younger brother’s martial talent is the greatest under heaven. No, it would not be an exaggeration to call it the greatest in all history.”
“W-What did you say?”
Jeok Cheongang barely managed to suppress the curse rising in his throat.
Even he, a living legend in all but name, did not dare claim to be the greatest beneath Heaven. And this man was calling his younger brother the greatest in all history?
Still, the confidence and conviction in Jin Wikyung’s voice compelled Jeok Cheongang to ask, “What makes you think that?”
Jin Wikyung silently held up three fingers.
“Three months.”
“That is how long Taekyung has been learning martial arts.”
“It’s also how long it took a Third Rate wastrel who frequented pleasure houses to become a Peak master.”
For an instant, Jeok Cheongang’s vision went white. Lightning flashed through his mind, and his heart pounded violently.
Three months to rise from Third Rate to Peak.
Absurd.
Utterly impossible.
But...
It is possible. If he possesses the Heavenly Martial Physique.
Jeok Cheongang was a Supreme Peak master.
Yet even he—powerful enough to kill a thousand people alone—was merely an old man whose body was withering beneath the force of time.
The Heavenly Martial Physique, however, was a being born of Heaven’s choice and whim.
How could a mere human presume to guess Heaven’s intentions?
Is this what lies beyond Heaven?
Jeok Cheongang slowly rose and approached the window. When he pushed open the tightly shut panes, an endless blue sky stretched before him.
As the cold wind rushed inside, he suddenly wondered:
Why had Heaven chosen Jin Taekyung?
And why had it brought the two of them together?
Who are you? Is there really someone there?
No answer came.
Jeok Cheongang stared in silence at the wisps of cloud drifting through the clear, tranquil sky. After a long while, he finally spoke.
“I think we need more liquor. What do you say?”
Jin Wikyung answered with a smile.
“Excellent. I was getting tired of tea myself.”
The next day, Hyuk Mujin came to me with unexpected news.
“They want you to attend the banquet.”
“Me?”
“Who else would they mean?”
I answered without a moment’s thought.
“I don’t want to.”
Sitting around taking up space would only make me restless.
People would gawk at me like I was a monkey in a zoo, and my biggest fan, Prince Shangshan, would probably ask for an autograph.
I would much rather hole up in my pavilion, circulate my qi, and think about martial arts. That sounded a hundred times better.
“Just tell them I can’t go.”
“It was the Lesser Family Head’s order.”
“Even better. My brother won’t make a fuss, will he? Besides, wouldn’t people find it strange if my closed-door training ended after only three days?”
“Just tell them you gained some insight. If you say that’s what happened, who’s going to argue?”
He had a point.
I narrowed my eyes at Hyuk Mujin, who seemed to be getting more logical by the day.
“I’m still a patient.”
“You’ve already recovered. When I saw you this morning, nearly all your bruises were gone.”
Just as Hyuk Mujin said, most of the bruises that had covered my upper body had already disappeared.
Judging by that, cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow really had done something.
Of course, gaining more stats would have been far more useful from my perspective.
Hyuk Mujin scratched the back of his head as though this was giving him a headache.
“Why don’t you just go?”
“Tell them I’m still in pain. Who’s going to argue when I’m the one saying it hurts?”
“Great Hero Jeok.”
“Huh?”
“He said you should have recovered by now, so don’t even think about pulling anything. Otherwise, he’ll come here and drag you out himself.”
“Damn it. That old man is still at the banquet hall?”
“He drank with the Lesser Family Head all night, then showed up a moment ago completely wasted.”
I let out a deep sigh.
Jeok Cheongang had said he would remain at the Jin Family of Taiyuan only until this gathering ended.

According to the original schedule, he should have left yesterday. But more and more people had arrived, including several heavyweights, and the gathering had been extended. Naturally, so had his stay.
“Shit. Fine, let’s go. Let’s go.”
“Good choice. If you refused, I was going to be the one who died.”
I followed Hyuk Mujin, who was grinning foolishly, toward the banquet hall.
It was still crowded enough to make a marketplace look deserted, but perhaps because they had finally begun controlling admission, there were far fewer people than on the first day.
“We had no choice. More people kept coming every day. With that many eating and drinking from morning to night, the expense was one thing, but we simply ran out of room.”
“You should’ve turned more of them away. It still looks packed.”
“If we turn away any more, people will curse us. Everyone left is at least the head of a small martial arts academy.”
“So you’re preserving their pride?”

They’re even managing grassroots opinion?

“Yes.”

The Shandong Yue Family?

“Oh.”

“Pardon?”
You can only see as much as you know.
Even Jeok Cheongang, one of the most renowned Supreme Peak masters in the world, had never imagined that Jin Taekyung’s bones and muscles could be that exceptional.

His voice rang with certainty.

In his youth, Jeok Cheongang had been every bit as accomplished as Jin Taekyung—more so, if anything.
The Supreme Peak masters who now dominated the Murim had displayed their genius from childhood.

Everything Jeok Cheongang said was true.
The people sheltered by the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were not the only ones who existed.

Three months to rise from Third Rate to Peak.
Absurd.

It is possible.

paragraphs: “Take your hand off what’s mine.”
At Jeok Cheongang’s words, the air grew heavy. A moment later, Ak Bulgun slowly removed his hand from my shoulder.
“Great Hero Jeok, I merely—”
A sharp voice cut him off.
“Who taught you to go around touching what belongs to someone else?”
Belongs to someone else?
Treating a person like an object was bad enough, but why was I the object in question? It wasn’t as if I were Jeok Cheongang’s Disciple or grandson.
I had been seriously considering Heaven’s Gate Temple as a promising option. I hadn’t expected him to come along and dump chili powder all over it.
What’s gotten into this old man?
Unlike me, Ak Bulgun remained calm.
“I apologize for offending you, but I merely wished to offer Young Hero Jin an opportunity.”
“An opportunity, my ass. You can dress it up however you like, but you’re still trying to spirit him away behind my back. Did you think this old man wouldn’t see through your filthy intentions?”
“Spirit him away? Certainly not.”
“Then what?”
Even under Jeok Cheongang’s fierce glare, Ak Bulgun continued without wavering.

“I came here not as a member of the Shandong Yue Family, but as an Instructor of Heaven’s Gate Temple. In conveying the wishes of the academy’s higher-ups, how could I allow personal feelings to influence me?”
“So those so-called higher-ups gave you those orders without even knowing what sort of relationship this boy and I have?”
“If I may be so bold, could I ask what exactly that relationship is?”
“What?”
Jeok Cheongang glared at Ak Bulgun, his face stiff.
“This old man entrusted that boy with our sect’s divine artifact.”
“I am well aware. I have heard all about it.”
“Then you must know what that means. Are you mocking this old man?”
“How could I dare harbor such an intention? It is simply...”
Ak Bulgun looked back and forth between Jeok Cheongang and me.
“You do not appear to be master and Disciple at all, so I cautiously conveyed the offer.”
We both flinched.
I didn’t know how warm and affectionate the average master-Disciple relationship was supposed to be, but a Disciple probably didn’t address his master as “Great Hero.”
And Jeok Cheongang’s treatment of me hadn’t exactly suggested otherwise.
Damn, he’s sharp.
We had been far too careless. When I glanced aside, I saw Jeok Cheongang chewing on his lip. Ak Bulgun’s gaze deepened at our reaction.
“Young Hero Jin also hesitated when he heard the offer. Had he truly been your Disciple, he would have rejected it without a second thought.”
Everything he said was true, so there was no way to argue.
Why would the Disciple of the Fire King—one of the handful of Supreme Peak masters beneath Heaven—ever enter Heaven’s Gate Temple?
It would be like ignoring a lump of gold to pick up a pretty pebble.
Looks like the truth is coming out anyway.
The three of us weren’t the only ones at the table of honor. Everyone else was looking away, but their ears were pricked.
Once word of today’s conversation spread, my sturdy shield of being the Fire King’s Disciple would vanish. And after that?
Every bastard under the sun will come crawling out.
Until recently, the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been little more than a fleshless skeleton.
But things were different now. We had put on a fair amount of meat, and the wolves would soon start prowling around us.
They would watch one another until the time was right, then pounce.
The Fire King was already over a hundred years old. His death would be the starting signal for those bastards to sink their teeth into us.
And the Zhongnan Sect will obviously be first in line.
I had to grow stronger before then. To do that, Heaven’s Gate Temple was a hundred times better than the empty title of the Fire King’s Disciple, an illusion that would disappear before long.
All right. I’m going to Heaven’s Gate Temple.
Having made up my mind, I turned to Ak Bulgun.
“Actually, I...”

I have no relationship with Great Hero Jeok. We just happen to share a slight connection. I desperately want to enter Heaven’s Gate Temple, so would someone like me qualify for a scholarship? Or perhaps the Shanxi Province rural special-admissions track?
All the words poised to pour out of me like a waterfall were dammed by a single sentence from Jeok Cheongang.
“He is my Disciple.”
“Great Hero Jeok and I have no relationship at all... Pardon?”
What the hell was he talking about?
I whipped around to stare at Jeok Cheongang.
What did he just say?
Ignoring my bewildered gaze, Jeok Cheongang continued as calmly as ever.
“I intended to keep him hidden until he was ready, but it seems that will no longer be possible. Everyone appears to have plenty to say on the matter, so I might as well settle it once and for all.”
“No, wait—”
The voice I had barely managed to force out was swallowed by Jeok Cheongang’s shout, charged with internal energy.
“I proclaim this to the Murim beneath Heaven!”
A terrifying wave of energy shook the ground and pressed down upon the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s estate. Every other sound vanished, and hundreds of pairs of eyes turned toward us.
It had happened before I even had a chance to stop it.
Veins bulged on Jeok Cheongang’s liver-spotted neck.
“I, Jeok Cheongang, eighteenth Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan, hereby accept Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan as my Disciple and name him heir to our sect’s orthodox lineage!”
A brief silence followed. Then those who understood his words erupted into thunderous exclamations and cheers.
It was the moment when everyone’s lingering suspicions became fact—and one old man’s perfect bullshit became reality.
And I...

“I have committed a grave discourtesy. I apologize to you as well, Young Hero Jin. I will convey the news properly to Heaven’s Gate Temple. No one would dare interfere with Great Hero Jeok’s Disciple, so even the Temple Master will surely abandon the idea.”
Every path into Heaven’s Gate Temple—or to becoming anyone else’s Disciple—had just been slammed shut.
Ak Bulgun chuckled at my devastated expression.
“Look at you. Why the long face on such a joyous day?”
Because I knew perfectly well that there wasn’t even a one-percent chance Jeok Cheongang would actually take me as his Disciple.
I had gained absolutely nothing, yet my entire future had been blocked off. My clenched fists trembled.
Damn old man.
I could already see my bleak future unfolding before me. He wouldn’t teach me a single martial art, but he would torment me, beat me up, and send me on every petty errand imaginable.
At best, I would become an Inventory for storing his belongings.
I’m screwed.
Congratulations poured in from all around the table of honor, but I didn’t hear a word of them.
Jeok Cheongang spread his arms wide, wearing a thoroughly fake smile.
“Come. Let your master give you a hug, my dear Dis. ci. ple.”
“Oh, look at this rascal. Shy because everyone’s watching, are you? Ho ho ho.”
Laughing heartily, Jeok Cheongang secretly crooked a finger.
At that moment, an irresistible force unlike anything I had ever felt seized my ankle.
One step. Two steps.
My feet began moving toward him against my will.
...Seizing an Object Through Empty Space?
Was this really happening?
The tiny old man finally pulled me into a tight embrace and moved his lips.
“Hey. Smile.”
“Put your arm around my shoulders. Get those corners of your mouth up to your ears.”
Fuck it. Whatever happens, happens.
With our arms around each other’s shoulders, we beamed like a loving master and Disciple. Instead of camera flashes, thunderous cheers rained down around us.
And that day, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao received a hyper-rare, limited-edition autograph:
Fire King & Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
Late that night, darkness lay thick over the estate.
Standing behind a secluded wall on the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s grounds, I finally spoke.
“Why are you doing this to me?”
The small silhouette gave no answer.
“Protecting the Jin Family of Taiyuan? Fine. I’m grateful for that. I’m grateful that you drove those Zhongnan bastards away, too. But!”
“You’re blocking my future! This has gotten so out of hand that I can’t enter Heaven’s Gate Temple anymore, and I can’t take anyone else as my master either! Do you know why?”
Jeok Cheongang, who had been silently drinking straight from a liquor bottle, answered.
“Because no matter how foolhardy someone might be, they would never approach this old man’s Disciple.”
“Yes, exactly! Great Hero Jeok, you’ve completely blocked every path ahead of me!”
“I see.”
“That’s not the point! You’re more than smart enough to know better, so why are you doing this? I have to make a living, too!”
Glug. Glug. Buuurp.
Jeok Cheongang drained the bottle to the last drop, let out a tremendous belch, and stared at me.
“You know better yourself, so why are you acting this way?”
“Pardon?”
The liquor bottle in his hand suddenly struck the wall.
Whoosh—BOOM!
Ordinarily, the bottle should have shattered with a sharp crash.
Instead, the wall exploded with a deafening roar.
The round liquor bottle was already rippling with tangible internal energy.
“Have you forgotten who this old man is? Why, you little—are you trying to die?”
“Gasp!”
“Even a full prostration wouldn’t be enough, and you dare raise your voice? You wet-behind-the-ears little bastard, I ought to...”
“W-Wait! Calm down! Please calm down!”
“Calm down? Would you like to lie nice and still in a grave until your bones turn to dust?”
I had briefly forgotten.
The old man in front of me might have looked like the head honcho at a nursing home, but he was a notorious thug in the Murim.
Then I remembered that what he extorted from people wasn’t money, but their lives. The blood in my veins seemed to turn cold.
I hit the wrong nerve.
The night was already dark, but now my vision went black as well.
Then Jeok Cheongang, who had been staring at me, abruptly spoke.
“Do you hate it that much?”
“Pardon?”
“Is taking this old man as your master truly so unbearable?”
What the hell was he talking about when he had no intention of making me his Disciple?
I had plenty to say, but keeping my mouth shut was clearly the better way to extend my lifespan.
Unfortunately, Jeok Cheongang had no intention of letting me stand there in silence, avoiding his gaze.
“Tell me.”
“W-What?”
“Judging by your expression, you have plenty on your mind. Tell me what you’re thinking.”
“I don’t have anything like that.”
“You don’t?”
BOOM!
What remained of the wall crumbled into dust and scattered.
I stared blankly at it, then hurriedly opened my mouth.
“Now that I think about it, I do.”
“You just said you didn’t.”
“I didn’t, but it turns out I did.”
“Fine. Tell me.”
I had blurted it out in a panic, but now that I actually had to speak, my heart shriveled. I fidgeted with my fingers and cleared my throat.
“Well, the thing is, it’s a little...”
“Speak frankly. I want your honest answer, without a single lie.”
“Really?”
“No matter what you say, I won’t touch a hair on your head. I swear it by the gods of Heaven and Earth.”
“You don’t believe in the gods of Heaven and Earth.”
I must have hit the nail on the head.
Jeok Cheongang glared at me with a terrifying expression before finally forcing the words out.
“I started believing today. I don’t know what damned bastard is up there in the heavens, but I saw something with my own eyes, so now I have no choice.”
I had no idea what he had seen, but he sounded sincere.
Only after making him stake the honor of his sect and his own name as well did I cautiously begin.
“First of all, your personality is a little...”
“A little?”
“Nasty, isn’t it?”
“Actually, it’s very nasty.”
He looked incredulous, but the liquor bottle in his hand remained still. Emboldened, I continued.
“And you’ve got a nasty habit of hitting people.”
“You remember what happened a few days ago, right? I know I was partly at fault, but does it make any sense to launch a Flame Divine Palm at me without warning?”
“...Go on.”

“I’m not opposed to a reasonable amount of discipline, but that means a flick on the forehead or a few strokes with a switch. What kind of Disciple wants to train while getting hit with the Flame Divine Palm? That isn’t the rod of love. It’s the rod of death. The rod of death. One wrong hit and I’ll die, I’m telling you.”
Once I started, everything came pouring out as if a dam had burst.
Beginning with my first encounter with Jeok Cheongang, I aired every complaint I had accumulated since. The longer I went on, the stiffer his face became.
Still, this feels pretty damn good.
A quarter of an hour later, when my stormy confession finally ended, Jeok Cheongang asked in a subdued voice,
“Are you finished?”
“There’s still one important thing left.”
“That... phew.”
Contrary to my expectations, the liquor bottle didn’t come flying. Jeok Cheongang merely heaved several deep sighs.
“Say it.”
“My biggest complaint is what I mentioned earlier. Why did you publicly declare me your Disciple when you aren’t even going to teach me martial arts?”
“Is that the problem?”
“Of course it is! If I’m going to teach myself, entering Heaven’s Gate Temple would be a hundred times better.”
“Learning from this old man is a thousand times better than entering Heaven’s Gate Temple.”
Did he think I didn’t know that?
I stared at him in disbelief. Then a thought suddenly flashed through my mind.
“Great Hero Jeok, could it be...?”
Jeok Cheongang replied curtly.
“What?”
“Never mind. I just had a ridiculous thought.”
“Say it.”
“No, there’s no point. Let’s just forget it.”
“Say it if you don’t want to die.”
Oh. Then I had to say it. If I didn’t want to die, I absolutely had to say it.
I gave a dry laugh.
“I wondered if perhaps you were actually thinking of taking me as a real Disciple, or something like that. It’s nonsense, so you don’t have to answer. Hahaha.”
“Hahaha.”
“Great Hero Jeok?”
Jeok Cheongang remained silent for a long while despite my calling him, then tossed out a single sentence.
“Would that be a problem?”
“What would?”
“I asked if there was something wrong with this old man being your master.”
“...Pardon?”
What the hell was with this atmosphere?

sentences.text: “Take your hand off what’s mine.”
At Jeok Cheongang’s words, the air grew heavy.
A moment later, Ak Bulgun slowly removed his hand from my shoulder.
“Great Hero Jeok, I merely—”
A sharp voice cut him off.
“Who taught you to go around touching what belongs to someone else?”
Belongs to someone else?
Treating a person like an object was bad enough, but why was I the object in question?
It wasn’t as if I were Jeok Cheongang’s Disciple or grandson.
I had been seriously considering Heaven’s Gate Temple as a promising option.
I hadn’t expected him to come along and dump chili powder all over it.
What’s gotten into this old man?
Unlike me, Ak Bulgun remained calm.
“I apologize for offending you, but I merely wished to offer Young Hero Jin an opportunity.”
“An opportunity, my ass.
You can dress it up however you like, but you’re still trying to spirit him away behind my back.
Did you think this old man wouldn’t see through your filthy intentions?”
“Spirit him away?
Certainly not.”
“Then what?”
Even under Jeok Cheongang’s fierce glare, Ak Bulgun continued without wavering.
“I came here not as a member of the Shandong Yue Family, but as an Instructor of Heaven’s Gate Temple.
In conveying the wishes of the academy’s higher-ups, how could I allow personal feelings to influence me?”
“So those so-called higher-ups gave you those orders without even knowing what sort of relationship this boy and I have?”
“If I may be so bold, could I ask what exactly that relationship is?”
“What?”
Jeok Cheongang glared at Ak Bulgun, his face stiff.
“This old man entrusted that boy with our sect’s divine artifact.”
“I am well aware.
I have heard all about it.”
“Then you must know what that means.
Are you mocking this old man?”
“How could I dare harbor such an intention?
It is simply...”
Ak Bulgun looked back and forth between Jeok Cheongang and me.
“You do not appear to be master and Disciple at all, so I cautiously conveyed the offer.”
We both flinched.
I didn’t know how warm and affectionate the average master-Disciple relationship was supposed to be, but a Disciple probably didn’t address his master as “Great Hero.”
And Jeok Cheongang’s treatment of me hadn’t exactly suggested otherwise.
Damn, he’s sharp.
We had been far too careless.
When I glanced aside, I saw Jeok Cheongang chewing on his lip.
Ak Bulgun’s gaze deepened at our reaction.
“Young Hero Jin also hesitated when he heard the offer.
Had he truly been your Disciple, he would have rejected it without a second thought.”
Everything he said was true, so there was no way to argue.
Why would the Disciple of the Fire King—one of the handful of Supreme Peak masters beneath Heaven—ever enter Heaven’s Gate Temple?
It would be like ignoring a lump of gold to pick up a pretty pebble.
Looks like the truth is coming out anyway.
The three of us weren’t the only ones at the table of honor.
Everyone else was looking away, but their ears were pricked.
Once word of today’s conversation spread, my sturdy shield of being the Fire King’s Disciple would vanish.
And after that?
Every bastard under the sun will come crawling out.
Until recently, the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been little more than a fleshless skeleton.
But things were different now.
We had put on a fair amount of meat, and the wolves would soon start prowling around us.
They would watch one another until the time was right, then pounce.
The Fire King was already over a hundred years old.
His death would be the starting signal for those bastards to sink their teeth into us.
And the Zhongnan Sect will obviously be first in line.
I had to grow stronger before then.
To do that, Heaven’s Gate Temple was a hundred times better than the empty title of the Fire King’s Disciple, an illusion that would disappear before long.
All right.
I’m going to Heaven’s Gate Temple.
Having made up my mind, I turned to Ak Bulgun.
“Actually, I...”
I have no relationship with Great Hero Jeok.
We just happen to share a slight connection.
I desperately want to enter Heaven’s Gate Temple, so would someone like me qualify for a scholarship?
Or perhaps the Shanxi Province rural special-admissions track?
All the words poised to pour out of me like a waterfall were dammed by a single sentence from Jeok Cheongang.
“He is my Disciple.”
“Great Hero Jeok and I have no relationship at all...
Pardon?”
What the hell was he talking about?
I whipped around to stare at Jeok Cheongang.
What did he just say?
Ignoring my bewildered gaze, Jeok Cheongang continued as calmly as ever.
“I intended to keep him hidden until he was ready, but it seems that will no longer be possible.
Everyone appears to have plenty to say on the matter, so I might as well settle it once and for all.”
“No, wait—”
The voice I had barely managed to force out was swallowed by Jeok Cheongang’s shout, charged with internal energy.
“I proclaim this to the Murim beneath Heaven!”
A terrifying wave of energy shook the ground and pressed down upon the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s estate.
Every other sound vanished, and hundreds of pairs of eyes turned toward us.
It had happened before I even had a chance to stop it.
Veins bulged on Jeok Cheongang’s liver-spotted neck.
“I, Jeok Cheongang, eighteenth Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan, hereby accept Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan as my Disciple and name him heir to our sect’s orthodox lineage!”
A brief silence followed.
Then those who understood his words erupted into thunderous exclamations and cheers.
It was the moment when everyone’s lingering suspicions became fact—and one old man’s perfect bullshit became reality.
And I...
“I have committed a grave discourtesy.
I apologize to you as well, Young Hero Jin.
I will convey the news properly to Heaven’s Gate Temple.
No one would dare interfere with Great Hero Jeok’s Disciple, so even the Temple Master will surely abandon the idea.”
Every path into Heaven’s Gate Temple—or to becoming anyone else’s Disciple—had just been slammed shut.
Ak Bulgun chuckled at my devastated expression.
“Look at you.
Why the long face on such a joyous day?”
Because I knew perfectly well that there wasn’t even a one-percent chance Jeok Cheongang would actually take me as his Disciple.
I had gained absolutely nothing, yet my entire future had been blocked off.
My clenched fists trembled.
Damn old man.
I could already see my bleak future unfolding before me.
He wouldn’t teach me a single martial art, but he would torment me, beat me up, and send me on every petty errand imaginable.
At best, I would become an Inventory for storing his belongings.
I’m screwed.
Congratulations poured in from all around the table of honor, but I didn’t hear a word of them.
Jeok Cheongang spread his arms wide, wearing a thoroughly fake smile.
“Come.
Let your master give you a hug, my dear Dis. ci. ple.”
“Oh, look at this rascal.
Shy because everyone’s watching, are you?
Ho ho ho.”
Laughing heartily, Jeok Cheongang secretly crooked a finger.
At that moment, an irresistible force unlike anything I had ever felt seized my ankle.
One step.
Two steps.
My feet began moving toward him against my will.
...Seizing an Object Through Empty Space?
Was this really happening?
The tiny old man finally pulled me into a tight embrace and moved his lips.
“Hey.
Smile.”
“Put your arm around my shoulders.
Get those corners of your mouth up to your ears.”
Fuck it.
Whatever happens, happens.

chapters.title: Chapter 200
paragraphs: “I asked if there was something wrong with this old man being your master.”
“Pardon?”
What the hell was he talking about? Taken out of context, that line could put a romance-drama male lead to shame.
I covered my vital areas and slowly backed away.
“What?”
“N-Nothing. But what do you mean?”
“Forget it. Pretend you never heard me.”
Jeok Cheongang’s expression was an odd mix of inexplicable hope, irritation, and disappointment. He stared at me for a moment, then abruptly said, “You possess the Heavenly Martial Physique.”
“Heavenly Martial what?”
Jeok Cheongang frowned at my reaction.
“You don’t know about the Heavenly Martial Physique? Are you making fun of this old man?”
“I’ve never heard of it in my life.”
“...Heaven truly is heartless. How could it give such a thing to someone like you?”
He looked like he genuinely wanted to hit me.
Jeok Cheongang trembled as he clutched his liquor bottle, then let out a sigh.
“Then do you know anything about the Nine Yin Severed Meridians?”
“Oh, the Nine Yin Severed Meridians. I know about that.”
I had seen it plenty of times before. Did I have it right?
I rummaged through my old memories and pulled out a few keywords related to the Nine Yin Severed Meridians.
“An unusual constitution. Sickly. Smart. Dies young.”
“Am I wrong?”
“You have the gist of it. It is a type of severed-meridian condition in which powerful innate yin energy blocks the meridians and soon leads to death.”
“Then what about the Heavenly Martial Physique?”
Unease began creeping into my chest. The fact that he had brought up the Nine Yin Severed Meridians as an example only made it worse.
What if it lets me learn martial arts quickly, but there’s something wrong with my body that makes me die young? That would be a disaster.
Jeok Cheongang spoke with a solemn expression.
“The Heavenly Martial Physique is a martial constitution bestowed by Heaven, one that might appear only once every several hundred years.”
A constitution bestowed by Heaven? It sounded incredible just hearing about it.
Which only made me more nervous. The Nine Yin Severed Meridians were practically a double-edged sword that traded genius-level intelligence for a short lifespan.
I stared tensely at Jeok Cheongang’s mouth.
“And?”
“What do you mean, ‘and’?”
“When am I going to die?”
“Why would you die?”
“I think I’ve been having headaches and feeling nauseous lately. My bones and joints ache even now.”
Doctor Choi Tae—no, Jeok Cheongang—gave me a short and concise diagnosis.
“That’s because this old man beat you.”
“Oh.”
“You didn’t seriously think the Heavenly Martial Physique makes you die young like the Nine Yin Severed Meridians, did you?”
“Ahem.”
“What kind of lunatic are you?”
Jeok Cheongang shook his head in disbelief.

“The Heavenly Martial Physique is as different from a severed-meridian condition like the Nine Yin Severed Meridians as Heaven is from Earth. Do you think it’s called a gift from Heaven for no reason? You were blessed by heavenly fortune from the moment you were born with that body.”
“Me?”
“I heard from the Lesser Family Head that you have only been seriously learning martial arts for three months. Do you truly believe your achievements so far were possible through effort alone?”
“Not really.”
“You are where you are because you possess a constitution that allows you to make any martial art your own faster than anyone else.”
Jeok Cheongang was only half right.
I didn’t bother correcting him because what had supplemented my efforts wasn’t an innate constitution. It was the System.
If I really possessed the Heavenly Martial Physique, I wouldn’t have remained Third Rate until I turned twenty.
A promising tree showed its potential from the moment it sprouted.
If the real Jin Taekyung—the previous owner of this body—had been born with such heavenly fortune, he would surely have distinguished himself long ago.
This body doesn’t possess the Heavenly Martial Physique.
I looked down at my hands. The size and length of my arms and hands, the shape of my muscles, and the strength hidden within them.
Everything was perfectly balanced, without the slightest deviation.
The System.
The points I gained from leveling up and training were converted into stats, and the System distributed those stats evenly.
Every tiny, delicate gear inside my body meshed perfectly with the rest.
Since it isn’t innate, it isn’t exactly the Heavenly Martial Physique... But at this point, could I call it an acquired Heavenly Martial Physique?
Jeok Cheongang had seen my body with his own eyes, so it wasn’t strange that he had mistaken it for one.
And from my perspective, it was better to let him keep making that mistake.
It had taken only three months for a Third Rate wastrel who did nothing but drink to become a Peak master.
Without the Heavenly Martial Physique as an explanation, it wouldn’t have been strange for people to suspect me of practicing demonic martial arts.
Either way, this worked out nicely.
The fact that even a Supreme Peak master like Jeok Cheongang could mistake my constitution for the Heavenly Martial Physique proved beyond doubt that my bones and muscles were exceptional.
And since I had none of the side effects associated with the Nine Yin Severed Meridians, this was an absolute win.
Is the road ahead finally lined with flowers?
When I thought about everything I had suffered until now, tears welled in my eyes.
I was lost in emotion when I sensed someone staring at me and turned my head.
Jeok Cheongang flinched when our eyes met, then abruptly looked up at the sky.
“T-The moon is bright.”
I followed his gaze and mumbled:
“There are thick clouds covering it.”
“Did you have something to say?”
“Ahem.”
After repeatedly clearing his throat, Jeok Cheongang cautiously spoke.
“As you know, this old man owes you a debt.”
“So?”
“I want to settle that debt properly before I leave this place. Is there anything you want from this old man?”
Honestly, nothing in particular came to mind.
If I had to name one thing, it would be for him to take back what he had said earlier.
But there was no chance Jeok Cheongang would do that. His pride wouldn’t allow it. I had to come up with a reasonable request that he could actually grant.
I scratched my head.
“Well, I haven’t really thought about it in detail, so I’m not sure.”
“Then think about it in detail.”
“Oh, I’ll tell you later if anything comes to mind. You’ll be staying for a few more days before you leave anyway.”
But Jeok Cheongang was firm.
“Right now.”
“Pardon?”
“I said tell me right now. There’s hardly anything to think about, is there?”

As he pressed me for an answer, Jeok Cheongang added in a mumble, “F-For example, perhaps you want to learn martial arts from this old man. Or you want to learn martial arts from this old man. Or you want to learn martial arts from this old man. Something like that.”
“It was only an example. Pay it no mind.”
“Ahem. Is there phlegm stuck in my throat? Ahem!”
I watched him for a moment before speaking.
“Great Hero Jeok. I’m only asking just in case.”
“Ahem! Ahem!”
“Do you want to take me as your Disciple?”
Jeok Cheongang froze in the middle of his violent coughing fit. His pupils shook as though caught in an earthquake.
“W-What are you talking about?”
“You heard me.”
“H-How absurd. You think this old man wants to take you as his Disciple?”
Yes. That’s exactly what it looks like.
At first, I had wondered if I was imagining things, but by this point, anyone who still didn’t get it would have to be a fucking idiot.
When I merely stared at him without saying anything, Jeok Cheongang was the one who grew flustered.
“You little bastard! What is that insolent look in your eyes?”
“I’m just looking at you. Don’t worry about it.”
“You seem to be laboring under a grave misconception, but you’re entirely wrong.”
“Right. Sure.”
“Do you think I would choose the heir to our sect, with its long and venerable history, so easily?”
“You chose one pretty easily earlier. And you said it in front of all those people, so you can’t take it back now.”
“Th-That... I can simply take another Disciple.”
“You said it was a single-successor, no-outside-transmission tradition, didn’t you? Either way, everyone in the world will think I’m the heir to the Fire Gate Clan.”
Struck right at the heart of the matter, Jeok Cheongang shrieked, “There isn’t a single reason for me to take you as my Disciple!”
“I possess the Heavenly Martial Physique.”
“Gasp.”
“It took me about three months to go from Third Rate to Peak. I wonder how long it’ll take me to reach Supreme Peak.”
“Y-You bastard. Do you think it’s that easy? Do you think Supreme Peak is some mutt’s name?”
“It was easy for me.”
How many times had I come within an inch of death?
It had been brutally difficult and painful, but from this point onward, it was going to be easy. No matter what.
While Jeok Cheongang struggled to find words, I muttered as though talking to myself.
“Actually, Supreme Peak might be difficult.”
“O-Of course it is.”
“Maybe by thirty?”
Jeok Cheongang’s mouth fell open.
“Th-Thirty? Supreme Peak?”
“Did I give myself too long? I deliberately padded it because it sounded difficult.”
I sighed and glanced sideways at him.

“Still, you must have been much faster than me, Great Hero Jeok. You’re powerful enough to rank among the Ten Kings, after all. And you had the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts, too. Wow, I’m jealous. If I learned high-level martial arts like those, I’d become strong in no time.”
Jeok Cheongang stared at me with trembling eyes. I could easily imagine what was playing out in his head.
What would happen if the Heavenly Martial Physique met the Fire Gate Clan’s supreme martial arts?
I had already displayed unbelievable achievements in only three months. It was possible that an unprecedented monster, unlike anything seen in history, would be born.
I’m almost there.
His pride kept him from saying the words aloud, so I drove in the final nail.
“Actually, this won’t do. I’m thinking of visiting Huashan once this gathering ends.”
“H-Huashan? Why would you go there?”

“Because of Great Hero Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint. I hear the two of you are quite close. If I explain my circumstances properly, I might be able to become his Disciple without letting word get out...”
“No!”
The shout burst from him before he could stop it. Jeok Cheongang flinched and swallowed dryly.
“If you are perhaps considering it...”
“Pardon? I can’t hear you. You’re speaking too quietly.”
“Whew.”
Jeok Cheongang steadied his breathing and tried again.
“If you’re interested, this old man could personally oversee your martial arts training.”
I widened my eyes in feigned surprise.
“Are you serious?”
“Of course. A debt must be repaid, mustn’t it?”
Perhaps he had belatedly decided that he needed to maintain his dignity. His voice was more stern than it had been until now.
It’s already too late for that, old man.
Barely holding back a laugh, I replied, “What you’ve already done is more than enough.”
“It is this old man’s principle to repay a debt tenfold, even twentyfold.”
“I see.”
“Exactly.”
“But aren’t you leaving in a few days anyway? You seem very busy.”
“It can be postponed. I plan to leave once you have achieved a certain level of progress.”
“Ah, so you’re the type who sees things through once you start.”
“It is simply my nature.”
“What if I fail to reach the level you want, Great Hero Jeok?”
Jeok Cheongang deliberately hardened his expression.
“Now listen here, you little bastard! Why are you already assuming you’ll fail?”
“I’m sorry. I just don’t know how many years it might take.”
“Did you already forget what sort of person I said I was?”
“The kind who sees things through once you start?”
“Once a martial artist draws his sword, he should see it through—even if he has to cut down a mountain.”
“Wow, that’s impressive. As expected of you, Great Hero Jeok!”
I gave him a thumbs-up, then asked in a suggestive tone, “But at this point, doesn’t that make us master and Disciple?”
After a brief silence, Jeok Cheongang shook his head vigorously.
“Master and Disciple? What nonsense! I am merely repaying a debt.”
“Ah, I see. I misunderstood your intentions, Great Hero Jeok. Please accept my sincere apologies.”
“...Ahem.”
Jeok Cheongang coughed uncomfortably before continuing.
“But I think we need to change the way you address me.”
“The way I address you?”
“Although we are not, well, truly master and Disciple, people are watching. Shouldn’t we at least keep up appearances?”
“That’s true.”
The way I address him? What should I call him?
After a moment’s thought, one word slipped from my mouth.
“Then should I call you Master from now on?”
“Master?”
“H-Huh?”
Jeok Cheongang came to his senses as though he had just woken up and stared at me with a complicated, subtle gaze.
“Yes. That would be good.”
“Yes. Then when it’s just the two of us...”
“Old Master. Call me that.”
“Understood, Old Master.”
I bowed deeply to him.
The Supreme Peak master whose fame resounded throughout the world, Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
It was the moment my subtle relationship with him began.
After sending Jin Taekyung away, Jeok Cheongang leaned back against an old wall.
The voice he had just heard echoed endlessly through his mind.
Master.
It had been ten years.
Ten years since anyone had called him Master.
Jin Taekyung’s build, face, and personality were all different, yet the sight of him reminded Jeok Cheongang of his dead Disciple.
As Jeok Cheongang quietly sank into thought, a faint smile suddenly appeared at the corner of his wrinkled mouth.
Not bad.
He had never imagined things would turn out this way, but he did not dislike it.
No, he even found himself looking forward to what lay ahead, filled with an inexplicable sense of cheer.
“Not bad. Not bad at all.”
Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh and looked up at the sky.
At some point, the dark clouds had parted, revealing a bright moon.

“Pardon?”
What the hell was he talking about?
Taken out of context, that line could put a romance-drama male lead to shame.
I covered my vital areas and slowly backed away.
“What?”
“N-Nothing.
But what do you mean?”
“Forget it.
Pretend you never heard me.”
Jeok Cheongang’s expression was an odd mix of inexplicable hope, irritation, and disappointment.
He stared at me for a moment, then abruptly said, “You possess the Heavenly Martial Physique.”
“Heavenly Martial what?”
Jeok Cheongang frowned at my reaction.
“You don’t know about the Heavenly Martial Physique?
Are you making fun of this old man?”
“I’ve never heard of it in my life.”
“...Heaven truly is heartless.
How could it give such a thing to someone like you?”
He looked like he genuinely wanted to hit me.
Jeok Cheongang trembled as he clutched his liquor bottle, then let out a sigh.
“Then do you know anything about the Nine Yin Severed Meridians?”
“Oh, the Nine Yin Severed Meridians.
I know about that.”
I had seen it plenty of times before.
Did I have it right?
I rummaged through my old memories and pulled out a few keywords related to the Nine Yin Severed Meridians.
“An unusual constitution.
Sickly.
Smart.
Dies young.”
“Am I wrong?”
“You have the gist of it.
It is a type of severed-meridian condition in which powerful innate yin energy blocks the meridians and soon leads to death.”
“Then what about the Heavenly Martial Physique?”
Unease began creeping into my chest.
The fact that he had brought up the Nine Yin Severed Meridians as an example only made it worse.
What if it lets me learn martial arts quickly, but there’s something wrong with my body that makes me die young?
That would be a disaster.
Jeok Cheongang spoke with a solemn expression.
“The Heavenly Martial Physique is a martial constitution bestowed by Heaven, one that might appear only once every several hundred years.”
A constitution bestowed by Heaven?
It sounded incredible just hearing about it.
Which only made me more nervous.
The Nine Yin Severed Meridians were practically a double-edged sword that traded genius-level intelligence for a short lifespan.
I stared tensely at Jeok Cheongang’s mouth.
“And?”
“What do you mean, ‘and’?”
“When am I going to die?”
“Why would you die?”
“I think I’ve been having headaches and feeling nauseous lately.
My bones and joints ache even now.”
Doctor Choi Tae—no, Jeok Cheongang—gave me a short and concise diagnosis.
“That’s because this old man beat you.”
“Oh.”
“You didn’t seriously think the Heavenly Martial Physique makes you die young like the Nine Yin Severed Meridians, did you?”
“Ahem.”
“What kind of lunatic are you?”
Jeok Cheongang shook his head in disbelief.
“The Heavenly Martial Physique is as different from a severed-meridian condition like the Nine Yin Severed Meridians as Heaven is from Earth.
Do you think it’s called a gift from Heaven for no reason?
You were blessed by heavenly fortune from the moment you were born with that body.”
“Me?”
“I heard from the Lesser Family Head that you have only been seriously learning martial arts for three months.
Do you truly believe your achievements so far were possible through effort alone?”
“Not really.”
“You are where you are because you possess a constitution that allows you to make any martial art your own faster than anyone else.”
Jeok Cheongang was only half right.
I didn’t bother correcting him because what had supplemented my efforts wasn’t an innate constitution.
It was the System.
If I really possessed the Heavenly Martial Physique, I wouldn’t have remained Third Rate until I turned twenty.
A promising tree showed its potential from the moment it sprouted.
If the real Jin Taekyung—the previous owner of this body—had been born with such heavenly fortune, he would surely have distinguished himself long ago.
This body doesn’t possess the Heavenly Martial Physique.
I looked down at my hands.
The size and length of my arms and hands, the shape of my muscles, and the strength hidden within them.
Everything was perfectly balanced, without the slightest deviation.
The System.
The points I gained from leveling up and training were converted into stats, and the System distributed those stats evenly.
Every tiny, delicate gear inside my body meshed perfectly with the rest.
Since it isn’t innate, it isn’t exactly the Heavenly Martial Physique...
But at this point, could I call it an acquired Heavenly Martial Physique?
Jeok Cheongang had seen my body with his own eyes, so it wasn’t strange that he had mistaken it for one.
And from my perspective, it was better to let him keep making that mistake.
It had taken only three months for a Third Rate wastrel who did nothing but drink to become a Peak master.
Without the Heavenly Martial Physique as an explanation, it wouldn’t have been strange for people to suspect me of practicing demonic martial arts.
Either way, this worked out nicely.
The fact that even a Supreme Peak master like Jeok Cheongang could mistake my constitution for the Heavenly Martial Physique proved beyond doubt that my bones and muscles were exceptional.
And since I had none of the side effects associated with the Nine Yin Severed Meridians, this was an absolute win.
Is the road ahead finally lined with flowers?
When I thought about everything I had suffered until now, tears welled in my eyes.
I was lost in emotion when I sensed someone staring at me and turned my head.
Jeok Cheongang flinched when our eyes met, then abruptly looked up at the sky.
“T-The moon is bright.”
I followed his gaze and mumbled:
“There are thick clouds covering it.”
“Did you have something to say?”
“Ahem.”
After repeatedly clearing his throat, Jeok Cheongang cautiously spoke.
“As you know, this old man owes you a debt.”
“So?”
“I want to settle that debt properly before I leave this place.
Is there anything you want from this old man?”
Honestly, nothing in particular came to mind.
If I had to name one thing, it would be for him to take back what he had said earlier.
But there was no chance Jeok Cheongang would do that.
His pride wouldn’t allow it.
I had to come up with a reasonable request that he could actually grant.
I scratched my head.
“Well, I haven’t really thought about it in detail, so I’m not sure.”
“Then think about it in detail.”
“Oh, I’ll tell you later if anything comes to mind.
You’ll be staying for a few more days before you leave anyway.”
But Jeok Cheongang was firm.
“Right now.”
“Pardon?”
“I said tell me right now.
There’s hardly anything to think about, is there?”
As he pressed me for an answer, Jeok Cheongang added in a mumble, “F-For example, perhaps you want to learn martial arts from this old man.
Or you want to learn martial arts from this old man.
Or you want to learn martial arts from this old man.
Something like that.”
“It was only an example.
Pay it no mind.”
“Ahem.
Is there phlegm stuck in my throat?
Ahem!”
